resources.address: 515 E 100 S, 12th Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: 211 Utah Ride United provides free short-term Lyft rides for Utahns in its service areas who lack other resources for one-time transportation needs such as medical, employment, food access, financial, and education trips.
resources.hours: Ride scheduling Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; 211 contact options are listed as available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free short-term Lyft rides coordinated by 211 Utah for one-time transportation needs. Eligible trip purposes include non-emergency medical appointments, returning from the emergency room, substance-use treatment or discharge, dental or vision appointments, job interviews, one-time work commute, fingerprinting or pre-employment paperwork, food pantry or benefit access, financial-service appointments, and education-related trips.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must lack other transportation resources and must be approved by 211 Utah team members. The program is short-term and not recurring; clients should generally expect one to three round trips to overcome a short-term barrier. Riders must follow Lyft rider safety policies and need access to a phone or internet to schedule the ride.

**Population Served**
Utahns in the listed Ride United service areas, including the Wasatch Front area from Tooele to Cottonwood Heights and Bountiful to Bluffdale.

**How to Best Connect**
Dial 211 or 888-826-9790, text a ZIP code to 801-845-2211, email 211@uw.org, use 211utah.org, the 211 Utah app, chat, or phone to ask about scheduling a ride. Ride scheduling is listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM and can be on demand or up to one day in advance.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not ongoing transportation. Eligibility and ride availability are determined by 211 Utah, and clients should not assume a ride is guaranteed until 211 confirms it.
resources.name: 211 Utah Ride United

resources.address: 2487 S 700 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84106
resources.description: 7th Street Treatment Center is a Salt Lake City drug and alcohol addiction treatment center offering substance-use and co-occurring mental-health treatment with admissions information available directly from the provider.
resources.hours: Office hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Drug and alcohol addiction treatment and co-occurring mental-health treatment. The official site describes a full-service mental health and substance-use disorder treatment center with admissions and program information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility and level of care are determined through the admissions process. Current openings, payer requirements, and clinical fit should be confirmed directly with the center.

**Population Served**
People seeking substance-use recovery support in Salt Lake City and surrounding Salt Lake County, including people with co-occurring mental-health needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call (385) 261-2070 or email info@7treatment.org. The main office is at 2487 S 700 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84106, and listed office hours are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a treatment provider, not an emergency detox or crisis line. Verify fees, insurance, and the exact level of care available before referral.
resources.name: 7th Street Treatment Center

resources.description: Free confidential 24/7 crisis support by phone, text, chat, and ASL videophone through 988, with Utah calls answered by HMHI when routed locally and connection to Salt Lake County Mobile Crisis Outreach Team when appropriate.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immediate emotional and mental-health crisis support by phone, text, chat, and ASL videophone. Utah callers can receive suicide prevention, de-escalation, stabilization, referrals, safety planning, and connection to Mobile Crisis Outreach Team services when clinically appropriate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available to anyone in the United States through 988, including Salt Lake County residents. Utah MCOT response depends on location, safety, availability, and crisis triage.

**Population Served**
People of any age experiencing emotional distress, suicidal thoughts, mental-health crisis, substance-related crisis, or concern for someone else. Utah routing includes options for Spanish and veterans through the 988 system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 988, use 988 Lifeline chat, or call the Utah Crisis Line local number 801-587-3000. Ask the crisis worker about mobile crisis outreach if in-person support is needed in Salt Lake County.

**Important Information to Know**
This is crisis support and referral, not ongoing therapy. 988 Utah states crisis workers only contact 911 in limited immediate-danger or mandated-reporting situations. Response type and MCOT timing depend on the situation.
resources.name: 988 / Utah Crisis Line and Salt Lake County Mobile Crisis Outreach Team

resources.description: A/D Psychotherapy provides Sandy-based mental health and addiction treatment, including substance-use IOP, PHP, outpatient support, medication support, aftercare, and recovery yoga.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient addiction and mental-health treatment, including substance-use intensive outpatient treatment, partial hospitalization, aftercare, medication support, and recovery yoga.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients should contact the Sandy team to discuss program availability, level-of-care fit, and payment options. Private pay is available; insurance details must be confirmed with the provider.

**Population Served**
People in Sandy and Salt Lake County seeking outpatient addiction treatment, mental-health treatment, or both.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-233-8577 or use the Get Help/contact form on the provider website. The office is at 9662 S 700 E, Sandy, UT 84070.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not presented as universally free care. Verify current insurance participation, schedule, and whether PHP or IOP is the clinically appropriate level before referral.
resources.name: A/D Psychotherapy & Clinical Consulting

resources.description: AARP Foundation BACK TO WORK 50+ offers free workshops, coaching and job-readiness resources for adults age 50 and older who need help returning to work or competing for better jobs.
resources.hours: Workshop and coaching schedules vary; use the online registration route or call the program contact number for current options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free job-search workshops, coaching, job-readiness tools and resources for people age 50 and older who want to return to work, improve job-search confidence or compete for in-demand jobs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for adults age 50+; AARP materials emphasize older adults with low income. AARP membership is not required for BACK TO WORK 50+ workshop participation.

**Population Served**
Adults age 50 and older, including Salt Lake County residents who can use national online options or any available partner-based workshops.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the BACK TO WORK 50+ workshop registration route on the AARP Foundation workforce page or call 855-850-2525 for program help. Local in-person partner availability may vary.

**Important Information to Know**
This is employment coaching and training support, not guaranteed job placement or cash assistance. Online access may be the practical route if no Salt Lake County partner session is available.
resources.name: AARP Foundation BACK TO WORK 50+

resources.address: Seasonal Salt Lake County sites vary by tax year
resources.description: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide provides free seasonal federal and state tax preparation and filing help through IRS-certified volunteers, with a focus on older adults and low- to moderate-income taxpayers.
resources.hours: Seasonal, generally during tax filing season; site schedules, appointment rules and service models vary each year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free seasonal tax preparation and filing help from IRS-certified volunteers. The related IRS Tax Counseling for the Elderly program specializes in pension and retirement-related tax questions for older taxpayers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open through Tax-Aide site rules, with a focus on adults 50+ and low- to moderate-income taxpayers. Return complexity limits, required documents and appointment rules vary by site and tax year.

**Population Served**
Older adults and other taxpayers who need free tax-preparation help, including Salt Lake County residents using nearby or virtual Tax-Aide options when available.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the AARP Tax-Aide locator or call 888-227-7669 during tax season to find current sites, hours and appointment rules. Do not rely on last year's site list without checking the locator.

**Important Information to Know**
This is seasonal tax help, not emergency financial assistance. Site locations and whether help is walk-in, appointment-based or virtual can change each year.
resources.name: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide / IRS Tax Counseling for the Elderly

resources.description: ABA Federal Free Legal Answers is an online pro bono site where eligible users can post federal immigration-law questions and receive limited-scope answers from volunteer attorneys.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online limited-scope legal answers for federal immigration-law questions, including deportation, asylum, green cards, work permits, DACA, children's cases, employment-based immigration, citizenship, and other immigration issues.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Users must register through the website and meet the site's eligibility requirements. The service is for immigration law and federal veterans issues, not unrelated state-law problems.

**Population Served**
Low-income people in the United States, including Salt Lake County residents, who need online answers to immigration-law questions and do not need full representation through this service.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ABA Federal Free Legal Answers website to review eligibility, create an account, and submit a question online. There is no local office or phone intake for this online service.

**Important Information to Know**
This is limited online advice, not full representation. The attorney answers through the website and is not required to call, meet, or continue representation after answering the posted question.
resources.name: ABA Free Legal Answers - Federal Immigration

resources.description: ABLE Utah is a statewide STABLE account savings and investment program for eligible Utah residents with disabilities, allowing savings for qualified disability expenses while preserving certain public benefits; the site also describes a $25 enrollment incentive for eligible new accounts.
resources.hours: Phone support listed Monday-Friday, 7:00 AM-6:00 PM Mountain Time; online enrollment is available through ABLE Utah/STABLE Account.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ABLE/STABLE savings accounts for qualified disability expenses such as housing, transportation, health, education, employment supports, assistive technology, legal fees, and other disability-related needs. ABLE Utah also describes a $25 enrollment incentive for eligible new funded accounts.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ABLE Utah states that a Utah resident may qualify if disability or blindness began before age 46 and the person receives SSI or SSDI because of disability or has a signed diagnosis form from a licensed physician.

**Population Served**
Utah residents with qualifying disabilities who need a protected way to save and spend money for disability-related expenses.

**How to Best Connect**
Enroll or review details online at ABLE Utah. Call 1-800-439-1653 Monday-Friday, 7:00 AM-6:00 PM Mountain Time, or use website live chat when available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a grant or emergency financial aid. It is a savings and investment account; accounts may involve fees, investment risk, and penalties or benefit effects if money is used for non-qualified expenses.
resources.name: ABLE Utah Savings Plan / STABLE Account Enrollment Incentive

resources.address: 355 North 300 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84103
resources.description: ACLU of Utah pursues strategic litigation and civil-liberties advocacy for Utahns. Its general legal intake is currently paused; the active request-help page is reviewing reports of warrantless entry by ICE or CBP and directs other people to free or low-cost legal resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Strategic civil-rights and civil-liberties legal advocacy, litigation, know-your-rights materials and limited issue-specific request-for-help opportunities. The current request-help page is focused on reports of warrantless entry by ICE or CBP.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The ACLU of Utah takes matters with broader civil-liberties impact and does not provide routine individual legal advice. General intake is paused, and submissions outside the currently listed issue may not be reviewed or receive a response.

**Population Served**
Utahns with civil-rights or civil-liberties concerns, especially matters affecting many people or involving government practices.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Request Help page or intake form when the issue matches the current request. Phone contact is 801-521-9862; older ACLU materials list intake@acluutah.org for intake questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Submitting information does not create legal representation and does not protect filing deadlines. People with urgent deadlines should also contact another legal provider or attorney.
resources.name: ACLU of Utah Request Help / Civil Liberties Legal Advocacy

resources.address: AGC Training Center, 2229 South 1070 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84119 (headquarters: 2207 South 1070 West)
resources.description: AGC of Utah offers USDOL-approved apprenticeship-related training for operating engineer, form builder carpenter, and construction craft laborer pathways through participating construction employers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Registered apprenticeship-related instruction using NCCER curriculum for construction trades including operating engineer, form builder carpenter, and construction craft laborer.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Apprentices must be hired and sponsored by an AGC member employer. There is no direct self-enrollment into classes without an employer sponsor.

**Population Served**
People seeking open-shop construction apprenticeship pathways with Utah construction employers and Salt Lake City-based training.

**How to Best Connect**
Call AGC of Utah at (801) 363-2753 or contact the apprenticeship director at rfullmer@agc-utah.org to ask about participating employers, start dates, and the interview path with sponsoring contractors.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in class registration program. The practical path starts by contacting AGC for current participating employers and then securing employer sponsorship; openings and schedules depend on employers.
resources.name: AGC of Utah Apprenticeship Program

resources.address: 5034-A Thoroughbred Lane, Brentwood, TN 37027
resources.description: AGS Cares is a national charitable pathway connecting qualifying uninsured, low-income insured, or underserved patients with volunteer glaucoma surgeons for no-cost surgical glaucoma care when a participating physician can assess and submit the application.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost surgical glaucoma care and postoperative care through volunteer glaucoma surgeons in the AGS Cares national network for qualifying patients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For uninsured, low-income insured, or underserved patients who qualify for surgical glaucoma care. A participating AGS Cares physician volunteer assesses the condition and submits the application.

**Population Served**
People in the United States with limited financial resources who are at risk of glaucoma progression or blindness and can access a participating volunteer surgeon.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the AGS Cares page to find a participating physician volunteer, or contact AGS at 501-367-8605 or info@americanglaucomasociety.org for general questions. Ask whether a Utah-area volunteer is available.

**Important Information to Know**
A client starts by locating a participating volunteer physician; the physician assessment and application submission are part of the access path. Volunteer availability in Utah is not guaranteed.
resources.name: AGS Cares Surgical Glaucoma Care Program

resources.description: Department of Labor-funded AMVETS employment reintegration program in Salt Lake City for veterans experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, with job training, placement, housing-assistance connections, counseling access, and VA claims support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AMVETS Homeless Veterans Reintegration Program provides veteran-focused workforce reintegration in Salt Lake City. Services include job training, occupational skills training, apprenticeships, employment placement, counseling connections, housing-assistance connections, and help connecting with AMVETS Service Officers for VA claims.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans must verify active-duty service with a discharge other than dishonorable, show literal homelessness, recent housing loss, or enrollment in a qualifying partner service such as HUD-VASH, SSVF, or transition from incarceration, and be motivated to engage in workforce development and employment. AMVETS also says veterans at risk of homelessness within 15 to 60 days may be eligible.

**Population Served**
Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Salt Lake City, including homeless women veterans, veterans with children, and veterans transitioning from penal institutions or long-term mental-health facilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Program Director Lewis Arnette at 623-309-6539 or larnette@amvets.org, or use the message form on the AMVETS HVRP page. The official page identifies Salt Lake City, Utah as one of the launch sites but does not list a Salt Lake street address.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an employment and reintegration program, not emergency shelter. Ask the program to confirm the current local meeting location, required documents, and whether they are accepting new participants before sending someone in person.
resources.name: AMVETS Homeless Veterans Reintegration Program - Salt Lake City

resources.address: 218 E 500 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: ASSIST Community Design Center's Emergency Home Repair program helps low-income homeowners in listed Salt Lake County communities address urgent health and safety repairs, including plumbing, heating, electrical, and other utility-related hazards.
resources.hours: For emergency home repair, best call times are Monday-Friday 8:00-9:00 AM or 1:00-2:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Emergency home repairs for serious health and safety problems. Supported repair examples include plumbing, heating, electrical, roof, pest, structural, window, door, and accessibility hazards; this category entry is most relevant when the repair affects heat, water, electricity, or other essential home utilities.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Emergency Home Repair is for low-income homeowners under 80% AMI in listed cities or unincorporated Salt Lake County. Renters are helped only in very limited safety or life-threatening cases.

**Population Served**

Low-income homeowners in Salt Lake City, South Salt Lake, Murray, Midvale, Sandy, West Jordan, Taylorsville, Holladay, Draper, Cottonwood Heights, South Jordan, Riverton, and unincorporated Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**

Call ASSIST at 801-355-7085 and ask for the Home Repair Program Director. Be ready to describe the repair, city of residence, ownership status, household size, and gross monthly income.

**Important Information to Know**

This is not a general remodel program or utility-bill fund. Funding, eligible cities, project scope, inspection results, ownership, income, and documentation requirements determine whether ASSIST can help.
resources.name: ASSIST Emergency Home Repair

resources.address: 2324 S Constitution Blvd, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Ability Found helps place adapted mobility and daily-living equipment such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, bathroom equipment, ramps, lifts, AAC devices, and pediatric adaptive equipment at low cost based on disability-related need.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adaptive and mobility equipment placement, including equipment such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, bathroom equipment, ramps, lifts, AAC devices, and pediatric adaptive equipment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The sealed evidence supports disability-related equipment need. Provider or therapist input may be needed, and low-cost fees may apply.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in the Intermountain West, including Salt Lake County residents who can reach the West Valley City office or contact the program remotely.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-505-0529 or use the Need Help page. The office listed in the source evidence is 2324 S Constitution Blvd, West Valley City, UT 84119.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not cash assistance and does not cover supplies, medications, co-pays, or home improvements. Equipment availability and cost should be confirmed before referral.
resources.name: Ability Found Mobility and Adaptive Equipment Placement

resources.address: 1275 W 2320 S, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Ability Inclusion Services, identified in the evidence as The Work Activity Center d.b.a. Ability Inclusion Services, offers community day services, residential supports, community inclusion, and therapeutic recreation therapy for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community day services, residential supports, community inclusion, and therapeutic recreation therapy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The evidence identifies the program for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Intake, funding source, waiver/private-pay options, and current capacity should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
Adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities in West Valley City, Salt Lake County, and surrounding areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-977-9779 or use the agency website. The listed address is 1275 W 2320 S, West Valley City, UT 84119.

**Important Information to Know**
The public evidence identifies the agency as The Work Activity Center d.b.a. Ability Inclusion Services. Confirm openings and funding before referral.
resources.name: Ability Inclusion Services Community Day, Residential, Community Inclusion, and Therapeutic Recreation Therapy

resources.address: 3855 S 500 W, Suite E, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Ability and Choice Services provides supported employment, job development, employment preparation, and related disability supports for adults with developmental disabilities in Salt Lake County and nearby counties.
resources.hours: Regular business days 8:00 AM-4:00 PM listed on the provider site; call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supported employment, job development supports, employment preparation, and related disability services for adults with developmental disabilities. Utah DHHS and USOR list the provider for individual supported employment and employment preparation/job-development roles.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services may depend on disability documentation and funding through Utah Vocational Rehabilitation, DSPD, Medicaid waiver, or private arrangements. Call to ask whether the person can start directly with Ability and Choice or should first apply through VR or DSPD.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities in Salt Lake County and nearby counties who need supported employment or related disability supports.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-281-0700 or contact the South Salt Lake office at 3855 S 500 W, Suite E. Ask specifically about community employment or supported employment intake and funding requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
Current openings, funding authorization, and exact intake steps were not fully posted. A failed fetch of the program page did not show closure; current Utah CRP/DHHS listings still support the provider identity and employment scope.
resources.name: Ability and Choice Services Community Employment

resources.address: 1650 Summit Lake Dr., Suite 102, Tallahassee, FL 32317
resources.description: Acentra Health is the Beneficiary and Family Centered Care Quality Improvement Organization for Utah, helping people with Medicare use their rights for discharge appeals, service-termination appeals, quality-of-care complaints and immediate advocacy.
resources.hours: Phone and online access; appeal and complaint timing can be urgent, so call as soon as a notice or care concern arises.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medicare rights help, including filing certain Medicare appeals, quality-of-care complaints, hospital discharge notice questions and immediate advocacy to resolve medical-care issues.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with Medicare in Acentra's service states, including Utah. It is not general Medicare plan shopping, enrollment counseling or ordinary billing help.

**Population Served**
Utah Medicare beneficiaries, including older adults and younger Medicare beneficiaries with disabilities, plus family members helping with Medicare care-quality or appeal issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Utah's Region 8 BFCC-QIO line at 888-317-0891 or use Acentra's online File an Appeal, Quality of Care Complaint or Immediate Advocacy options. Have the Medicare notice, facility name and deadline information available.

**Important Information to Know**
Appeal deadlines can be short, especially hospital discharge or skilled-service termination appeals. Acentra's role is Medicare quality/appeal advocacy, not replacing a doctor, attorney or SHIP benefits counselor.
resources.name: Acentra Health BFCC-QIO for Utah Medicare Appeals and Quality Complaints

resources.address: 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Acquired Brain Injury Waiver provides Medicaid home- and community-based services to help qualifying adults with acquired brain injury live as independently as possible.
resources.hours: Call DSPD or use the online intake route for current intake availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Waiver services may include behavior consultation, chore services, cognitive retraining, companion services, day supports, environmental adaptations, homemaker services, non-medical transportation, therapies, respite, supported employment, supported living, and support coordination.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be age 18 or older, have a documented acquired brain injury, require nursing-facility level of care, meet Medicaid financial eligibility, and have a primary condition not attributable to mental illness.

**Population Served**
Utah adults with documented acquired brain injury who need nursing-facility level of care and community supports, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact DSPD at 801-538-4200 or apply through DSPD intake online through MySteps. DSPD intake can also be reached at 1-844-275-3773.

**Important Information to Know**
The waiver serves a limited number of people and has a waiting list. Services are based on assessed need, and Medicaid financial eligibility is required.
resources.name: Acquired Brain Injury Waiver

resources.address: 2225 South State Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Adam L. Crayk is listed by DOJ EOIR as a private attorney on the Salt Lake City Immigration Court pro bono provider list for free immigration-court legal services, with Spanish listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free or pro bono immigration-court legal services for people in proceedings connected with the Salt Lake City Immigration Court. The EOIR listing names Adam L. Crayk as a private attorney and lists Spanish.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people seeking help with immigration-court proceedings. EOIR pro bono providers are not required to accept every case, and some may charge fees for matters outside the pro bono commitment.

**Population Served**
Immigration-court respondents who can use the Salt Lake City Immigration Court pro bono provider list, including Spanish-speaking clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-944-3459 or email adam@lawscb.com. The listed office address is 2225 South State Street, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
EOIR does not endorse listed providers and warns that providers decide whether to accept a case. Confirm whether the attorney can handle the specific immigration issue and whether any costs apply before relying on representation.
resources.name: Adam L. Crayk - EOIR Pro Bono Legal Service Provider

resources.address: 14675 South 855 West, Bluffdale, UT 84065
resources.description: Adaptive Arena offers organized indoor adaptive sports for youth with disabilities, including goalball, sitting volleyball, boccia, wheelchair pickleball, and wheelchair basketball, at a Bluffdale gym reachable from south Salt Lake County.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Indoor adaptive sports such as goalball, sitting volleyball, boccia, wheelchair pickleball, and wheelchair basketball.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The sealed evidence says the program invites children through high school graduation to register. Current free status depends on continued donor and grant support.

**Population Served**
Youth with disabilities through high school graduation who can participate at the Bluffdale location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-917-2838 or use the Adaptive Arena website. The listed address is 14675 South 855 West, Bluffdale, UT 84065.

**Important Information to Know**
The program was submitted as currently free for athletes due to donors and grants, but costs, schedule, and openings should be confirmed before referral.
resources.name: Adaptive Arena Free Indoor Adaptive Sports for Youth with Disabilities

resources.address: 54 West 2100 South, #4, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Adecco's Salt Lake City staffing office connects job seekers with temporary, contract, and other employment opportunities, with a public branch page and job-search path.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Staffing and recruiting services for job seekers, including access to Adecco job openings and recruiter support for temporary, contract, and other work opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements depend on the specific job. Applicants should expect employer-specific eligibility, work authorization, screening, and scheduling rules.

**Population Served**
Job seekers who can work in the Salt Lake City area and use Adecco's online or branch-based staffing process.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the branch page to search jobs or get directions to 54 W 2100 S, #4. Office hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Adecco warns job seekers about fraudulent recruiter messages and says it does not ask for payment during recruitment. Openings, pay, and assignment length vary by employer.
resources.name: Adecco Staffing - Salt Lake City

resources.address: Adult Autism Treatment Account, PO Box 144610, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-4610
resources.description: Utah DHHS Adult Autism Treatment Account administers grant funding for qualified Utah adults age 22 and older who need adult autism treatment from a qualified provider.
resources.hours: Phone listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Grant funding may be awarded on behalf of an eligible applicant to a qualified provider for adult autism treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be at least 22 years old, live in Utah, have autism spectrum disorder or another neurodevelopmental disorder requiring significant supports through applied behavior analysis, and show significant support needs through formal assessments.

**Population Served**
Utah adults with autism spectrum disorder or qualifying neurodevelopmental support needs, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Email the Adult Autism Treatment Account through the application contact on the program page or call 385-310-5238 during weekday business hours. Mail for the account goes to PO Box 144610, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-4610.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding depends on money available in the account and program approval. This is grant assistance for treatment from qualified providers, not guaranteed treatment or an emergency service.
resources.name: Adult Autism Treatment Account

resources.address: 60 South 400 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: The Utah System of Higher Education Adult Learner Grant Program provides financial assistance to Utah adult residents enrolled in eligible online programs in designated fields of industry need at participating Utah institutions.
resources.hours: Application timing and process are handled by the financial aid office at the institution where the student is enrolled or plans to enroll.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Adult Learner Grant Program provides financial assistance for adult learners enrolled in eligible online programs in designated fields of industry need. Awards may cover up to the cost of attendance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be Utah adult residents, be independent students as determined by FAFSA, enroll in an eligible online program at a participating institution, be Utah residents or qualify for resident tuition, complete FAFSA, and demonstrate financial need. Priority may go to applicants from rural areas, low-income applicants, or people pursuing programs aligned to high-demand jobs.

**Population Served**
Utah adult residents, including Salt Lake County residents, who are pursuing eligible online programs at participating public or nonprofit Utah institutions.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the financial aid office at the institution where the student is currently enrolled or plans to enroll. USHE lists participating institutions including Salt Lake Community College, the University of Utah, Utah State University, Weber State University, and others.

**Important Information to Know**
This is financial assistance, not guaranteed free school. Awards, eligible programs, deadlines, and funding availability depend on the institution and current program funding. USHE's scholarships phone is 801-646-4812.
resources.name: Adult Learner Grant Program

resources.address: 1383 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Salt Lake City Youth and Family Division's Adult Learning at Sorenson Community Campus offers free computer access and digital literacy classes to help adults build technology skills for employment, citizenship, higher education, and daily life.
resources.hours: Computer Center open access listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-7:00 PM and Saturday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM; closed Sundays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free adult learning services at Sorenson Community Campus, including computer center access, technology support, digital literacy classes, and educational resources that support employment, citizenship, higher education, parenting, financial skills, and self-sufficiency.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page describes community adult learning access and does not list income, immigration, or residency restrictions. Specific classes may require registration or have capacity limits.

**Population Served**
Adults in Salt Lake City, especially west-side residents and community members who need computer access or digital skills.

**How to Best Connect**

resources.description: Free year-long career and professional mentorship for eligible post-9/11 transitioning service members, veterans, and eligible spouses, usually by phone, video, or email with a mentor matched by ACP staff.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
American Corporate Partners provides a free one-on-one mentoring program focused on career exploration, resume and interview preparation, networking, career advancement, work-life balance, leadership, professional communication, and small business development. Each mentorship is a year-long commitment with monthly discussions and staff support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ACP welcomes applications from service members and veterans, including Reserve and National Guard members, who served at least 180 days on active duty since September 11, 2001. Veterans with less than 180 days may qualify if injured while serving or training. Eligible spouses include active-duty spouses, surviving spouses, spouses of severely wounded post-9/11 veterans, and spouses of veterans who transitioned off active duty within the past 12 months. Exceptions can be requested by emailing ACP.

**Population Served**
Transitioning service members, post-9/11 veterans, active-duty spouses, surviving spouses, and spouses of severely wounded post-9/11 veterans, including Salt Lake County residents who can participate remotely.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through ACP's application link or call 212-752-0700. ACP states that qualifying applicants are contacted within one business day after applying, then complete an orientation call before mentor matching. Most matches are long-distance and communicate by phone, video conference, and email.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is free, but it is not a job-placement service and does not guarantee employment. Mentor matching depends on program fit, goals, and available volunteer mentors; ACP says staff normally follow up on mentor searches within about four weeks after orientation.
resources.name: American Corporate Partners Transitioning Service Member and Veteran Mentoring Program

Outpatient mental health, substance-use, and domestic-violence-related behavioral health services; individual and group psychotherapy; case management; medication management; language interpreting; Mental Health First Aid; and IPS employment support.

AAU emphasizes services for refugees, refugee youth, and other community members. Fees, payer requirements, language support, and program fit should be confirmed at intake.

Refugees, refugee youth, immigrants, trafficking survivors, domestic-violence survivors, and other Salt Lake City-area community members needing culturally responsive behavioral health care.

Call 801-467-6060 or use AAU's online behavioral health referral route. The office is at 155 S 300 W, Salt Lake City.

This is outpatient care, not an emergency crisis line or shelter. AAU can be especially useful when language access, trauma history, refugee background, or cultural responsiveness matters.

Free English Language Learning classes with small classes and practical content such as civics, financial literacy, and life skills. Remote or worksite options may be available as needed.

Adult English-language learners in the Salt Lake City area, with a focus on refugees and immigrant communities.

Refugee and immigrant individuals and families connected to AAU services, and TANF-eligible families when TANF Family Housing funds apply.

Help is not guaranteed and depends on current funding, eligibility, documentation, and review by the housing team. AAU says a team member will reach out within two business days after a request is submitted.

For individuals at risk of or surviving human trafficking. AAU describes statewide reach for human-trafficking survivors of all ages, genders, trafficking types, and immigration statuses. People can complete AAU's online trafficking-survivor support form or call.

Human-trafficking survivors and people at risk of trafficking in Utah, including people with homelessness, safety, health, transportation, or basic-needs concerns.

Licensed domestic violence treatment and counseling, assessments, individual counseling, and group counseling. ACES also provides substance-abuse treatment and related education.

People in Millcreek and Salt Lake County who need domestic violence treatment, counseling, or assessment, including English- and Spanish-speaking clients.

Lifeline-supported mobile phone service. Assurance Wireless instructs applicants to check program availability by ZIP code and separately check network coverage for their area.

Eligible low-income consumers in selected geographic areas, including Salt Lake County residents only if their ZIP code/address is served.

ASAP membership is for immigrants seeking asylum in the United States. Membership is free, but the program does not guarantee representation or an individual legal outcome.

Asylum seekers in the United States, including Salt Lake County residents who can use remote online services.

Use ASAP's website to learn about membership and member help. ASAP does not have a walk-in office for clients at its mailing address.

This is not a local full-service legal aid office. Frame it as remote asylum navigation, legal information, updates, and limited help-desk support rather than guaranteed representation.

People in Murray, Salt Lake City, and surrounding Salt Lake County communities living with opioid addiction involving fentanyl, heroin, or prescription opioid pain medications.

Payment options include Medicaid, Medicare, Medicare Advantage, most private insurance, and self-pay; veterans may have VA Community Care Network options subject to authorization. Medicaid transportation may be available depending on plan. Confirm coverage before intake.

Talent acquisition and staffing services, including direct, temporary, and contract-to-hire staffing. The local page includes a Find a Job route for job seekers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements depend on the open position and client employer. Applicants should expect job-specific screening and hiring steps.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in the Salt Lake City area who want to search BBSI-connected openings, especially in fields BBSI staffs such as administrative services, construction/general labor, manufacturing/production, food and beverage, and finance/accounting.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Find a Job link on the Salt Lake City branch page or email Richard.Webb@bbsi.com. The listed branch address is 257 East 200 South Suite 100.

**Important Information to Know**
BBSI's local page is strongly employer-facing and includes payroll, HR, benefits, workers' compensation, and business consulting. For a client referral, use it only when the job-seeker path or active openings are the reason for referral.
resources.name: BBSI Salt Lake City Talent Acquisition

resources.address: Provo, UT 84602
resources.description: BYU Independent Study offers online high school and university courses with open, self-paced enrollment for credit recovery, original credit, or college credit.
resources.hours: Online enrollment; course timelines and support hours vary by course.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online high school and university courses with enrollment available any time. Courses can support high school credit recovery or original credit and can also provide university credit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No BYU admission is required for independent-study course enrollment. Students should confirm age, school approval, proctoring, prerequisite, and credit-transfer requirements for the specific course.

**Population Served**
High school students, adult learners, and college-credit seekers who can use online self-paced courses from Salt Lake County or elsewhere.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the BYU Independent Study website to search courses, review fees and requirements, and enroll online. No phone number was supplied in the sealed evidence.

**Important Information to Know**
Courses provide credit, not a high school diploma by themselves. Students should confirm with their school district, adult-education counselor, or college how credits will apply. Per-course fees, proctored testing, and technology requirements may apply.
resources.name: BYU Independent Study Online High School and University Courses

resources.address: BYU Office of Belonging, Wilkinson Center #2400, 1060 E Campus Dr, Provo, UT 84604
resources.description: BYU Law's Community Legal Clinic provides free legal services through supervised law students for people in need, including immigration, contracts, housing and other civil matters, with email intake and statewide online clinic access listed by Utah Courts.
resources.hours: Thursdays 5:00 PM-7:00 PM, closed holidays; statewide online clinic appointments are by appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal services through supervised BYU Law students. The clinic lists matters including immigration, contracts, housing and other civil issues; citizenship and other community classes may also be available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people in need of free legal help whose issue fits the clinic. Utah Courts notes the online clinic handles general civil matters and does not handle family law.

**Population Served**
Utah residents needing free civil legal help, including Salt Lake County residents who can use online appointments.

**How to Best Connect**
Email communitylegalclinic@law.byu.edu. The BYU page says to use email rather than phone. In-person clinic is Thursdays 5:00 PM-7:00 PM at the BYU Office of Belonging in Provo; Utah Courts lists statewide Zoom appointments.

**Important Information to Know**
Clinic acceptance and appointment availability are limited. Contact by email before traveling to Provo or relying on help for a deadline.
resources.name: BYU Law Community Legal Clinic

resources.description: BYU-Pathway Worldwide provides an online pathway into PathwayConnect, certificates, and accredited online degrees from BYU-Idaho and Ensign College, with a direct application route.
resources.hours: Online application and online courses; program schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online PathwayConnect, certificate, and degree pathways designed to build academic and professional confidence and lead into accredited online programs through BYU-Idaho and Ensign College.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must meet BYU-Pathway admission and program requirements. Religious courses are required for all students, tuition is not free, and non-Latter-day Saint students may pay more.

**Population Served**
Adults and students in Utah and other operating locations who want a low-cost online pathway to certificates or degrees and can meet BYU-Pathway requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the BYU-Pathway application page to review requirements and apply online. Confirm location availability and current admissions status before relying on enrollment.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a religiously affiliated education pathway with required religion coursework. Tuition, program availability, and admissions details should be checked for the student's circumstances.
resources.name: BYU-Pathway Worldwide PathwayConnect and Online Certificates/Degrees

resources.description: Baby Your Baby is temporary Medicaid coverage for qualifying low-income pregnant women, covering pregnancy-related outpatient services while the ongoing Medicaid application is processed.
resources.hours: Online application available; call for current assistance hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary Medicaid coverage for pregnancy-related outpatient services provided by Utah Medicaid providers. The Baby Your Baby application also serves as an ongoing Medicaid application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For low-income pregnant women who qualify. A Baby Your Baby representative determines eligibility after the application questions are completed. Coverage can only be received once per pregnancy.

**Population Served**
Pregnant Utah residents, including Salt Lake County residents, who need temporary pregnancy-related Medicaid coverage.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Baby Your Baby application link on Utah Medicaid's page, or call 1-800-826-9662 for more information. Applicants choose a Baby Your Baby site close to where they live, and a representative from that site determines whether they qualify.

**Important Information to Know**
Baby Your Baby does not cover delivery. If ongoing Medicaid is approved, coverage can continue for the rest of pregnancy, delivery, and the baby may be covered under Medicaid for one year.
resources.name: Baby Your Baby Temporary Prenatal Medicaid

resources.address: 1864 West 12600 South, Suite 7-9, Riverton, UT 84065
resources.description: Bear-O Care is a DSPD-licensed nonprofit offering weekday day support and DSPD-certified residential homes for adults with complex multiple disabilities and high support needs.
resources.informationText:

Weekday day support and DSPD-certified residential homes for adults with complex multiple disabilities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The evidence supports adults with complex disabilities and indicates access depends on fit and funding. A waitlist is reported; behavior-specialist needs may be outside the provider's capacity.

**Population Served**
Adults with combinations of complex support needs such as deaf-blindness, brain injury, cerebral palsy, CHARGE syndrome, g-tube feeding, total ADL dependence, wheelchair use, or similar needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-604-3203 or use the Bear-O Care website. The listed address is 1864 West 12600 South, Suite 7-9, Riverton, UT 84065.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted evidence says the provider has a waitlist. Confirm current openings, funding route, transportation, and whether the person's support needs fit the program.
resources.name: Bear-O Care Day Support and BOC Homes for Adults with Complex Multiple Disabilities

resources.hours: By appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individualized supported employment, job placement, and job coaching. The provider helps clients find integrated community jobs at or above minimum wage and supports them after placement until independence increases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with disabilities needing supported employment. Funding may involve VR, DSPD, school-transition services, or another source; call to confirm whether a client can self-refer and what documentation is needed.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in Weber, Davis, and Salt Lake counties who need help finding and keeping integrated employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 801-200-2764, email beautifulability@outlook.com, or use the website contact form. The office is at 610 N Main St Suite A in Clearfield and is by appointment only.

**Important Information to Know**
The office is outside Salt Lake County, but the provider states it serves Salt Lake County. Confirm travel expectations, funding authorization, and current capacity before referral.
resources.name: Beautiful Ability Supported Employment Services Job Placement and Job Coaching

resources.address: 260 S Central Campus Dr, Suite 3525, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: The University of Utah Behavioral Health Innovation and Dissemination Center offers evidence-based therapy for adults, children, adolescents, and couples, plus groups, assessment services, and medication management, beginning with a free intake appointment.
resources.hours: Phone questions: Monday-Friday, excluding Wednesdays, 9:00 AM-3:00 PM for assessment-service questions; other hours depend on service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Evidence-based mental-health services including individual therapy for adults, child and family therapy, couples therapy, group services such as DBT skills group when running, assessment services for adults and children/adolescents, and medication management through a psychiatric provider.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Treatment starts with a free initial intake appointment to determine whether the center is a good match. Assessment services are currently limited to English-speaking clients, and not all referrals are appropriate for the training/research center.

**Population Served**
Adults, children, adolescents, and couples in Utah who can use University of Utah campus or secure telehealth services and are appropriate for the center's evidence-based care model.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-581-4697 or email bhidc@utah.edu. The clinic is at Gardner Commons on the University of Utah campus, 260 S Central Campus Dr, Suite 3525, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a research/training-oriented clinic, not a crisis center. Costs vary by service; the DBT skills group page listed $100 and advised contacting BHIDC about financial assistance options when needed.
resources.name: Behavioral Health Innovation and Dissemination Center

One-to-one friendship, integrated employment, leadership development, inclusive living, and family-support pathways for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Specific local program openings and which Best Buddies program pillars are active in Utah should be confirmed before referral.

People with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Utah, with submitted evidence referencing Salt Lake-area participation.

Call 1-800-89-BUDDY (28339) or use the Best Buddies Utah webpage and get-involved route.

The Utah page was submitted as expanding programmatic impact. Confirm the active local chapter, employment, friendship, or family-support option before making a specific referral.
resources.name: Best Buddies in Utah

resources.address: 249 HWY 101, Suite 312, Solana Beach, CA 92075
resources.description: No-cost national veteran programs including battlefield-return trips for WWII, Korean War, and Vietnam veterans, an Education Initiative, and Stronghold transition cohorts for Special Operations Forces operators and women veterans.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Best Defense Foundation offers no-cost veteran programs. Battlefield Return brings WWII, Korean War, and Vietnam veterans back to places where they served. Stronghold is a weeklong in-person transition program for active-duty and veteran Special Operations Forces operators, with a women-veteran Stronghold program, focused on injury, identity, purpose, relationships, and peer connection. The Education Initiative preserves and shares veterans' stories with students.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility is program-specific. Battlefield Return is reserved for WWII, Korean War, and Vietnam veterans. Stronghold has served active-duty and veteran Special Operations Forces operators and women veterans. Participants must be selected for a scheduled program.

**Population Served**
Veterans from older conflicts, active-duty and veteran Special Operations Forces operators, and women veterans; Salt Lake County residents can inquire through the national sign-up/contact routes.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Best Defense Foundation veteran sign-up forms for the program of interest, call 858-367-0079, or email info@bdf.org. The organization lists a Solana Beach, California mailing office; participation requires travel when selected.

**Important Information to Know**
Programs are selective and tied to scheduled cohorts or trips. These are not crisis, clinical treatment, or general financial-assistance programs. Best Defense Foundation states its veteran programs are provided at no cost to participating veterans.
resources.name: Best Defense Foundation Veteran Programs

Food pantry boxes for community members needing groceries; the listing says the pantry distributes food received from Utah Food Bank.

Specific eligibility and document rules were not confirmed in the opened listing. Clients should call before visiting to confirm whether ID, proof of address, or household information is needed.

People and households near Kearns and west Salt Lake County who need food assistance and can reach the pantry.

Call 801-964-2888 before going. The pantry is listed at 4750 S 4800 W, Kearns, UT 84118, with Tuesday hours of 10:00 AM-2:00 PM.

The public listing was last updated in 2023 and recommends calling ahead because pantry days and hours can change. Do not promise food availability without confirmation.
resources.name: Bible Baptist Church food pantry

resources.description: Bicycle Collective is a Salt Lake City nonprofit bike shop that provides refurbished bicycles, lower-cost bikes, bike education, memberships, bench time, and charitable bike access focused on children and lower-income households.
resources.hours: Salt Lake City location: Tuesday-Friday 11:00 AM-6:00 PM; Saturday 11:00 AM-5:00 PM; Sunday-Monday closed.
resources.informationText:

Refurbished bicycles, bike sales at reduced cost, bike education, memberships with bench time and parts discounts, and charitable programs such as Bikes-For-Goodwill supported by volunteers. The mission is to promote cycling as transportation and recreation and provide refurbished bicycles and education to the community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Low-cost shop services and sales are public. Free or charitable bike distribution depends on program rules, donations, partners, and current availability; contact the Salt Lake City shop before assuming a walk-in free bike is available.

**Population Served**
Community members who use bicycles for transportation, especially children and lower-income households; submitted evidence also notes focus on refugees and immigrants, people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity, and people recovering from substance use when program cycles or partners support access.

Call 801-328-2453, email slc@bicyclecollective.org, or visit the Salt Lake City shop at 325 West 900 South during posted hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Inventory and free-bike availability depend on donated bicycles and program capacity. Clients should ask whether they need a referral, appointment, fee, or partner connection for a specific bike-access program.
resources.name: Bicycle Collective Salt Lake City Bike Access and Education

Affordable Section 42 and market-rate apartment homes in Murray with standard apartment amenities and online application access.

Section 42 units are income-restricted; market-rate units have ordinary leasing requirements. The website does not publish full income limits, screening criteria, deposits, or fees.

Renters seeking apartments in Murray or the central Salt Lake Valley, including households who may qualify for Section 42 affordable units.

Call 801-263-0600, use the website's Apply Online or Schedule a Tour options, or contact the leasing office at 16 E Gilbride Avenue, Murray.

This is not emergency housing or rent-free assistance. Verify current vacancies, whether an available unit is income-restricted or market-rate, application fees, deposits, and income limits before applying.
resources.name: Birkhill Apartments Section 42 and Market-Rate Apartment Homes

resources.description: Catholic Community Services' Bishop Weigand Resource Center is a Salt Lake City day shelter and resource center for people experiencing homelessness, offering daytime refuge, intake on entry, case management, storage, hygiene products, showers, laundry, computer access, benefit and employment help, housing-placement connections, medical-service partners, and a clothing room on Tuesday and Friday mornings.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Daytime shelter and homeless resource center services, including case management, storage, hygiene products, showers, laundry, a computer lab, employment and benefit-program help, resume and job-application assistance, a clothing room, housing-placement connections, benefit enrollment, and medical-service partnerships.

**Eligibility Requirements**
All are welcome. Clients are asked to complete an intake form upon entry to the facility.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County who need daytime refuge, hygiene, laundry, storage, computer access, case management, or service connections.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 437 W 200 S, Salt Lake City, or call 801-363-7710. The center is open daily 7:00 AM-7:00 PM, closed 11:00 AM-12:30 PM for lunch and closed on holidays.

**Important Information to Know**
The clothing room is limited to Tuesday and Friday 7:15-10:15 AM. Capacity, partner-service schedules, storage availability, and holiday closures can change, so call if the need is time-sensitive.
resources.name: Bishop Weigand Resource Center

resources.address: 1600 Duke Street, Suite 510, Alexandria, VA 22314
resources.description: National Blinded Veterans Association Veterans Service Program with accredited service officers helping blind and low-vision veterans and their families with VA compensation and benefits claims at no cost.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-7:00 PM Eastern Time
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
BVA's Veterans Service Program helps blinded veterans with VA compensation and benefits claims and appeals. Accredited National Service Officers provide claims preparation, presentation, prosecution support, benefits education, and practical help related to VA services for blind and low-vision veterans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The intake form is for requesting VA claims assistance. The program is focused on blinded veterans and only works with VA compensation and benefits matters. Veterans provide personal, address, military service, conflict, service type, and character-of-service information through the intake process.

**Population Served**
Blind and low-vision veterans across the United States and their families, including Salt Lake County residents who need VA benefits or claims help related to blindness/vision loss.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the BVA Veteran Service Program intake form before calling, then call the toll-free claims hotline at 844-250-5180. Hours are Monday-Friday, 9:00 AM-7:00 PM Eastern Time. Mail can be sent to 1600 Duke Street, Suite 510, Alexandria, VA 22314.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are no cost, but BVA states the Veterans Service Program only works with VA compensation and benefits. It is not a general disability-services provider or local Utah chapter intake.
resources.name: Blinded Veterans Association Veterans Service Program

resources.description: Blood Cancer United, formerly The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society, offers patient financial-assistance programs for eligible blood cancer patients, including urgent-need, patient-aid, co-pay, travel, local financial assistance, and insurance case-management supports.
resources.hours: Information Specialists: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Patient financial-assistance programs for blood cancer patients. Current listed programs include Urgent Need grants, Patient Aid stipends, Co-Pay Assistance, travel assistance, Local Financial Assistance, Veterans Dental Partnership, and insurance case-management support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on diagnosis, disease fund, program type, household and treatment circumstances, insurance status, documentation, and whether a fund is open. Applicants should check the current program page or call before applying.

**Population Served**
Eligible U.S. blood cancer patients, survivors, and some caregivers or veterans with blood cancer, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Patient Financial Assistance Team at 877-557-2672. For information and navigation, call Blood Cancer United Information Specialists at 800-955-4572, Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time, or use live chat/email from the website.

**Important Information to Know**
Blood Cancer United is the current name for The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society. Funds and disease-specific programs can open or close; award amounts and direct-payment rules vary by program.
resources.name: Blood Cancer United / Leukemia & Lymphoma Society Patient Financial Assistance Programs

resources.description: Blood Cancer United's Susan Lang Pay-It-Forward Patient Travel Assistance Program provides a $500 grant for eligible blood cancer patients to help with treatment-related transportation and lodging expenses when funds and eligibility allow.
resources.hours: Patient Financial Assistance Team phone is listed; Information Specialists are available Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Treatment-related travel assistance for eligible blood cancer patients. The Susan Lang program helps with transportation and lodging expenses and currently lists a $500 grant. Related Blood Cancer United financial-assistance programs may also help with transportation, car repair, car insurance, lodging, food, utilities, and other treatment-related non-medical expenses when eligible.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on blood cancer diagnosis, program fund status, household income, insurance or citizenship/permanent-resident requirements where applicable, Social Security number, physician signature or attestation, and treatment or surveillance status. Applicants should check current program eligibility and whether the fund is open.

**Population Served**
Eligible U.S. blood cancer patients, including Salt Lake County residents, who need help paying treatment-related travel or lodging costs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Patient Financial Assistance Team at 877-557-2672. For information and navigation, call Blood Cancer United Information Specialists at 800-955-4572, Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time, or use the website's email/live chat options.

**Important Information to Know**
Funds can open or close and grant amounts or rules can change. This is financial travel assistance, not a ride scheduler, and approval is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Blood Cancer United Susan Lang Patient Travel Assistance

resources.description: Utah chapter and online community for military-connected families, offering events, local chapter connection, perks, communities, volunteer opportunities, and Blue Star Neighborhood digital support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Blue Star Families Utah connects military-connected families through the Utah Chapter and Blue Star Neighborhood. The online community shares chapter information, event registration, perks, exclusive content, volunteer opportunities, and communities for peer connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The chapter and Blue Star Neighborhood are for military-connected families. Specific events, perks, and programs may have their own eligibility or registration requirements.

**Population Served**
Military-connected families in Utah, including service members, veterans, spouses, caregivers, and family members who can use online Blue Star Neighborhood or Utah Chapter events.

**How to Best Connect**
Join the Utah Community through the Blue Star Families Utah page, use the Contact Utah Chapter link, or call the national Blue Star Families number at 202-630-2583. Most local contact is web-based.

**Important Information to Know**
Specific help varies by event and program. This is a community connection and family-support resource, not emergency financial assistance, clinical care, or case management.
resources.name: Blue Star Families Utah Chapter / Blue Star Neighborhood

resources.description: Bookshare is a national online accessible ebook library for people with qualifying print disabilities, including no-cost access for eligible U.S. students and paid adult memberships.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Accessible ebooks for school, work, career learning, and leisure reading, with formats such as audio, braille, large text, and highlighted reading through reader tools.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Members must have a qualifying print disability. U.S. students with qualifying disabilities are described as free; adult memberships may require an annual fee.

**Population Served**
People with qualifying print disabilities who need accessible reading materials, including students and adults in Salt Lake County using the online library.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Bookshare website to review eligibility, create an account, and submit any required proof of disability. No local office is needed because the service is online.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an accessible library service, not tutoring, a school, or a credential program. Adult membership cost was submitted as $79.99 per year and should be confirmed before enrollment.
resources.name: Bookshare Accessible Ebook Library

resources.address: 33735 Snickersville Turnpike, Bluemont, VA 20135
resources.description: No-cost Boulder Crest Warrior PATHH posttraumatic-growth training for active serving military, veterans, and first responders, beginning with a 5-day in-person initiation followed by 90 days of support and training.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Warrior PATHH is a 90-day peer-delivered posttraumatic-growth training program that begins with a 5-day in-person initiation and continues with three months of support, training, accountability, and connection. Boulder Crest also offers related family and retreat programming, but Warrior PATHH is the primary program for this lead.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Warrior PATHH is for active serving military, veterans, and first responders. Applicants must complete the online application and be selected. It is a training and growth program, not medical treatment or crisis care.

**Population Served**
Active serving military members, veterans, and first responders who are ready to participate in a structured posttraumatic-growth program; Salt Lake County residents can apply but must travel to a program location if accepted.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Boulder Crest's Apply for Warrior PATHH link or call the foundation at 540-554-2727 with questions. Program locations are nationwide, and participation begins with a 5-day in-person initiation.

**Important Information to Know**
Boulder Crest states Warrior PATHH is no cost to participants. Travel, selection, schedule, and location should be confirmed before referral. For immediate crisis needs, use emergency or crisis resources rather than this program.
resources.name: Boulder Crest Warrior PATHH

Brain-injury resource facilitation and assistance, including connection to housing, employment, therapy, benefits, local supports, communication with providers, and advocacy.

Utahns with brain injury and their caregivers, including Salt Lake County residents.

resources.name: Brain Injury Alliance of Utah Brain Injury Resource Facilitation

Resource facilitation, free intake assessment and consultation, coaching, neuropsychological testing, rehabilitation therapy, and possible help with therapy or daily-living equipment for eligible brain injury, spinal cord injury, or non-progressive neurological condition needs.

The fund supports individuals, families, and caregivers impacted by brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, or non-progressive neurological conditions. Financial help is described as payor of last resort, so other funding sources may need to be unavailable.

Utahns affected by brain injury, spinal cord injury, or non-progressive neurological conditions, including Salt Lake County residents and caregivers.

Everyone who calls may receive a free intake assessment and consultation, but added therapy, testing, equipment, or rehabilitation help depends on eligibility and funding.

resources.description: Bridges from School to Work offers free supported employment for young adults with disabilities in Salt Lake City, including job preparation, employer matching, supported onboarding, and one year of retention support.

Free one-on-one supported employment for young adults with disabilities, including career readiness, resume and interview preparation, employer matching, supported onboarding, paid-job placement, and structured support for about a year after placement.

Generally for young adults with disabilities ages 17-26 in a Bridges service city, including Salt Lake City. Local criteria vary and final eligibility is determined by the local Bridges program after the interest/application process.

**Population Served**
Young adults with disabilities in Salt Lake City who are in their last year of school or have left school and want paid employment support.

Use the Apply Now or interest form on the Bridges get-support page. A local Youth Employment Specialist follows up to discuss fit, goals, and next steps.

The website confirms Salt Lake City as a service city but does not show a local office address or phone in the checked page text. The program is free, but eligibility is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Bridges from School to Work Salt Lake City Supported Employment

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Charitable disability-related home renovation projects such as ramps, widened doorways, grab bars, walk-in showers, and accessibility renovations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The submitted evidence describes qualifying homeowners whose disability or condition limits movement, senses, or activities in the home. Applicants submit their story; exact criteria and project selection should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Homeowners in Salt Lake and Davis counties who need disability-related accessibility renovations and are selected by the program.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Giving Back page on the Brighton Communities website. No phone or physical intake address was supplied in the sealed evidence.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Canines With a Cause helps veterans train psychiatric service dogs using a train-the-trainer model. Veterans attend weekly classes, learn positive-reinforcement training, complete program levels and tests, and may work with a shelter/rescue dog selected for the program or discuss whether an owned dog may fit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans must have a verifiable military-related disability, specifically PTS(D), TBI, or MST. They must be physically, emotionally, and financially able to handle and care for a dog, have mobility and dexterity to train and control the dog, have reliable transportation other than public transportation, be in a stable living environment, be under the care of a mental-health provider, and not be in inpatient treatment or within six months of successful substance-use or mental-health treatment.

**Population Served**
Utah veterans within reasonable commuting distance of Holladay classes, especially Salt Lake County veterans with military-related psychiatric disabilities who can attend weekly training for up to two years.

**How to Best Connect**
Fill out the application form on the veterans program page or call 801-792-1737 with questions. Classes are held at the main office/training room, The Family Dog, in Holladay, Utah.

**Important Information to Know**
The training is free, but veterans must cover dog-care costs and commit to weekly sessions for up to two years. CWAC does not provide fully trained service dogs, does not train for all disability-related tasks, and places applicants in a queue after screening and foundation classes.
