resources.address: 1860 S 300 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Columbus Adult Education Center offers adult English Language Learning classes in Salt Lake City, with in-person and virtual options noted in referral materials.
resources.hours: Daytime and evening classes were submitted; confirm current registration, virtual options, and childcare before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult English Language Learning classes, including in-person and virtual options. Referral materials note daytime and evening classes and childcare availability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adult English-language learners in the greater Salt Lake area. Registration requirements, class placement, childcare, and virtual enrollment should be confirmed with the center.

**Population Served**
Adults in the greater Salt Lake area who are learning English.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-559-7533 or use the adult-students page for current registration information. The listed location is 1860 S 300 E, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Class availability, schedule, childcare, and virtual access can change. Confirm before referral, especially if transportation or childcare is a barrier.
resources.name: Columbus Adult Education Center Adult English Language Learning Classes

resources.address: 3495 S West Temple, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Columbus Community Center is a longstanding South Salt Lake provider for people with intellectual and/or physical disabilities, offering day activity, residential homes, supervised apartments, supported living, community employment, and youth pre-employment transition services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day activity, residential homes, supervised apartments, supported living, community employment, and youth pre-employment transition services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Day and residential services generally require secured funding unless self-pay, according to the submitted evidence. Confirm DSPD, VR, or other funding and current openings.

**Population Served**
People with intellectual and/or physical disabilities in Salt Lake County and the South Salt Lake area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-262-1552 or use the Columbus Community Center website. The listed address is 3495 S West Temple, South Salt Lake, UT 84115.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding must be clarified before referral. The provider may not be able to begin services without DSPD, VR, self-pay, or another secured payment source.
resources.name: Columbus Community Center Day, Residential, Supported Living, and Employment Services

resources.address: 3495 S West Temple, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Columbus Connects provides no-cost pre-employment transition services for students ages 14-21 with documented disabilities, including job exploration, workplace readiness, resume and interview practice, job coaching, transition planning, and work-based learning.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost Pre-Employment Transition Services, including job exploration counseling, post-secondary education counseling, workplace readiness, practice job applications and interviews, resume building, job coaching, comprehensive assessment, transition planning, work-based learning, job shadowing, and possible short-term paid internships.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must be ages 14-21, have a documented disability, and not currently be on the waitlist for Vocational Rehabilitation services. Documentation may include an IEP, 504 plan, SSI benefits confirmation, medical disability records, or an approved USOR form signed by a licensed professional.

**Population Served**
Students and young adults with documented disabilities in the Salt Lake County/South Salt Lake area preparing for employment and independent adult life.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Columbus Community Center at 801-262-1552 and ask about Columbus Connects intake. The Columbus Community Center is at 3495 S West Temple in South Salt Lake.

**Important Information to Know**
This is separate from Columbus Community Center's broader adult disability programs. Confirm current capacity and documentation requirements before referral.
resources.name: Columbus Connects

resources.address: 3150 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84119
resources.description: Utah Food Bank's Commodity Supplemental Food Program provides eligible Utah seniors with a free monthly USDA food package, nutrition education, and recipes. Boxes may be delivered to residences or senior housing sites or picked up at assigned local pantries, and capacity may be limited.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free monthly USDA food package for eligible seniors, described by Utah Food Bank as about 10 days of food, plus nutrition education and recipes. Boxes may be delivered to residences or senior housing sites or picked up at assigned local pantries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must reside in Utah, be age 60 or older, and have income at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines. Capacity is limited and eligible applicants may be waitlisted.

**Population Served**
Low-income older adults in Utah, including eligible seniors in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through Utah Food Bank's CSFP sign-up link or use the PDF application options. For application and sign-up event questions, call 801-887-1246. For recertification, delivery, or pickup schedule questions, call 801-887-1264.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a recurring senior food box, not same-day emergency food. Utah Food Bank states applications have a processing period and applicants may be approved, denied, or added to a waitlist.
resources.name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP)
resources.phone: 801-887-1246 application questions; 801-887-1264 current client questions; 801-978-2452 main

resources.description: CommonSpirit Health financial assistance for uninsured and underinsured patients who received emergency or medically necessary care at CommonSpirit facilities, including Utah Holy Cross facilities, with relief based on household size, income, and expenses.
resources.hours: Use the website's state selector and financial-assistance materials; contact the billing or financial-assistance office for the specific CommonSpirit/Holy Cross facility on the bill.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Charity and discounted-care financial assistance for eligible CommonSpirit Health patients with emergency or medically necessary care bills. Assistance reduces the medical bill rather than giving cash to the patient.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CommonSpirit says uninsured or underinsured patients must complete an application with household size, income, and expenses. The policy generally applies to patients who receive medically necessary care and qualify by income and financial resources.

**Population Served**
Patients with eligible CommonSpirit/Holy Cross facility bills, including Salt Lake County residents who received covered care at a Utah CommonSpirit Holy Cross facility.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the CommonSpirit financial-assistance page, select Utah or the relevant state/facility materials, and contact the billing or financial-assistance office tied to the bill.

**Important Information to Know**
This program only applies to covered CommonSpirit/Holy Cross bills and may not cover non-CommonSpirit providers. The applicant should use the Utah/CommonSpirit Mountain Region materials when applying for a Utah bill.
resources.name: CommonSpirit Health Financial Assistance / Charity and Discounted Care

resources.address: 501 East 1700 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
resources.description: Community Development Corporation of Utah offers down-payment assistance for approved first-time homebuyers as a deferred loan, plus financial coaching and education to improve budgeting, credit, debt management, and homebuyer readiness.
resources.hours: Call or use the website contact route to connect with a CDCU intake specialist; interpretation services are available upon request.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Down-payment assistance for approved first-time homebuyers as a deferred loan, with terms and interest depending on the specific program. CDCU also offers free financial coaching and education on budgeting, credit improvement, debt management, and financial goals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For down-payment assistance, CDCU lists first-time homebuyer status, owner-occupancy, at least $1,000 buyer contribution, income-related criteria, and program-specific requirements. A completed application does not guarantee funding.

**Population Served**
Utah and Salt Lake County homebuyers who meet current program geography, income, and mortgage-readiness rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-994-7222 or use the CDCU website to connect with an intake specialist and ask whether funding is available for the home location. The process may take 25-30 days.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency rent help. Down-payment awards are competitive, first-come first-qualified, and may be structured as a deferred loan rather than a grant.
resources.name: Community Development Corporation of Utah Down Payment Assistance and Financial Coaching

resources.address: Multiple Salt Lake County clinics including Stephen D. Ratcliffe Clinic, 1365 W 1000 N, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Community Health Centers, Inc. operates Salt Lake County community health centers offering prenatal, pediatric and family primary care, dental care, pharmacy support and limited vision-related links for underserved patients, with integrated behavioral health as a related clinic service.
resources.hours: Hours vary by clinic; call the desired site before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Prenatal care, pediatrics, family medicine, primary medical care, dental care, pharmacy/prenatal services, limited optometry or ophthalmology links, sliding-fee clinic access and related integrated behavioral health support.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The clinics serve underserved patients and offer sliding-fee options. Confirm costs, appointments, insurance acceptance and which site offers the prenatal, pediatric, medical, dental or vision-related care needed.

**Population Served**

Uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid and other underserved Salt Lake County patients, including Spanish-speaking and low-income families needing prenatal, pediatric, family health, medical, dental or limited vision help.

**How to Best Connect**

Use CHC's main clinic-network route and individual clinic contacts. Ask specifically about prenatal, pediatric, medical, dental or vision-related services rather than treating this as a standalone behavioral-health intake.

**Important Information to Know**

This resource is retained for CHC clinic services. Behavioral health should stay secondary unless a Mental Health membership is separately supported; do not make the record read like a behavioral-health-only program.
resources.name: Community Health Centers, Inc. Prenatal, Family, Medical, Dental and Limited Vision Clinics

resources.address: Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: Community Housing Services, Inc. operates low-income apartment communities and provides preliminary applications for HUD-subsidized or market-rate housing, with property managers handling availability and qualification questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Preliminary applications for HUD-subsidized or market-rate apartments at Community Housing Services properties. CHS operates properties for seniors, people with disabilities, families, and other income-based housing categories.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the specific property, subsidy, income rules, age or disability designation, and apartment availability. CHS says applying for HUD-subsidized housing takes time and move-in depends on availability.

**Population Served**
People seeking HUD-subsidized, income-based, senior, disability, or market-rate housing through CHS properties, including Salt Lake County properties where available.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the English or Spanish preliminary application links on the CHS Apply for Housing page, then contact the relevant property manager directly for qualification and availability questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The application page is actionable, but it is not a guarantee of an open unit. Applicants should be flexible about location and confirm the waitlist or vacancy status for each property.
resources.name: Community Housing Services HUD-Subsidized and Income-Based Apartment Applications

resources.address: 2964 W 4700 S, Suite 107, West Valley City, UT 84129
resources.description: Community Options is listed by Utah Vocational Rehabilitation as a Salt Lake County Community Rehabilitation Program and Pre-ETS provider offering supported job-based training, supported employment, customized employment, financial literacy, supported education, and student work-based learning.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vocational Rehabilitation partner services for people with disabilities, including supported job-based training, supported employment, customized employment, financial literacy, supported education, and Pre-Employment Transition Services. USOR student materials describe Community Options Pre-ETS work-based learning experiences and summer programming.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services may require VR eligibility, Pre-ETS eligibility, school/student status, or provider authorization. Pre-ETS generally serves students with disabilities ages 14-21, or age 22 when participating in special education under Utah rules.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities and students with disabilities in Salt Lake County and nearby Utah counties who need employment or transition support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-206-7315 or email shannon.wilkins@comop.org. For the listed West Valley City office, confirm address and appointment requirements before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
The national provider website was not specific enough in this pass, but current Utah VR documents corroborate the Salt Lake County service and direct contact. Confirm current office access and whether VR authorization is required.
resources.name: Community Options Utah Employment Services and Pre-ETS

resources.address: 195 North 1950 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Community Supports Waiver provides Medicaid home- and community-based supports for people with intellectual disabilities or related conditions who can live safely in community settings.
resources.hours: Call DSPD or use the online intake route for current intake availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Waiver services may include behavioral consultation, day supports, companion services, community transitions, environmental adaptations, homemaker services, non-medical transportation, personal assistance, residential habilitation, respite, supported employment, supported living, and support coordination.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must have functional impairment in 3 or more major life activity areas, onset before age 18 for intellectual disability or before age 22 for related conditions, primary condition not attributable to mental illness, meet ICF/ID level-of-care and Medicaid financial criteria, and be able to live safely in the community. There are no age restrictions.

**Population Served**
Utahns with intellectual disabilities or related conditions who need home- and community-based supports, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact DSPD at 801-538-4200 or apply through DSPD intake online through MySteps. DSPD intake can also be reached at 1-844-275-3773.

**Important Information to Know**
The waiver serves a limited number of people and has a waiting list. Services are based on assessed need, and Medicaid financial eligibility is required.
resources.name: Community Supports Waiver

resources.address: Salt Lake City, UT 84117
resources.description: Bilingual maternal support program offering prenatal classes, childbirth preparation, Spanish-language lactation support, resource connection, and doula/lactation-related support routes.
resources.hours: Prenatal classes include virtual sessions and one monthly in-person meeting in Salt Lake City or Utah County; Spanish lactation support group is listed as the second and fourth Mondays at 7:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comunidad Materna en Utah offers free bilingual pregnancy and postpartum education through Semillas para la Maternidad, prenatal and childbirth classes, Spanish-language breastfeeding support groups, in-home lactation consultations, and help connecting families to food, diapers, transportation, medical appointments, legal help, emotional wellness, and family support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program page describes support for pregnant people and families with babies up to 12 months. Some services require sign-up forms and may depend on current capacity.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum families, especially Spanish-speaking and bilingual families in Salt Lake City, Utah County, and online.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the sign-up forms linked on the program page. For lactation consultation, the page lists 801-613-0002 and 801-613-0034.

**Important Information to Know**
The page supports free bilingual programming, but exact openings, costs for any individualized service, and funding limits should be confirmed during intake.
resources.name: Comunidad Materna en Utah Maternal Support and Prenatal Classes

resources.address: 1750 Research Way, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Comunidades Unidas provides culturally and linguistically responsive referrals and assistance, including legal-service referrals, worker's rights, housing, health, education and community supports, with a direct phone route for immigrant and Latino community members.
resources.hours: Legal/immigration services have been listed Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM by Utah DHHS; confirm current clinic availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Legal-service referrals and community assistance. Comunidades Unidas' referrals page lists legal services among referral areas and says staff and volunteers use cultural and linguistic skills to assist the community and point people in the right direction; public listings also describe immigration services and consultations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page invites community members to call for referrals or more information. Some immigration services may have fees or case-type limits; direct representation should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
Latino, immigrant and Spanish-speaking community members in West Valley City, Salt Lake County and nearby areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-415-9785 for referrals or more information. The office is at 1750 Research Way, West Valley City.

**Important Information to Know**
The current official page emphasizes referrals and navigation more than direct legal representation. Treat it as a culturally specific legal-navigation access point unless direct immigration legal service is confirmed at intake.
resources.name: Comunidades Unidas Legal Services and Referrals

resources.address: 1750 Research Way, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Comunidades Unidas Promotoras are community health workers who provide culturally appropriate health education, navigation assistance, referrals, resources, informal counseling, and help bridging cultural and language barriers for Utah Latino and immigrant communities.
resources.hours: Promotoras meetings are listed as the first and third Tuesday of the month, 6:00-8:00 PM, at the Comunidades Unidas office; call to ask about individual navigation help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community health worker support, including culturally appropriate education, navigation assistance, referrals and resources, informal counseling and guidance on health behaviors, and help bridging community members to organizations, government agencies, and services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No formal medical eligibility is listed on the page. Call to ask whether the client's need fits the Promotoras/community health worker support available.

**Population Served**
Utah Latino and immigrant communities, especially people who need culturally and linguistically accessible help navigating health and community resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-415-9785, or contact the Promotora Coordinator at 801-487-4143 or cecy@cuutah.org. The office is at 1750 Research Way, West Valley City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is health navigation and advocacy, not a direct medical, dental, or vision clinic. Clinical services must be obtained through referred providers.
resources.name: Comunidades Unidas Promotoras / Community Health Workers

resources.address: 1750 Research Way, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Comunidades Unidas' Raices Unidas food access work helps Latinx and immigrant community members with emergency food assistance, SNAP enrollment support, resource navigation, and partner food-distribution connections. The practical intake route is to call the office for food access resources.
resources.hours: Food distribution schedule is not posted; call the office for current food access resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food access navigation, emergency food assistance, SNAP enrollment support, and connections to partner food distribution resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page does not publish a public pantry schedule or detailed eligibility rules. Call Comunidades Unidas to ask what food access support is currently available and what documents, if any, are needed.

**Population Served**
Latinx and immigrant communities in Utah, with a West Valley City office accessible to Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-415-9785 and ask for food access resources. The office address is 1750 Research Way, West Valley City, UT 84119.

**Important Information to Know**
This is best treated as food-access assistance and navigation, not a guaranteed walk-in pantry. Distribution details and availability should be confirmed by phone.
resources.name: Comunidades Unidas Raices Unidas: Food Access

resources.address: 1235 W California Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: The Concern Center of Salt Lake provides recurring food pantry assistance and a clothes closet in west/central Salt Lake City. Current 211/Salt Lake food-resource evidence and TEFAP participation support the food pantry, but income, ZIP-code, and case-by-case rules should be confirmed before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food pantry assistance and a clothes closet. This food-category entry is for the pantry/grocery help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Referral evidence describes service for specified west and central Salt Lake City ZIP codes, with case-by-case consideration noted in 211 materials. Current income and document rules were not confirmed from a provider-maintained page.

**Population Served**
People in listed Salt Lake City ZIP codes who need pantry food; the pantry may consider some situations case by case.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-972-5708 before going to 1235 W California Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84104. Ask for current pantry hours, eligible ZIP codes, and required documents.

**Important Information to Know**
No current provider-maintained page was verified in the sealed evidence. Public referral PDFs and TEFAP evidence support the pantry, but clients should call before traveling.
resources.name: Concern Center Food Pantry and Clothes Closet

resources.address: 660 S 200 E, Suite 300, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: The Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City provides consular protection, emergency assistance, and general legal orientation for Mexican nationals in Utah, including people detained by immigration authorities and their families.
resources.hours: General consulate hours listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; emergency line available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Consular protection, emergency assistance, and general orientation about legal and administrative processes for Mexican nationals, including people detained by immigration authorities and their families. The consulate helps people understand their legal situation and monitors respect for physical integrity and rights.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Generally for Mexican nationals and their families in the consular district. The Salt Lake City consular district includes Utah, including Salt Lake County, and parts of western Wyoming.

**Population Served**
Mexican nationals in Utah and the consular district who need consular protection, emergency assistance, or general legal orientation related to detention or immigration-related concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the consulate at 801-521-8502. For protection matters, use extensions 111, 114, or 116 as listed on the protection page; the emergency line is 801-971-7305 and is available 24 hours a day.

**Important Information to Know**
The consulate states that its guidance is informational and does not replace legal advice from an immigration attorney. It cannot represent a person in court or cover legal-process costs.
resources.name: Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City Consular Protection and Legal Orientation

resources.address: 660 S 200 E, Suite 300, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: The Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City is listed by Salt Lake County New Americans as a location for free legal clinic consultations for Mexican nationals and the consular community. Current schedule and appointment rules should be confirmed because the official consulate page was blocked during review.
resources.hours: Salt Lake County New Americans has listed a free legal clinic on the second Thursday of each month; confirm current schedule before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free civil and immigration legal clinic consultations connected with the Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City. Submitted official-consulate evidence describes immigration and DACA help and civil/family issues such as divorce, protection orders and child support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Primarily for Mexican nationals and consular community members. Confirm whether the person needs an appointment, Mexican consular eligibility or specific documents.

**Population Served**
Mexican nationals and members of the Mexican consular community in Salt Lake City and surrounding Utah areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-971-7305 or contact the Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City at 660 S 200 E, Suite 300. Confirm the current clinic schedule before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
The official consulate page could not be opened because of a bot-protection block, and public schedule listings may be older. Use the phone number to confirm current clinic dates, walk-in rules and scope before referral.
resources.name: Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City Free Civil and Immigration Legal Clinic

resources.address: 660 S 200 E Suite 300, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Local Mexican consular office for Mexican passports, matrícula consular identification, voter credential appointments, certified Mexican birth certificates, and civil registry services for eligible Mexican nationals and family members.
resources.hours: Passport, matrícula consular, and voter credential services generally require an appointment and are listed for weekdays. Mexican birth certificate copies are listed on weekday mornings without prior appointment in the consulate schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City provides Mexican identity and civil registry services, including Mexican passports, matrícula consular, voter credential services, certified Mexican birth certificates, birth registration for dual nationality, marriage registration, and related civil records.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for eligible Mexican nationals and qualifying family members. Document requirements, parent consent for minors, originals, and fees vary by document type.

**Population Served**
Mexican nationals and eligible family members who need Mexican identity documents or Mexican civil registry records in the Salt Lake City consular area.

**How to Best Connect**
Use MiConsulado at 1-424-309-0009 or https://citas.sre.gob.mx for appointments. The consulate is at 660 S 200 E Suite 300 in Salt Lake City. The main consulate phone listed is 801-521-8502.

**Important Information to Know**
The consulate is not a general U.S. ID provider. Fees vary; published 2026 examples include fees for passports, matrícula consular, and certified civil-record copies, while some registrations are listed as free.
resources.name: Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City Mexican Identity Documents and Civil Registry Services

resources.address: 4315 South 2700 West, Suite 2300, Taylorsville, UT 84129
resources.description: Utah Insurance Department Consumer Complaints and Independent Review helps Utah insurance consumers understand coverage, file insurance complaints, and request eligible health-insurance independent review after internal appeal steps.
resources.hours: Consumer service personnel are listed as available Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Insurance consumer assistance, complaint intake, and health-insurance independent review for eligible denied claims after the plan's appeal process. Complaints can involve health insurance, PBM/pharmacy, annuities, life insurance, and property/casualty insurance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The issue must fall under Utah Insurance Department authority. Self-funded employer health plans, out-of-state fully insured plans, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid complaints may need federal, Medicare, another state, or Utah Medicaid routes instead.

**Population Served**
Utah insurance consumers, including Salt Lake County residents, whose complaint or independent-review request is within the department's jurisdiction.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online complaint portal when possible. Call 801-957-9200 in the Salt Lake City area or 800-439-3805 in-state toll-free for consumer assistance. Paper forms are available if online filing is not possible.

**Important Information to Know**
The complaint process is not private attorney representation. The department says the complaint process usually takes three to four weeks, and health insurance jurisdiction depends on the type and state of the plan.
resources.name: Consumer Complaints and Independent Review

resources.description: Utah-based no-cost recreational, educational, camaraderie, mental-health-awareness, and suicide-prevention activities for registered veterans, service members with injuries or disabilities, and family/support members.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Continue Mission offers year-round recreational and educational events, mental-health support, camaraderie, and suicide-prevention activities. Examples include ski and ride events, snowshoeing, biking, bowling, pickleball, disc golf, softball, paddleboarding, hiking, museum tours, multi-day adventures, and family events.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Continue Mission serves veterans and service members with physical, mental, and emotional injuries or disabilities, plus their family/support members. Participants should register with the program and confirm event-specific requirements.

**Population Served**
Utah veterans, service members with injuries or disabilities, and family/support members who can attend events across Utah.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Started or Register links on the Continue Mission website, or call 801-560-9889. Check the events calendar for locations, dates, registration requirements, and whether family/support members may attend a specific event.

**Important Information to Know**
Events are listed as no cost for registered veterans and their family/support members. Exact locations, capacity, transportation, equipment, and physical demands vary by event and should be checked before referral.
resources.name: Continue Mission No-Cost Therapeutic Recreation and Veteran Community Activities

resources.address: 7762 S 700 W, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: Cornerstone Evangelical Free Church is listed by Utahns Against Hunger as a Midvale emergency food pantry. Public confirmation is limited, so clients should call to confirm hours, documents, and availability before traveling.
resources.hours: Hours not confirmed in opened reliable sources; call before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency food pantry assistance. Public listings identify Cornerstone Evangelical Free Church as a food pantry but do not confirm current distribution details.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility, service-area limits, and document requirements were not confirmed. Call the church before referral.

**Population Served**
People in Midvale and south/central Salt Lake County who can reach the pantry and need food assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-568-0954 before going to 7762 S 700 W, Midvale, UT 84047. Ask for current pantry hours, documentation rules, and whether food is available.

**Important Information to Know**
The current reliable public evidence gives only name, address, and phone. Do not rely on unofficial social media or old schedules without confirmation.
resources.name: Cornerstone Evangelical Free Church food pantry

resources.description: Corporate Angel Network begins registration through an online patient inquiry form for ambulatory cancer patients, bone marrow or stem cell donors, and recipients seeking free domestic air travel to cancer-related care.
resources.hours: Online inquiry form; representative follow-up is stated within 24 business hours after submission.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free air travel assistance inquiry for travel within the United States. The patient inquiry form starts registration for flight support to treatment, from treatment, or round trip.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The patient inquiry asks for patient type, treatment center, ability to walk up and down aircraft stairs unassisted, whether the patient requires medical assistance such as oxygen while traveling, appointment date, and travel windows. The form states there is a 10-business-day lead time and that submission does not confirm a flight.

**Population Served**
Ambulatory cancer patients and related eligible travelers such as bone marrow or stem cell donors and recipients traveling domestically for treatment, surgery, clinical trials, or second opinions.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the online Patient Inquiry Form. A Corporate Angel Network representative will reach out to complete registration and process the request after connecting with the requester.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency service and the inquiry form does not confirm a flight. Patients must be able to travel safely without in-flight medical assistance, and flight availability depends on matching and scheduling.
resources.name: Corporate Angel Network Cancer Patient Air Travel

resources.address: 2277 E Bengal Blvd., Cottonwood Heights, UT 84121
resources.description: Cottonwood Heights Police Department's Victim Advocate supports victims of violent crimes occurring in Cottonwood Heights with crisis intervention, lethality assessment, safety planning, rights information, referrals, reparations/restitution help, and criminal-justice navigation.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, excluding holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victim advocacy for violent-crime victims, including crisis intervention, lethality assessment, safety planning, immediate-needs assessment, community-resource referrals, rights information, support, reparations/restitution help, and criminal-justice navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page states the advocate is for victims of violent crime that occurred in Cottonwood Heights, whether or not a police report was filed.

**Population Served**
Victims of violent crime occurring in Cottonwood Heights, including domestic violence survivors whose situation falls within that city/police service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the full-time victim advocate at 801-944-7042 during listed weekday business hours. For emergencies call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
This is system-based police victim advocacy, not confidential community shelter advocacy. Confidentiality and records may differ from a community domestic violence agency.
resources.name: Cottonwood Heights Police Department Victim Advocate

resources.address: 1275 W 2320 S, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Covenant Employment Services, connected with Work Activity Center/Ability Inclusion Services, is listed by DWS as an Employment Network providing career planning, job leads, job placement, ongoing employment support, benefits counseling, and wage reporting for SSI/SSDI beneficiaries.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career planning, job leads, job placement, ongoing employment support, benefits counseling, and wage reporting for people receiving SSI or SSDI who want to return to work and eventually reduce reliance on Social Security cash benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The DWS Employment Network listing describes services for individuals receiving SSI or SSDI benefits who are interested in returning to work. Confirm whether services use Ticket to Work, VR, DSPD, or another funding path.

**Population Served**
SSI and SSDI beneficiaries in Salt Lake County who need employment support, with older DWS listing also describing statewide virtual service.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-973-9249 or email ehigley@covenantemployment.org. The listed in-person service area is Salt Lake, with the address at 1275 W 2320 S, West Valley City.

**Important Information to Know**
The DWS Employment Network PDF is older, while current public Ability Inclusion Services information supports the Work Activity Center address and phone but not detailed Covenant intake. Confirm the current intake route, funding path, and whether new clients are being accepted before referral.
resources.name: Covenant Employment Services Supported Employment and Ticket to Work Support

resources.description: Crisis Text Line provides free, confidential, 24/7 text-based crisis counseling by trained volunteer crisis counselors for people in the United States who need support by text, web chat, or WhatsApp.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free text-based crisis support with a live trained volunteer crisis counselor who listens, supports, and helps the person move from an intense moment toward calm. Web chat and WhatsApp options are also listed by the organization.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available from anywhere in the United States. No insurance, appointment, or referral is required; message and data rates may apply depending on the phone plan.

**Population Served**
People in emotional distress who prefer text or online support, including Salt Lake County residents who may not be able or willing to call a voice line.

**How to Best Connect**
Text HOME to 741741 from the United States, or use Crisis Text Line's website options for web chat or WhatsApp.

**Important Information to Know**
This is crisis counseling and emotional support, not ongoing therapy, medication care, emergency medical response, or local mobile crisis dispatch.
resources.name: Crisis Text Line

resources.address: 1385 West Indiana Avenue, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Crossroads Urban Center gives most donated clothing and household items away free at its Salt Lake City thrift store to people who have vouchers from a Crossroads food pantry or community partner.
resources.hours: Thrift store: Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 AM-6:00 PM. Downtown pantry: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. Westside pantry: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, food only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free clothing and household items through thrift-store vouchers. Items listed include children's, women's and men's clothing, shoes, work boots, socks, jackets, coats, underwear, jeans, work pants, blankets, towels, sheets, dishes, silverware, pots, pans, crock pots, small appliances, household goods, tents, and sleeping bags.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A voucher is required. The page says vouchers come from Crossroads food pantries or community partners. Inventory depends on donations.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County who need clothing or household goods and can access a voucher through Crossroads or a community partner.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the thrift store at 801-359-8837 or visit 1385 West Indiana Avenue, Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 AM-6:00 PM, with a voucher. For a starting point, contact the Downtown Emergency Food Pantry at 347 South 400 East, 801-364-7765, Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
A voucher is needed for free items; the Westside pantry is listed as food only. Specific sizes and household goods are not guaranteed because inventory depends on donations.
resources.name: Crossroads Thrift Store clothing and household goods vouchers

resources.address: 347 S. 400 E., Salt Lake City, UT 84111; 1358 W. Indiana Ave., Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Salt Lake City emergency food pantry provider listed by Utah DHHS as providing free diapers for children up to age 4, with photo ID and child ID required.
resources.hours: Downtown Emergency Food Pantry: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. Westside Food Pantry: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

For Children/Pregnancy, describe only diaper and child-material assistance supported by the pantry route; food pantry services belong to Food.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For diaper help, Utah DHHS says families must bring photo ID and ID for children. Pantry limits and diaper inventory should be confirmed before going.

**Population Served**

Low-income individuals and families in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County, including families with young children needing diapers.

**How to Best Connect**

Visit or call the Downtown Emergency Food Pantry at 347 South 400 East, 801-364-7765, or the Westside Food Pantry at 1358 West Indiana Avenue, 801-935-4079, during weekday pantry hours.

**Important Information to Know**

Inventory, ID rules and availability must be confirmed; do not present Crossroads as broad parenting support.
resources.name: Crossroads Urban Center Diaper Assistance and Emergency Food Pantries

resources.address: Downtown: 347 S 400 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; Westside: 1358 W Indiana Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Crossroads Urban Center operates two weekday food pantry access points in Salt Lake City: the downtown Emergency Food Pantry and the Westside Food Pantry. The Westside site is food-only; the downtown site also connects people with other emergency supports.
resources.hours: Both pantries are listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency food pantry assistance at the downtown pantry and food-only pantry assistance at the Westside pantry. Crossroads also helps low-income individuals and families with food and other necessities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Specific document and visit-limit rules were not confirmed on the opened homepage. Clients should call the pantry they plan to use before traveling if documentation is a concern.

**Population Served**
Low-income individuals and families in Salt Lake City and nearby Salt Lake County who need food assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Downtown Emergency Food Pantry: 347 S 400 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111, 801-364-7765. Westside Food Pantry: 1358 W Indiana Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, 801-935-4079. Both are listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
The Westside location is listed as food only, with no emergency services. Call the specific pantry for holiday closures, documents, and current food availability.
resources.name: Crossroads Urban Center Downtown Emergency Food Pantry and Westside Food Pantry

resources.address: 347 S 400 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Crossroads Urban Center's Emergency Fund can help with urgent needs including utility shutoff prevention through its Salt Lake City basic-needs service site, subject to current funding and rules.
resources.hours: Downtown pantry: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. Emergency Fund availability and documentation should be confirmed by phone before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Emergency Fund help for urgent needs such as utilities, utility-shutoff prevention, gasoline vouchers, prescription assistance, transit passes, and other basic needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Current detailed eligibility, documentation, benefit limits, and distribution rules are not fully published. Assistance is limited by available funds and current Crossroads procedures.

**Population Served**

Low-income people and families in Salt Lake City and nearby Salt Lake County areas who can access Crossroads' downtown service site.

**How to Best Connect**

Call the Downtown Emergency Food Pantry at 801-364-7765 or visit 347 S 400 E during weekday pantry hours to ask specifically about Utility Shut-Off Prevention Assistance and current documentation.

**Important Information to Know**

This is limited emergency help, not a guaranteed bill-payment program. Verify whether the specific utility need is being funded before sending someone.
resources.name: Crossroads Urban Center Emergency Fund / Utility Shut-Off Prevention

resources.description: Cyber-Seniors provides free technology support and training for older adults through a toll-free tech-help line, one-on-one tech calls and online webinars.
resources.hours: Tech help line listed as toll-free; webinar schedule varies by date and time zone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free technology support and training for older adults, including toll-free tech help, one-on-one tech calls, daily webinars and online learning resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for older adults needing help with technology. No Salt Lake County residency requirement is listed for remote help.

**Population Served**
Older adults, including Salt Lake County residents who can access help by phone or online.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-844-217-3057 for technology help or use the Cyber-Seniors website to book a one-on-one tech call or sign up for webinars.

**Important Information to Know**
This is remote technology coaching and training, not in-home device repair. Some help may require phone, video-call or internet access depending on the question.
resources.name: Cyber-Seniors Free Technology Support and Training

resources.address: East site: 670 E 3900 S, Suite 302, Salt Lake City, UT 84107; West site: 3540 S 5600 W, West Valley City, UT 84120
resources.description: DDI Vantage Baby Watch Early Intervention provides free evaluation referral and early intervention services for children under 3 with developmental delays, disabilities, or diagnosed conditions in its Salt Lake County service area.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DDI Vantage Early Intervention provides assessment, service coordination, family coaching, developmental services, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language therapy, nursing, child development, and special education services based on the child's needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children under age 3 with developmental delays, disabilities, or diagnosed conditions in the DDI Vantage service area. A public referral form starts a free evaluation.

**Population Served**
Infants and toddlers under 3 and their families in Salt Lake, Tooele, and Duchesne Counties, including Salt Lake County families in the DDI Vantage area.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online referral form for a free evaluation or call the East site at 801-266-3939 or West site at 801-957-0855. The prior reviewed record says someone will reach out in 1-3 business days after referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The evaluation is free. Ongoing service fees may depend on Baby Watch rules, insurance, Medicaid/CHIP, and family circumstances; ask about cost before services begin. Home address determines the correct Baby Watch provider.
resources.name: DDI Vantage Baby Watch Early Intervention

resources.address: 670 East 3900 South Suite 105, Salt Lake City, UT 84107
resources.description: Early Head Start Child Care Partnership serving low-income infants and toddlers at partner child care centers in Salt Lake County, with family goal support, referrals, meals, and application/waitlist process.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DDI Vantage Early Head Start Child Care Partnerships provides child care and early education at partner centers, family goal support, child development activities, medical and dental referral help, meals, parent committee opportunities, and family self-reliance services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Child must be under age 3, attend one of six partner child care locations, currently receive child care subsidy, and meet federal low-income criteria unless an exception applies. Pregnant women count as two people in household size for eligibility.

**Population Served**
Low-income Salt Lake County families with infants and toddlers under age 3 using participating child care centers.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the English or Spanish application links on the program page or call the Early Head Start office at 801-707-1698. After referral, staff contact the family for an application appointment and document collection.

**Important Information to Know**
The program uses a waiting list after application, and families may be contacted when an opening becomes available at any time during the year.
resources.name: DDI Vantage Early Head Start Child Care Partnerships

resources.description: VA Form 21P-534EZ is the direct application pathway for eligible survivors seeking DIC, Survivors Pension, accrued benefits, or Aid and Attendance/housebound increases.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Direct application for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, Survivors Pension, accrued benefits, and related survivor benefit increases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the survivor relationship, the veteran's service and death circumstances, income/net worth for pension, and VA documentation rules.

**Population Served**
Surviving spouses and children, and in some cases other eligible survivors, of deceased veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through VA.gov using the DIC, Survivors Pension, and Accrued Benefits page, call the VA benefits hotline at 800-827-1000, or get help from an accredited representative.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a benefits application, not emergency financial assistance. Deadlines and documentation can matter, especially for accrued benefits.
resources.name: DIC, Survivors Pension, and Accrued Benefits Application

resources.address: PO Box 5490, Parsippany, NJ 07054
resources.description: DOWC Cares Fix It Forward Giveaway considers nominations from people facing financial or personal hardship who cannot afford necessary vehicle repairs, and if selected, DOWC coordinates approved repairs through the dealership's service center at no cost to the nominee.
resources.hours: Online submission form; phone listed for DOWC Administration Services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vehicle repair assistance giveaway. Applicants submit their story, vehicle information, charitable request amount, required-repair description, repair order, and dealership information. DOWC reviews submissions and selects one nominee at a time; selected repairs are coordinated with the dealership's service center at no cost to the nominee.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone facing a financial or personal hardship that prevents them from affording necessary vehicle repairs may submit one nomination during the giveaway. A current repair order and dealership/service-center information are required.

**Population Served**
People in the United States with a vehicle repair need and hardship who can supply a repair order and dealership information, including Salt Lake County residents if their repair can be coordinated through the program.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Fix It Forward online submission form. DOWC Administration Services lists PO Box 5490, Parsippany, NJ 07054 and phone 201-777-1000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a limited giveaway, not an entitlement or emergency repair fund. One winner is selected at a time, and approved repairs are coordinated through a dealership's service center.
resources.name: DOWC Cares Fix It Forward Giveaway

resources.address: Driver License Division, PO Box 144501, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-4501
resources.description: Utah Driver License Division DUI Hearing Request is the official route for a person arrested for DUI to request an administrative driver-license hearing, generally within 10 days of arrest.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Administrative DUI driver-license hearing requests to contest Driver License Division license action after a DUI arrest. The page provides online and printable hearing request options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people arrested for driving under the influence who need to request a Driver License Division hearing. Requests are generally due within 10 calendar days of the arrest; late requests require an explanation and supporting information.

**Population Served**
People arrested for DUI in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online DUI Hearing Request submission on the DLD page as the recommended route, or use the printable form. Call DLD customer service at 801-965-4437 with process questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is only for the driver-license administrative action and is separate from the criminal DUI case. Deadlines are strict, and a late request must explain why it is late, why a late hearing should be granted, and why the person believes they will prevail.
resources.name: DUI Hearing Request

resources.address: 101 Monroe Street, Denver, CO 80206
resources.description: Daniels Fund offers the Daniels Scholarship Program for graduating high school seniors in Utah and other eligible states, covering up to the full cost of attendance at accredited nonprofit colleges and universities.
resources.hours: Annual application window was submitted as September 1 to October 15; confirm the current cycle.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A major postsecondary scholarship for graduating high school seniors that can cover up to the full cost of attendance at accredited nonprofit colleges and universities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For graduating high school seniors in Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, or Wyoming who meet program requirements such as financial need, GPA, test-score, FAFSA, and document rules. It cannot be used for trade schools or certificate-only programs according to the sealed evidence.

**Population Served**
Utah graduating high school seniors with financial need who plan to attend an eligible accredited nonprofit college or university.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Daniels Fund scholarship page or call (877) 791-4726. The fund office is in Denver, but Utah residents are eligible to apply remotely.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted application window was September 1 to October 15. Confirm the current year's deadline, test requirements, FAFSA/tax documentation, partner-school details, and award rules before applying.
resources.name: Daniels Fund Daniels Scholarship Program

resources.address: 2240 North Hwy 89 Suite C, Harrisville, UT 84404-2824
resources.description: Day One Charity's Charitable Mental Health Program helps eligible Utah residents access 8 weekly low-cost telehealth psychotherapy sessions on a $0-$30 sliding scale when they are low-income and uninsured or fully responsible for therapy costs.
resources.hours: Apply online; Day One states applicants receive an email within 48 hours requesting proof of income. Therapists are listed as 100% telehealth at the time of the official page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost psychotherapy access for families, individuals, and children through 8 weekly therapy sessions, with grants paid directly to the mental health agency providing services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Primary residence in Utah; household income at or below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level; no health insurance or insurance that leaves the client 100% responsible for mental-health appointments; commitment to complete the prescribed treatment period. Awards depend on demonstrated need, qualified applications, and funding availability.

**Population Served**
Low-income Utah families, adults, and children who need psychotherapy and cannot reasonably pay standard therapy costs.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Client Application on the Day One Charity website. For questions, call 877-393-6232 ext. 3 or email info@dayonecharity.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is financial assistance/access for therapy, not guaranteed free treatment. The award is limited and based on funding. The official page says therapists are 100% telehealth at this time.
resources.name: Day One Charity Charitable Mental Health Program

resources.description: Deaf Multicultural Counseling provides deaf-led online ASL therapy throughout Utah with Utah-licensed therapists for Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, DeafDisabled, late-deafened, ASL-using, LGBTQIA+, multicultural, and family clients.
resources.hours: Daytime, evening, and weekend slots are advertised; request a session and confirm therapist availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online individual, couples, family, and group therapy in ASL, with trauma-informed care, no interpreter required, secure video, captions on videos, and therapists licensed to serve Utah clients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to Utah clients who fit the practice and therapist availability. DMC accepts many insurance plans and self-pay; benefits are verified before the first appointment.

**Population Served**
Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, DeafDisabled, late-deafened, ASL-using, LGBTQIA+, multicultural, neurodivergent clients, CODAs, hearing family members, children, teens, adults, couples, and families in Utah.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Request a Session form, email hello@deafmulticulturalcounseling.com, call or text 470-944-8185, or use videophone 470-763-5282. DMC says it usually responds within 1-2 business days.

**Important Information to Know**
This is online therapy, not a Salt Lake City walk-in clinic. Insurance, therapist match, licensure fit, and appointment availability should be confirmed before relying on it for an immediate need.
resources.name: Deaf Multicultural Counseling Online ASL Therapy in Utah

resources.address: 7019 S 400 W, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: Dental On Location provides mobile dental exams, X-rays, cleanings, preventive care, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions, whitening, and denture services onsite at assisted living, memory care, independent living, and skilled nursing facilities throughout Utah.
resources.hours: Phone hours listed Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; facility visits are scheduled with the provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mobile dental care brought to facilities, including dental exams, digital X-rays, cleanings, preventive care, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions, whitening, denture services, and priority scheduling for urgent dental needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for residents of assisted living, memory care, independent living, and skilled nursing facilities. Facilities, residents, or families should contact the provider to confirm service to the specific location, fees, insurance, and scheduling.

**Population Served**
Facility residents throughout Utah, including Salt Lake City, Sandy, South Jordan, and other Salt Lake County/Wasatch Front communities; the site also states bedbound residents can be treated in their rooms when necessary.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-707-8740, email info@dentalol.com, or use the scheduling/contact options on the Dental On Location website. The office is in Midvale.

This is not advertised as free care. The provider says it is out-of-network but can work with most insurance for reimbursement documentation and offers self-pay options.
resources.name: Dental On Location Mobile Dental Care

resources.address: 743 W 700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Deseret Industries provides a paid job-training program through its thrift stores, including work experience, job readiness, education support, barrier removal, career exploration, development counseling, and help moving toward future employment.
resources.hours: Contact the Welfare Square DI store for current store hours and job-training application steps.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Paid work-training through Deseret Industries, including on-the-job training, job readiness, education support, employment-barrier removal, confidence building, career exploration, development counseling, and support during the job-search process.

Public pages say people struggling with employment should contact the nearest DI location to learn more and apply. Detailed eligibility and any church, bishop, counselor, or community referral requirements were not fully stated on the checked pages.

People in Salt Lake City and the DI store network who face barriers to employment and need a structured work-training pathway.

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, 1st Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah DHHS Disabilities Ombuds/ADA Coordinator helps people with disabilities raise equal-access concerns, ask disability-services questions, and seek resolution of concerns involving programs, services, and opportunities.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The ombuds office listens to disability-related concerns, answers questions about disability services and programs, reviews or investigates issues for legal and policy compliance, helps identify resolution options, and educates people about legal rights.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Contact generally must be made within 3 months of the incident or concern. The office serves people with disabilities who need help with access, services, or disability-rights concerns.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents, who need help with DHHS disability access or broader disability ombuds concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online contact option on the DHHS page, call 801-538-4580, or use Utah Relay 7-1-1 for TTY access. Mail may be sent to DHHS Office of Ombuds/ADA Coordinator, 195 N 1950 W, 1st Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84116.

**Important Information to Know**
The office says it will contact people within 3 business days and keeps information confidential. It cannot give legal advice, impose fines or sanctions, share confidential information, or force other agencies to act.
resources.name: Disabilities Ombuds Services

resources.address: 960 S Main St, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Disability Law Center is Utah's Protection and Advocacy agency for disability-related legal rights, offering self-advocacy information, referrals, attorney consultation and possible advocacy or representation for disability-related legal issues statewide.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Disability-related legal rights help, including self-advocacy information, referrals, attorney consultation and possible advocacy or representation. Issue areas include accessibility, assistive technology, community living, education, employment, health care, housing, institutional rights, transportation and voting.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be an individual with a disability in Utah and the legal issue must relate to disability rights and fit the organization's priorities, resources and conflict rules. Not every request becomes representation.

**Population Served**
Utahns with disabilities, including Salt Lake County residents, who have disability-related legal-rights concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for help online through the Get Help page, call 800-662-9080 or use 711 video relay. The office is at 960 S Main St, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are free, but limited staff and priority setting mean help is not guaranteed. DLC does not generally assist with applications or denials of public benefits such as Social Security Disability or Medicaid.
resources.name: Disability Law Center Protection and Advocacy Legal Help

resources.address: 550 Foothill Drive, Suite 105, Salt Lake City, UT 84113-1106
resources.description: No-cost Disabled American Veterans benefits experts at the Salt Lake City VA Regional Office who help veterans navigate VA benefits, claims, and appeals.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DAV benefits experts help veterans navigate VA benefits and provide counseling on VA claims and appeals at no cost. The Utah DAV page lists a Salt Lake City National Service Office connected to the VA Regional Office.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for veterans and eligible family members seeking help with VA benefits, claims, or appeals. Representation or formal claims help may require VA appointment-of-representative paperwork and proof of service or claim details.

**Population Served**
Utah veterans and families seeking VA claims or benefits help, including Salt Lake County residents who can contact or visit the Salt Lake City VA Regional Office location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-326-2375 or contact the DAV office at 550 Foothill Drive, Suite 105, Salt Lake City, UT 84113-1106. Confirm current walk-in availability and hours before sending someone in person.

**Important Information to Know**
DAV benefits help is distinct from DAV van transportation even though the phone number overlaps. This is claims/appeals assistance, not emergency cash assistance or legal representation outside VA benefits matters.
resources.name: Disabled American Veterans Department of Utah VA Benefits Claim Assistance

Job seekers in Salt Lake and Utah counties, including people needing disability-informed employment support, accommodations guidance, or VR partner services.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Non-emergency domestic-violence survivor support, including victim advocacy, case management, weekly mentoring and goal planning, resource referrals, support groups, financial-workshop basics, employment resources, retreats, and beauty/wellness programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Wellness Program serves domestic violence survivors across Utah. Complete the intake form or contact DARS to confirm fit, availability, insurance/payment issues, and safe contact preferences.

**Population Served**
Domestic violence survivors and families in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents who can use statewide phone/online access.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Wellness Program intake form on the website, call the office voicemail at 801-864-7987, or email DARS.utah@gmail.com. The mailing address is PO Box 1811, Sandy, UT 84091.

resources.description: Double Up Food Bucks helps SNAP users stretch food benefits for fresh fruits and vegetables at participating Utah locations. Salt Lake County residents with SNAP can use the location finder to identify current participating markets and groceries.
resources.hours: Varies by participating market or grocery location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SNAP produce match benefit at participating locations. Eligible shoppers can earn a dollar-for-dollar match on qualifying SNAP fruit and vegetable purchases and spend Double Up on more fruits and vegetables, subject to program rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requires an EBT/SNAP card. The FAQ states anyone using an EBT card is eligible; WIC alone is not eligible for Double Up.

**Population Served**
Utah SNAP households, including Salt Lake County residents who shop at participating markets or stores.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Double Up Utah/DHHS location finder to find current participating locations and ask the cashier how the Double Up card or market match works. Questions can be directed to 866-586-2796 or info@doubleupfoodbucks.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not free emergency food and requires SNAP spending at participating locations. Rules, match caps, locations, and expiration can change; check the current location finder before travel.
resources.name: Double Up Food Bucks Utah SNAP produce match

resources.address: 1020 E. Pioneer Road, Draper, UT 84020
resources.description: Draper City's Military Utility Abatement Agreement stops applicable Draper City water, garbage, and storm water billing for eligible residential Draper families when the head of household is on active military duty in a designated combat zone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Utility abatement for applicable Draper City water, garbage, and storm water utilities. Approved households are not billed for covered Draper City utilities during the qualifying abatement period.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Family must reside in Draper, the head of household must be on active military duty in a designated combat zone, and the household must be a residential Draper City water user. It does not apply to WaterPro customers or customers of any other water provider.

**Population Served**
Eligible military households living in Draper City and served by Draper City utilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Military Utility Abatement Form and hand-deliver it with a copy of the military orders to the Draper City Finance Department. For utility billing questions, call 801-576-6302 or email draper.utilities@draperutah.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is very narrow and excludes many Draper renters or residents whose water provider is WaterPro. Use Draper's utility services app or contact Utility Billing to confirm the water provider before applying.
resources.name: Draper City Military Utility Abatement Agreement

resources.address: 1020 E. Pioneer Road, Draper, UT 84020
resources.description: Draper Police Department Victim Services provides public-system victim advocacy for violent-crime victims, including crisis intervention, criminal-justice support, safety strategies, and referrals for counseling, legal assistance, shelter, and other services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Crisis intervention and support for crime victims, criminal-justice process support, safety strategies, and referrals to community partners for counseling, legal assistance, shelter, and other services. The page links to orders of protection and safety planning resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for victims of violent crime connected to Draper Police, Draper City Prosecutor, or crimes occurring in Draper. Call to confirm whether a specific situation is within scope.

**Population Served**
Victims of violent crime in Draper-related matters, including domestic violence survivors in the Salt Lake County portion of Draper.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Crime Victim Services at 801-576-6355. For emergencies call 911; Draper dispatch is 801-840-4000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is public-system victim advocacy, not a confidential shelter hotline. The Draper page also lists the Utah Domestic Violence Hotline at 800-897-5465 for broader DV support.
resources.name: Draper Police Department Victim Services

resources.description: The EEOC Phoenix District Office handles federal employment-discrimination charge intake for Utah, with online, phone, video, telephone, and in-person intake options.
resources.hours: Phoenix office Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; appointments through the EEOC Public Portal are strongly recommended.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Federal employment discrimination intake and charge filing. People can schedule telephone, video, or in-person intake interviews through the EEOC Public Portal, or call the national intake line for help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The complaint must involve employment discrimination covered by federal EEOC laws and must meet strict filing deadlines. The Phoenix District Office has jurisdiction over Utah.

**Population Served**
Utah workers, including Salt Lake County workers, and federal-sector complainants who need EEOC intake or charge-filing information.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the EEOC Public Portal at https://publicportal.eeoc.gov/ to schedule intake, or call 1-800-669-4000. Deaf or Hard of Hearing callers can use TTY 1-800-669-6820 or ASL video phone 844-234-5122.

**Important Information to Know**
There are strict filing deadlines. The EEOC page recommends scheduling an appointment; walk-ins are screened and appointments receive priority.
resources.name: EEOC Phoenix District Office Federal Employment Discrimination Charge Intake for Utah

Sunday prepared meals through the Chuck Wagon meal site.

resources.address: 195 North 1950 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah DHHS Early Hearing Detection and Intervention oversees newborn hearing screening, diagnosis, and intervention follow-up, and provides guidance for families after missed, failed, or concerning newborn hearing screens.
resources.hours: Office hours not stated on the opened page; call during business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Newborn hearing screening guidance and follow-up pathways, including rescreening after a failed screen, congenital CMV testing guidance when needed, pediatric audiology referral guidance, early intervention connection, and family support resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Relevant for Utah newborns and infants who need hearing screening, rescreening, diagnostic hearing evaluation, or follow-up after a hearing-loss diagnosis. Babies born outside a hospital should be screened before 10 days of age.

**Population Served**
Utah newborns and infants, including Salt Lake County families, who need newborn hearing screening or hearing-follow-up support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Utah EHDI at 801-273-6600 for guidance, especially if a newborn hearing screen was missed, failed, or follow-up is delayed. Families may also work with the baby's pediatrician, hospital, midwife, or pediatric audiologist.

**Important Information to Know**
EHDI is a hearing screening and follow-up pathway, not broad early intervention or general medical care. Time matters: failed second screening may require CMV testing before 21 days of age and diagnostic hearing evaluation before 3 months of age.
resources.name: Early Hearing Detection and Intervention / Newborn Hearing Screening

resources.description: East Millcreek Interfaith Mobile Food Pantry distributes food at Christ United Methodist Church on posted distribution dates. The church page provides English and Spanish instructions, a contact link, and upcoming-date calendar information.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mobile food pantry distribution at Christ United Methodist Church. Food is distributed on published dates until food runs out.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Specific income, document, or residency rules were not confirmed on the opened page. Clients should review the posted policy/procedures file or contact the pantry for requirements.

**Population Served**
People in the East Millcreek and Salt Lake City area who need food pantry support and can attend the scheduled distribution.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the pantry webpage for upcoming dates, then go to 2375 East 3300 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84109. Parking opens at 2:30 PM, and distribution starts at 3:30 PM. Call Christ UMC at 801-486-5473 or use the pantry contact link for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is calendar-based, not a simple weekly pantry. Food is first-come, first-served until supplies run out, so clients should verify the next distribution date before travel.
resources.name: East Millcreek Interfaith Mobile Food Pantry

resources.description: Easterseals-Goodwill Northern Rocky Mountain operates Utah's Senior Community Service Employment Program, providing paid temporary community-service assignments, training and job-search support for eligible low-income adults age 55+.
resources.hours: Call the Utah SCSEP number or use the SCSEP contact form for current appointment, waitlist and enrollment steps.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Senior Community Service Employment Program services, including paid temporary work assignments at nonprofits or government agencies, help overcoming employment barriers, resume and interview support, job-search help, training and employer connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For low-income adults over age 55 in Utah and other ESGW service states. Final eligibility, income rules, waitlist status and host-agency placement depend on SCSEP screening.

**Population Served**
Low-income unemployed older adults age 55 and older in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Utah SCSEP number at 800-771-2153 or submit the contact form on the ESGW SCSEP page. Local directory evidence lists a Salt Lake site at the Department of Workforce Services, 720 S 200 E.

**Important Information to Know**
Assignments are temporary and are meant to build skills and move toward unsubsidized employment. Participation is not guaranteed and depends on eligibility, funding, host sites and openings.
resources.name: Easterseals-Goodwill Senior Community Service Employment Program - Utah
