resources.description: Utah DWS and DCFS Education Training Voucher funding through WIOA Youth can help eligible current or former foster youth with college or technical training tuition, books, mentoring, support services, and job-search help.
resources.hours: DWS employment center hours vary; call or use jobs.utah.gov office locator before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Education Training Voucher funding through WIOA Youth, including up to $5,000 per year for tuition and books for college or technical training, plus mentoring, supportive services such as basic living and transportation help while attending school, skill development, and job-search assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Must be in foster care, have aged out, or have been adopted or entered guardianship after age 16; be under 26; face school or work barriers; have applied to or been accepted by a qualified college, university, or vocational school; complete WIOA Youth or Adult program enrollment; apply for federal financial aid/Pell Grant; and maintain required academic progress. Youth still in foster care may need a DCFS referral form.

**Population Served**
Eligible current and former foster youth in Utah, including Salt Lake County youth and young adults pursuing college, university, or vocational training.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through jobs.utah.gov/career by selecting the service or support, clicking How to Apply and Apply Now, and creating a Utah ID account if needed. A person can also contact the local Workforce Services employment center; Salt Lake area DWS phone is 801-526-0950.

**Important Information to Know**
The flyer is dated 04/22, so funding limits and forms should be confirmed through DWS. It lists $3,000 without a DCFS waiver and up to $5,000 with DCFS approval, for a lifetime maximum of five years through age 26.
resources.name: Education Training Voucher Funds through WIOA Youth

resources.description: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Education for Better Work self-reliance course is a free faith-based education planning course focused on learning habits, education and career goals, job-market understanding, training options, program choice, and paying for education.
resources.hours: Group availability varies by location and online registration; self-study materials are available online.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free self-reliance course focused on education planning, learning principles and habits, self-reliance planning, job-market understanding, training options, choosing a program of study, options to pay for education, presenting a plan, and staying on course. Materials can also be studied independently.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list income or membership restrictions, but the course is explicitly faith-based and groups may depend on local availability. People can register online or ask a local church leader for help finding or starting a group.

**Population Served**
People seeking faith-based support to plan education and career training, including Salt Lake County residents who can join a local or online group when available.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Enroll Now link on the official page to find an online or local group, or use the course manual for self-study if no group is available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an accredited school, financial-aid award, or tuition grant. It is a faith-based planning and peer-learning course, and group availability varies.
resources.name: Education for Better Work Self-Reliance Course

resources.description: The University of Utah Educational Assessment and Student Support Clinic provides affordable child and adolescent evaluations plus individual, group, and intervention services through supervised graduate clinicians.
resources.hours: Flexible scheduling with after-school and weekend appointment efforts; closed over University of Utah observed holidays and winter and summer breaks.
resources.informationText:

Affordable evaluations for children and adolescents, including learning difficulties, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, and related concerns. The clinic also offers individual and group therapy and other intervention services through school-psychology graduate student clinicians supervised by licensed psychologists.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children and adolescents needing assessment or intervention services. Adults over 18 seeking individual counseling are directed to the Utah Community Mental Health Clinic. Families start with a brief screening/initial call.

**Population Served**
Children, adolescents, and families who need educational or mental-health-related assessment, therapy, or intervention support in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-581-6068, email eassc-sp@utah.edu, or use the Schedule an Initial Call route. The clinic is in the Business Classroom Building, Suite 401, 1635 Campus Center Drive, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a graduate training clinic; services are supervised but may run on the academic calendar. Exact fees, wait time, and fit should be confirmed before referral.
resources.name: Educational Assessment and Student Support Clinic (EASSC)

resources.description: Elevate Career Services is listed by the Utah State Office of Rehabilitation as an approved Community Rehabilitation Program provider serving Weber, Davis, and Salt Lake counties for supported employment, with Spanish capacity noted.

Supported-employment services through Utah State Office of Rehabilitation's approved Community Rehabilitation Program network. The USOR directory lists Elevate Career Services as approved for Salt Lake County and notes Spanish capacity.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Likely for people with disabilities who are eligible for vocational rehabilitation or related supported-employment services. USOR or the provider should confirm whether a VR counselor authorization is required before services begin.

People needing disability-related supported employment in Weber, Davis, or Salt Lake County.

Call 385-595-5096 to ask about current intake, service availability, and whether to start through USOR Vocational Rehabilitation. No public street address was confirmed.

resources.name: Elevate Career Services Supported Employment

resources.description: National Elizabeth Dole Foundation and Hidden Heroes caregiver resources for military and veteran caregivers, including peer/community resources and Hope Fund critical financial assistance when available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Elizabeth Dole Foundation supports military and veteran caregivers through Hidden Heroes resources, peer support, caregiver mental-health and wellness resources, advocacy, and the Hope Fund for Critical Financial Assistance. The Hope Fund may help with natural disaster assistance, medical and dental bills, home repairs, emergency transportation, vehicle modifications, home appliances, and loss of income.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs are for military and veteran caregivers and their families. Hope Fund eligibility, application timing, documentation, and funding availability are program-specific and should be checked through Hidden Heroes/Elizabeth Dole Foundation before relying on assistance.

**Population Served**
Military and veteran caregivers and their families nationwide, including Utah caregivers who can use the online resource and application pathways.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the Find Help or Explore Our Resources links on the Elizabeth Dole Foundation website and the Hidden Heroes Hope Fund page. No general public phone number was confirmed on the official page reviewed.

**Important Information to Know**
Financial assistance is not guaranteed and depends on current Hope Fund criteria and available funding. The foundation is primarily caregiver-focused; it is not a general veteran emergency-aid fund for veterans without a caregiver connection.
resources.name: Elizabeth Dole Foundation Hidden Heroes and Hope Fund Caregiver Support

resources.description: Utah Medicaid Employment-related Personal Assistant Services helps working Medicaid members with disabilities pay for personal assistance needed to maintain integrated competitive employment.
resources.hours: Call program coordinator for current availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Self-directed personal assistance for activities of daily living and instrumental activities of daily living directly related to maintaining employment, such as mobility, eating, meal preparation, transferring, toileting, housework, ambulation, hygiene, laundry, dressing, bathing, medication reminders, shopping, and work-related transportation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must have a disability determination by SSA or the State Medical Review Board, currently receive Utah Medicaid, be employed in an integrated community setting at least minimum wage, work at least 40 hours per month or be self-employed, and need personal assistance to maintain employment.

**Population Served**
Working Utah Medicaid members with physical, mental, cognitive, or developmental disabilities, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the EPAS application linked on the program page. For questions, call the EPAS Program Coordinator at 801-538-6955 or write to DHHS Division of Integrated Healthcare, Attn: EPAS Specialist, PO Box 143112, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3112.

**Important Information to Know**
EPAS cannot be used for job coaching, job training, employer ADA accommodations, medical transportation, or tasks outside the authorized care plan. People receiving personal care through certain HCBS waivers may not also receive EPAS.
resources.name: Employment-related Personal Assistant Services (EPAS)

resources.description: Enbridge Gas Utah offers direct account protections and billing options for Utah customers, including deferred payment agreements, Budget Billing, deposit installments, medical-necessity delay, winter shutoff protection, and financial-assistance information.
resources.hours: Customer service: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provider account options and protections for Enbridge Gas Utah customers who are having trouble paying or are at risk of gas service shutoff. Options include credit arrangements such as a Deferred Payment Agreement, Budget Billing, deposit installments, winter shutoff protection for qualifying ratepayers, information about financial assistance, and temporary medical-necessity protection with a physician statement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be an Enbridge Gas customer and meet the conditions for the specific option. Budget Billing depends on account status and usage history; medical protection requires a doctor statement verifying serious illness or infirmity requiring continued natural gas service.

**Population Served**
Enbridge Gas Utah residential customers, including customers in Salt Lake County service areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Enbridge Gas at 1-800-323-5517 as soon as a payment problem, service concern, or medical-necessity issue is expected. For gas smell or suspected leak, use the emergency number 1-800-767-1689.

**Important Information to Know**
These are provider billing arrangements and consumer protections, not grants. Customers remain responsible for gas used, and shutoff notices and deadlines are time-sensitive.
resources.name: Enbridge Gas Utah Deferred Payment, Budget Billing, and Medical/Illness Protections

resources.description: Enbridge Gas Utah's Energy Assistance Credit provides a one-time bill credit per heating season to HEAT-qualified customers who designate part of their HEAT benefit to Enbridge Gas.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
One-time Enbridge Gas Utah bill credit per heating season for HEAT-qualified customers. Utah DWS listed the current credit as $109 on the reviewed page, while utility/regulatory materials note the amount can vary by year.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Customer must qualify for HEAT or an equivalent program and designate at least part of the HEAT benefit to Enbridge Gas Utah. Qualification is for the current heating season and must be renewed to continue assistance.

**Population Served**
HEAT-qualified Enbridge Gas Utah customers, including eligible Salt Lake County customers whose gas account is with Enbridge.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for HEAT through the Salt Lake County HEAT application route, usually Utah Community Action for Salt Lake County, and designate Enbridge Gas when applicable. Enbridge customers can also call 801-359-2444 or ask a HEAT worker about the Energy Assistance Credit.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a credit, not a full arrears-payment program. Customers who receive the credit are not assessed the Energy Assistance charge for 12 months following qualification, according to Enbridge tariff language.
resources.name: Enbridge Gas Utah Energy Assistance Credit

resources.description: REACH is an Enbridge Gas Utah supplemental natural-gas bill credit administered by The Salvation Army for eligible customers who have already been approved for HEAT in the same heating season and meet additional household criteria.
resources.hours: Call The Salvation Army REACH line and leave name and phone number, or use the linked application route on the Enbridge page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supplemental credit on an eligible Enbridge Gas Utah natural-gas bill. The program helps qualifying households keep up with home-heating costs after HEAT approval.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must already be approved for HEAT in the same heating season, have income at or below the current Federal Poverty Level, have an active gas account with a past-due balance, and have a household member who is receiving SSI/SSDI, age 60 or older, under age 5, or a veteran for an added credit.

**Population Served**
Eligible Enbridge Gas Utah residential customers, including Salt Lake County customers, with qualifying household circumstances.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through The Salvation Army link on the Enbridge REACH page or call 801-969-0526 and leave a message with name and phone number.

**Important Information to Know**
Enbridge lists a $350 benefit per eligible applicant and an additional $50 for veterans. REACH supplements HEAT; it does not replace the HEAT application and households may qualify once per calendar year.
resources.name: Enbridge Gas Utah REACH - Residential Energy Assistance through Community Help

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
English Skills Learning Center's Empowering Parents program helps parents, grandparents, and caregivers learn English while learning how to navigate school systems, read report cards, communicate with teachers, participate in PTA, and read with children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adult language learners with a child attending elementary school in Salt Lake County.

**Population Served**
Immigrant, refugee, multilingual, and English-learning parents/caregivers with children in Salt Lake County elementary schools.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the enrollment button on the program page, email info@eslcenter.org, or call 801-328-5608. Classes are held at elementary schools in Granite and Salt Lake School Districts.

**Important Information to Know**
Classes are free and meet twice weekly for 90 minutes. This is school-navigation and parent education for families with elementary-school children, not pregnancy or infant care.
resources.name: English Skills Learning Center Empowering Parents

resources.address: 1270 W 2320 S, Suite F, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: English Skills Learning Center offers free adult English classes across Salt Lake County, with workforce English and career-exploration supports described in funding materials and prior Scout evidence when available.
resources.hours: Class placement, schedules, and locations vary; contact ESLC before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free English classes for adult language learners across Salt Lake County. Workforce English and career-exploration services may be available through ESLC's Upward Mobility work, but the public intake is ESLC's general adult English enrollment rather than a separate employment program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adult English-language learners. Workforce/career services are described for low- to moderate-income adult English-language learners; ESLC should confirm placement, current class location, childcare availability, and enrollment requirements.

**Population Served**
Adult English-language learners in Salt Lake County, including learners seeking workplace English, career exploration, or navigation support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-328-5608, email info@eslcenter.org, or use ESLC's website to ask about enrollment and current class locations. The office is in West Valley City.

**Important Information to Know**
This record should not be treated as job placement. It is best for clients whose employment barrier is English language access or who need workforce-related English instruction.
resources.name: English Skills Learning Center Workforce English and Adult English Classes

resources.description: EnglishConnect is a faith-based English-learning program from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints offering no-cost English conversation groups and online learning options where groups are available.
resources.hours: Groups usually meet weekly or more often for 60-90 minutes; schedules depend on the local or online group found through EnglishConnect/QuickReg.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost English language learning through EnglishConnect 1, 2, and 3 resources, conversation groups, self-paced practice, and participation/completion recognition depending on the level.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to English learners where a local or online group is available. Minors need a signed parental consent form before participation in EnglishConnect groups.

**Population Served**
English learners, including immigrants, refugees, and community members who want to improve English for education, employment, service, or daily life.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the EnglishConnect join/find-a-group or the Church self-reliance course finder to look for a local or online group. If no group is listed, contact local Church leaders or self-reliance leaders about current availability.

**Important Information to Know**
EnglishConnect is provided by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. EnglishConnect 1 and 2 are no cost but are not accredited and do not grant academic degrees or professional certifications; materials and groups include religious principles and faith-based content.
resources.name: EnglishConnect

resources.address: 95 North 300 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Ensign College offers career-focused certificates, associate degrees, and bachelor's degrees in downtown Salt Lake City and online, including programs in trades, IT, and health-related fields.
resources.hours: Admissions and program schedules vary; contact admissions before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career-focused certificates, associate degrees, and bachelor's degrees, including submitted examples such as Electrical-Residential Journeyman, IT, and medical assisting. Some programs may be available online.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must meet Ensign College admissions and program requirements. As a Latter-day Saint-affiliated college, ecclesiastical endorsement and religion course requirements may apply.

**Population Served**
Postsecondary students seeking career-focused certificates or degrees in downtown Salt Lake City or online.

**How to Best Connect**
Call admissions at (801) 524-8145 or the main number at (801) 524-8100, or use the degrees and certificates page to review programs. The campus is at 95 North 300 West, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Tuition rates may differ by church membership or residency status. Confirm accreditation, financial aid, scholarships, program length, UTA pass availability, and requirements for the intended program.
resources.name: Ensign College Career-Focused Certificates and Degrees

resources.address: 9798 S Sunflower Lane, Sandy, UT 84094
resources.description: Entrada Adult High School provides adult high school, GED preparation, English learning, counselor appointments, and tutoring for adult learners in Sandy and southeast Salt Lake County.
resources.hours: Day and evening office hours were submitted; confirm current registration and counseling hours before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult high school completion, GED preparation, English learning classes, counselor appointments, and tutoring support for enrolled students working on classes, packets, or GED preparation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adult-education eligibility, fees, residency or district expectations, and fee-waiver options should be confirmed with Entrada before enrollment.

**Population Served**
Adult learners in Sandy, Canyons District, and southeast Salt Lake County who need high school completion, GED preparation, or English learning.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-826-6670 or use the Entrada website for enrollment steps and counselor appointment information. The school is at 9798 S Sunflower Lane, Sandy.

**Important Information to Know**
Program fees and assistance options can change by semester. Confirm current costs, required documents, orientation steps, and class format before referral.
resources.name: Entrada Adult High School

resources.address: 770 E Main St #438, Lehi, UT 84043
resources.description: Epilepsy Foundation Utah offers support for people and families affected by epilepsy, including virtual support groups, education days, advocacy, and seizure first aid training.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Monthly support groups, education, advocacy, and seizure first aid training. Submitted evidence describes virtual teen, adult, parent, caregiver, and sibling groups and Salt Lake City education days.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people and families affected by epilepsy. Event registration, group schedules, and current local staff contact should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Utahns affected by epilepsy, including people with epilepsy, parents, caregivers, siblings, teens, and adults.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-332-1000 or use the Epilepsy Foundation Utah webpage. The submitted mailing address is 770 E Main St #438, Lehi, UT 84043.

**Important Information to Know**
Some events are date-specific and may require registration. Verify current support-group links before sending a client to a particular meeting.
resources.name: Epilepsy Foundation Utah Monthly Support Groups, Education, and Seizure First Aid Training

resources.address: 451 N LaSalle Street, Chicago, IL 60654
resources.description: Free phone warmline for families struggling with infant crying, sleeping, or feeding; infant specialists provide phone consultation in English and Spanish to callers anywhere.
resources.hours: Warmline answered Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Central Time; after-hours messages are returned the next business day.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Fussy Baby Network offers free phone consultations with infant specialists for caregivers worried about infant crying, sleep, feeding, colic, or caregiver stress.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available by phone to any family caring for a fussy baby. Phone consultations are free and available in English and Spanish.

**Population Served**
Families with infants, including Salt Lake County families who can use phone support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-888-431-2229 or send a message through the website. Calls are answered Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Central Time.

**Important Information to Know**
In-home services are Chicagoland-focused; Salt Lake County fit is the phone consultation route. This is not emergency medical care; urgent feeding, dehydration, weight-gain, or safety concerns should go to a medical provider or emergency service.
resources.name: Erikson Institute Fussy Baby Network Warmline

resources.address: 3712 West 3500 South, West Valley City, UT 84120
resources.description: Express Employment Professionals lists Salt Lake County offices, including West Valley and Cottonwood Heights, where job seekers can search jobs and submit an application for local staffing placements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Staffing-agency job search, application, and placement support through Express Employment Professionals offices in Salt Lake County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements vary by job assignment and employer. Applicants should submit an application, search current openings, or call the nearest office to ask about documentation, background checks, skills, and availability.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in Salt Lake County looking for temporary, temp-to-hire, or direct-hire work through Express.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Express's online Search Jobs or Submit an Application links. For the West Valley office, call 801-255-1441 or visit 3712 West 3500 South, West Valley City. The Cottonwood Heights office is also listed at 7177 South Highland Drive, Suite A, 801-566-5026.

**Important Information to Know**
Openings and placement speed change frequently. A listed office does not guarantee immediate placement or eligibility for every job.
resources.name: Express Employment Professionals Salt Lake County Offices

resources.address: 655 Beach St, San Francisco, CA 94109
resources.description: EyeCare America connects eligible uninsured or underinsured adults with volunteer ophthalmologists for no-cost medical eye exams and limited follow-up care for conditions found during the initial exam.
resources.hours: Call or use the online eligibility tool; volunteer availability depends on ZIP code and program match.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost medical eye exam by an ophthalmologist for eligible adults, with up to one year of care for disease diagnosed during the initial exam when the program match applies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for uninsured and underinsured individuals age 18 and older. Eligibility and volunteer availability are determined through EyeCare America's screening process.

**Population Served**
Adults in the United States, including Salt Lake County residents, who need medical eye care and cannot otherwise access it.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 877-887-6327 or use the EyeCare America website to see if the person qualifies. The program is national and matches by location where a volunteer ophthalmologist is available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is medical eye care, not routine eyeglass help. The submitted evidence notes that refraction exams, eyeglass or contact lens prescriptions, glasses, contacts, procedures, surgeries, anesthesia, medications, injections, diagnostic tests, and facility fees are not covered by the program.
resources.name: EyeCare America

resources.address: 6911 S State Street, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: EyeCare4Kids Midvale Clinic provides affordable vision care for people in need, including eye exams, frames and lenses, contact lenses, and follow-up care, with Medicaid and CHIP accepted.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed Friday-Sunday and listed holidays/holiday weeks.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable vision care, including eye exams, frames and lenses, contact lenses, and follow-up care at the Midvale clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
EyeCare4Kids states it provides affordable vision care for those in need and accepts Medicaid and CHIP. Bring photo ID for adults, an insurance card if available, current glasses if worn, and a parent or guardian for anyone under 18.

**Population Served**
Children and adults needing affordable vision care in Salt Lake County and Utah, with an emphasis on families and people in need.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-255-8525 or book online through the Utah clinic page. The Midvale clinic is at 6911 S State Street.

**Important Information to Know**
Insurance is not required, but exact out-of-pocket cost and appointment availability should be confirmed when booking. English and Spanish are listed for Utah clinics.
resources.name: EyeCare4Kids Midvale Clinic

resources.address: 3188 South 1100 West, South Salt Lake, UT 84119
resources.description: The FIGS Community Fridge at Wasatch Community Gardens' Farm Incubator Group Site is managed by Salt Lake Mutual Aid and provides free refrigerated and pantry items for anyone who may need them.
resources.hours: No hours or stocking schedule posted on the opened page; availability is variable.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-barrier community fridge with free refrigerated and pantry items.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Wasatch Community Gardens states the fridge provides free access to items for anyone who may need them. No ID, income, or residency requirement is posted on the opened page.

**Population Served**
People in South Salt Lake and nearby Salt Lake County communities who can reach the FIGS site.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Farm Incubator Group Site at 3188 S 1100 W in South Salt Lake and look for the community fridge. The page does not list a phone, hours, or stocking schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
Community fridge inventory is variable and may be empty between restocks. This is useful as a low-barrier supplemental option, not a guaranteed food box appointment.
resources.name: FIGS Community Fridge

resources.address: 1300 W 300 N, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Fairpark Family Learning Center offers free adult digital literacy classes, computer access, internet and office software support, job-search help, scanning, printing, and related adult learning workshops.
resources.hours: Public flyer listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-8:00 PM; confirm current hours before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free computer access, technical support, job-search help, scanning, printing, and adult digital literacy classes. Posted digital literacy topics include basic computer skills, internet basics, email, Windows 10/11, Mac OS, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Google Docs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to community members using the learning center. Posted rules say youth under 16 must be with a parent or guardian and youth 16 or older need a signed waiver from a parent or guardian.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City west-side community members and families who need computer access or adult digital literacy support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-1333, email FairparkFamilyLearningCenter@slc.gov, or visit 1300 W 300 N. The public flyer says the entrance is on the southeast side of the Northwest Community Center building.

**Important Information to Know**
The registration form and flyers are dated 2024-2026; confirm the current class calendar and whether the center is operating at the posted address before referral.
resources.name: Fairpark Family Learning Center Digital Literacy for Adults

resources.address: 1388 S Navajo St, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; 2500 S State St Suite 404, South Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Family Dental Care is an affordable family dental provider serving Salt Lake City and South Salt Lake, including the Glendale location, with Spanish-speaking access, online booking, flexible pricing, and general/restorative dental services.
resources.hours: South Salt Lake listed Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Glendale listed every other Friday 9:00 AM-12:30 PM; by appointment only. Confirm current site schedule when booking.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family dentistry, routine cleaning, restorative treatment such as implants and crowns, and appointment-based dental care at Salt Lake City/Glendale and South Salt Lake locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No formal income eligibility or charity policy is posted on the provider site. The provider describes itself as affordable and offering transparent pricing and flexible options.

**Population Served**
Families and individuals in Salt Lake City, South Salt Lake, and Glendale/Mountain View Community Learning Center areas who need dental care and can schedule with the provider.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-646-4748, email gtifamilydentalcare@gmail.com, or use the Book Now link. The Glendale/Salt Lake location is 1388 S Navajo St, and the South Salt Lake office is 2500 S State St Suite 404.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider site does not document a sliding-fee or free-care policy. Confirm fees, payment options, emergency availability, and the correct location schedule before sending a client.
resources.name: Family Dental Care Glendale and South Salt Lake Dental Appointments

resources.address: 814 W 800 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Family Promise Salt Lake helps families with children experiencing homelessness request services through a public form and provides a family-specific emergency shelter and stabilization pathway.
resources.hours: Request services online anytime; call to confirm current response timing, shelter capacity, and appointment needs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family homelessness services, including service-request screening, emergency shelter or shelter coordination, case management, stabilization support, and connection to community resources for families with children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Family Promise states it can only offer support to families, defined as at least one parent and one dependent child. The public request page says rental-assistance applications are not currently being accepted.

**Population Served**
Families with at least one parent and one dependent child who are experiencing homelessness or serious housing instability in the Salt Lake area.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Request Services form on the Family Promise Salt Lake website or call 801-961-8622. The site says someone from the organization will contact the family after the form is submitted.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general adult shelter and shelter capacity is not guaranteed. The public page specifically says rental-assistance applications are not currently being accepted.
resources.name: Family Promise Salt Lake Emergency Shelter and Transitional Housing

resources.description: Fathers and Families Coalition of Utah's Jobs Work Program provides workforce-readiness workshops, mentoring, stipends, food-handler permit support, and paid work opportunities for youth, typically ages 14-24.
resources.hours: Workshops have historically been offered through partner schools and summer library locations such as Glendale, Granite, and Kearns; confirm current schedule before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Job-readiness workshops, resume creation, interview coaching, mentorship, financial literacy when available, stipends for workshop attendance, food-handler permit support, and paid work opportunities through Good Start food enterprises after completing required workshops.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for youth, typically ages 14-24. The official page says there are no enrollment limits based on financial standing or educational background, but current cohorts and partner locations should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Youth and young adults in Salt Lake County and regional partner communities who need early work experience and employment-readiness support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Jobs Work Program landing page or Sign Up for a Program link, or email information@ffcutah.org to ask about current workshops, locations, and paid work steps.

**Important Information to Know**
Paid work is not immediate for everyone; students generally complete workshops first and then may apply for food-handler permitting and public-event work opportunities.
resources.name: Fathers and Families Coalition of Utah Jobs Work Program

resources.address: 895 N 900 E, American Fork, UT 84003
resources.description: Featherstone Ridge Dental Clinic provides no-charge dental care for qualifying Utahns with intellectual or developmental disabilities who cannot access quality dental care elsewhere, including exams, cleanings, x-rays, fillings, limited root canals, extractions, stainless-steel crowns, IV sedation or general anesthesia when needed, and referrals to specialists.
resources.hours: Hours are not posted publicly; call the clinic before travel or referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Dental care for qualifying people with intellectual or developmental disabilities, including oral exams, diagnosis and treatment planning, x-rays, professional cleanings, fillings, limited crown/bridge work, limited root canals, gingivoplasty, extractions, soft-tissue oral surgery, biopsy referral, general anesthesia or IV sedation when needed, consultation with family members, and referral to community dental specialists when needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic is for Utah residents with disabilities who meet the clinic criteria, including eligibility for Division of Services for People with Disabilities services, full-time Utah residency, lack of available private-practitioner services, and a dental need the clinic provides. Current web text says the clinic is available for people who receive DSPD services and live in community group homes or private homes; call to confirm whether active DSPD service enrollment or DSPD eligibility is required.

**Population Served**
Utah residents with intellectual and developmental disabilities who cannot access quality dental care elsewhere, including people living in community group homes or private homes.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-763-4164 to ask for the Request for Services packet and current intake instructions. Application materials and medical/dental records are reviewed by clinic staff before a visit is approved and scheduled. Packets may be returned by fax to 801-763-7219 or email to frdp@utah.gov. The clinic is at 895 N 900 E in American Fork.

**Important Information to Know**
The clinic states that patients and providers are not charged for these services because of legislative funding. Approval is not automatic; staff review the application, records, dental need, and fit with clinic services before scheduling. If anesthesia is needed, physician-completed forms and guardian signatures may be required before the dental appointment.
resources.name: Featherstone Ridge Dental Clinic

resources.address: A. Ray Olpin Student Union basement, University of Utah, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: Feed U Pantry is the University of Utah campus food pantry for current students, staff, and faculty with an active uNID and valid U Card. Users self-report meeting federal poverty income guidelines because the pantry partners with Utah Food Bank.
resources.hours: Fall 2026 posted hours: Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-6:00 PM; Friday 1:00 PM-6:00 PM
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost campus pantry groceries and food support through the University of Utah Basic Needs Collective.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requires an active University of Utah uNID and valid U Card. Users self-report meeting federal poverty income guidelines as a Utah Food Bank partner pantry.

**Population Served**
University of Utah students, staff, and faculty who have active campus credentials and need food support.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit the Feed U Pantry in the A. Ray Olpin Student Union basement during posted hours. Fall 2026 hours are listed as Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-6:00 PM and Friday 1:00 PM-6:00 PM; check for holiday or satellite-pantry changes.

**Important Information to Know**
This pantry is campus-affiliated and is not open to the general public. A valid U Card/uNID is required.
resources.name: Feed U Pantry

resources.address: 7588 Union Park Ave Ste. 200, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: Fight Against Domestic Violence offers Utah domestic-violence survivor support through funding-gap programs such as Housing First, Flex Fund, and Crisis Cash, plus resource routing to LINKLine and local domestic violence providers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial and housing-related survivor support programs. FADV describes Housing First flexible housing assistance for domestic violence victims, Flex Fund help up to $1,000 for survivors working with advocates or case managers, and Crisis Cash grants to service providers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Program eligibility, current funding, and whether a survivor must work through an advocate or case manager must be confirmed with FADV. The Get Help page also routes Utah survivors to LINKLine and local domestic violence service providers.

**Population Served**
Domestic violence survivors in Utah, including Salt Lake County survivors, and domestic violence service providers assisting survivors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-210-0218 or email info@fadv.org. For immediate help finding DV services, the Get Help page points Utah residents to LINKLine at 800-897-5465 and local DV providers.

**Important Information to Know**
FADV is not a crisis shelter or 24/7 hotline. Some financial help may be routed through advocates, case managers, or providers rather than a direct public application.
resources.name: Fight Against Domestic Violence Survivor Resources and Financial Support

resources.address: 500 W 300 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Fill the Pot Ministry describes daily outreach in downtown Salt Lake City offering food, clothing, hygiene supplies, warm clothing, companionship, and partner connections to housing, health care, and recovery resources. Public client access details are not clear enough for routine referral yet.
resources.hours: Client outreach times and locations were not confirmed. The website lists volunteer-facing Sunday service 8:00 AM-12:00 PM and states walk-ins are not accepted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Homeless outreach in downtown Salt Lake City with meals, clothing, hygiene supplies, seasonal winter gear, companionship, and partner connections to housing, health care, and recovery resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public language describes service to unsheltered and less-fortunate neighbors. Specific client eligibility, service boundaries, and whether someone can request outreach directly were not confirmed.

**Population Served**
Unsheltered and less-fortunate neighbors in downtown Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-513-0163 before relying on this as a client referral. Do not send someone to the listed address without confirmation; the website says walk-ins are not accepted and much of the schedule information is volunteer-facing.

**Important Information to Know**
This lead needs administrator follow-up. The public website supports the outreach service but does not provide a clear client-facing schedule, distribution location, or intake sequence.
resources.name: Fill the Pot Ministry Downtown Homeless Outreach
resources.resolutionReason: Keep as needs-resolution only; do not make it a routine referral until a client-facing access route and schedule are verified.; Service identity and general downtown outreach scope are supported, but the practical client access route remains unresolved because the website says walk-ins are not accepted and does not publish where or when clients can receive services.

resources.address: 4445 W 5175 S, Kearns, UT 84118
resources.description: First Baptist Church of Kearns is listed by Utahns Against Hunger as a Kearns emergency food pantry. Other public food-resource pages describe it as a free pantry for people in need, with proof-of-address and household ID requirements.
resources.hours: Hours not confirmed in opened current sources; call before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food pantry groceries for people in need.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public health-resource listings state that proof of address and ID for everyone in the household may be required. Call to confirm current requirements.

**Population Served**
People in Kearns and nearby Salt Lake County who need pantry food and can reach the church.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-529-9402 before going to 4445 W 5175 S, Kearns, UT 84118. Some public listings show older or alternate phone numbers, so verify the current line if the call fails.

**Important Information to Know**
The church page could not be opened because of a redirect issue during research. Use current public food-resource lists and phone confirmation before referral.
resources.name: First Baptist Church of Kearns Food Pantry

resources.description: First Choice Imaging's self-referral program lets patients schedule qualifying non-contrast MRI scans at the Sandy location without a provider order, using an upfront self-pay price.
resources.hours: Call or message the clinic to confirm price and schedule; self-referral starts through the online self-referral form.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Self-referral non-contrast MRI scans, including the exam, radiologist report, and image access, without waiting for a provider order or insurance authorization.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Only non-contrast MRI qualifies for self-referral. Contrast MRI and other imaging such as CT, X-ray, ultrasound, DEXA, and arthrogram require a provider order.

**Population Served**
Patients who can travel to the Sandy/Salt Lake City imaging location and can pay the self-pay MRI fee.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the self-referral link on the First Choice Imaging page or call the Sandy location at 801-576-1290. The Sandy location is 9844 S 1300 E #175.

**Important Information to Know**
The posted standard non-contrast MRI self-pay price is $299. Insurance cannot be billed for a self-referral MRI because insurers require a provider order. This is diagnostic imaging access, not free care or clinical treatment.
resources.name: First Choice Imaging Self-Referral Non-Contrast MRI

resources.address: 440 S 500 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: First Step House's REACH program combines behavioral-health treatment, housing, case management, employment readiness, job placement, outpatient step-down care, psychiatric support, and peer recovery for men leaving jail or prison who have substance-use disorders and high risk of returning to jail.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
REACH provides residential treatment with integrated substance-use and mental-health care, housing support, case management, employment readiness, job placement, outpatient step-down therapy, psychiatric support, and peer recovery.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is designed for men leaving jail or prison who have substance-use disorders and are at high risk of returning to jail. Admission depends on assessment, program fit, funding, and bed availability.

**Population Served**
Men returning to the Salt Lake County community from jail or prison with substance-use and reentry-stability needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call First Step House at 801-359-8862 and ask about REACH reentry admissions. The provider lists its Salt Lake City contact address as 440 S 500 E.

**Important Information to Know**
REACH is reentry-specific but does not guarantee immediate admission or housing. Confirm wait time, funding source, documentation, and whether a criminal-justice or treatment referral is helpful for the client's situation.
resources.name: First Step House REACH Reentry & Recovery Support Program

resources.address: 440 S 500 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: First Step House provides men’s residential and outpatient treatment for substance-use disorder, serving men with moderate to high risk of criminal behavior; self-referrals are accepted, though most admissions are referral-based.
resources.hours: Admissions staff can answer questions at 434 S 500 E between 8:00 AM and 3:00 PM Monday-Friday; main contact listed at 440 S 500 E.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Men’s residential and outpatient treatment for substance-use disorder, with residential, outpatient, long-term recovery, veterans, and reentry-related supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program primarily serves men with substance-use disorders at moderate to high risk of criminal behavior; a criminal record is not required. Most admissions are referral-based, but self-referrals are accepted. Walk-in assessments are not available.

**Population Served**
Adult men in Salt Lake County with substance-use disorders, including men with justice-system, veterans, homelessness, or reentry-related needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-359-8862. Admissions questions can be directed to staff at 434 S 500 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102, Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM. The general address listed by the provider is 440 S 500 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102.

**Important Information to Know**
Typical residential bed wait is listed as 2-4 weeks, and ARS availability changes frequently. Funding may include Medicaid, Salt Lake County Behavioral Health, Medicare, VA, sliding-scale fees, private pay, or outside support; verify current funding and availability before referral.
resources.name: First Step House Treatment Admissions

resources.address: 720 Valdez Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
resources.description: Veteran-specific transitional housing at Valor House on the Salt Lake City VA Medical Campus, with private units, meals, treatment, case management, employment/benefits navigation, and recovery support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Valor House provides veterans transitional housing with 72 private units with private bathrooms, shared kitchens, gym, laundry, two daily meals, therapy, substance-use treatment, medication management, intensive case management, employment and benefits navigation, legal and financial support, peer support, and a VA liaison. Program tracks include a 90-day bridge, 9-month service intensive, and 2-year clinical/special needs track.

**Eligibility Requirements**
First Step House lists eligibility as veterans of all discharge statuses who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, have no active substance use, disclose and manage psychiatric or legal issues, and have no violent convictions. Admission depends on fit, referral/admissions process, documentation, and bed availability.

**Population Served**
Veterans experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness who need transitional housing and integrated behavioral health or recovery support in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility is based on the military scholarship track and qualifying service-member relationship. Applicants must use the online portal and submit required documentation there. Applicants must reapply each year they want funds.

**Population Served**
Spouses and children in military families, including Salt Lake County families, who meet Folds of Honor's military scholarship requirements.

Apply through the Folds of Honor online scholarship portal during the annual application window. Documentation is not accepted by mail, fax, email, or phone. Award notifications are sent in mid-July, and awards are paid to schools rather than directly to recipients. Check the current eligibility downloads before applying.

Forcibly displaced women in the Salt Lake area, including refugee and asylum-seeking women, and eligible American-born daughters age 25 and under for the scholarship.

resources.hours: Online application only; FAQ says applicants should not call about receiving a vehicle.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
National free vehicle request program. Charity Cars awards donated program vehicles to selected eligible applicants and nonprofit organizations; applicants create an account and complete an online vehicle request.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be U.S. residents, age 18 or older, have a valid driver's license, be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, have a genuine need because they lack sustainable transportation, have computer/internet access, complete the online application, promote the charity to help generate donations, and be able to pay tag, title, emissions, insurance, maintenance, and upkeep if selected.

**Population Served**
U.S. residents without sustainable transportation, including working poor families, domestic violence survivors, medically needy people, disaster survivors, families moving from public assistance to work, families in transitional living shelters, military families, and some nonprofits.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Free Charity Cars vehicle request process after reviewing the FAQ. The FAQ states applicants must use the online process and should not call the office about receiving a vehicle.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no guarantee of a vehicle and there may be an extensive wait. The program does not provide repair money for a vehicle the applicant already has. Applications are deleted after three months, and applicants may need to reapply.
resources.name: Free Charity Cars Vehicle Request Application

The page is for CNA Program 2026. Cohort dates, total costs beyond the refundable deposit, and future availability should be confirmed before relying on a start date.

Discounted GreenBike bike-share access. The Go Pass provides a $5 annual pass with unlimited 1-hour bike rides for 365 days when bikes are checked into a station within the time limit.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The Go Pass is listed for Utah residents with household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines, people receiving food assistance such as SNAP, WIC, or TANF, and clients of Go Pass partner organizations.

**Population Served**

Low-income Utah residents and people receiving listed public benefits who can safely use GreenBike stations and bikes in the Salt Lake City/Ogden bike-share service area.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the Go Pass request page, call or text 801-333-1110, or email info@greenbikeslc.org. GreenBike's listed office is 150 S State Street, Suite 300, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**

Bike share is useful only where stations and bikes are available and is not accessible door-to-door transportation. Riders must follow program rules, dock bikes on time, and confirm current Go Pass payment or promo-code steps before enrolling.
resources.name: GreenBike Utah Go Pass

National phone and online clients, including Salt Lake County residents who can use remote counseling.

Walk-in adult mental-health crisis assessment, immediate stabilization, supportive care, case management, connection to inpatient or outpatient services, peer support, and medication or medication-assisted treatment options when clinically appropriate.

For adults ages 18 and older experiencing mental-health crisis. Anyone can walk in for psychiatric crisis care. Other outpatient or inpatient services use standard insurance and patient billing models.

Adults in Salt Lake County and surrounding areas experiencing emergency mental-health conditions, including suicidal thoughts, psychosis, depression, anxiety, PTSD, bipolar disorder, substance-use disorders, or other psychiatric crises.

Structured day treatment for older adults, including group therapy, emotional regulation and coping skills, relaxation, aging education, creative activities, yoga, meditation, exercise, geriatric psychiatry oversight and medication management.

For adults age 50+ who need focused mental health support, such as people stepping down from inpatient hospitalization, at risk for hospitalization or not improving with less intensive treatment. Adults age 50 and older in the Salt Lake County area needing specialized older-adult mental health day treatment.

Call 801-587-8007 to ask whether the program is a fit and to enroll. The program is at the HMHI Crisis Care Center, 955 W 3300 S, South Salt Lake.

Pregnant, postpartum, trying-to-conceive, adopting, pregnancy-loss, infertility, NICU, and reproductive-journey clients in Utah who need specialized maternal/perinatal mental-health support.

Immediate walk-in youth crisis assessment by licensed mental-health professionals, supportive counseling, de-escalation, short-term stabilization for up to 23 hours, medication for symptom relief when needed, family-involved care planning, and referral coordination for follow-up outpatient, inpatient, or community services.

For children and teens ages 5-17, or 18 if still in high school, experiencing acute mental-health crisis or needing same-day mental-health care. No referral and no appointment are required.

Youth and families in Salt Lake County who need immediate mental-health crisis support for concerns such as suicidal thoughts, depression, anxiety, trauma, self-harm, family conflict, school stress, or overwhelming behavioral concerns.

Walk in to 501 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, or call HMHI at 801-583-2500 with questions. For life-threatening emergencies, call 911; for crisis guidance before going, call or text 988.

The program is short-term crisis stabilization and connection to next care, not ongoing outpatient therapy. Billing/cost details should be confirmed with HMHI, especially for services beyond initial stabilization.
resources.name: HMHI Youth Crisis Care Program

Critical home repairs that can include plumbing and electrical hazards, roof leaks, weatherproofing, structural and safety issues, accessibility upgrades, and water heater, furnace, or A/C repairs. Low- to moderate-income homeowners in Salt Lake, Davis, and Tooele counties who need critical repairs to remain safely housed.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Salt Lake Area Critical Home Repair Program

Transitioning service members, veterans, and military-connected job seekers interested in construction, skilled trades, registered apprenticeships, or related career pathways, including Salt Lake County residents who can search Utah opportunities online.

Create an account through the Sign Up and Get Going/Create Resume links at careers.helmetstohardhats.org, then search jobs or training by city and state. Use the platform's contact link for site questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Helmets to Hardhats is a matching and search platform, not a guarantee of apprenticeship placement or employment. Costs, union requirements, apprenticeship tests, travel, and openings vary by local program and employer.
resources.name: Helmets to Hardhats Veterans Apprenticeship and Skilled Trades Career Matching

resources.address: 5355 W Herriman Main Street, Herriman, UT 84096
resources.description: Herriman Police Department is listed by Utah Safe at Home as a Salt Lake County Certified Program Assistant for address-confidentiality applications for people threatened by domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, abuse, or human trafficking.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Certified Program Assistant access for Utah Safe at Home, the address confidentiality program. A certified assistant completes and submits the application with a victim; Safe at Home does not accept direct self-submitted applications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Safe at Home eligibility includes being a victim of, or threatened by, abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, or human trafficking; living in Utah; having moved recently, moving soon, or living at an address unknown to the person feared; and working with a Certified Program Assistant.

**Population Served**
Utah survivors who need address confidentiality, including Salt Lake County survivors who can contact the Herriman Police Department certified assistant.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Herriman Police Department's listed Safe at Home Program Assistant contact at 801-727-0945. The listed address is 5355 W Herriman Main Street, Herriman.

**Important Information to Know**
Safe at Home cannot accept applications directly from individuals; working with a Certified Program Assistant is required. This listing is for address confidentiality enrollment help, not shelter or general domestic-violence advocacy.
resources.name: Herriman Police Department Safe at Home Certified Program Assistant

**Services Offered**
Inpatient drug and alcohol rehab, detoxification, and treatment for co-occurring substance-use and mental-health issues. The program includes psychiatric evaluation and medication when needed during treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility, age-program fit, detox appropriateness, insurance, and admission route must be confirmed directly with admissions.

**Population Served**
Adolescents, adults, and older adults in Midvale and Salt Lake County who need inpatient, detoxification, or psychiatric-hospital-based substance-use care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the official number listed on the provider page, (888) 925-9146. The hospital is at 7309 S 180 W, Midvale, UT 84047.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted phone number differed from the official page opened during research; use the official listed admissions number unless the office confirms otherwise. This is hospital-based care, so level of care and payer authorization may matter.
resources.name: Highland Ridge Hospital Drug and Alcohol Rehab

**Services Offered**
Behavioral-health services with addiction listed among treatment areas. Utah DHHS material supports general outpatient SUD treatment, dual diagnosis, telehealth, and psychiatric medication management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients should complete the scheduling form or call to confirm addiction-specific intake, location, insurance, and whether outpatient SUD care is currently available.

**Population Served**
People in Holladay, Riverton, and Salt Lake County needing outpatient behavioral-health care with addiction or co-occurring concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
For the Holladay clinic, call 801-273-6335 at 4460 S Highland Dr, Suite 100, Salt Lake City, UT 84124. For Riverton, call 801-727-8744. The website also offers a scheduling form.

The official site is broad behavioral health and does not give detailed public SUD program information. Ask specifically about current SUD services and which location provides them.
resources.name: Highland Springs Specialty Clinic

resources.description: Hilarity for Charity's Caregiver Respite Program provides competitive respite grants for unpaid caregivers of people professionally diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia who live at home with the caregiver.
resources.hours: Online applications; application review and award timing depend on the program cycle and provider coordination.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Respite grants that cover professional in-home care or adult day center care. Award types listed include 100 hours of in-home respite care or 24 days of adult day center respite, with care used within the program's stated time limits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The caregiver must care for someone professionally diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia, the person receiving care must live at home with the caregiver, the caregiver must be facing financial and emotional hardship, and the caregiver must reside in the United States or Canada. Puerto Rico and other U.S. territories are excluded by the program page.

**Population Served**
Unpaid dementia caregivers in the United States and Canada, including Utah caregivers when professional in-home or adult day center care can be coordinated locally.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the HFC Caregiver Respite Program online application. For general contact, use info@wearehfc.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Awards are not cash and are not guaranteed. HFC coordinates in-home care through its preferred provider, and the grant can become void if licensed care cannot be provided within the stated timeframe.
resources.name: Hilarity for Charity Caregiver Respite Program

resources.address: 231 E 100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Hildegarde's Food Pantry at the Cathedral Church of St. Mark is a choice-style pantry in downtown Salt Lake City. The pantry serves customers several days each week and requires identification for household members.
resources.hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday 11:00 AM-1:30 PM; Thursday 5:00 PM-6:30 PM. Customers must be in line 15 minutes before closing, and the pantry may close early if the lobby is full.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Choice-style food pantry with food and personal care items selected by guests from pantry shelves, depending on supply.

**Eligibility Requirements**
One visit per household per week. Identification is required for all household members on every visit; adult ID must be a current picture ID, and children's ID can include documents such as a Social Security card, Medicaid card, passport, school ID, or document showing relationship to parents.

**Population Served**
Utah residents and households needing food assistance who can reach the downtown Salt Lake City pantry.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 231 E 100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111 during posted customer hours. Call 801-328-2303 or email hildegardes@stmarksutah.org with questions. Arrive at least 15 minutes before closing.

**Important Information to Know**
Copies of ID are accepted according to the pantry page. Bring reusable bags if possible. The pantry may close earlier than posted if the lobby is full.
resources.name: Hildegarde's Food Pantry

resources.address: Building 546, Hill AFB, UT 84056
resources.description: Hill Air Force Base Family Advocacy and the Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate Hotline provide domestic-abuse support for active-duty members and military families, including reporting-options support, crisis intervention, safety planning, court/medical accompaniment, counseling, and referrals.
resources.hours: Family Advocacy Clinic: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 7:30 AM-4:30 PM; Wednesday 9:30 AM-4:30 PM. DAVA hotline available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family maltreatment prevention and treatment, counseling and referral resources, and Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate hotline support. DAVA can discuss reporting options and provide 24/7 crisis intervention, safety planning, in-person support at court or medical appointments, and other information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Family Advocacy Clinic is for preventing and treating family maltreatment involving active-duty members and their families. Call to confirm eligibility for military-connected household members.

**Population Served**
Active-duty members and military families connected to Hill Air Force Base, including eligible Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Family Advocacy at 801-777-3497. For domestic abuse victim advocate support, call the DAVA hotline at 385-209-1811, available 24/7.

**Important Information to Know**
This is limited to military-connected clients. Base access, TRICARE/military eligibility, and reporting options should be discussed before referral.
resources.name: Hill Air Force Base Family Advocacy Program / Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate Hotline

resources.description: Free national personalized career support for transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses, including resume help, interview preparation, one-on-one coaching, job resources, hiring events, and job board access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hire Heroes USA provides free personalized one-on-one career support for transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses. Services include career guidance, professional resume reviews, interview preparation, personalized career coaching, job board access, hiring events, training-partner referrals, and job-search resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are intended for transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses. Applicants register through the online portal and are connected with services based on fit and availability.

**Population Served**
Transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents who can use remote services.

**How to Best Connect**
Register through the Hire Heroes USA online portal using the Register for Services/Start Your Journey link. Returning clients can use the client login. Services are remote and national.

**Important Information to Know**
Hire Heroes USA is not a guaranteed job placement service. It offers free career coaching and tools; timing may depend on registration review and staff capacity.
resources.name: Hire Heroes USA Career Coaching and Job Search Services

resources.address: 1628 W 700 N Ste. A4, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: HireQuest Direct lists a Salt Lake City office and online job access for on-demand staffing and local temporary work.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
On-demand staffing and job access through HireQuest Direct, including online Find a Job access and a local Salt Lake City branch.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements vary by assignment. Applicants should ask the branch about accepted identification, onboarding, work authorization, background restrictions, pay timing, and current industries before planning on same-day work.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in Salt Lake City looking for temporary, on-demand, or short-term staffing work.

**How to Best Connect**
Use HireQuest Direct's Find a Job link or visit/contact the Salt Lake City office at 1628 W 700 N Ste. A4. The submitted branch phone is 801-521-9675.

**Important Information to Know**
The locations page verifies the Salt Lake City branch but does not list detailed local dispatch practices. Confirm branch process before sending a client for same-day work.
resources.name: HireQuest Direct Salt Lake City Staffing Branch

resources.description: Hiring Our Heroes career services for the military community, including Career Connectors, hiring events, workshops, professional networking, and fellowships/SkillBridge pathways for eligible transitioning service members and military spouses.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hiring Our Heroes offers career services that connect military-community job seekers with employers. Services include Career Connectors, career counseling, hiring events, workshops, career development intensives, professional networking, fellowships, industry-focused internships, professional development, and certificate opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by program. Corporate Fellowships are a DoD SkillBridge program for active-duty transitioning service members within 180 days of transition who meet education and experience requirements and receive command approval. Other career services, events, and Career Connectors serve veterans, transitioning service members, and military spouses more broadly.

**Population Served**
Veterans, transitioning service members, military spouses, and military-connected job seekers nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents who can use virtual events, Career Connectors, and remote resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the Career Services page and Contact the Career Connectors link for individualized guidance. Eligible fellowship candidates can use the Fellowship Programs Application. Check each program for remote, local, or employer-specific requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
Fellowship eligibility can be narrow and may require SkillBridge timing, command approval, and host-company availability. Veterans who are no longer eligible for fellowships may still use Hiring Our Heroes hiring events, workshops, webinars, and Career Connector support.
resources.name: Hiring Our Heroes Career Services and Fellowships

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive support for people from polygamous cultures, including safety and stability resources, basic-needs support, case management, therapy services, life skills, community referrals, and a direct help line.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The organization focuses on people in or from polygamous culture who need support becoming independent and self-sufficient. Call or email to discuss needs, eligibility, and current service availability.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in or from polygamous communities, primarily in Utah and the Salt Lake area, including people experiencing abuse, isolation, or safety/stability barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-548-3492 or email help@holdingouthelp.org. Hotline hours are Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM Mountain Time.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a 24/7 emergency domestic violence shelter hotline. Confirm emergency housing availability before presenting it as a shelter placement route.
resources.name: Holding Out HELP Client Support Services / Help Hotline

**Services Offered**
Counseling for victims of crime from underserved communities, including individual therapy, family therapy, psychoeducation group therapy, and a domestic violence support group. Services are available in English and Spanish, in person and through phone or video platforms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program focuses on victims of crime from underserved communities; most clients have experienced domestic violence, assault, human trafficking, or other crimes. Call the listed appointment contact to confirm availability and fit.

**Population Served**
Underserved victims of crime in the Salt Lake City area, especially English- and Spanish-speaking people affected by domestic violence, assault, trafficking, or similar trauma.

**How to Best Connect**
To schedule an appointment, contact Rodrigo Coloma at 385-257-2441. The main Holy Cross Ministries number is 801-261-3440, and the office is at 860 East 4500 South, Suite 204.

**Important Information to Know**
Holy Cross describes the services as low-cost, not universally free. Counseling is distinct from the agency's immigration legal program.
resources.name: Holy Cross Ministries Counseling Program

resources.description: Holy Cross Ministries provides low-cost or no-cost immigration legal consultations and services in Salt Lake City for immigrant families, including DACA, humanitarian parole, TPS, trafficking and crime-victim matters, family reunification, citizenship and naturalization.
resources.hours: By appointment only; telephone and virtual appointments are available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost or no-cost immigration legal consultations and services, including DACA, humanitarian parole, Temporary Protected Status, victims of human trafficking and other crimes, family reunification, citizenship and naturalization.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For immigrants and families whose case fits the program's immigration legal-service areas. Fees, no-cost eligibility, appointment availability and case acceptance should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Immigrant families in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents, survivors of violence, people seeking humanitarian or temporary status, families seeking reunification and people pursuing citizenship.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-261-3440 to schedule an appointment. If the line is busy, leave name, phone number and reason for the call. Services are by appointment at 860 East 4500 South, Suite 204, Salt Lake City, with telephone and virtual appointments also available.

**Important Information to Know**
HCM also participates in the Utah Immigration Collaborative helpline at 801-382-9027, live Monday-Thursday during regular business hours. Capacity and fees can change.
resources.name: Holy Cross Ministries Legal Immigration Program
