resources.description: Holy Cross Ministries Promotor/a Outreach Program provides bilingual, bicultural health outreach, case management, health access help, referrals, translation services, support groups, and prenatal health classes for under-insured families in Utah.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Bilingual, bicultural Promotor/a health outreach, including case management, support groups, health access help, referrals, translation services, and regular prenatal health classes. Holy Cross Ministries also offers counseling through a separate program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The health outreach program is described as serving under-insured families living in Utah and working through community and low-income clinics. Call to confirm current intake, language support, and fit for the client's health navigation need.

**Population Served**
Underserved and under-insured families in Utah, including Spanish-speaking and bilingual families in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Holy Cross Ministries at 801-261-3440 or use the appointment/contact option on the website. The Salt Lake City office is at 860 E 4500 S, Suite 204.

**Important Information to Know**
This is health outreach and navigation, not a medical clinic. No one is turned away from Holy Cross Ministries because they cannot afford services, but specific classes, partner-clinic services, and case-management availability should be confirmed.
resources.name: Holy Cross Ministries Promotor/a Health Outreach and Case Management

resources.address: 428 W. 300 S., Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: A Tall Order Foundation's HomeInn program offers low-cost transitional single-room occupancy housing in the Salt Lake City area for people working toward stability after homelessness.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost transitional housing through HomeInn single-room occupancies in the Salt Lake City area. The program describes 80 low-cost rooms, utilities included, and a bridge toward saving money and moving into more stable housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site says guests must qualify for housing and follow program rules. Exact screening criteria, vacancies, identification requirements, guest policies, and move-in timing must be confirmed with the outreach office.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or major housing barriers in the Salt Lake City area who can pay program rent and participate in a self-reliance-oriented transitional housing setting.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact or visit the Homeless Outreach Office at 428 W. 300 S., Salt Lake City. Call 801-965-8628 or email atallorderfoundation@gmail.com to ask about qualifications, current openings, and the intake process.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not free emergency shelter. The official page lists entry rent at $510 per month with utilities included and says housing privileges are extended every six months as guests demonstrate ability to follow rules.
resources.name: HomeInn Transitional Housing

resources.address: 541 23rd Street, Ogden, UT 84402-1706
resources.description: Ogden-based Homeless Veterans Fellowship VA Grant and Per Diem transitional housing with on-premises housing, case management, treatment planning, life-skills support, and direct case manager contact.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Homeless Veterans Fellowship provides VA Grant and Per Diem transitional housing in Ogden. The program includes on-premises transitional housing, individual treatment planning, case management, community and life-skills learning opportunities, and no credit or background checks for service.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible veterans must have at least one day of active duty and a discharge status other than dishonorable. Program eligibility, bed availability, and case-management assessment should be confirmed with the agency.

**Population Served**
Veterans experiencing homelessness who can use Ogden-based transitional housing. Ogden is outside Salt Lake County but reasonably reachable for some Salt Lake County veterans, and the program is connected to VA homeless veteran service networks.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-392-7662 or email ssvf@homelessveterans.org to talk with a case manager about the housing situation or schedule an appointment. Office hours are Monday-Friday, 8:30 AM-4:30 PM, and callers may need to leave a message.

**Important Information to Know**
Their SSVF rapid rehousing program explicitly excludes Salt Lake County, so this entry is for Ogden transitional/supportive housing rather than Salt Lake County SSVF. All transitional housing units are in Ogden.
resources.name: Homeless Veterans Fellowship Grant and Per Diem Transitional Housing

resources.address: 6 Main Street, Taunton, MA 02780
resources.description: National Homes For Our Troops program that builds and donates specially adapted custom homes for severely injured post-9/11 veterans at no financial cost to the veteran, with an intake team and request-assistance route.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Homes For Our Troops builds and donates specially adapted custom homes nationwide for severely injured post-9/11 veterans. HFOT also states its intake team can help veterans locate services and resources, and the program provides homes at no financial cost to the veteran.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The main homebuilding program is for severely injured post-9/11 veterans. Applicants must go through HFOT's intake/eligibility review and project process.

**Population Served**
Severely injured post-9/11 veterans nationwide, including eligible veterans in Salt Lake County because homes are built where approved veterans live.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Request Assistance link on the HFOT website or call 866-787-6677. The main office address is 6 Main Street, Taunton, MA 02780.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a highly specialized, selective, long-term housing construction program, not emergency housing or home repair. Application review and project timelines can be lengthy.
resources.name: Homes For Our Troops Specially Adapted Custom Homebuilding

resources.address: 65 E 6850 S, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: Hope Clinic is a volunteer-run free clinic in Midvale providing no-cost medical care, lab services ordered by its team, specialty clinics, medication assistance, immunizations, imaging access, women's health, diabetes care, and health education for uninsured low-income patients.
resources.hours: General medical and lab hours: Tuesday and Wednesday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM. Specialty clinics: Tuesday and Wednesday noon-5:00 PM; Friday as scheduled.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free health care including general medical care, health and wellness promotion, orthopedic care, minor surgery, blood tests ordered by Hope Clinic, dermatology, gynecology, diabetes care and education, nephrology, neurology, medical education, ear/nose/throat care, immunizations, X-ray, ultrasound, and screening mammograms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Hope Clinic states it serves uninsured individuals and families who are 150% below poverty guidelines; patient cost is listed as $0. Call to confirm how eligibility is currently interpreted and what documentation is needed.

**Population Served**
Uninsured low-income individuals and families in the Salt Lake/Midvale area who need non-emergency medical care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-568-6700. The clinic is at 65 E 6850 S, Midvale. Use clinic hours for general medical/lab care and ask about specialty clinic scheduling.

**Important Information to Know**
Hope Clinic does not provide emergency care, work-injury care, car-accident injury care, prenatal care or pregnancy issues, dental care, controlled-substance prescriptions, labs ordered by outside doctors, medications prescribed by outside doctors, or vision exams.
resources.name: Hope Clinic Free Clinic for Uninsured Individuals and Families

resources.description: National Hope For The Warriors online intake for post-9/11 service members, veterans, military spouses, caregivers, and military family members seeking needs assessment, financial assistance when eligible, mental-health support, peer support, career support, and community resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hope For The Warriors Connect to Services provides a secure registration form and intake coordinator connection. Together they identify needs and connect eligible clients to services such as financial assistance, mental-health support, community resources, critical needs assistance, Warrior's Compass, peer support, spouse/caregiver scholarships, clinical support, career-related resources, and other HOPE programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The intake route is for post-9/11 service members, veterans, military spouses, caregivers, and military family members. Specific assistance depends on need, eligibility, funding, and program scope.

**Population Served**
Post-9/11 service members, veterans, military spouses, caregivers, and military family members nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents who can apply online.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Connect to Services Now link on the Hope For The Warriors page and complete the secure registration form. An intake services coordinator then connects with the applicant.

**Important Information to Know**
Financial help is limited and not guaranteed. HOPE states it cannot help with home or vehicle purchases, down payments or closing costs, child support, credit-card debt, service animals, legal fees, auto repairs, or medical and mental-health treatment costs, though staff may try to connect applicants to other trusted resources.
resources.name: Hope For The Warriors Connect to Services

Food pantry groceries for eligible households in the Kearns/Taylorsville area.

Public food-resource listings say the pantry serves people residing in ZIP codes 84118 and 84123 and asks for photo ID and proof of residency.

People living in ZIP codes 84118 or 84123 who need food assistance and can reach the Kearns church location.

Text FOOD BANK to 833-680-6903 or call the church number to confirm. The pantry is listed at 4115 W Sams Blvd, Kearns, UT 84118, with Tuesday 4:00 PM-6:00 PM pantry hours.

This is ZIP-code restricted. It passes for clients in those Salt Lake County ZIP codes but is not a countywide pantry. Contact appears text-oriented in food listings.
resources.name: Hope Unlimited Church Pantry

**Services Offered**
Structured driver education and licensing support for refugee women in Utah. Program components include accessible online instruction through Salt Lake International Driving School LLC, linguistically adapted curricula and interpreters, targeted permit and road-test preparation, behind-the-wheel training, and help navigating licensing barriers such as fees, documentation, and scheduling.

The program is specifically designed for refugee women in Utah. Public materials do not list application deadlines, cost to participants, documentation rules, or current openings; contact the organization to ask about intake.

**Population Served**
Refugee women in Utah who face cultural, linguistic, financial, or logistical barriers to obtaining a Utah driver's license and independent transportation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-371-8809, email contact@hopeforherinternational.org, or use the website contact form. The listed contact address is 170 S Main St, Ste 1100, Salt Lake City, UT 84101.

This is licensing and driver-education support, not a ride service or immediate vehicle placement. Confirm current enrollment capacity, any cost, language support, and required documents before referral.
resources.name: Hope for Her International Drive to Thrive

**Services Offered**
Outpatient therapy, in-home services, day treatment, school-based services, group therapy, medication management, skills development, respite, case management, peer support, and crisis services for established clients.

Insurance accepted is listed as Medicaid, SelectHealth, foster-care funding, Blue Cross Blue Shield, UnitedHealthcare, UMR, CHIP, Ecclesiastical Pay, Employee Assistance Pay, Aetna, Molina, University of Utah, and PEHP. Children, youth, families, and other clients in West Valley City and Salt Lake County needing outpatient or more intensive community-based behavioral-health support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-979-1351 and ask about the specific needed service, eligibility, payer acceptance, and openings. The office is at 3280 W 3500 S, Suite E, West Valley City.

The crisis service described on the site is for Hopeful Beginnings clients, not a public crisis line. Use 988 for immediate public crisis support.
resources.name: Hopeful Beginnings Mental Health Services

resources.description: Horizonte Instruction and Training Center offers adult high-school diploma and GED Fast Track options, with in-person evening/day options and online GED Fast Track components.

Adult high-school diploma classes and GED Fast Track. The adult high-school option includes day and evening schedules; GED Fast Track includes in-person and online schedule options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adult education students registering for adult high school or GED. Current registration instructions say to bring one proof of address, such as a bill, Utah ID card, rental agreement, or library card.

Adult learners in Salt Lake City and nearby Salt Lake County who need a high-school diploma or GED pathway.

Call 801-578-8574 or visit Horizonte at 1234 Main St. The official page posts 2026-2027 registration sessions; check the next available date before going.

**Important Information to Know**
Registration dates are specific and change through the school year. The city English-class guide separately lists a $30 adult English registration fee with fee waivers available; confirm exact fees for the chosen adult education track.
resources.name: Horizonte Adult High School and GED Fast Track

resources.address: 1135 East South Temple, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: House of Hope's Amaryllis House is a sober living recovery housing program for women leaving residential treatment and transitioning to outpatient care, with 6-12 months of housing support and recovery services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Recovery housing at Amaryllis House for women leaving residential treatment and transitioning to outpatient care. The program provides sober living beds, structured housing, house rules, curfew, supportive house managers, peer support, case management, and life skills training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Women must be in recovery and leaving residential treatment or transitioning to outpatient care. Admission requires House of Hope application or enrollment review; current bed availability and clinical requirements must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Women in substance-use recovery who need sober living support after residential treatment in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Heidi Lund at hlund@houseofhopeut.org, use the Amaryllis House Apply for Admission/Get Started links, or call House of Hope at 801-487-3276.

**Important Information to Know**
This is treatment-linked recovery housing, not general emergency shelter or ordinary affordable housing. The candidate also mentioned House of Hope residential treatment; that treatment housing is part of substance-use treatment and belongs primarily under addiction services.
resources.name: House of Hope Amaryllis House Recovery Housing

resources.address: 857 E 200 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: House of Hope provides women’s residential treatment, day treatment, intensive outpatient care, therapeutic childcare for children of mothers in treatment, and aftercare in Salt Lake City.
resources.hours: Outpatient/day treatment typically occurs Monday-Friday on site; schedules are determined by individual need.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential treatment for women with substance-use disorders, day treatment, intensive outpatient care, outreach/aftercare, and therapeutic childcare and parenting support for children of mothers in treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Women with substance-use disorders may be eligible depending on program fit, openings, and assessment. Children’s services are connected to mothers receiving House of Hope treatment.

**Population Served**
Women with substance-use disorders in Salt Lake City, including mothers with children who need treatment-supported childcare and family services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call (801) 487-3276. ARS lists admissions@houseofhopeut.org and admissions extensions for day treatment, residential, and IOP. The Salt Lake City treatment facility is at 857 E 200 S.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general co-ed provider. Recovery housing/aftercare services may be connected to House of Hope treatment participation or alumni status. ARS opening data changes and is not a guarantee of admission.
resources.name: House of Hope Salt Lake City Treatment Programs

resources.address: 1776 S West Temple, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: The Housing Authority of Salt Lake City provides direct instructions for applying to assisted, subsidized, project-based voucher, public housing, and affordable housing waitlists serving the Salt Lake valley.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Applications and waitlist access for assisted/subsidized housing programs, including tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers, project-based vouchers, public housing, and non-subsidized affordable or market-rate HASLC-owned properties.

**Eligibility Requirements**
All adult household members must meet HUD and HASLC eligibility rules, including family definition, citizenship or eligible immigration status, property or program criteria, criminal and rental-history screening, any prior debt rules, and applicable income limits. Some properties have population-specific criteria such as senior or veteran status.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City and Salt Lake valley households seeking long-term subsidized or affordable housing through HASLC.

**How to Best Connect**
Review HASLC housing options and waiting lists, apply through AffordableHousing.com when lists are open, or visit the HASLC main office at 1776 S West Temple, Salt Lake City. Call 801-487-2161 or email contact@haslcutah.org with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency shelter or immediate rental assistance. HASLC says waitlists are not always open and selection can take years. The tenant-based HCV waitlist is combined with Housing Connect, while some project-based or property-specific lists are HASLC-specific.
resources.name: Housing Authority of Salt Lake City Subsidized and Affordable Housing Waitlists

resources.address: 3595 South Main Street, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Housing Connect is Salt Lake County's housing authority, administering affordable housing properties, Housing Choice Voucher rental subsidies, public housing, project-based/RAD voucher waitlists, and supportive housing referral partnerships.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable housing properties, Housing Choice Voucher rental subsidies, public housing, Project-Based Voucher and RAD Project-Based Voucher waitlists, and supportive housing partnerships across Salt Lake County. Housing Connect's homepage listed New City Plaza and RAD Properties waiting lists open as of June 1, 2026.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the program or property. Housing Connect says households qualify based on annual gross family income and federal income-limit guidelines. Supportive housing requires partner or coordinated-entry referral; it is not a direct public application route.

**Population Served**
Low- and moderate-income households in Salt Lake County, including families, older adults, people with disabilities or chronic illness, veterans, refugees or immigrants, and people needing affordable housing when a program or property fits.

**How to Best Connect**
Check Housing Connect's homepage and Connect to Housing page for current waiting-list openings and application links, or call 801-284-4400, TDD 801-284-4407, or email info@housingconnect.org. Use AffordableHousing.com when Housing Connect directs applicants there.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency housing or emergency financial assistance. Some Housing Connect pages say major HCV/PBV/RAD/Public Housing waitlists are closed, while the homepage lists selected property waitlists open; check the current page before referral. Supportive housing clients must be referred through partners such as Coordinated Entry or behavioral-health systems.
resources.name: Housing Connect Affordable Housing Waitlists and Properties

resources.address: 3595 South Main Street, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Housing Connect administers the federally funded Housing Choice Voucher program in Salt Lake County, helping eligible lower-income families, older adults and people with disabilities afford safe private-market housing when vouchers and waiting lists are available. West Valley City states services previously managed by its Housing Authority are now available through Housing Connect.
resources.hours: Main office hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance, formerly Section 8, for eligible households to rent safe and decent private-market housing. Housing Connect also administers other subsidized housing waiting lists and pays rental subsidies to landlords for participating households.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Households qualify based on annual gross family income and federal income limits. Housing Connect states families must qualify under the very-low-income category for the household size. Voucher availability depends on waiting-list status, eligibility review and subsidy funding.

**Population Served**
Lower-income families, older adults and people with disabilities in Salt Lake County, including West Valley City residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Check Housing Connect's Connect to Housing page for current waiting-list openings and apply online when lists are open. Call 801-284-4400, TDD 801-284-4407 or email info@housingconnect.org for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Housing Connect's Connect to Housing page says its HCV, PBV, RAD PBV and Public Housing waiting lists are currently closed and not accepting applications, while its homepage lists selected property waiting lists open as of June 1, 2026. This is not emergency housing or emergency financial assistance; Housing Connect says the wait may be several years.
resources.name: Housing Connect Housing Choice Voucher Program

resources.address: 1999 W 1700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; work page also lists 1665 S Bennett Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: The Latter-day Saint Humanitarian Center provides paid job training for displaced people and others seeking employment skills, with work in production, forklift operation, food service, custodial and maintenance areas, plus English practice, certifications, job placement, and longer-term career planning.
resources.hours: Humanitarian Center operational hours are listed as Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; call before visiting for job-training/application entrance and current hiring steps.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Paid job training at the Humanitarian Center, including sorting and processing donations, production, forklift operation, food service, custodial, maintenance, practical employment skills, certifications, English practice for immigrant associates, job placement, and longer-term career planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Prior reviewed evidence for the work page stated applicants must be at least 18, eligible to work in the United States, willing to learn, and have a strong work ethic. Current acceptance, hiring openings, and documentation requirements should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
Adults in Salt Lake City seeking employment skills, including displaced people, immigrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and others who may benefit from paid work training and English practice.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-240-6887 for work/application questions or 801-240-5846 for the Humanitarian Center English class/work route. The official Humanitarian Center visitor page lists 1999 W 1700 S; the work/English-class evidence also lists 1665 S Bennett Road, so call first to confirm the correct entrance.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a paid work-training program, not a general job board or open-enrollment ESL class. The visitor-tour phone, 801-240-5954, is not the best intake number for work training. Current openings and exact application steps require confirmation.
resources.name: Humanitarian Center Job Training

resources.address: Huntsman Cancer Institute / University of Utah Health community clinic screening sites vary by screening type
resources.description: Huntsman Cancer Institute's Cancer Screening Voucher Program provides free breast, cervical, colorectal, and lung cancer screening vouchers and navigation for eligible Utah residents with low income and limited or no insurance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free cancer screening vouchers for breast, cervical, colorectal, and lung cancer screening, plus coordinator navigation through eligibility, scheduling, screening preparation, language access, and post-screening financial counseling referral when needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah residents must meet cancer screening guidelines, be uninsured or underinsured, and have low income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. Some screenings require a primary care visit and referral; colorectal and lung screening require provider referral forms.

**Population Served**
Eligible low-income, uninsured, or underinsured Utah residents, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-213-6251 or email vouchers@hci.utah.edu to reach the screening voucher coordinator. Eligible patients may be screened at Huntsman Cancer Institute or a University of Utah Health community clinic.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a cancer screening voucher program, not a general oncology treatment payment program. Breast and cervical programs have specific age/screening criteria; colorectal and lung screening require provider referral.
resources.name: Huntsman Cancer Screening Voucher Program

resources.address: 450 S 900 E, Suite 300, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: Huntsman Mental Health Institute’s Assessment & Referral Services is the Salt Lake County alcohol and drug treatment network access point for professional SUD assessments, referrals, and current network availability information.
resources.hours: Salt Lake County lists ARS phone hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Professional substance-use disorder assessment and referral into Salt Lake County alcohol and drug treatment programs. The ARS page also posts provider availability by program and level of care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Salt Lake County residents seeking assessment and referral may call to schedule. Placement depends on level of care, co-occurring needs, medication management needs, childcare needs, payer/funding, and provider availability.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake County who need SUD assessment or help matching to treatment within the county alcohol and drug treatment network.

**How to Best Connect**
Call ARS at 801-587-2770 Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. The listed location is 450 S 900 E, Suite 300, Salt Lake City, UT 84102.

**Important Information to Know**
ARS is an assessment and referral route, not a treatment bed itself. Availability shown online is fluid and does not guarantee an opening, because clinical fit and other factors affect placement.
resources.name: Huntsman Mental Health Institute Assessment & Referral Services (ARS)

resources.address: 501 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
resources.description: HMHI Recovery Clinic provides outpatient treatment for adults with alcohol or drug addiction and mental-health issues, using medication management, therapy, MAT, recovery support groups, individual therapy, and family support resources.
resources.hours: Hours not listed on the opened page; call to schedule and confirm virtual visit options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient treatment for alcohol addiction, drug addiction, and mental-health issues. Services include medication management, therapy, MAT medications such as Suboxone, Subutex, Zubsolv, Sublocade, Vivitrol, and naltrexone when appropriate, recovery support group, individual therapy, psychiatric medication management, case management, and family resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults should contact the clinic to schedule and confirm insurance, wait time, clinical fit, and whether medication or therapy services are appropriate. Virtual visits are available by arrangement.

**Population Served**
Adults with alcohol or drug addiction, opioid-use concerns, and/or co-occurring mental-health concerns who can participate in outpatient care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-587-8288. The listed HMHI Recovery Clinic location is 501 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108, with virtual visits available by contacting the office.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outpatient clinic care, not a detox bed. Medication options depend on clinician assessment and may involve frequent early visits.
resources.name: Huntsman Mental Health Institute Recovery Clinic

resources.address: 955 W 3300 S, South Salt Lake, UT 84119
resources.description: HMHI Recovery Works is an adult intensive outpatient addiction recovery program for drug addiction, alcoholism, and other substance-use disorders, with group therapy, family support, medication evaluation access, drug screening, and aftercare.
resources.hours: IOP groups meet Monday-Thursday 6:00 PM-8:30 PM; optional aftercare groups are on Fridays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult intensive outpatient addiction recovery for drug addiction, alcoholism, and other substance-use disorders. The program includes group therapy using CBT, DBT, motivational enhancement, ACT, mindfulness, experiential therapy, family/friend support, medication evaluation through Recovery Clinic providers, substance-use screenings, relapse planning, and aftercare groups.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults age 18 and older call to discuss goals and schedule a one-hour clinical assessment. The clinical team determines whether IOP is the appropriate level of care.

**Population Served**
Adults in Salt Lake County with substance-use disorders who need structured outpatient support and can attend evening groups.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-587-3235. The program is at Huntsman Mental Health Institute Crisis Care Center, 955 W 3300 S, South Salt Lake, UT 84119.

**Important Information to Know**
Groups run four nights per week for about eight weeks, with limited absences expected. Screening costs are included in IOP charges. Staff help determine insurance coverage and out-of-pocket costs.
resources.name: Huntsman Mental Health Institute Recovery Works IOP

resources.address: 7044 Commerce Park Drive, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: IEC of Utah offers electrical apprenticeship classroom training and job-opportunity connections for electrical apprentices and contractors from its Midvale campus.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Electrical apprenticeship training, apprentice support, online classroom access, job-opportunity connection between electrical apprentices and contractors, expedited licensure testing, transcript and tuition-receipt access, and related trade training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants may need employment with an electrical contractor and may need to complete IEC registration or assessment steps. Confirm current tuition, registration windows, sponsorship, and placement expectations before referral.

**Population Served**
People seeking electrical apprenticeship training and work opportunities with Utah electrical contractors, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the IEC of Utah Apprenticeships page and Apply Here or Register links. The main office and first through third year classrooms are at 7044 Commerce Park Drive, Midvale; campus 2 is at 7065 Commerce Park Drive.

**Important Information to Know**
IEC describes itself as both an apprenticeship school and an association supporting contractors and apprentices. It is not a guarantee of immediate employment.
resources.name: IEC of Utah Electrical Apprenticeships

resources.description: IRC Salt Lake City's New Roots program provides farm-business training for refugee and New American farmers, including land access, technical assistance, market support, and business skills.
resources.hours: Farm and training schedules vary; confirm current application and capacity with IRC/New Roots.

**Services Offered**
Farm-business training that can include access to land, agricultural training, technical assistance, market access, buyer communication, invoicing, and digital payment support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for refugee and New American farmers or food growers interested in farming or produce-business training. Current application process, eligibility, and capacity should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
Refugee and New American farmers in Salt Lake County, with farm sites submitted in West Valley City, Draper, and Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Call IRC Salt Lake City at 801-328-1091 or use the New Roots SLC website. Redwood Farm is listed at 3005 S Lester St, West Valley City; the IRC office is at 221 S 400 W, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialized farm-business pathway, not a general ESL, GED, or college program. Openings, farmer applications, and site availability need confirmation before referral.
resources.name: IRC New Roots Farm Business Training Program

resources.description: IRC Salt Lake City's Digital Inclusion program has helped newly arrived refugees and other New Americans obtain broadband connection, devices, and basic digital-literacy support, but current public intake and device/broadband availability need confirmation before routine referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Digital inclusion support for refugees and other New Americans, historically including help with broadband connection, household devices, and basic digital literacy such as using computers, email, Zoom, online school, work, and services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The supported public materials describe the program for newly arrived refugees and broader refugee/immigrant communities served by IRC Salt Lake City. Current public eligibility rules, device supply, broadband-subsidy process, and whether non-current IRC clients can self-apply are not published clearly.

**Population Served**
Refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, survivors of torture, other immigrants, and New Americans served by IRC Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Call IRC Salt Lake City at 801-328-1091 or email SaltLakeCity@Rescue.org to ask whether Digital Inclusion support is currently available and what intake route applies. The office is at 1149 West 2240 South, West Valley, UT 84119.

This lead is useful but needs administrator resolution before routine referral. resources.description: IRC Salt Lake City provides economic empowerment and employment support for refugees, asylees, trafficking survivors, torture survivors, and other immigrants, including job-readiness and early employment help.

Employment and economic empowerment support for IRC Salt Lake City clients, including job readiness, help understanding U.S. employers, application and interview navigation, employer-employee relationship support, financial and computer literacy, and related services that help adults become self-reliant.

IRC Salt Lake City serves refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, survivors of torture, and other immigrants. Some services may focus on newly arriving or eligible clients; the office should confirm eligibility and intake.

Refugees, new Americans, asylees, trafficking survivors, torture survivors, and other immigrants in the Salt Lake City area.

Call 801-328-1091, email SaltLakeCity@rescue.org, or contact the office at 1149 W 2240 S, West Valley City.

**Important Information to Know**
The employment-services announcement is older, but IRC's current Salt Lake City page still lists economic empowerment and job, computer, and financial literacy supports. Confirm current program fit before referral.
resources.name: IRC Salt Lake City Employment Services

resources.description: IRC Salt Lake City offers vocational ESL and adult education for eligible refugees, asylees, SIV holders, and other new Americans, including English for work and daily life, digital skills, and job readiness.
resources.hours: Class schedules and enrollment route should be confirmed with IRC Salt Lake City.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Vocational ESL and adult education, including English for work and daily life, computers and digital skills, job readiness, citizenship preparation, and flexible community-based classes. Some class models may include childcare or transportation supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Evidence describes the program as free for eligible refugees, asylees, SIV holders, and other new Americans. Exact current eligibility and self-enrollment steps should be confirmed with IRC.

**Population Served**

Eligible refugees, asylees, SIV holders, and new Americans in the Salt Lake area.

**How to Best Connect**

Call IRC Salt Lake City at 801-328-1091 or use the official Salt Lake City office website to ask about current class eligibility, enrollment and location. The current office address is 1149 W 2240 S, West Valley, UT 84119; confirm where the requested class meets before travelling.

**Important Information to Know**

Class schedule, current openings, and whether enrollment is through a caseworker or public intake were not fully established in the sealed evidence. Confirm before referral, especially for people not already connected to IRC.
resources.name: IRC Salt Lake City Vocational ESL and Adult Education Classes

resources.description: International Union of Operating Engineers Local 3 offers a Utah operating engineers apprenticeship pathway for heavy equipment, crane operation, mechanics, and lube service technicians, with applications available at the Sandy administrative office.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Earn-while-you-learn apprenticeship and training for operating engineers, including heavy equipment operation, crane operation, mechanics, lube service technicians, safety credentials, equipment classes, and related annual training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants are tested and interviewed before acceptance. Applicants must present valid identification, including driver's license and Social Security card, when applying. Apprentices must attend 160 hours of related training annually.

**Population Served**
People seeking operating engineer, crane, equipment, mechanic, or lube technician apprenticeship pathways in Utah.

Call the Utah Training Center/JATC at 801-664-6934. Applications are available at the Local 3 Administrative Office, 8805 S. Sandy Parkway, Sandy. The training center is in Morgan County.

Most training classes are scheduled in winter months. Training center travel to Morgan may be required after application. Acceptance is not guaranteed.
resources.name: IUOE Local 3 Utah Training Center Operating Engineers Apprenticeship

resources.description: IUPAT District Council 5 / Local 77 is a finishing-trades union access point for painters, drywall finishers, sign workers, and related apprenticeship, training, job-opportunity, and dispatch resources in Utah and Idaho.
resources.hours: Office hours listed Monday-Friday by appointment.

Union access point for painters, drywall finishers, and sign workers, with local representative contact, union meetings, job-opportunity resources, dispatch/out-of-work information, and links to Local 77 training and apprenticeship information.

Eligibility for apprenticeship, dispatch, union membership, dues, contractor placement, and work availability must be confirmed with Local 77 or the training link. Trade requirements vary by pathway.

People seeking finishing-trades work, union membership, dispatch, or apprenticeship/training routes in Utah and Idaho, with a Salt Lake County office/training center.

Call Local 77 at 801-977-0732 or contact representative Brandt Goble at 801-414-5710 or brandt@iupatdc5.org. The office/training center is at 1975 W. 3500 South, West Valley City.

The Local 77 page points to apprenticeship and training resources but does not fully describe current application windows or class openings. Confirm steps before referral.
resources.name: IUPAT DC5 / Local 77 Finishing Trades Apprenticeship and Dispatch Access

resources.description: Free IVMF Onward to Opportunity career training program offering professional certification preparation, career coaching, employer connections, and online or location-based learning pathways for transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Onward to Opportunity is a free career training program with industry-validated curricula, professional certification preparation, career coaching, and employer support designed to prepare and match participants with their next career. Learning pathways and locations vary, and online options are available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses. Applicants must complete the O2O admissions/application process and meet current program and pathway requirements.

**Population Served**
Transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents who can participate through online learning pathways or other available formats.

Use the Apply to O2O or Sign up link on the IVMF career training page. The page also links to admissions information, learning pathways, O2O locations, FAQs, and a contact-us route for normal business hours.

Course offerings, certification pathways, cohort timing, and whether any in-person instruction is available in Utah can change. Confirm current course availability and deadlines before relying on a specific credential path.
resources.name: IVMF Onward to Opportunity (O2O) Career Training

resources.description: National nonprofit offering free identity-theft victim assistance, direct advisors, custom remediation plans, and online recovery guidance for people whose identity documents or personal information were stolen or misused.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Identity Theft Resource Center provides free assistance for victims of identity theft, fraud, scams, and identity crimes. Help includes direct assistance, a custom remediation plan, resources, and a Victim Help Center for figuring out recovery steps.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available to people affected by identity theft, fraud, scams, or identity misuse. It does not require Utah residency and can be used by Salt Lake County residents by phone or online.

**Population Served**
People whose identity, documents, accounts, or personal information have been stolen, misused, or compromised.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 888-400-5530 or use the ITRC website to start identity-theft recovery help.

**Important Information to Know**
ITRC does not issue replacement government documents. It helps clients make a recovery plan, understand next steps, and navigate identity-theft remediation.
resources.name: Identity Theft Resource Center Free Identity Theft Victim Assistance

resources.description: Immigrant Legal Services is a Salt Lake City nonprofit immigration legal provider offering affordable immigration legal representation and a public contact route by call, text, visit, email or online message.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable immigration legal representation and help navigating the immigration system. The contact page says an immigration attorney will respond after a call, text, visit or online message.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For immigrants and families needing affordable immigration legal help. Fees, case acceptance and eligibility depend on the case and organization capacity.

**Population Served**
Immigrants, disadvantaged individuals and families in Salt Lake County and Utah who need immigration legal representation or consultation.

LGBTQ asylum seekers and HIV-positive asylum seekers in the United States, including eligible Salt Lake County residents who can use national remote services.

Infants ages 6 to 12 months in the United States, including Salt Lake County families who can locate a participating provider.

Eligible Lifeline consumers in states and areas where Infiniti Mobile offers service, including Utah consumers where current provider enrollment and coverage are confirmed.

People in Salt Lake City, West Jordan, West Valley City, and nearby areas who can use a smartphone/app-based platform for flexible hourly work.

Immediate behavioral-health access for serious issues such as severe depression, suicidal thoughts, psychosis, substance abuse, and other mental-health crises. No appointment is needed for a crisis care access center. Patients receive a medical exam and mental-health evaluation; the treatment plan may include discharge follow-up or inpatient admission if clinically needed.

People in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County experiencing urgent behavioral-health or psychiatric crisis needs.

The center acts like an emergency room and may involve hospital billing. It is for crisis assessment and stabilization, not routine outpatient therapy.

For families who learn that an unborn baby may have a life-threatening or life-limiting condition. Intermountain states the service is free and available to any family regardless of where in Utah they plan to deliver.

Families in Utah and the Intermountain West facing a life-threatening or life-limiting fetal diagnosis.

Use the email link on the Angel Watch page or call the listed program phone, 801-698-4486, to ask about enrollment and support options.

People with opioid-use disorder in Salt Lake County and other participating Utah counties who need outpatient, telehealth-supported MAT and recovery support.

Financial assistance for eligible Intermountain medical bills, including full or partial discounts for qualifying emergency or medically necessary care. It reduces the bill rather than giving cash to the patient.

Intermountain considers family size, gross annual household income, medical bills, and medical hardship. Patients with eligible care from Intermountain hospitals, clinics, or employed providers, including Salt Lake County facilities.

Applicants must be at least 18, provide proof of age, be physically able to perform ironwork when employment is offered, have aptitude and interest in the trade, and appear for a personal interview. Trade work is physically demanding and often outdoors.

Adults seeking ironworker apprenticeship and construction-trades work in Salt Lake County and Local 27's area.

Selection is based on qualifications and interview; applying does not guarantee acceptance or work. Applicants should bring required documentation and be prepared for physical trade expectations.

No-cost family support services, classes, support groups, a lending library, and short-term child-centered counseling for concerns such as anxiety, depression, anger, ADHD, autism-related needs, divorce, grief, and family stress.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current official page describes services for families and students in Jordan School District. District materials say to call for an intake assessment and that classes/support groups are available at no cost.

Students and families connected to Jordan School District communities in southwest Salt Lake County, including South Jordan, West Jordan, Riverton, Herriman, Bluffdale, Draper, and nearby areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-565-7442 for information, class registration, support groups, or counseling intake. The center is housed at River's Edge School, 319 W 11000 S, South Jordan.

This is school-district family support and short-term counseling, not a public crisis center or long-term therapy clinic. Confirm eligibility if the family does not have a Jordan School District student.
resources.name: Jordan Family Education Center

Deseret Industries vouchers for clothing and household items. The page is for Jordan School District Health Services and appears intended for district families. It does not state income criteria or voucher frequency.

Jordan School District students and families in southwest Salt Lake County. Spanish is available.

Call 801-567-8515 or visit Jordan School District Health Services at 8400 S Redwood Rd, Classroom 9, West Jordan. Call before visiting because office hours and voucher availability are not posted.

Outpatient substance-use treatment, dual-diagnosis support, and mental/behavioral health therapy. The provider says it is state-licensed as a chemical dependency outpatient treatment facility and mental health agency.

Call or book an appointment to confirm clinical fit, insurance, fees, and whether substance-use treatment is available for the client's age and needs.

Children, adolescents, adults, and families in West Jordan and Salt Lake County seeking mental health, substance-use, domestic violence, or family therapy services.

Call 801-566-0749 or use the appointment/contact option on the website. The office is at 9263 Redwood Road, Building 8, Suite B, West Jordan, UT 84088.

resources.address: 5428 Sundew Drive, Sarasota, FL 34238
resources.description: Josh Provides offers Medical Services and Transportation and Travel grants for people with epilepsy or seizure disorders, covering eligible transportation and travel tied to diagnostic testing and related medical needs when criteria, documentation, and funding allow.
resources.hours: Call before applying to check criteria, funding caps, and availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Grants for medical services and transportation/travel related to epilepsy or seizure-disorder care. Eligible assistance may include diagnostic testing, specific safety items, and transportation or travel for diagnostic testing. Payments are made directly to the physician, facility, or vendor.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants need physician documentation and client photo. Grants are date-specific, must be used within three months from the award date, and must be indicated by the neurologist. Diagnostic testing must be scheduled at least three weeks after application submission. Funding is not available for medication, prior services, or outstanding balances, and applicants may submit one Medical Services and Transportation and Travel application in a 12-month period.

**Population Served**
People living with epilepsy or other seizure disorders who need help with eligible medical services or related transportation/travel costs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-706-2740 before applying to check criteria, funding caps, and availability. Completed signed applications can be emailed to Info@JoshProvides.org or mailed to JoshProvides Epilepsy Assistance Foundation, 5428 Sundew Drive, Sarasota, FL 34238.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a financial grant paid to vendors or providers, not a ride scheduler. Assistance depends on documentation, funding caps, and current availability.
resources.name: Josh Provides Medical Services and Transportation and Travel Grants

Therapy, targeted case management, psychiatric medication management, medication-assisted treatment, housing services, and employment services. Therapy supports behavior, beliefs, feelings, relationships, and coping; case management helps connect clients to needed services.

Detailed eligibility and payer rules are not listed on the public page. Call or use the get-started/contact route to confirm intake, insurance, fees, and whether supports such as housing or employment are available to new clients.

People in Salt Lake County seeking behavioral-health care, with source submissions noting emphasis on refugee and immigrant populations.

Call 801-232-7633 or use the website's get-started/contact route. The office is at 1743 W. North Temple, Salt Lake City.

Wraparound supports may depend on program eligibility and availability. Medication-assisted treatment on the site appears in the behavioral-health service menu; confirm whether the client needs psychiatric medication management, substance-use MAT, or both.
resources.name: Journey Center for Behavioral Health

**Services Offered**
Housing Services that assist families with support needed to find and maintain housing through emergency rental assistance and other services. Journey also provides targeted case management, therapy, medication assisted treatment, and employment services that may support housing stability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list detailed housing-service eligibility. State TANF Family Housing materials identify Journey as a TANF Family Housing provider, which requires TANF eligibility including a minor child in the household. Other program eligibility, documentation, funding status, and behavioral-health enrollment expectations should be confirmed with Journey.

**Population Served**
Families in Salt Lake County needing housing stabilization support, especially families who may qualify for TANF Family Housing or Journey's behavioral-health/case-management services.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Housing Case Manager Gabby Paredes at gabrielap@journeyslc.org, call 801-232-7633, or use Journey's Service Request Form. The office is at 1743 W. North Temple, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance depends on eligibility, available funding, and program review. Journey's page says to contact the housing case manager for details, so confirm covered expenses, documentation, and whether treatment or case-management enrollment is required.
resources.name: Journey Center for Behavioral Health Housing Services

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential treatment for chemical dependency and alcohol abuse, with a continuum that includes residential care, IOP, general outpatient services, evidence-based therapy, and social detox support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults 18 and older seeking private care for chemical dependency or alcohol abuse. Contact admissions to confirm level of care, medical appropriateness for withdrawal, openings, and insurance/payment.

**Population Served**
Adult men and women in the Salt Lake City area, including Cottonwood Heights and Riverton locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-351-5483 or 801-294-6400, or use the online admissions/get-started form. The Cottonwood Heights program address is 8072 S Highland Dr.

The provider describes social detox, which may not mean medically managed withdrawal. Verify the clinical withdrawal-management scope before sending a client with serious alcohol, benzodiazepine, or opioid withdrawal risk.
resources.name: Journey Treatment Center

resources.description: Journey of Hope provides trauma-informed, peer-led case management and prison mentoring for women, girls, affected youth, and LGBTQIA+ people facing violence, homelessness, incarceration, addiction, mental-health concerns, and reentry barriers.
resources.hours: Appointment only; no walk-ins at the administrative location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HER Empowerment case management, social advocacy, mentoring, peer leadership, basic-needs navigation, safe housing-resource navigation, employment support, food and clothing help, processing groups, Seeking Safety aftercare, and HOPE Prison Mentoring before and after release.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Journey of Hope focuses on vulnerable and harmed women, girls, affected youth, and LGBTQIA+ community members. People can call, email, message, or complete case-management intake forms to secure a spot on the waiting list. Prison mentoring is described for women 3-6 months before release and up to 12 months after release.

**Population Served**
Women, girls, affected youth, and LGBTQIA+ people across Salt Lake City and the Wasatch Front who are facing homelessness, violence, exploitation, incarceration, recidivism, addiction, or mental-health barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-633-9409, email info@journeyofhopeutah.org, send a website message, or complete the case-management intake forms. Do not send walk-ins to the administrative location; clients should make an appointment and wait for contact from a case manager or peer support specialist.

**Important Information to Know**
Submitting an intake may place the person on a waiting list rather than guarantee immediate service. The program is population-specific and trauma-informed; preserve client privacy and safety when contacting.
resources.name: Journey of Hope HER Empowerment Case Management and HOPE Prison Mentoring

resources.description: Justice By Objectives is a Utah nonprofit focused on individuals and families impacted by incarceration, offering peer support, family peer support, court assistance, vocational and housing resources, recovery resources, transportation, case management, and advocacy.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer support, family peer support, goal planning, court assistance and court support, attorney-option navigation, vocational assistance, housing resources, recovery resources, mental-health resources, case management, transportation, advocacy, education, support groups, and community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The organization focuses on individuals and families impacted by the criminal justice system and incarceration. Public eligibility limits, fees, and capacity are not fully posted; call or email to ask about current intake.

**Population Served**
People in Utah impacted by incarceration and their family members, including people seeking reintegration, peer support, and fair-chance opportunities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 435-565-5229 or email channae@justicebyobjectives.org. The Murray address is listed in local and reentry directories; confirm whether meetings are by appointment before going in person.

The official site is broad and informal, so clients should confirm current services, location, appointment requirements, and capacity. Use it as a peer/family support and navigation resource rather than a guaranteed housing or legal-service placement.
resources.name: Justice By Objectives Reentry Peer and Family Support

resources.description: National K9s For Warriors program providing trained service dogs at no financial cost to eligible veterans with clinically verified service-connected PTSD, TBI, or MST, followed by an 18-day residential campus training program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
K9s For Warriors provides trained service dogs to veterans with PTSD, TBI, and/or MST at no financial cost. Accepted veterans attend an 18-day residential training program where housing, meals, equipment, on-campus veterinary care, and training are provided, followed by ongoing check-ins and annual recertification.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be veterans with a verified clinical diagnosis of service-connected PTSD, TBI, or MST. Required documents include a primary care physician's report, a mental-health verification form completed by a clinician, a support agreement, DD214 member 4 copy showing signature and discharge status, and a full-length photo. Application review includes interviews, references, and a background investigation.

**Population Served**
Veterans from all 50 states, Puerto Rico, and Guam, including Utah veterans, with service-connected invisible wounds who can travel to the Florida or Texas campus if accepted.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the Apply for a Service Dog link at apply.k9sforwarriors.org. The Warrior Operations team reviews applications and contacts applicants during the process.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is free for accepted veterans except travel to and from training; outside travel resources may be available. K9s For Warriors reports an 18-24 month waiting period. Training is at the National Headquarters in Ponte Vedra, Florida or Warrior Ranch in Helotes, Texas. Visitors or caregivers cannot attend training with the veteran.
resources.name: K9s For Warriors Warrior and Service Dog Program

resources.address: Training takes place at various training centers and community partner locations throughout the Salt Lake area; mailing address listed by prior proposal as PO Box 543, West Jordan, UT 84084.
resources.description: Utah Women in Trades offers the Karen Mayne Pre-Apprenticeship Program, a 12-15 week Salt Lake-area pathway that helps adults explore skilled construction trades, learn safety and basic construction skills, prepare for apprenticeship entry requirements, and connect with training centers and employers.
resources.hours: Cohorts typically run 12-15 weeks with classes two days per week; days vary by cohort and training schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Karen Mayne Pre-Apprenticeship Program offers classroom and hands-on training for people exploring skilled building and construction trades. Participants learn construction safety, tool use, industry expectations, job readiness, apprenticeship math and aptitude preparation, and may earn credentials such as OSHA 10, First Aid/CPR, and MC3.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants should be at least 18, have a high school diploma or GED or be willing to obtain one, have state ID, Social Security card, reliable transportation, ability to pass drug testing for apprenticeship programs, a driver's license or willingness to obtain one, and citizenship or eligible immigrant status for apprenticeship eligibility. Participants must be able to safely perform essential construction work such as lifting 25-50 pounds, bending, using tools, and following safety rules.

**Population Served**
People in the Salt Lake area who are interested in construction and skilled trades, especially those with less than one year of total construction experience.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the online application linked on the program page. Training takes place at various training centers and community partner locations throughout the Salt Lake area. Use the Utah Women in Trades contact page if cohort details or application status are unclear.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a registered apprenticeship; it prepares participants to apply for and succeed in apprenticeship opportunities. No prior construction experience is required. Public cost information was not posted on the opened program page.
resources.name: Karen Mayne Pre-Apprenticeship Program

resources.description: Kourageous Vision's Kourageous Threads clothing program provides clothing such as coats, shoes, purses, gloves, scarves, hats, pajamas, professional attire, and everyday essentials for women in treatment centers, sober living homes, and halfway houses.

resources.informationText:

Clothing support for women who need basics while in treatment, sober living, or halfway-house settings. Listed items include coats, shoes, purses, gloves, scarves, hats, pajamas, professional attire, and everyday essentials, with deliveries made during the week.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The program page says it serves women in treatment centers, sober living homes, and halfway houses who have limited or no family, friends, finances, or transportation to obtain basic clothing.

**Population Served**

Women in Utah recovery, sober living, treatment-center, and halfway-house settings.

**How to Best Connect**

Confirm the direct client request process before promising clothing delivery.

**Important Information to Know**

This is targeted clothing delivery, not a general public clothing closet. Service area, delivery timing, and item availability should be confirmed when requesting help.
resources.name: Kourageous Threads Clothing Program

resources.informationText:

Construction laborers union membership, application access, dispatch/out-of-work list, and career pathway into commercial building, heavy/highway, industrial, refinery, refractory, and pipeline construction work across Utah.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must follow Local 295 application steps and dispatch rules. Job calls are based on the out-of-work list, qualifications, special skills, dues or registration-fee status, and employer needs. Drug testing or certifications may affect dispatch.

**Population Served**
People seeking Utah construction labor work through LIUNA Local 295, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply Here page, submit the application as directed, or contact dispatch at dispatch@utahlaborers.com. Call the office at 801-972-5380 or dispatcher extension 21 for dispatch questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Dispatch is not immediate for everyone. Applicants must keep their out-of-work list status current and maintain accurate skill/certification information with the dispatcher.
resources.name: LIUNA Local 295 Utah Laborers Membership and Dispatch Pathway

resources.description: Free peer breastfeeding/chestfeeding support across Utah and Idaho, including Salt Lake leader phone help, email contact, and virtual/local meetings for expecting and nursing parents.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
La Leche League Utah and Idaho provides free peer breastfeeding support, leader phone help, meetings, education, information, and encouragement for parents who want to breastfeed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
All nursing parents are welcome regardless of La Leche League membership. Expecting parents may attend meetings before the baby arrives.

**Population Served**
Pregnant, nursing, breastfeeding, and chestfeeding parents in Utah and Idaho, including Salt Lake County families.

**How to Best Connect**
For Salt Lake support, call 801-251-MILK (801-251-6455) or email breastfeedingslc@gmail.com to request the Zoom link. The statewide toll-free number from the submission is 877-452-5324.

**Important Information to Know**
La Leche League leaders are trained volunteer peer supporters, not a substitute for urgent medical or clinical lactation care when a baby has dehydration, poor weight gain, jaundice, or other concerning symptoms.
resources.name: La Leche League Utah and Idaho Salt Lake Breastfeeding Support

Temporary staffing, temp-to-hire, seasonal work, general labor, construction, landscaping, manufacturing, hospitality, and skilled-trades staffing. The office page includes Start Your Application and View Current Openings links.

Job seekers in the Salt Lake City area looking for temporary or temp-to-hire blue-collar staffing work.

Staffing help for temporary, temp-to-hire, and direct-hire jobs. The Salt Lake City branch advertises job search support, employer connections, flexible work options, and placement with companies in South Salt Lake and nearby areas.

Requirements vary by job. Applicants should ask about identification, work authorization, transportation, background checks, skills, physical requirements, and current job availability.

Job seekers in South Salt Lake and surrounding areas seeking staffing-agency work.

Free home-cooked lasagna or main dish delivered by a local volunteer after an online request and match.

The request page says kindness is for everyone and does not list income screening. Service depends on whether Lasagna Love is active in the person's area and whether a local volunteer match is available.

Households needing help with dinner, including Salt Lake County residents if a local volunteer is available.

Use the request page to check whether Lasagna Love is in the area, then request for yourself or nominate someone else. After matching, coordinate delivery day and time with the volunteer. Email info@lasagnalove.org for general contact.

Free job-search support, including resume writing, job leads, networking, interview practice, personalized coaching, computer and printer access, active job-search groups, online workshops, and help using the online job board.

All are welcome and a person does not need to be a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Bring a resume or job description if available, but the center can help without one.

Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County job seekers who want in-person, phone, or web-conference help with job search and employment preparation.

Call the Sugarhouse office at 801-467-6443, call the toll-free Employment Services number at 888-818-4484, email EmploymentServices@ChurchofJesusChrist.org, use the Request Assistance link, or visit 724 E 2100 S, Suite A. Appointments are encouraged but walk-ins are welcome.

This is a coaching and job-search support center, not a guaranteed job placement. If the local office hours are not visible online, call before sending someone in person.
resources.name: Latter-day Saint Employment Services - Sugarhouse

resources.description: Tooele Technical College's Learn to Dream Scholarship is a needs-based 2025-2026 award for Salt Lake County and Tooele County residents that can help cover tuition, books, kits, and internal testing for most Tooele Tech certificate programs.
resources.hours: Campus hours listed Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-8:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Needs-based scholarship assistance for eligible Tooele Technical College certificate-seeking students. The award may cover tuition, books, program kits, and internal testing fees up to the program's stated limit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must complete the scholarship application, complete the FAFSA and meet FAFSA eligibility criteria, meet college admission requirements, enroll as a certificate-seeking student in an eligible program, attend at least 12 hours per week, maintain satisfactory academic progress, be a high school graduate or GED completer at the time of application, and reside in Salt Lake or Tooele County. Electrical Apprenticeship and Composites are excluded.

**Population Served**
Recent high school graduates and adult learners from Salt Lake County or Tooele County pursuing eligible Tooele Tech certificate programs.

**How to Best Connect**
Start through the Learn to Dream Scholarship page or call Tooele Technical College at 435-248-1800. The campus is at 88 S Tooele Boulevard, Tooele, UT 84074.

**Important Information to Know**
The page identifies the 2025-2026 award year and a $1,000 coverage limit for covered costs. Availability, award limit, and excluded programs should be confirmed before a student commits expenses.
resources.name: Learn to Dream Scholarship

resources.address: 960 South Main Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Legal Aid Society of Salt Lake provides free domestic violence victims assistance for Salt Lake County protective orders, child protective orders, dating violence protective orders, and civil stalking injunctions, regardless of income or legal status.
resources.hours: Courthouse intake locations listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal representation for petitioners seeking protective orders, child protective orders, dating violence protective orders, and civil stalking injunctions. Intakes for orders of protection can be done online or at listed courthouse locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Legal Aid can represent domestic violence victims regardless of income or legal status when the case is in Salt Lake County. Generally, at least one party must live in Salt Lake County or the incident must have occurred in Salt Lake County. They cannot help respondents in these matters.

**Population Served**
Domestic violence victims and stalking survivors with cases filed or fileable in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Begin virtual intake through the website or go to walk-in intake at Matheson Courthouse, 450 South State Street Room W-17, Salt Lake City, or West Jordan Courthouse, 8080 S Redwood Road Room 2501. Bring police reports or evidence of abuse if available.

**Important Information to Know**
For immediate danger call 911. This program is specific to protective-order/stalking matters; other civil legal issues may require a different provider.
resources.name: Legal Aid Society of Salt Lake Domestic Violence Victims Assistance / Protective Orders

resources.address: Scott Matheson Courthouse, 450 S State St, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; West Jordan Courthouse, 8080 S Redwood Rd, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: Legal Aid Society of Salt Lake's Family Law Pro Se Clinics provide free brief family-law information, forms help, hearing-scheduling help and virtual Ask an Attorney access for self-represented people in Salt Lake County family law cases.
resources.hours: Walk-in clinic locations and virtual availability vary; the official assisted pro se page should be checked before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free brief help for self-represented people in family law matters such as divorce, parentage/custody and guardianship. Clinic staff can provide process information, access to forms and help scheduling hearings; the phone Ask an Attorney clinic can provide legal advice by appointment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For pro se individuals in family law matters, especially cases connected to Salt Lake County courts. Full representation is a separate Legal Aid intake.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents and court users representing themselves in family law cases.

**How to Best Connect**
Email familylawclinic@lasslc.org to request an intake form and appointment. Virtual access is listed through 801-328-8849 option 3; the clinic page also lists 801-233-9675 for Family Law Clinic questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Paralegal clinic services are not the same as attorney representation. Use the current Assisted Pro Se page to confirm walk-in courthouse days, rooms and virtual availability before going.
resources.name: Legal Aid Society of Salt Lake Family Law Pro Se Clinic

resources.address: 960 South Main Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Legal Aid Society of Salt Lake provides free legal representation to low-income families in Salt Lake County family law cases and free representation regardless of income for domestic violence victims seeking protective orders and civil stalking injunctions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal representation in family law cases such as divorce, custody/parentage and guardianship of minors. Legal Aid also provides free representation for domestic violence victims seeking protective orders and civil stalking injunctions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Family law representation is for low-income families with cases filed or able to be filed in Salt Lake County. Protective-order and civil-stalking representation is available to domestic violence victims regardless of income.

**Population Served**
Low-income Salt Lake County families with family law cases and domestic violence victims needing protective orders or civil stalking injunctions in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-328-8849 or use the Legal Aid Society website menu for the relevant case type. The office is at 960 South Main Street, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Legal Aid handles specific Salt Lake County family and victim-protection matters; other civil legal issues are referred elsewhere. Representation depends on eligibility, conflicts and capacity.
resources.name: Legal Aid Society of Salt Lake Family Law and Protective Order Representation

resources.address: 6671 S Redwood Rd, West Jordan, UT 84084; 1088 E 390 S, American Fork, UT 84003
resources.description: Liberty Addiction Recovery Centers provides Utah drug and alcohol treatment, including residential treatment, PHP, IOP, sober/recovery housing supports, and family support, with Medicaid and many Utah insurance plans listed by the provider.
resources.hours: Call for current intake hours and placement availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Drug and alcohol addiction treatment, including residential treatment, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient programming, sober/recovery-home support, family support, mentoring, and employment/education pathway supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call or use the admissions/insurance links to confirm level-of-care fit, location, openings, and payer acceptance. The official page says Liberty accepts Medicaid, Molina, Aetna, BlueCross BlueShield, and most Utah insurance plans.

**Population Served**
People seeking drug or alcohol addiction recovery in Utah, including Salt Lake County clients who can use the West Jordan outpatient site and the American Fork residential program.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-997-9183 or email info@libertyaddictionrecovery.com. The provider site also links to admissions and insurance-check forms.

**Important Information to Know**
Detox language on the site appears to include placement or referral information; confirm whether any detox service is directly provided at the intended site.
resources.name: Liberty Addiction Recovery Centers

resources.description: Income-restricted Section 42 apartment pathway in downtown Salt Lake City with a waiting-list form, income limits, and direct application instructions.

**Services Offered**
Liberty CityWalk offers Section 42 income-based reduced-rent apartments. The property uses a waiting-list request form and a Section 42 rental application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Household gross annual income must be below the property's posted maximum income limits, and each household member must meet Section 42 requirements including income, asset, and student-status verification.

**Population Served**
Households seeking income-restricted rental housing in Salt Lake City who can meet property and Section 42 screening requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 844-593-2775 or use the application page to download the waiting-list request and Section 42 application. The page says to contact the property for current availability before applying and to submit completed paperwork by fax or email.
