This is reduced-rent housing, not emergency shelter or a rent-payment program. The property says it generally works from a waiting list; applications can take days to weeks depending on verification needs.
resources.name: Liberty CityWalk Section 42 Affordable Housing

resources.address: 3818 W 4700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84129
resources.description: Life Church Utah's Food Share distributes free produce, non-perishables, and other groceries weekly during its March-October season. The provider states photo ID and proof of income are not required.

Weekly seasonal free food distribution with fresh produce, non-perishable items, and other essential groceries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider says Food Share is open to the community and that photo ID and proof of income are not required.

**Population Served**
People in the Salt Lake Valley, including West Valley and Taylorsville-area residents, who are facing food insecurity and can attend the distribution.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to Life Church Utah at 3818 W 4700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84129 on Tuesdays during the March-October season; distribution starts at 5:30 PM. Call 801-968-3715 or email life@lifechurchutah.com to confirm the current week.

**Important Information to Know**
This is seasonal. As of late September 2026 it falls inside the March-October window, but clients should confirm current-week availability before going.
resources.name: Life Church Utah Food Share

resources.description: Life Skills Vocational Center is listed by Utah DHHS/211 for employment preparation and supported employment services, and USOR lists it as an approved CRP provider serving Salt Lake County.

Employment Preparation Service, Supported Employment for an Individual, Supported Employment in a Group, day supports, and related services. USOR also lists Life Skills Vocational Center as an approved CRP provider serving Salt Lake County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The DHHS listing shows a DSPD contract for intellectual disability, related conditions, and acquired brain injury services. Eligibility, funding, and whether USOR or DSPD authorization is needed should be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**
People with qualifying disabilities who need employment preparation or supported employment; Salt Lake County coverage is listed through USOR, with an Orem provider address.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-233-9014. The DHHS/211 listing says the application/referral process is to call.

The office is in Orem, while USOR lists Salt Lake County coverage. Confirm service location, transportation expectations, and funding/authorization steps before referral.
resources.name: Life Skills Vocational Center Supported Employment and Employment Preparation

resources.address: 4113 Monticello St, Covington, GA 30014
resources.description: Life Wireless offers Utah Lifeline mobile service for eligible low-income households, with online ZIP-code application and a Utah plan listing free monthly cellular service with unlimited talk, unlimited text, and data subject to plan and coverage limits.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lifeline mobile phone service for eligible Utah households. The Utah plan page lists free monthly wireless service with unlimited nationwide calling, unlimited text messaging, and high-speed data, subject to network availability and plan terms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must qualify for Lifeline by income or participation in a qualifying program such as SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension or Survivors Benefit, or eligible Tribal programs. The Lifeline benefit is limited to one per household and cannot be combined with another Lifeline offer.

**Population Served**
Low-income Utah residents, including Salt Lake County residents, who qualify for Lifeline and live at an address where Life Wireless service is available.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online with ZIP code and email at the Life Wireless website, continue an existing order online, or call 1-888-543-3620 for eligibility and terms questions. Confirm service and plan availability for the specific address before relying on it.

**Important Information to Know**
Plan details, data allowance, device terms, fees, and coverage can change. Lifeline eligibility is determined through federal/state rules and may require documentation or National Verifier approval.
resources.name: Life Wireless Lifeline Wireless Service

resources.address: First Baptist Church, 777 S 1300 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: LifeRing Utah offers free, confidential, secular peer recovery meetings in the Salt Lake Valley for people seeking substance-use recovery support without a religious or 12-step requirement.
resources.hours: Salt Lake Valley meeting listed Saturdays 11:00 AM; Wednesday 7:00 PM meeting is listed as on hiatus until further notice.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Secular, self-empowered peer recovery meetings for addiction recovery. Meetings are peer support, not clinical treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Meetings are listed as free, confidential, and open to all, with voluntary donations requested.

**Population Served**
People in the Salt Lake Valley seeking secular peer support for recovery from alcohol or other non-medically indicated drug use.

**How to Best Connect**
Attend the listed Saturday 11:00 AM meeting at First Baptist Church, 777 S 1300 E, Salt Lake City. Check the LifeRing Utah meeting page before attending because times and locations can change.

**Important Information to Know**
The Wednesday 7:00 PM meeting is listed as on hiatus. LifeRing is peer support and should not be used as a substitute for detox, medication treatment, or emergency care.
resources.name: LifeRing Utah Salt Lake Valley Secular Recovery Meetings

resources.description: Lifeline is a federal phone or internet service discount for eligible low-income households, including Utah and Salt Lake County residents. Consumers verify eligibility, then choose a participating phone or internet company.
resources.hours: Lifeline Support Center: 7 days a week, 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time. Online application and carrier search are available through LifelineSupport.org/USAC.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Monthly discount on phone, internet or bundled service. USAC states the standard Lifeline discount is up to $9.25 per month, with a higher amount for consumers living on qualifying Tribal lands.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A household may qualify through participation in programs such as Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension or Survivors Benefit, qualifying Tribal programs, or household income at or below 135% of the federal poverty guidelines. Only one Lifeline discount is allowed per household, except where program rules allow separate households at one address.

**Population Served**
Eligible low-income consumers in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents. Survivor benefit rules may also help survivors of domestic violence, human trafficking or related crimes who meet USAC requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at LifelineSupport.org to check eligibility and apply, then contact a participating phone or internet company to set up service. For application help, call the Lifeline Support Center at 800-234-9473 or email LifelineSupport@usac.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The Utah Office of Consumer Services page explains that getting service is a two-step process: verify eligibility, then contact a participating provider. Plan costs and participating companies vary, and consumers must recertify when required to keep the benefit.
resources.name: Lifeline Phone or Internet Discount

resources.description: Lime Access provides discounted e-bike and e-scooter rides for qualifying riders in communities where Lime operates, with online application, text-to-unlock, and cash-payment options.
resources.hours: Online application and help email; device availability follows local Lime operating zones and hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Discounted Lime e-bike and e-scooter rides for eligible riders. Lime Access also offers options for riders without a smartphone to text to unlock a device and, once qualified, cash payment through a PayNearMe payment code.

**Eligibility Requirements**
U.S. applicants qualify by stating a reason for eligibility such as SNAP, Medicaid, reduced-rate utility bill, free or reduced school lunch, reduced transit fare program, SSI, WIC, federal subsidized housing, Pell Grant, or local/state-subsidized housing. The application asks for name, email, birthdate, and phone number.

**Population Served**
Low-income or benefit-eligible riders in places where Lime operates, including Salt Lake City when Lime devices are available and the rider can safely use e-scooters or e-bikes.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Lime Access page. Riders without a smartphone can text +1 888-495-5014 to unlock an e-bike or e-scooter and follow prompts. Use Lime's help email links on the page for eligibility or pricing questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not door-to-door accessible transportation. It depends on local device availability, geofenced operating areas, rider safety, weather, account status, and city rules.
resources.name: Lime Access

resources.address: 2369 West Orton Circle, Suite 20, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Take Care Utah's Linkage Coordinator Project is a free DHHS-partnered navigation program connecting Utah adults with IDD, TBI, or mobility limitations to preventive care, mental health care, health promotion, transportation, housing, and community supports.
resources.hours: Appointments may be in person, by phone, or online; call or use the online form for scheduling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Screening for unmet health needs, health education, referral to preventive healthcare, mental healthcare, health promotion programs, transportation, housing, and other community services, plus a 3-month follow-up.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must be 18 or older, live in Utah, and have an intellectual or developmental disability, traumatic brain injury, or mobility limitation.

**Population Served**
Utah adults with IDD, traumatic brain injury, or mobility limitations, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Linkage Project referral/registration form and mark self-referral if appropriate, email linkage@healthpolicyproject.org with questions, or call Take Care Utah at 801-433-2299.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is free and provides navigation/referrals, not direct medical treatment. The online registration survey is estimated at about 8 minutes and is used so a Linkage Coordinator can schedule screening.
resources.name: Linkage Coordinator Project

resources.description: Literacy Action Center provides adult literacy instruction and tutoring for English-speaking adults with reading, writing, or math skills below about fifth-grade level.

**Services Offered**
Adult literacy instruction, including small-group instruction and one-on-one tutoring for reading, writing, and math skills.

Designed for English-speaking adults whose reading, writing, or math skills are below about a fifth-grade level. Current intake, assessment, and schedule requirements should be confirmed by phone.

Adults in Salt Lake County and Davis County who need basic literacy, writing, or math support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-265-9081 or use the Literacy Action Center website to look for current intake information.

The website content appears dated in the sealed evidence. That is not evidence of closure, but current operations, location, and intake should be confirmed before referral.

**Services Offered**

Diapers, wipes, hygiene products, clothing, comfort kits, baby and family essentials, education, and community-resource connections for families experiencing financial hardship.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The official site describes service for Utah families experiencing financial hardship. Specific documents, diaper-bank limits, and whether Salt Lake County families can be served by pickup, outreach, or partner distribution should be confirmed before travel.

**Population Served**

Utah children and families, including families with infants and young children needing diapers, wipes, clothing, hygiene items, or other essentials.

**How to Best Connect**

Confirm Salt Lake County distribution/outreach before travel because the resource center is in Logan.

**Important Information to Know**

The public office is in Logan, which is not a routine Salt Lake County errand. Use this as a phone-confirmed statewide lead and verify Salt Lake County access, outreach, or partner distribution before a client travels.
resources.name: Little Lambs Foundation for Kids diapers, children's clothing, and essentials

Immigration legal services from the Salt Lake City LFSRM office. Prior provider materials list immigration consultations, lawful permanent resident card renewal or replacement, employment authorization, refugee travel documents, waivers and naturalization including disability medical waiver forms.

For immigrants, refugees and asylees whose issue fits LFSRM's immigration legal services. Fees, documents and case acceptance should be confirmed with the office.

Utah immigrants, refugees and asylees, including Salt Lake County residents who can reach the Salt Lake City office.

Call 801-290-2008, email ilsutah@lfsrm.org or use the website contact form. The Salt Lake City location is 415 E 3900 South.

The locations page confirms the Salt Lake City immigration legal services site, but detailed fees and case limits are not fully listed there. Confirm before referral.
resources.name: Lutheran Family Services Rocky Mountains Immigration Legal Services - Salt Lake City

resources.description: Muscular Dystrophy Association offers a directly contactable National Resource Center for neuromuscular-disease navigation and identifies Salt Lake City MDA Care Center routes at the University of Utah for adult and pediatric neuromuscular care.

Neuromuscular-disease specialty care through local MDA Care Centers and one-on-one resource navigation through the MDA National Resource Center for services, activities, benefits, and support questions.

For people with muscular dystrophy, ALS, and related neuromuscular diagnoses. Care Center appointments may require a physician referral and an established neuromuscular diagnosis.

Salt Lake County residents with neuromuscular diseases who can use the national phone/email resource center or seek care through Salt Lake City MDA care-center sites.

Call 833-ASK-MDA1 for the MDA National Resource Center. For the University of Utah adult MDA/ALS Care Center, the submitted phone is 801-585-7575. Adult clinic address submitted: 175 N. Medical Drive East, 4th Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84132.

The local clinic is not a walk-in service and may require medical referral. Current financial assistance, camp offerings, and the pediatric clinic ZIP/address should be confirmed before detailed referral.

resources.phone: 833-ASK-MDA1; University of Utah adult MDA/ALS Care Center 801-585-7575

The official calendar says first-time food clients complete a one-time two-page food eligibility form with voluntary ID. The page says food could be received twice a week during the pandemic; clients should ask whether that frequency still applies.

Individuals and families in the Salt Lake County area who can reach South Salt Lake food distribution sites.

Go to the MANNA Pantry at 20 W 2700 S, South Salt Lake. Pantry hours are Monday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM and Tuesday-Thursday 10:30 AM-3:00 PM; sign in by 2:45 PM. MANNA Market is Tuesday-Thursday 8:00-10:00 AM behind Central Park Community Center at 2797 S 300 E; sign up by 9:45 AM.

Food availability may depend on distribution supply. MOSAIC also lists employment consultations after food service, but this Food resource is for pantry and market access.
resources.name: MOSAIC MANNA Pantry and MANNA Market

resources.description: Magna FACT provides no-cost clothing, work clothing, baby clothing, household goods, grooming supplies, and food pantry help to Magna residents in need, with walk-in or call-ahead access for most material items.

Baby clothing, general adult and youth clothing, work/job clothing, household goods, personal grooming supplies, food pantry assistance, and related basic-needs services. Items are provided as available.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For Magna residents in need. Utah 211 lists no cost for clothing, baby clothing, work clothing, household goods, grooming supplies, and food pantry services.

**Population Served**

Low-income, at-risk children, youth, and families living in the City of Magna.

Walk in or call 801-250-4811 to check availability at 9113 W Magna Main St Ste 102, Magna. DHHS 211 lists food and clothing hours Tuesday-Friday 11:00 AM-4:00 PM; confirm the current schedule before travelling.

Services are for Magna residents in need and items depend on stock. Confirm current hours and any requested documentation. The public directory is evidence of the listed services, not confirmation of today's inventory.
resources.name: Magna FACT Food, Clothing and Household Assistance

resources.description: Magna United Communities That Care Coalition provides free 30-day UTA bus passes for Magna residents who meet program requirements and submit the online application with supporting documents.
resources.hours: Online application; email program contact for questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free 30-day UTA bus passes intended to reduce transportation barriers so Magna residents can access services, opportunities, and positive activities supported by the coalition.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be Magna residents and provide required supporting documents. Once the application is approved, the applicant receives a 30-day UTA bus pass at no cost.

**Population Served**
Youth and adults who live in Magna, Salt Lake County, and need help overcoming transportation barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the online application linked on the Magna United CTC resources page. For questions, contact Julia Wentz at jwentz@magna.utah.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This program is geographically limited to Magna residents and depends on application approval and program capacity. It provides a time-limited UTA bus pass, not paratransit, rideshare, or vehicle repair.
resources.name: Magna United CTC Free 30-Day UTA Bus Pass

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Same-day appointments for urgent medical conditions, adult family medicine, pediatric care, help obtaining medications, adult and childhood immunizations, onsite lab testing, X-ray, ultrasound, screening mammograms, women's health, diabetes specialty clinic, and healthy living classes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients must be uninsured, with no Medicaid, Medicare, or PCN, and have household income under 250% of the federal poverty level.

**Population Served**
Uninsured low-income patients in the greater Salt Lake area who can use the Millcreek clinic for non-emergency medical care.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online request appointment page or call 801-266-3700. The clinic is at 941 E 3300 S, Millcreek.

**Important Information to Know**
Maliheh does not provide emergency care, prenatal care, dental care, or controlled-substance prescriptions. Eligibility and appointment availability should be confirmed before sending a client.
resources.name: Maliheh Free Clinic

Citizenship preparation for permanent residents, including civics questions, the updated 128-question list, basic English speaking, reading, and writing, and step-by-step practice for the U.S. citizenship interview.

For permanent residents, also called Green Card holders, preparing for the English and civics portions of the citizenship interview. The listed class is free with a one-time $30 study-materials fee.

Adults in Salt Lake City preparing for naturalization, including learners at different English levels who benefit from a gradual and supportive class pace.

Use the Manos Unidas Foundation website or email info@manosunidasfoundation.org to confirm current class dates and registration. The citizenship class location is listed as 960 W 1700 S, Salt Lake City.

resources.description: Utah Medicaid Work Incentive is a Medicaid buy-in pathway for people who meet Social Security disability criteria, have earned income, and meet program income rules.
resources.hours: Use DWS medical benefits application/contact routes for current intake hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medicaid coverage pathway for working people with disabilities, allowing eligible workers to keep Medicaid by paying no premium or a calculated premium depending on income.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must meet Social Security disability criteria, have earned income, and have household income within the Medicaid Work Incentive limit. Premiums may apply when household net income is above 100% of the federal poverty level and below the program limit.

**Population Served**
Working Utahns with disabilities who need Medicaid coverage, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for medical benefits through DWS/Utah Medicaid and ask about Medicaid Work Incentive. For questions about applying, call Salt Lake County DWS at 801-526-0950 or toll-free 1-866-435-7414.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not free for everyone. DWS determines eligibility and any premium amount, and current income limits should be confirmed during application.
resources.name: Medicaid Work Incentive Program

resources.description: Utah Medicaid and DWS provide the statewide application route for Medicaid medical assistance and long-term-care Medicaid, including forms needed for nursing-home, long-term-care, and some waiver pathways.
resources.hours: DWS medical benefits phone line availability should be confirmed; applications are available online, by mail, fax, and in person.
resources.informationText:

Application access for Medicaid medical benefits and long-term-care Medicaid. People can apply online, by mail, by fax, or in person at a DWS office. Long-term-care Medicaid requires the Medical Only Application and Long Term Care Addendum.

**Eligibility Requirements**
DWS determines eligibility and may request proof such as identity, income, or other documents. Program eligibility depends on the specific Medicaid category, financial rules, and medical/long-term-care criteria.

**Population Served**
Utah residents applying for Medicaid medical assistance or long-term-care Medicaid, including Salt Lake County residents with disability-related care needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through DWS, mail the completed application to DWS PO Box 143245, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3245, fax to 801-526-9505 or 1-888-522-9505, or apply at a DWS office. For questions, call Salt Lake County 801-526-0950 or toll-free 1-866-435-7414.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an eligibility/application front door, not a direct disability-service provider. Specific waiver eligibility may also require the relevant waiver office or DSPD process.
resources.name: Medicaid and Long-Term Care Medicaid Application

resources.address: 860 East 4500 South, Suite 204, Salt Lake City, UT 84107
resources.description: Community Justice Advocates of Utah's Medical Debt Legal Advocate Program authorizes trained Medical Debt Community Justice Advocates to provide limited-scope legal advice, advocacy, negotiation help and Utah court-form assistance for medical debt issues; Holy Cross Ministries is listed as a local advocate partner.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Limited-scope medical debt legal advice and advocacy through trained Community Justice Advocates. Help may include identifying medical debts, explaining debt collection and court documents, advising on defenses and judgments, negotiating with providers or collectors and helping complete Utah court forms in collections cases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with medical debt legal issues in Utah. Services depend on connecting with an available trained advocate; individual advocate agencies may set additional eligibility or capacity limits.

**Population Served**
Utah residents, including Salt Lake County residents, who are anticipating medical debt, dealing with collections, facing court papers or handling a medical debt judgment or garnishment.

**How to Best Connect**
Use CJAU's Find an Advocate route on the medical-debt page. The assigned local partner lead is Holy Cross Ministries at 801-261-3440, 860 East 4500 South, Suite 204, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Advocates are trained nonlawyer Community Justice Advocates, not necessarily attorneys. Confirm current advocate availability and whether the issue is medical debt rather than a different consumer debt.
resources.name: Medical Debt Legal Advocate Program

resources.address: PO Box 143112, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3112
resources.description: Utah Medically Complex Children's Waiver offers Medicaid services, RN case management, respite, personal attendant services, and related supports for eligible medically complex children.
resources.hours: Online application available; call program for phone support hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Traditional Medicaid state plan benefits, RN case management, skilled nursing respite, routine respite, personal attendant services, and financial management services for enrolled children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Child must be 18 or younger, have 3 or more separate specialty physicians in addition to a primary care provider, have medical complexity involving 3 or more organ systems, have ADL milestone limitations, meet medical-score criteria, and have an SSI disability designation or state disability determination coordinated through the application process.

**Population Served**
Utah medically complex children and their caregivers, including Salt Lake County families.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the MCCW application link for fastest processing, or request paper application options. Call 801-538-6155 option 5 or 800-662-9651 option 5, fax 801-323-1593, or email mccw@utah.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Eligible applications are placed on a waitlist, and enrollment is based on highest confirmed acuity score as spots become available. The program is funded for a limited number of children.
resources.name: Medically Complex Children's Waiver

resources.description: Medicare Extra Help is a national Medicare program that helps people with limited income and resources pay Medicare Part D premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and other drug costs; applicants can also be linked to Medicare Savings Programs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Extra Help helps eligible Medicare beneficiaries with Medicare Part D drug plan premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and other prescription drug costs. Medicare states that applicants can apply for Extra Help and Medicare Savings Programs at the same time, with information sent to the state unless the applicant opts out.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Some people receive Extra Help automatically if they have full-benefit Medicaid, Medicare Savings Program help with Part B premiums, or SSI. Others can apply if income and resources are below current limits. Medicare lists 2026 income/resource limits and notes that limits may change each year.

**Population Served**
Medicare beneficiaries with limited income and resources, including Salt Lake County older adults and Medicare beneficiaries eligible because of disability.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the Medicare page's official Social Security application link, call Social Security at 1-800-772-1213, call Medicare at 1-800-633-4227 for Medicare questions, or contact Salt Lake County SHIP at 385-468-3200 for free help applying.

**Important Information to Know**
Extra Help is not cash paid to the person; it reduces Medicare drug costs when the person qualifies. Income/resource limits and 2027 prescription copays listed by Medicare should be checked for the current year when applying.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer support from people with lived experience, mental-health education and advocacy, statewide virtual peer support, group activities at a Salt Lake City drop-in center, homeless peer-support outreach in Salt Lake County, and 24/7 peer chat line/respite access.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Peer support is described as available to Utahns and to individuals and families affected by mental illness. Peer respite is for people who need a safe non-hospital place during crisis and meet respite availability and safety criteria.

**Population Served**
Utahns needing mental-health peer support, including individuals and families affected by mental illness and people experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mental Health America of Utah at 801-810-6522 or the 24/7 Peer Chat Line at 801-946-1374. The Salt Lake peer respite/drop-in address is listed by Utah 988 and MHA National as 150 South 600 East, Suite 3B.

This is peer support and respite, not emergency medical care. For immediate suicide or mental-health crisis support, use 988 or emergency services as appropriate.
resources.name: Mental Health America of Utah Peer Support and Drop-In Center

resources.description: Mercy Medical Angels provides no-cost medical travel assistance for qualifying longer-distance treatment trips, including gas cards, train or bus tickets, rideshare assistance in limited locations, and air transportation options for farther care.
resources.hours: Online travel request; delivery timing varies by assistance type.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost medical travel assistance for qualifying treatment trips. Ground support may include gas cards, train or bus tickets, or rideshare assistance depending on needs and location. Air transportation assistance may be available for farther treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ground assistance may be available when an appointment is 50 miles one way or travel to the same facility totals more than 100 miles per month. Gas-card applicants need access to a car, an appointment within the next 45 days, and income verification. Bus/train support may be considered for longer distances. Rideshare assistance is listed only for specific Virginia cities.

**Population Served**
Patients in the United States, including Utah residents, who need help reaching verified medical treatment and meet distance, timing, income, and travel-mode requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Start a travel request online through Mercy Medical Angels. Use the eligibility links on the website before applying if unsure.

**Important Information to Know**
Mercy Medical Angels does not provide local bus passes, subway, or light rail assistance. Gas cards can be virtual or mailed, are not reloadable, and must be used inside participating gas stations rather than at the pump. Assistance is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Mercy Medical Angels Medical Transportation Assistance

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Comprehensive primary health care for all ages, including well care, prenatal care, pediatrics, immunizations, women's health, family planning, geriatrics, acute and chronic illness care, treatment for diabetes, hypertension, and asthma, behavioral health, dental services, retinal eye exams, lab services, pharmacy, prescription assistance, specialty care coordination, and enrollment/application help. Substance-use services include medications for opioid-use disorder and Vivitrol; confirm current clinical availability.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Patients of all ages and backgrounds may use the clinic. Midtown accepts Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP, PCN, and most private medical insurance. Uninsured patients are welcome and charged at time of service on a discounted sliding fee scale based on income and family size.

**Population Served**

Families, children, adults, pregnant patients, uninsured patients, insured patients, and underserved residents in South Salt Lake and surrounding Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-486-0911 for an appointment. For clinical advice when the center is closed, call 866-821-3687. Call 911 for life-threatening emergencies.

**Important Information to Know**

This is not automatically free care; uninsured patients pay on a sliding fee scale. Services are available in English, Spanish, and other languages. Confirm prenatal availability, new-patient access, insurance, and exact costs when scheduling. Ask specifically about substance-use intake, medication availability and payer requirements when that is the need.
resources.name: Midtown CHC of South Salt Lake

resources.description: 24/7 national Military OneSource confidential non-medical counseling and support by phone, chat, video, or in person for eligible service members, Guard/Reserve members, immediate family, survivors, and service members/families up to 365 days post separation.
resources.hours: 24/7, 365 days a year
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Military OneSource offers free short-term, solution-focused, confidential non-medical counseling for relationship and marriage challenges, stress management, parenting issues, grief and loss, and deployment-related concerns. Counseling may occur in person, by phone, secure video, or secure online chat. Military OneSource also provides personalized help and navigation by phone and online.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible groups include active-duty service members and immediate family, National Guard and Reserve members regardless of activation status and immediate family listed in DEERS, designated Department of War expeditionary civilians and immediate family, service members and immediate family listed in DEERS for 365 days after separation, and surviving spouses who have not remarried and surviving children listed in DEERS. Children ages 6-17 may receive counseling in person or video only with required parent/caregiver involvement.

**Population Served**
Eligible military-connected households nationwide, including Salt Lake County service members, Guard/Reserve members, immediate family members, survivors, and recently separated service members/families within the 365-day eligibility window.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-342-9647 any time or use the Military OneSource live chat/account route online. Support is available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a universal veteran benefit for all former service members. Counseling does not diagnose or treat diagnosed mental-health conditions and is not for active suicidal or homicidal thoughts, sexual assault crisis, child abuse, domestic violence, substance abuse, or mental-health conditions requiring treatment. Use crisis or emergency services when needed.
resources.name: Military OneSource Confidential Counseling and Peer-to-Peer Support

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MST-related outpatient counseling, psychological assessment, medication evaluation and treatment, physical-health treatment related to MST, Vet Center counseling, and higher levels of VA care when needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VA states MST-related care can be available without service connection, proof that the MST occurred, or standard length-of-service requirements. Some former service members with Other Than Honorable discharge or short service may qualify; current service members may need a Department of Defense referral for some services.

**Population Served**
Veterans and many former service members affected by sexual assault or threatening sexual harassment during military service.

**How to Best Connect**
Call VA Salt Lake City Health Care at 801-582-1565 and ask for the MST coordinator, or contact a Vet Center and ask about MST-related counseling. In crisis, go to the nearest VA medical center regardless of enrollment or discharge status.

**Important Information to Know**
VA says people do not need to disclose MST details when first registering; they can ask for clinical evaluation and referral. Crisis needs should use 988 then press 1, 911, an emergency room, or the nearest VA medical center.
resources.name: Military Sexual Trauma (MST) Care and Salt Lake City MST Coordinators

Applicants must be at least 18 and submit the completed application, nonrefundable application fee, high school or GED transcript or qualifying degree, algebra or higher math documentation, DOT medical certification, and a current driving record. Outside lineman applicants must already have a valid unrestricted Class A CDL; traffic signal technician applicants must have a valid driver's license and later obtain a CDL once in the program.

People seeking electrical construction apprenticeship work in Utah, Idaho, Wyoming, Colorado, or Montana who can meet physical, travel, documentation, and licensing requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the MSLCAT Apply Now/TradeSchool route or call the West Jordan office at 801-562-2929. The Utah office address is 8781 South Redwood Road, Suite 150, West Jordan.

**Important Information to Know**
Selection depends on the formal application and interview process and available work. Outside lineman work can require extensive travel and physically demanding outdoor work. Published tuition is charged per hour worked, and application fees are nonrefundable.

resources.address: 5102 S Commerce Drive, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Public school district front door for Murray families with developmental or special education concerns, including preschool and Child Find questions for children in district boundaries.
resources.hours: District office regular hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:15 PM; summer hours Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-4:15 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
District contact point for families who need help starting special education or preschool-developmental evaluation questions for children in Murray City School District boundaries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children and students who live in Murray City School District boundaries and may need special education evaluation or services. Children under age 3 may be routed to early intervention rather than school-district preschool services.

**Population Served**
Murray City School District families with children or youth who may have developmental delays or disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the district office at 801-264-7400 or email info@murrayschools.org. The district office is at 5102 S Commerce Drive, Murray, and regular office hours are Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:15 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a countywide access point. Families outside Murray City School District should contact their resident school district or Utah early intervention front door. Exact preschool evaluation intake steps should be confirmed when calling.
resources.name: Murray City School District Child Find / Preschool Special Education Access

resources.address: 10 E 4800 S, Room 160, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Murray City's Utility Relief Program provides a limited one-time winter-season city utility credit for Murray residents who first qualify for HEAT and bring their HEAT award verification to Murray City Utility Billing.
resources.hours: City program runs during the winter season listed by the city, November to May, while funds last.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Limited assistance with Murray City utility bills in addition to the state HEAT benefit. Murray lists a one-time winter-season city award credited to eligible utility accounts after the household has qualified for HEAT.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be a Murray resident, qualify for the Home Energy Assistance Target (HEAT) Program, and provide written HEAT award verification to Murray City Utility Billing. City funds are limited and subject to annual appropriation.

**Population Served**
Murray City utility customers with low income who qualify for HEAT and have eligible city utility bills.

**How to Best Connect**
After receiving HEAT approval, bring the HEAT verification form showing the grant amount to Murray City Utility Billing, 10 E 4800 S, Room 160, Murray. Call Utility Billing at 801-264-2626 with questions. The city also lists HEAT application numbers 801-359-2444 and 866-205-4357.

**Important Information to Know**
The city credit is small, one-time, and available only while city funds remain. It does not replace applying for HEAT first.
resources.name: Murray City Utility Relief Program / Limited Assistance HEAT Program

resources.address: 494 East 5300 South, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Murray Park Church of Christ operates a Thursday food pantry in Murray and refers people to Utah Food Bank locations when its pantry is closed.
resources.hours: Thursday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community food pantry at Murray Park Church of Christ. The church page identifies it as a food pantry and points people to Utah Food Bank for alternate locations outside its hours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The opened church page does not list income, residency, or document requirements. Clients should call if they need to confirm documents or household limits.

**Population Served**
People in Murray and nearby Salt Lake County communities who can reach the pantry during Thursday hours.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 494 East 5300 South in Murray on Thursday between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM, or call 801-293-7000 before going.

**Important Information to Know**
Third-party lists also describe this as a Utah Food Bank extension. The church page is the clearest current public source for the Thursday schedule.
resources.name: Murray Park Church of Christ Food Pantry

resources.address: 10 East 4800 South, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Murray Police Department's Crime Victim Advocate Program assists victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking/harassment, child abuse, and other crimes with justice-system support, counseling resources, financial-assistance resources, and referrals.
resources.hours: Call Monday-Friday during business hours; 24-hour on-call coverage for police-related call-outs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Crime victim advocacy, including support through the justice system, accompaniment and support at some court hearings, counseling resources, criminal-justice information, financial-assistance resources, prevention work, and community referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for victims and family members in Murray Police-related matters. The official page lists domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking/harassment, child abuse, assault, homicide, robbery, DUI, suicide, and other traumatic loss.

**Population Served**
Victims of crime in Murray-related matters, including domestic violence and dating violence survivors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-284-4201 or 801-284-4203 Monday-Friday during business hours. For emergencies call 911; for non-emergency dispatch call 801-840-4000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is police-based advocacy, not confidential shelter advocacy. Murray also notes 24-hour on-call coverage for police-related call-outs.
resources.name: Murray Police Department Crime Victim Advocate Program

resources.address: 77 Franklin Street, 9th Floor, Boston, MA 02110
resources.description: My Immigrant Pathway is a nonprofit online legal resource for workers and employers with employment-based immigration questions. It offers free consultations and can evaluate whether an employer-sponsored green card may be possible, with low-cost legal services if a case moves forward.
resources.hours: Online scheduling is available through the website; no Utah office or public phone was verified.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Employment-based immigration consultations for workers and employers, including questions about whether a worker may qualify for an employer-sponsored green card. The program offers free consultations for general employment-based immigration questions and low-cost legal services for eligible cases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for workers and employers exploring employment-based immigration or employer green-card sponsorship. It is not a general family, humanitarian, detention, or removal-defense immigration clinic.

**Population Served**
Workers in the United States and employers with employment-based immigration questions, including Utah workers who can use the online scheduling route.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the worker page to schedule either a green-card eligibility review or a free consultation. Email Info@MyImmigrantPathway.org for follow-up questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The office address is in Boston and no Utah walk-in location or phone was verified. The employment-based green-card process can take well over a year and no outcome is guaranteed.
resources.name: My Immigrant Pathway Employment-Based Immigration Consultations

resources.address: PO Box 382, Springville, UT 84663
resources.description: My Story Matters offers Captain Your Story justice-involved programming designed to build confidence, empowerment, resiliency, relationships, future planning, and reentry success for incarcerated or formerly incarcerated participants and justice-involved families.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Captain Your Story justice-involved programming, a self-reflective course and community-support model focused on ownership of personal story, life skills, confidence, resilience, relationships, goal orientation, and reentry success. The program page includes a sign-up link.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page is for justice-involved participants and justice-involved families. It does not fully explain current openings, facility partners, cost, or whether every community applicant can enroll; contact the organization before promising access.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved people in Utah correctional or community settings and their families, including incarcerated participants, county-jail participants, and people transitioning after release.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Sign Up link on the justice-involved program page, call 801-477-7071, or email questions@mystorymatters.org. The organization lists a Springville PO Box rather than a Salt Lake walk-in site.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a reentry-preparation and personal-development program, not housing, benefits, legal representation, or clinical treatment. Confirm current enrollment route and whether the client can participate from their current facility or community location.
resources.name: My Story Matters Captain Your Story Justice-Involved Programming

resources.description: NALEO Educational Fund operates a toll-free bilingual hotline at 1-888-839-8682 that provides trusted information about naturalization and U.S. citizenship and can help eligible immigrants take next steps toward citizenship assistance.
resources.hours: Hotline listed 8:00 AM-8:00 PM; confirm time zone when calling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Bilingual hotline information about naturalization and U.S. citizenship, including citizenship assistance, trusted information, application support pathways, and civic-participation information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for lawful permanent residents and other eligible immigrants seeking information about the U.S. citizenship process. It is focused on citizenship and naturalization, not every immigration matter.

**Population Served**
Eligible immigrants, including Spanish-speaking and bilingual callers nationwide, who need citizenship information or help finding the next step.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 1-888-839-8682. NALEO's help page lists the hotline from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a national information and assistance hotline, not guaranteed legal representation. Local appointment availability depends on partner and clinic capacity.
resources.name: NALEO National Bilingual Citizenship Hotline

resources.address: 3269 South Main Street #230, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: NAMI Utah offers mental-health support groups, family support groups, education, classes, resources, and advocacy for individuals living with mental illness and their families or caregivers throughout Utah.
resources.hours: Program schedules vary by class or support group; call or check the website calendar.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family support groups, connection support groups, mental-health education, classes, resources, HelpLine-style navigation, advocacy, and suicide-prevention education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Support and education programs are for individuals living with mental illness and families or caregivers. Specific classes or groups may have registration, schedule, age, or audience requirements.

**Population Served**
Utah individuals experiencing mental illness, family members, caregivers, and supporters who need peer education, support, and mental-health resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-323-9900 or email information@namiut.org. The Salt Lake office is at 3269 South Main Street #230, Salt Lake City. Use the website to find current support groups and classes.

**Important Information to Know**
NAMI is support and education, not clinical therapy, psychiatry, or crisis response. For crisis, use 988 or emergency services.
resources.name: NAMI Utah Support Groups and Classes

resources.address: Salt Lake City, UT
resources.description: NU HUEMAN's Liferaft Path is a Salt Lake City reentry support program focused on financial education, credit repair, debt negotiation training, online learning, in-person workshops, and personalized coaching for formerly incarcerated people.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial education, credit repair, debt negotiation training, budgeting, credit understanding, debt management, online learning, in-person workshops, and personalized coaching for reentry financial stability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is designed specifically for people who were formerly incarcerated. The website does not publish detailed eligibility, documentation requirements, fees, or schedule.

**Population Served**
Formerly incarcerated people seeking financial stability and reentry support in Salt Lake City or through online/in-person programming when available.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 425-238-9563 or email liferaftpath@gmail.com. Ask about current workshop dates, whether coaching is remote or in person, fees, and enrollment steps.

**Important Information to Know**
The website is sparse. Do not assume immediate openings, no-cost service, or a regular workshop schedule until confirmed by the program contact.
resources.name: NU HUEMAN Liferaft Path

resources.address: 1100 Wilson Blvd., Suite 900, Arlington, VA 22209
resources.description: Free NVLSP pro bono legal help for veterans and service members with four Department of Defense matters: discharge upgrades, medical retirement, Combat-Related Special Compensation, and TSGLI claims.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lawyers Serving Warriors offers free legal help for four Department of Defense issue areas: discharge upgrades, medical retirement, Combat-Related Special Compensation, and Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance Traumatic Injury Protection claims.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans from all eras and veterans located anywhere who need help with one of the four listed DOD matters. The program does not accept VA claims, criminal law, family law, real estate, debt, or other unrelated issues.

**Population Served**
Veterans and service members nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents who can use the online application and remote intake.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from the Lawyers Serving Warriors page. For help applying, email LSW.intake@nvlsp.org or call 202-265-8305 option 5 and leave a detailed message naming the DOD matter.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general legal-aid program and is not a referral service. It is limited to the four DOD issue areas named by NVLSP.
resources.name: NVLSP Lawyers Serving Warriors

resources.description: Nar-Anon Family Groups provides 12-step peer support for relatives and friends of people affected by drug addiction, with in-person, virtual, and Narateen meeting finders on the official site.
resources.hours: Meeting times vary by group; use the official meeting finder and contact-email instructions for virtual meetings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer-led Nar-Anon meetings for families and friends of people with drug addiction, plus Narateen meeting listings where available. The site includes in-person and virtual meeting finders.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people affected by someone else's addiction. Virtual meeting links generally require contacting the meeting email listed in the meeting table.

**Population Served**
Family members and friends of people with substance-use disorders, including Salt Lake County residents who can attend online meetings or search for Utah-area meetings.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Nar-Anon website meeting finder for in-person meetings or the virtual meeting pages for online meetings. For virtual meetings, contact the listed meeting email to receive the meeting link.

**Important Information to Know**
Nar-Anon is peer support, not treatment for the person using substances and not a crisis service. Narateen availability should be checked on the official Narateen meeting page before referring a youth.
resources.name: Nar-Anon Family Groups

resources.address: 1000 Ability Way, Park City, UT 84060
resources.description: National Ability Center is a Park City adaptive recreation provider offering year-round sport, recreation, camps, equestrian, cycling, ski/snowboard, rafting, and outdoor programs for youth and adults with disabilities and related needs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Year-round adaptive sport, recreation, camps, equestrian, cycling, ski/snowboard, rafting, and outdoor programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility, fees, scholarships, transportation, and openings vary by program. Confirm current program requirements before registration.

**Population Served**
Youth and adults with physical, cognitive, developmental, mental health, and neurodiversity-related needs who can participate in Park City or other listed Utah program locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 435-649-3991 or use the National Ability Center website. The main address is 1000 Ability Way, Park City, UT 84060.

**Important Information to Know**
Salt Lake County residents generally must travel unless a specific program offers transportation or offsite access. Confirm costs and scholarships before referral.
resources.name: National Ability Center Adaptive Recreation and Outdoor Programs

resources.address: 1000 Ability Way, Park City, UT 84060
resources.description: National Ability Center military program offering adaptive recreational, rehabilitative, and therapeutic activities, lessons, camps, and adventure programs for active-duty service members and veterans in Park City and other Utah sites.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
National Ability Center welcomes members of the Armed Forces and veterans from every era to participate in recreational, rehabilitative, and therapeutic programs. Military offerings include inclusive camps, ongoing lessons, specialized camps, cycling, Nordic skiing, retreats, hiking, and other adaptive recreation programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs are for active-duty service members and veterans from every era. Activity-specific eligibility, registration, health/safety requirements, fees, and openings vary by program.

**Population Served**
Active-duty service members and veterans who can participate in Park City or other Utah program sites, including Salt Lake County residents able to travel to Park City.

**How to Best Connect**
Register through the National Ability Center participant registration link, call 435-649-3991, or visit/contact 1000 Ability Way, Park City, UT 84060. Confirm the exact activity, schedule, cost, and scholarship before registering.

**Important Information to Know**
The military page states that, in most cases, service members are provided access to recreation and adventure programs at no cost and scholarships are available for accompanying family members. Costs and availability should still be confirmed for each activity.
resources.name: National Ability Center Military Programs

resources.description: The National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline provides 24/7 domestic violence advocacy for Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing survivors by video phone, live chat, instant messenger, and email through a partnership of the National Domestic Violence Hotline and ADWAS.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
24/7 domestic violence hotline advocacy for Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing survivors. Advocates can provide support, crisis intervention, education about domestic violence, safety planning, and community resources/referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people affected by domestic violence who are Deaf, DeafBlind, or hard of hearing. Salt Lake County residents can use the national remote service.

**Population Served**
Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing survivors of domestic violence and people supporting them.

**How to Best Connect**
Video phone: 855-812-1001. Instant messenger: DeafHotline. Email: hotline@adwas.org. Live chat access is available through the linked Deaf Services page.

**Important Information to Know**
The Hotline does not provide direct financial assistance, hotel vouchers, or transportation vouchers, but can connect people to community resources. If internet use is unsafe, consider a safer device or call method.
resources.name: National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline

resources.address: 266 Elizabeth Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: National Federation of the Blind of Utah is a peer-led statewide affiliate focused on self-confidence, self-determination, advocacy, and integration of blind people into society, with Salt Lake City contact information.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Blind peer support, advocacy, and community programs focused on self-confidence, self-determination, and integration of blind people into society.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Exact current chapters, meetings, and direct assistance offerings should be confirmed with the affiliate.

**Population Served**
Blind Utahns, including Salt Lake County residents, and people seeking peer-led blindness advocacy or community connection.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-463-6632 or use the National Federation of the Blind of Utah website. The listed address is 266 Elizabeth Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84102.

**Important Information to Know**
This is distinct from state blind services. Confirm current meeting schedules and whether the affiliate can help with the specific request.
resources.name: National Federation of the Blind of Utah Blind Peer Support, Advocacy, and Community Programs

resources.address: 3707 N Canyon Rd. Ste 1D, Provo, UT 84604
resources.description: National Kidney Foundation of Utah and Idaho lists medical transportation assistance among patient programs for kidney patients in Utah and Idaho; Salt Lake County residents can inquire by phone about current help and application steps.

**Services Offered**

Medical transportation assistance for kidney patients is listed as part of local patient programs, along with emergency financial aid and scholarships. The sealed evidence does not establish whether help is direct rides, reimbursement, gas cards or grant assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For kidney patients in Utah and Idaho. Specific diagnosis rules, income rules, documentation, covered trip types and funding limits were not established in the sealed evidence.

**Population Served**

Utah and Idaho kidney patients, including Salt Lake County residents, who need help reaching kidney-related medical care.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-226-5111 and ask specifically about patient programs, medical transportation assistance, current funding and how to apply. The listed office is in Provo.

The located page was a fundraising/event page rather than a full intake page. Confirm current availability, required documentation, covered transportation expenses and whether payments are made to a provider, vendor or patient before promising assistance.

resources.description: The National Maternal Mental Health Hotline provides free, confidential, 24/7 phone, text, and chat support, resources, and referrals for pregnant and postpartum people and their families.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emotional support, maternal mental-health resources, local support-group and organization connections, and referrals to health care professionals when more care is needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to pregnant people, people who recently had a baby, partners, and family members. No insurance or referral is required.

**Population Served**
Expecting parents, new parents, postpartum people, partners, and family members, including Salt Lake County residents who can use national phone, text, or chat support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 1-833-TLC-MAMA (1-833-852-6262), or use the chat link on the HRSA hotline page. TTY users can use relay services.

**Important Information to Know**
The hotline provides support and referrals, not in-person treatment or emergency response. Counselors speak English and Spanish, and interpreter support is available for many additional languages.
resources.name: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
resources.phone: Call or text 1-833-TLC-MAMA (1-833-852-6262); TTY relay 711 then 1-833-852-6262

resources.address: 5296 S Commerce Drive, Suite 204, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: National Tongan American Society provides citizenship workshops, Tongan and Samoan translation services, and Tongan passport filing assistance from its Murray office, with appointments preferred.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-3:00 PM; Fridays by appointment only; appointments preferred.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Citizenship workshops to help immigrants become citizens, Tongan and Samoan translation services, and Tongan passport filing assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For immigrants seeking citizenship workshop support and community members needing listed Tongan, Samoan, or Tongan passport services. Appointment availability and workshop dates should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Pacific Islander, Tongan, Samoan, and other immigrant community members in Salt Lake County who need citizenship, translation, or Tongan passport assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-467-8712, email info@ntasutah.org, use the contact form, or visit 5296 S Commerce Drive, Suite 204, Murray. Office hours are listed Monday through Thursday from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM, Fridays by appointment only, and appointments are preferred.

**Important Information to Know**
Workshop schedules are not listed on the services page, so call before sending a client. Translation and passport help are not the same as immigration legal representation.
resources.name: National Tongan American Society Citizenship Workshops and Translation Services

resources.description: Free national phone support for women's health and breastfeeding questions, answered in English or Spanish by health information specialists trained as breastfeeding peer counselors.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-6:00 PM Eastern Time; closed on federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free phone information and support for women's health questions and breastfeeding concerns, including questions about milk supply and whether a baby is getting enough during breastfeeding.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open nationally by phone. No insurance, referral, or appointment is required.

**Population Served**
People with women's health or breastfeeding questions, including Salt Lake County residents who can use a national phone helpline.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-994-9662 during listed helpline hours. Support is available in English and Spanish.

**Important Information to Know**
The helpline is an information resource and does not diagnose, treat, prescribe medication, provide medical advice, or refer to specialists. For a medical emergency, call 911 or go to an emergency room.
resources.name: National Women's Health and Breastfeeding Helpline

resources.description: Navajo Nation General Assistance is a federally funded temporary financial-support program, now managed by the Department for Self-Reliance, for eligible Navajo tribal members living in Arizona, New Mexico, or Utah who need help with essential needs such as rent, utilities, and food.
resources.hours: Call or use the Navajo Nation DSR/Division for Children and Family Services contact routes to confirm office routing and application steps.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary financial assistance for essential needs such as rent, utilities, and food, along with case management, an Individual Self-Sufficiency Plan, and employment/training service connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says Navajo tribal members living in New Mexico, Arizona, or Utah will be referred to the Department for Self-Reliance to apply for General Assistance. The DSR team determines qualification.

**Population Served**
Navajo tribal members living in Utah, Arizona, or New Mexico, including Utah residents who can use the phone or DSR routing process.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 928-871-6556 or email info@ndcfs.org, and ask for the Department for Self-Reliance General Assistance application route. Use the DSR office locations link if an in-person office is required.

**Important Information to Know**
Benefit-payment details on the public page are incomplete. Applicants should confirm routing, documents, and whether an off-reservation Salt Lake County address affects processing before relying on assistance.
resources.name: Navajo Nation Department for Self-Reliance General Assistance

resources.description: Needs Beyond Medicine's Relief Program provides financial assistance grants for Utah residents undergoing active cancer treatment, supporting essential non-medical living expenses such as groceries, transportation, rent, and utilities.
resources.hours: Online application; the page states applicants do not need to contact the organization after applying and that selected applicants are contacted by phone or email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance grants for essential non-medical living expenses, including groceries, transportation, rent, and utilities, for people in active cancer treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be Utah residents, undergoing active cancer treatment, submit a complete application, and provide a signed letter on facility letterhead from an oncology nurse, doctor, or hospital social worker verifying diagnosis, current treatment plan, and financial need.

**Population Served**
Utah residents undergoing active cancer treatment who have essential living-expense needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the online Relief Program application and upload the required treatment verification letter. Questions can be sent to ReliefProgram@NeedsBeyondMedicine.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The 2026 application lists a requested grant amount up to $575. Missing components will prevent review, and the page says applicants should wait for phone or email communication after applying.
resources.name: Needs Beyond Medicine Relief Program

resources.address: 1031 W Center St, Suite 302, Orem, UT 84057
resources.description: TANF family housing and homeless-prevention assistance lead for families with children, including possible rent, deposit, utility, and related housing-stabilization help.
resources.hours: Office hours listed by NeighborWorks Mountain Country Home Solutions: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-6 PM; closed Friday-Sunday.
resources.informationText:

NeighborWorks Mountain Country Home Solutions is listed by DWS/partner sources for TANF family housing services that can help eligible families in short-term housing crises with deposits, rent, utilities, mortgage payments, back payments, and planning to stay housed.

The DWS TANF Family Housing program is for TANF-eligible families with a dependent child under age 18 and a short-term crisis. Providers must verify eligibility and may require participation with DWS employment counseling.

**Population Served**
Families with children who meet TANF family-housing eligibility and need help stabilizing housing. Salt Lake County use should be confirmed when calling because the provider office is in Orem.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-375-5820 and ask specifically about TANF Family Housing or homeless-prevention assistance for a Salt Lake County family. The office address is 1031 W Center St, Suite 302, Orem.

This is not guaranteed rental assistance. Funding, geography, eligibility, and documentation should be confirmed before relying on it. The organization's own website confirms housing counseling and affordable-housing work; specific TANF details are supported by DWS and partner housing-resource listings.
resources.name: NeighborWorks Mountain Country Home Solutions TANF Family Housing / Homeless Prevention

resources.address: 622 W 500 N, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: NeighborWorks Salt Lake CareerWorks offers adult workforce education, including medical training and skilled-trades pre-apprenticeship pathways for people preparing for higher-wage career entry.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-6:00 PM; Friday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CareerWorks offers workforce education for adults, including medical tracks such as community interpreter, CNA, and phlebotomy, plus skilled-trades pre-apprenticeship pathways in electrical and energy systems, welding and metalwork, HVAC/R, plumbing, utility line construction, heavy equipment, and related trades.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The posted pre-apprenticeship requirements include age 18 or older, high school diploma or GED or willingness to obtain one, reliable transportation and driver's license, English proficiency, physical ability to lift 25-50 pounds and use tools, ability to pass a drug test, and U.S. citizenship or work authorization.

**Population Served**
Adults in the Salt Lake area who are ready to train for health care or skilled-trades work and can meet program requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply Now link on the CareerWorks page for the pathway of interest, or call NeighborWorks Salt Lake at 801-539-1590. The Salt Lake office is at 622 W 500 N.

**Important Information to Know**
Training dates, costs, and cohort openings were not fully posted on the public page. Confirm current availability, cost, and required documents before applying.
resources.name: NeighborWorks Salt Lake CareerWorks

resources.address: 622 West 500 North, Salt Lake City, UT 84116; Murray office: 4843 S Poplar Street, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: NeighborWorks Salt Lake provides confidential financial counseling, budgeting help, credit building, debt-management relief, financial education, Individual Development Accounts, and matched-savings support.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-6:00 PM; Friday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial guidance counseling, budgeting help, credit building, debt-management relief, financial literacy classes, free online courses, Individual Development Accounts with up to a 2-to-1 match, and Utah Saves support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by service. IDA and matched-savings programs may have income, savings-goal, class, coaching, and documentation requirements. Debt-management services require review of the person's debts and ability to participate.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in Salt Lake County and Utah who need help with budgeting, credit, debt, financial education, or matched savings.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Started link on the financial education page or call 801-539-1590. Offices are at 622 West 500 North in Salt Lake City and 4843 S Poplar Street in Murray; listed hours are Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-6:00 PM.
