resources.description: Project Reality provides opioid-use and other substance-use treatment integrated with primary care and mental-health services, including methadone, buprenorphine, naltrexone, counseling, and medication hours in Salt Lake City and Murray.
resources.hours: Salt Lake Downtown medication hours: Monday-Friday 6:30 AM-noon; Saturday-Sunday 7:00-8:30 AM. Murray medication hours: Monday-Friday 6:30 AM-noon; weekends and holidays closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medication treatment for opioid-use disorder and other SUD care, including methadone, buprenorphine, naltrexone, addiction treatment, counseling, primary care, mental-health services, harm reduction, and prevention.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults with opioid-use disorder or other substance-use disorders seeking recovery and wellness. The provider says no one is turned away regardless of income, insurance status, or ability to pay.

**Population Served**
Adults in Salt Lake City, Murray, and Salt Lake County seeking MOUD and integrated care for opioid use disorder or other substance-use disorders.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-881-0170 for general contact and Murray, or 801-364-8080 for Salt Lake Downtown medication hours. Email Project@projectreality.net for general inquiries.

**Important Information to Know**
Medication hours differ by location. Confirm intake location, first-dose requirements, payment, and documentation before sending a client.
resources.name: Project Reality Opioid Treatment and Integrated Care

resources.description: Project Water ASSIST helps qualifying Salt Lake City Public Utilities customers with monthly utility bills when household income is at or below 150% of the federal poverty line and there is an active disconnection notice.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Water and public-utilities bill assistance for qualifying Salt Lake City Public Utilities customers through Project Water ASSIST, managed with the Salt Lake City Chapter of The Salvation Army.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be Salt Lake City Public Utilities customers, have household income at or below 150% of the federal poverty line, and have an active disconnection notice.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City Public Utilities customers who meet income and disconnection-notice requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Call The Salvation Army Salt Lake City Chapter at 801-969-0526 or Salt Lake City Public Utilities at 801-483-6900. Use the Project Water ASSIST application link from the Salt Lake City Public Utilities water-bill assistance page.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance is case-by-case and donation-funded. It is limited to Salt Lake City Public Utilities customers, not every water provider in Salt Lake County.
resources.name: Project Water ASSIST

resources.address: South Salt Lake Co-Op / South Salt Lake program sites; see program page
resources.description: Free 9-session early-childhood and parenting program for caregivers of children ages 0-3, including expecting parents, with meals, child care during sessions, local experts, resources, community connection, and possible My529 scholarship account for children 0-5 after full attendance.
resources.hours: 2026 cohort listed Saturdays, September 12-November 14, 2026; 2027 dates pending on the page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Nine-session program with parenting tools, early-development education, local experts, resource connections, meals, and child care during sessions for children ages 9 months to 12 years. Children under 9 months stay with the caregiver.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Free and open to caregivers of children ages 0-3, including new and expecting parents, grandparents, and foster parents. Capacity is limited to about 20 families per cohort, and families who can attend all sessions are prioritized.

**Population Served**
Caregivers of infants and toddlers in South Salt Lake and nearby Salt Lake County communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply using the online application link on the Promise Baby & You page. The 2026 cohort is listed for Saturdays September 12-November 14, 2026; 2027 dates and application information were listed as coming soon.

**Important Information to Know**
Cohort dates and capacity change. The page says families attending all workshops may have a My529 scholarship account opened with $500 for a child ages 0-5, with SSN or Tax ID required.
resources.name: Promise South Salt Lake Baby & You

resources.address: 220 E Morris Ave. St. 350, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Promise South Salt Lake's Community Baby Closet helps families with children ages 0-5 access new or gently used baby clothing, shoes, books, diapers, wipes, and toys through Early Childhood Family Support appointments.
resources.hours: Appointments required or recommended for family support; call or email before visiting. General contact listed at 801-483-6057.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Baby Closet with new or gently used baby clothing, shoes, books, diapers, wipes, and toys. Early Childhood Family Support can also provide individual appointments, child-development guidance, community-resource navigation, and practical steps for accessing services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Early Childhood Family Support page is for families with children ages 0-5. Exact closet limits, appointment requirements, and inventory should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
South Salt Lake and nearby Salt Lake County families with young children ages 0-5.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-483-6057 or email lmiramontes@sslc.gov or promise@sslc.gov to ask for an Early Childhood Family Support appointment and Community Baby Closet access. The listed address is 220 E Morris Ave. St. 350, South Salt Lake.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not described as open shopping hours; families are connected through individual appointments and available community closet supplies. Inventory changes with donations.
resources.name: Promise South Salt Lake Community Baby Closet

resources.address: 220 E Morris Ave, Suite 350, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: South Salt Lake housing-navigation program connecting community members to homeownership education, foreclosure guidance, rental/eviction resources, down-payment information, and related housing supports.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Promise South Salt Lake's Housing Navigator helps eligible home seekers navigate homebuying, connects community members to affordable-housing resources and education, and points renters facing eviction or rental-assistance needs to a liaison team and partner resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the specific support. Some linked programs have city, income, homeowner, buyer, or utility-account rules; the South Salt Lake utility-assistance portion is limited to South Salt Lake residents with qualifying utility billing and income/crisis criteria.

**Population Served**
South Salt Lake community members, homeowners, aspiring homeowners, renters seeking resource navigation, and households dealing with housing instability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-483-6057 or email promise@sslc.gov. Ask for the Housing Navigator or Liaison Team depending on whether the need is homeownership/foreclosure, rental assistance, eviction, or utility-assistance navigation.

**Important Information to Know**
This is primarily navigation and connection to resources; it is not a guaranteed rent fund or shelter. Some services are referrals to countywide or statewide partners rather than direct Promise funding.
resources.name: Promise South Salt Lake Housing Navigation

resources.address: 2530 S 500 E, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Promise South Salt Lake's SSL Co-Op is a city-run community support site where people can meet with staff and access free or low-cost classes and partner programs, including digital literacy, workforce advancement, English/language skills, financial literacy, and small business support.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-8:00 PM; Friday 9:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
One-on-one community engagement support plus free or low-cost classes and partner programs. Education-related offerings include digital literacy, workforce advancement, English and language skills, financial literacy, art programs, and small business support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page describes programs for the community and does not list a strict eligibility screen. Some partner classes may have their own rules, registration steps, or schedule limits.

**Population Served**
South Salt Lake and nearby Salt Lake County community members who can use the SSL Co-Op in person.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit the SSL Co-Op at 2530 S 500 E, South Salt Lake, or call 801-412-3294. Staff are available during posted weekday and evening hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a mixed community-support access point, not a single school. Specific class dates and partner requirements should be checked on the current calendar or by calling staff.
resources.name: Promise South Salt Lake SSL Co-Op Community Support and Education Programs

resources.description: Utah nonprofit with online intake for affordable immigration services, including a published resident card renewal service to renew or replace a lost, stolen, or expired green card, plus DACA renewal and other immigration forms.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Proseyo offers affordable immigration services with online intake. Document-related services include resident card renewal to renew or replace a lost, stolen, or expired green card, DACA renewal and work permit renewal, citizenship and naturalization help, petition for immigrant relative, U visa, VAWA, fiancé visa, and USCIS-related forms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the immigration service requested and USCIS requirements. Proseyo reviews intake information before accepting a request.

**Population Served**
Utah immigrants and families seeking affordable immigration application and document help. Services are available in Spanish, Portuguese, and English.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Proseyo website's Get Started or Schedule a Callback route. After intake, Proseyo says it reviews requests and contacts the client, usually within up to 48 hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Published prices are base service fees and do not include possible USCIS fees. Proseyo states its immigration specialists can only be reached by scheduled appointment and that clients must sign and submit forms to USCIS themselves.
resources.name: Proseyo Affordable Immigration Services

resources.address: Department of Workforce Services - Fair Hearings, PO Box 143245, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3245
resources.description: Utah Department of Workforce Services Fair Hearings is the public administrative-hearing route for SNAP, financial assistance, medical, child care, General Assistance, training, and other DWS-administered benefit actions a person disagrees with.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Administrative fair-hearing requests for DWS public-assistance and training-service decisions, including SNAP, financial assistance, medical, child care, General Assistance, training, and other DWS-administered programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people affected by an action from the Department of Workforce Services or Department of Health. The person should follow the hearing rights and deadline information on the notice they received.

**Population Served**
Utah public-benefit applicants or recipients, including Salt Lake County residents, who disagree with a covered benefit action.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Hearing Rights and Request for Hearing form and mail, fax, email, or deliver it to DWS. Phone: 877-837-3247. Fax: 877-824-6534. Email: fairhearings@utah.gov. Mail: DWS Fair Hearings, PO Box 143245, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3245.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an appeal process, not legal representation. A person may bring an attorney or another representative, but DWS states it cannot find or pay for an attorney. Deadlines depend on the notice.
resources.name: Public Assistance and Training Services Fair Hearings

resources.description: Utah's Purple Heart Tuition Waiver provides Purple Heart recipients a tuition waiver at Utah public institutions of higher learning, up to and including a master's degree.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tuition waiver at public institutions of higher learning in Utah for eligible Purple Heart recipients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
UDVMA states the veteran must be a Purple Heart recipient and must submit proof of Purple Heart status to the state institution they are attending. The benefit can be used toward a degree up to and including a master's degree.

**Population Served**
Purple Heart recipients attending Utah public higher-education institutions.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the admissions office or veterans/military benefits office at the Utah public institution the student attends or plans to attend.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a tuition waiver, not cash assistance. Campus procedures and degree-program limits should be confirmed with the school.
resources.name: Purple Heart Tuition Waiver

resources.address: 213 W 4800 S, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: RCCG House of His Glory Pantry is listed in public resource guides as a Murray food pantry; the church's direct public phone and address match the listed pantry location.
resources.hours: Public food-resource listings conflict; one current list says Saturday noon-3:00 PM. Call before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free weekly food pantry listed at Redeemed Christian Church of God - House of His Glory.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah DHHS lists photo ID and proof of address for this pantry. Other current public listings may differ, so clients should confirm documents and limits before going.

**Population Served**
People in Murray and nearby Salt Lake County communities who can reach the pantry.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the church at 801-889-1751 or email info@rccgslc.org. The pantry address is 213 W 4800 S, Murray, UT 84107. Because pantry phones and hours differ across public lists, confirm the Saturday distribution before going.

**Important Information to Know**
The church homepage confirms the church identity, address, and phone but does not describe the pantry. Utah DHHS and food-resource lists support the pantry listing but conflict on phone numbers.
resources.name: RCCG House of His Glory Pantry

resources.address: P.O. Box 381, Pleasant View, TN 37146
resources.description: Faith-based 12-week Military REBOOT trauma-healing course for veterans, active-duty military, and their families, with course signup and MyREBOOT online trauma-healing hub access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Military REBOOT is a 12-week, faith-based, peer-led course addressing service-related trauma. The program includes weekly course meetings, a field guide workbook, MyREBOOT online trauma-healing hub access, and peer discussion.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans, active-duty military, and their families. Participants select or request a Military REBOOT location/course through the sign-up process. A Utah in-person course was not confirmed from the public page.

**Population Served**
Veterans, active-duty military members, spouses, and families affected by service-related trauma.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Sign Up to Join a Course/Register Now form on the Military REBOOT page. Ask about virtual options or the nearest current course before planning in-person attendance.

**Important Information to Know**
This is faith-based and rooted in Christian language, though REBOOT says participants do not have to share that faith. It is a course, not clinical treatment or emergency crisis care. The page lists a $25 participant cost, with many groups covering the cost for participants.
resources.name: REBOOT Recovery Military REBOOT

resources.address: 479 E 2100 S, Unit C, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: RISE Culinary Institute provides free 12-week hands-on culinary training for refugee and immigrant women from low-income families, with kitchen skills, food safety, soft skills, mentorship, employer connections, paid internships, and career support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free 12-week hands-on culinary training covering core culinary skills, food safety, kitchen etiquette, menu planning, mentorship, soft skills, employer connections, paid internships, and career or business support after graduation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is focused on refugee and immigrant women from low-income families. The application asks about age 18 or older, U.S. work eligibility, unemployment or underemployment, drug-free status, ability to stand and lift with reasonable accommodation, reliable transportation, and interest in food or hospitality work. Current cohort dates should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Refugee and immigrant women in the Salt Lake City area who are seeking culinary employment training and career support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply Now link on the RISE Culinary Institute website. The listed training address is 479 E 2100 S, Unit C, Salt Lake City. No public phone number was verified on the checked pages.

**Important Information to Know**
The home page is current and describes the program, but the application form still displayed older cohort options in the page text. Confirm the next cohort and application deadline through the online apply/contact route before referral.
resources.name: RISE Culinary Institute Free Culinary Training for Refugee and Immigrant Women

resources.description: RISE Services Utah provides developmental-disability supports including day, employment, family, residential, respite, and supported living services through Utah locations, including a Salt Lake County-area office in Draper.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day services, after-school and summer programs, employment services, family services, professional parenting, adult host homes, respite care, residential services, and supported living.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The website does not list complete eligibility or funding rules. Call the appropriate Utah location to ask whether DSPD/Medicaid waiver authorization, private pay, or another funding route is required.

**Population Served**
Children, adults, and families needing person-centered developmental-disability and community-based supports in Utah.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official locations page and call the Draper office at 801-208-1031 for Salt Lake County-area service questions. The submitted West Jordan phone was not confirmed on the official locations page.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted West Jordan address conflicts with the current official locations page, which lists Draper as the Salt Lake County-area location. Confirm the correct intake site before arranging travel.
resources.name: RISE Services Utah Developmental Disability Services

resources.address: 12257 S Business Park Dr, Draper, UT 84020
resources.description: RISE Services Utah provides employment services for adults with developmental disabilities, including job search, resume and interview preparation, job development, supported employment, customized employment, job coaching, and life-skills restoration.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Employment Specialists help adults with developmental disabilities find and sustain meaningful work. Services include job search, resume creation, interview preparation, supported job-based training, supported employment, customized employment, training and coaching, on-the-job coaching, vocational assessments, job development, and life-skills restoration.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. RISE states it partners with USOR and DSPD and that supported employment can be funded through those agencies. People working with a VR counselor may request RISE as a preferred provider.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities in Utah, including Salt Lake County-area residents using the Draper location route.

**How to Best Connect**
Call RISE employment services at 801-373-1197 for general service questions, or call the Draper location at 801-208-1031 for Salt Lake County-area access. Ask whether USOR, DSPD, Medicaid waiver, or private-pay authorization is needed.

**Important Information to Know**
The employment page lists 801-373-1197 for services while the locations page lists Draper at 801-208-1031. Use phone confirmation before travel or provider selection.
resources.name: RISE Services Utah Employment Services for Adults With Disabilities

resources.address: 2035 South 1300 East, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
resources.description: Rape Recovery Center provides no-cost trauma-informed services for sexual-assault survivors, including intake assessment, advocacy, short-term case management, individual therapy, healing/support groups, forensic-exam accompaniment, and 24-hour helplines.
resources.hours: Office Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM; Utah Sexual Violence HelpLine available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost trauma-informed services for sexual-assault survivors at any stage of healing, including intake assessment, individual therapy, healing and support groups, advocacy, short-term case management, forensic-exam accompaniment, Crime Victims Reparations help, and criminal-justice advocacy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For survivors of sexual assault. The center states it assists survivors regardless of gender, race, religion, income, language, ability, ethnicity, sexual orientation, sex-work involvement, or immigration status.

**Population Served**
Sexual-assault survivors in Salt Lake County and Tooele County, including survivors needing counseling, advocacy, or healing support after recent or past assault.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-467-7282 or use the online intake appointment link. For 24-hour sexual-violence support, call 801-736-4356; Spanish 24-hour support is 801-924-0860. Office address is 2035 South 1300 East, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a sexual-violence survivor resource, not general counseling for unrelated issues and not an emergency shelter. Email is monitored Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM, and the site says to expect a response within one business day.
resources.name: Rape Recovery Center Survivor Therapy and Support

resources.description: Rasa Legal provides Utah record-clearance screening and low-cost flat-rate legal services for expungement and 402 reductions, including an online eligibility tool, optional legal review, representation, and direct phone contact.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online Utah criminal-record eligibility screening, legal review, expungement representation, and 402 reduction representation. Rasa's Utah page describes full legal representation for eligible expungement or 402 reduction matters.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with Utah criminal records who may qualify for expungement or a 402 reduction. The online tool can show record-clearance options, but attorney review determines available legal strategy.

**Population Served**
People with Utah criminal records who want to reduce housing, employment, licensing, or background-check barriers through record clearance.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online eligibility tool on the Utah page or call 385-376-4701 with questions. The screening tool does not require hiring Rasa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not usually free representation. The Utah page lists a $25 legal review and flat-rate $500 services for expungement or 402 reduction, with filing fees included, but clients should confirm current pricing and case fit before relying on those amounts.
resources.name: Rasa Legal Utah Record Clearance, Expungement, and 402 Reduction Services

resources.address: 873 W Baxter Drive, South Jordan, UT 84095; 3006 South Highland Drive, Suite 206, Salt Lake City, UT 84106
resources.description: Mental-health practice offering postpartum intensive outpatient therapy, outpatient counseling for postpartum/family concerns, and in-person or telehealth appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Postpartum Intensive Outpatient Program meeting three times a week for new moms, individual and family/postpartum counseling, and broader therapy services for mood, trauma, teen/youth, behavioral, couples, and family concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must complete intake/scheduling with Reach Counseling. Insurance, self-pay costs, Medicaid/Optum participation, and IOP openings should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
New mothers and families needing perinatal/postpartum mental-health support in Salt Lake County, with in-person and telehealth options.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 801-446-3515 or use the appointment/contact form on the website. Locations include South Jordan, Salt Lake City, and Eagle Mountain; Salt Lake County families can use the South Jordan and Salt Lake City offices or telehealth.

**Important Information to Know**
The site stated it was accepting new patients when inspected. This is clinical mental-health care and is not listed as free; verify fees, insurance, and IOP availability before referral.
resources.name: Reach Counseling Utah Postpartum Intensive Outpatient Program and Perinatal Counseling

resources.address: 6084 S 900 E Suite 200, Murray, UT 84121
resources.description: Youthlinc's Real Life is a Salt Lake-area peer-to-peer mentoring and afterschool academic-support program for refugee and immigrant youth, providing homework help, mentoring, belonging, life skills, financial literacy, communication, and college preparedness through community partner locations.
resources.hours: Program activities are afterschool at partner/community locations; call or email to confirm current sites and openings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Real Life supports refugee and immigrant youth after school with academic help, peer-to-peer mentoring, meaningful relationships, life skills, communication, financial literacy, and college preparedness. The program reports serving students at 16 community-based locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes the program for refugee and immigrant youth. Student access appears connected to community-based partner locations, and current site openings are not fully listed publicly.

**Population Served**
Refugee and immigrant youth in the Salt Lake area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-467-4417 ext. 705 or email reallifeutah@youthlinc.org to ask about student participation and current partner sites. The listed office address is 6084 S 900 E Suite 200, Murray.

**Important Information to Know**
The public interest form wording is oriented toward people interested in serving with Real Life, so families should use the phone or email to ask directly about student enrollment. Scholarship information appears tied to Real Life participation.
resources.name: Real Life

resources.description: Recovery Dharma lists RD Salt Lake at USARA as an English-language in-person and online peer recovery meeting using Buddhist-informed recovery principles.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer recovery meeting through Recovery Dharma, offered both in person and online. The meeting is English-language and listed as open to anyone.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking peer support for recovery can attend; no clinical intake is listed on the meeting page.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake County seeking Buddhist-informed peer recovery support, including those who need an online or hybrid option.

**How to Best Connect**
Attend Saturdays 5:00-6:00 PM at USARA, 180 E 2100 S, Suite 100, Salt Lake City, or use the Zoom link on the official meeting page.

**Important Information to Know**
Recovery Dharma is peer support, not clinical treatment, detox, or emergency care. Check the official meeting page before attending because meeting details can change.
resources.name: Recovery Dharma RD Salt Lake at USARA

resources.description: Recovery Ways provides mental health, alcohol, and substance-use disorder treatment in Murray, with admissions coordinators available around the clock to help determine level of care, verify benefits, and begin enrollment.
resources.hours: Admissions coordinators are described as available around the clock.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mental-health, alcohol, and substance-use disorder treatment, including detox, residential treatment, PHP, IOP, medication-assisted treatment, dual-diagnosis treatment, specialty programs, family support, and post-treatment support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call or submit the contact form to determine the appropriate level of care and verify insurance benefits. The contact form accepts inquiries for self or a loved one.

**Population Served**
People in Murray and Salt Lake County seeking private behavioral-health, alcohol, or substance-use disorder treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 888-986-7848 or complete the contact form. Locations listed include Brunswick Place at 4848 South Commerce Dr and Copper Hills at 5288 Allendale Dr in Murray.

**Important Information to Know**
This is primarily an insurance/private-pay route. Verify network status, out-of-pocket costs, medical necessity, and current program availability before referral.
resources.name: Recovery Ways

resources.description: Recovery at the U is a University of Utah collegiate recovery program that supports students seeking or sustaining recovery through peer community, support groups, skills trainings, sober social events, and workshops.

**Services Offered**
Collegiate recovery support, including peer community, support groups, skills trainings, sober social events, and workshops for students seeking or sustaining recovery from addiction.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility appears campus/student-specific. It is not a clinical treatment program.

**Population Served**
University of Utah students in Salt Lake City who are seeking or sustaining recovery.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Recovery at the U page through the University of Utah Center for Campus Wellness. The listed campus address is Student Services Building, Room 330, 201 S 1460 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84112.

**Important Information to Know**
This is peer and campus recovery support, not detox, medication treatment, or outpatient clinical addiction treatment.
resources.name: Recovery at the U

**Services Offered**
Substance Abuse IOP, Recovery IOP, addiction support, alcohol and drug assessments, drug and alcohol consultation, addiction intervention, Prime for Life, individual therapy, group therapy, family support, care coordination, continuing care, and telehealth options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients do not need a diagnosis to get started. Call or book online to determine whether therapy, assessment, IOP, or another service fits; payment and insurance should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake City, Murray, and surrounding Salt Lake County seeking outpatient addiction support, substance-use assessment, or co-occurring mental-health care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-313-0055 for therapy or 385-202-5315 for IOP, or use the website's Book Therapy/Book IOP options.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outpatient and IOP care, not residential detox. Confirm payer acceptance and whether the client needs a court-related assessment, therapy, or IOP before referral.
resources.name: Red Willow Counseling & Recovery Substance Abuse IOP and Assessments
