resources.description: Refugee Justice League is a Salt Lake City nonprofit legal advocacy organization focused on defending the constitutional rights of refugees, with direct phone and message contact and corroboration in Utah refugee legal-resource materials.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Refugee-rights legal advocacy and community legal support. Utah refugee-resource materials list Refugee Justice League among legal programs and providers for refugee-related legal needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site focuses on defending refugees' constitutional rights but does not publish detailed intake eligibility, case types, fees or capacity. Call or message to ask whether the person's refugee-related legal issue is within scope.

**Population Served**
Refugees and refugee-community members in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-390-3001, use the website contact/message option or email jwmcconkie@gmail.com. The listed address is 415 E 3900 S, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not present this as confirmed full-service immigration representation. The public site is limited, so clients should ask directly about current case types, costs and whether legal representation is available.
resources.name: Refugee Justice League Refugee Rights Legal Advocacy

resources.address: 160 East 300 South, 4th Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Relay Utah provides statewide 7-1-1 telecommunications relay service and no-cost specialized telephone equipment for qualified Utah residents who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or speech-challenged.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
7-1-1 relay services and specialized telecommunications equipment such as amplified phones, caption phones, low-vision and speech phones, mobile accessories, and in-line amplifiers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For equipment, applicants must live in Utah, be Deaf, hard of hearing, or speech-challenged, and either receive qualifying public assistance or have income at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Applications need documentation and professional or agency certification.

**Population Served**
Utah residents who are Deaf, hard of hearing, speech-challenged, or need accessible telephone equipment.

**How to Best Connect**
Dial 711 for relay services. For equipment, call 801-715-3470 or use the online application instructions; applications can be mailed, faxed, or emailed to Relay Utah/Public Service Commission.

**Important Information to Know**
Equipment is no cost only for qualified applicants. Redact sensitive account or Social Security numbers from income or benefit documentation before submitting.
resources.name: Relay Utah Telecommunications Equipment and Relay Services

resources.address: 138 W 300 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Repertory Dance Theatre's Creative Aging programs include free Music in Motion movement classes for community members 55+ at Salt Lake County-area sites and Prime Movement for adults 40+ at RDT's Dance Center on Broadway.
resources.hours: RDT office hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. Music in Motion and Prime Movement schedules vary by site and season.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Creative aging dance and movement programs, including Music in Motion movement and music exploration classes for older adults, free community 55+ classes at listed sites, and Prime Movement modern dance/improvisation classes for adults 40+.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Music in Motion free community classes are for people age 55+; some sites require senior center membership or have site-specific attendance rules. Prime Movement is for adults age 40+ and may have its own registration or fee rules.

**Population Served**
Older adults and adults 40+ in the Salt Lake County area seeking movement, creative expression, exercise and social connection.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the Creative Aging page for current schedules. Call RDT at 801-534-1000 or email rdt@rdtutah.org; for Music in Motion questions, the page lists nick@rdtutah.org. RDT's Dance Center is at 138 W 300 S, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Free class availability and site rules vary. The page lists Salt Lake County-area locations including Midvale Senior Center and South Valley Creative Dance in Sandy; confirm schedule before attending.
resources.name: Repertory Dance Theatre Creative Aging / Music in Motion and Prime Movement

resources.description: Official VA/National Archives route to request DD214, separation documents, and other military service records online, by mail, or by fax for veterans, next of kin, and other eligible requesters.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official pathway to request DD214 and other military service records from the National Archives. Records may include character of discharge, duty stations, medals and decorations, qualifications, licenses, certificates, and medical or health records.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans may request their own records. Next of kin of a deceased veteran may request records with required proof of death. Public access rules differ for records more or less than 62 years after discharge. Some newer records may be requested through DOD milConnect instead.

**Population Served**
Veterans, next of kin, authorized requesters, and people eligible to request older archival military records nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Start through the VA Request Your Military Service Records page and use the National Archives eVetRecs online tool, or download Standard Form 180 to mail or fax to the appropriate address listed on the form.

**Important Information to Know**
Online requests require an identity-verified ID.me account. If someone is applying for VA benefits, VA says it will request the DD214 when it receives the benefits application, so a separate National Archives request may not be needed for that purpose.
resources.name: Request Military Service Records, including DD214

resources.address: 1165 S State Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Faith-based emergency shelter and recovery-support location for women and women with children, including shelter, food, clothing, hygiene, work therapy, life-skills training, and addiction-recovery supports.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

The Rescue Mission of Salt Lake Center for Women provides shelter for women and women with children, plus food, clothing, hygiene, addiction recovery, work therapy, life-skills training, and support for women seeking safety from abusive relationships.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The official page identifies women and women with children as the population. Specific bed availability, family composition limits, faith-based program expectations, and check-in rules should be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**

Women and women with children who are homeless, low-income, seeking safety, or seeking recovery support in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-521-5925 or go to 1165 S State Street to ask about shelter access and current availability. For immediate safety concerns, use emergency or domestic-violence crisis resources as appropriate.

**Important Information to Know**

This is a faith-based provider; ask about program expectations. Beds are not guaranteed. Clothing is listed, but separate hours, inventory and access for women who are not shelter guests are not published; call first.
resources.name: Rescue Mission of Salt Lake Center for Women

resources.address: 463 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Rescue Mission of Salt Lake provides faith-based emergency services for people experiencing homelessness, including overnight shelter, three daily meals, hygiene, day room, phone message board, mail reception, baggage check, brown-bag lunches for working guests, family food boxes for low-income households, Bible studies, chapel services, and faith-based recovery meetings.
resources.hours: Call or go to the front desk for current meal, day-room, shower, baggage-check, and shelter timing; detailed public daily schedule was not posted on the checked page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Emergency homeless services including overnight shelter, three daily meals, hygiene, day room, phone message board, mail reception, baggage check, brown-bag lunches for working guests, family food boxes for low-income households, Bible studies, chapel services, and faith-based recovery meetings. Clothing and the men's New Life recovery program are also offered at this facility.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Overnight shelter and the New Life program at this site serve men; family food boxes serve qualifying low-income households. Meal, day-room, clothing and other emergency-service access can differ; ask the front desk about guest requirements and current availability.

**Population Served**

People experiencing homelessness or poverty in Salt Lake City and the Wasatch Front, including working guests who need brown-bag lunches and low-income families needing food boxes.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-355-1302 or go to 463 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, and ask about current emergency-service access, meals, day room, hygiene, baggage check, and shelter intake.

**Important Information to Know**

Services are faith-based. Confirm bed and recovery-program eligibility, check-in rules and service times. Clothing has no published separate room schedule and depends on donations; ask whether non-guests can receive it. Meals and food boxes are not guarantees of overnight shelter.
resources.name: Rescue Mission of Salt Lake Men's Homeless Service Center and Emergency Services

resources.address: 14658 S Bangerter Pkwy, Suite 300, Draper, UT 84020
resources.description: Return & Rise helps women in Utah return to work or advance after time away through virtual classes, on-demand courses, certification, career reentry coaching, and returnship access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career reentry and advancement support, including Return Prep and Return Ready classes, on-demand online courses, Return and Rise certification, access to an exclusive returnship board after certification, Rise Promotion classes for advancement, financial confidence classes, events, and appointment/contact routes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for women returning to the workforce after time away or seeking advancement. Returnship board access requires completing Return Prep/Return Ready and certification or passing the certification-only path; returnship placements are competitive and not guaranteed.

**Population Served**
Women across Utah who are reentering the workforce, refreshing skills, rebuilding confidence, or seeking promotion after a workforce interruption.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the website's Book an Appointment, Join a Class, or Returnships form routes. Call 801-566-5058 or email info@returnandrise.org. The listed office is 14658 S Bangerter Pkwy, Suite 300, Draper.

**Important Information to Know**
Many offerings are virtual. Confirm current fees, class schedule, returnship availability, and whether a specific returnship is paid before treating this as immediate placement.
resources.name: Return & Rise Return Prep, Return Ready, Rise Promotion, and Returnships

resources.description: Ria Health offers telehealth alcohol-use treatment throughout Utah, combining medical check-ins, anti-craving medications, weekly recovery coaching, digital tools including a breathalyzer, and online group meetings.
resources.hours: Online program; schedule a call through the website or call for current availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
100% online alcohol treatment for Utah residents, including medical check-ins, medication-assisted treatment/anti-craving medication, weekly recovery coaching, a breathalyzer connected to the app, digital tools, and online group meetings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Utah residents seeking help to quit or reduce drinking. Schedule a call to confirm medical fit, urgent withdrawal risk, licensure, accepted insurance, and cost.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake City and throughout Utah seeking telehealth alcohol-use care without in-person office visits.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-504-5360 or use the Schedule An Appointment link on the Utah page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is alcohol-specific telehealth care, not opioid treatment, residential treatment, or urgent detox. People at risk of severe alcohol withdrawal need medical evaluation before attempting to stop drinking.
resources.name: Ria Health Virtual Alcohol Care in Utah

resources.address: 2906 S Richmond Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84106
resources.description: CDCU's Richmond Flats is a 55-unit affordable rental property in Salt Lake City with one- to four-bedroom units, ADA-accessible units, and rents for households making 30% to 55% AMI.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable rental apartments at Richmond Flats in Salt Lake City, including one-, two-, three-, and four-bedroom units and ADA-accessible units.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CDCU states rents are for households making between 30% and 55% AMI, with income limits and income-dependent rental costs. Additional leasing, screening, deposit, and waitlist requirements are handled through the property manager/application route.

**Population Served**
Low-income households seeking affordable rental housing in Salt Lake City, including households needing larger bedrooms or ADA-accessible units when available.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Property Manager Claudia Aceves at 385-429-7087 or use the Richmond Flats application link from CDCU's affordable rental housing page.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability is not guaranteed. Confirm openings, waitlist status, application requirements, and all fees before applying.
resources.name: Richmond Flats Affordable Rental Housing

resources.description: Rides for Refugees provides donated vehicles or vehicle grants for eligible low-income refugees and asylees in the United States who need private transportation for self-reliance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vehicle grants or donated vehicles for refugees and asylees who need reliable private transportation for work, school, family responsibilities and self-reliance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The submitted evidence describes low-income refugees or asylees permanently resettled in the United States who have, or are working toward, a U.S. driver license and can afford fuel, insurance and maintenance.

**Population Served**
Refugees and asylees in the United States, potentially including Salt Lake County residents, who cannot meet essential transportation needs without a vehicle.

**How to Best Connect**
Email Hello@RidesforRefugees.org to ask about the waiting list, application timing, eligibility and whether the applicant or sponsoring organization should submit information.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a ride service or emergency transportation. Applications are rolling as funding allows, demand exceeds available vehicles, and recipients may still need to cover license, insurance, fuel, registration and maintenance costs.
resources.name: Rides for Refugees Vehicle Grants / Donated Vehicles for Refugees

resources.address: 2001 S State St, Ste N1-200, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Riverton City's fee schedule lists utility rate relief for Senior Circuit Breaker and Disabled Veteran customers on culinary and secondary water charges, with qualification approved through Salt Lake County property tax relief.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Utility-rate relief for eligible Riverton City utility customers. The fee schedule lists Senior Circuit Breaker water rate relief and Disabled Veteran rate relief for culinary water and secondary water.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Customer must be a Riverton City utility customer and qualify through Salt Lake County's Property Tax Relief Division for Senior Circuit Breaker or Disabled Veteran relief. Disabled Veteran relief depends on the qualified disability percentage.

**Population Served**
Riverton City utility customers who qualify for Salt Lake County senior circuit breaker or disabled veteran property tax relief.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Salt Lake County Treasurer Tax Relief at 385-468-8300 option 2 for qualification, and contact Riverton City utility billing to confirm how the approved rate relief is applied to the utility account.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a rate relief program, not emergency payment assistance. The available public source is a fee schedule; renters, non-owner account holders, and current application steps should be confirmed before promising the discount.
resources.name: Riverton City Senior Circuit Breaker and Disabled Veteran Utility Rate Relief

resources.address: 111 E Broadway, Suite 750, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Robert Half Salt Lake City is a local professional staffing office helping job seekers find contract, temporary, project, remote, hybrid, and full-time roles in accounting, finance, technology, administrative support, creative, marketing, and legal fields.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Professional staffing and recruiting for remote and on-site jobs, including contract, temporary, project, and full-time roles. Fields include finance and accounting, technology, marketing and creative, legal, administrative, customer support, operations, and human resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to job seekers seeking professional and office-based roles. Suitability depends on the person's skills, work history, and current openings; this is not usually the best fit for immediate general labor.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City metro job seekers with office, accounting, technology, creative, marketing, legal, administrative, customer service, or related professional skills.

**How to Best Connect**
Search jobs through the Robert Half Salt Lake City page or call the local Salt Lake City staffing office at 801-895-2001. The office is at 111 E Broadway, Suite 750, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Robert Half is a staffing and recruiting firm, not a social-service job program. Placement is not guaranteed and depends on current employer demand and candidate qualifications.
resources.name: Robert Half Salt Lake City Staffing Office

resources.address: 358 South 700 East, Suite B235, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: Rocky Mountain Innocence Center provides pro bono post-conviction innocence investigation and litigation services for people wrongfully convicted in Utah, Nevada and Wyoming, with a direct request-assistance route for prisoners or family members.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pro bono post-conviction innocence investigation and litigation for people who may have been wrongfully convicted. Accepted cases are investigated for evidence of factual innocence and may proceed to litigation with cooperating counsel.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The case must involve post-conviction factual innocence in Utah, Nevada or Wyoming and pass RMIC screening. Requests are carefully vetted, and accepted investigations can take years.

**Population Served**
People convicted in Utah, Nevada or Wyoming who claim factual innocence, including incarcerated people and family members seeking help on their behalf.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Request Assistance route on the RMIC website, email contact@rminnocence.org or call 801-355-1888. The Salt Lake City office is at 358 South 700 East, Suite B235.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a narrow innocence program, not general criminal defense, appeal help, expungement help or civil legal aid. Screening and investigation do not guarantee acceptance or a fast outcome.
resources.name: Rocky Mountain Innocence Center Post-Conviction Innocence Investigation and Litigation Services

resources.description: Rocky Mountain Power's customer assistance page is the provider front door for payment arrangements, due-date extensions, Equal Pay, medical certificate information, and referrals to energy-assistance programs for Utah electric customers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provider account help for Rocky Mountain Power electric customers, including due-date extensions, payment arrangements, Equal Pay, medical certificate information, and referrals to bill assistance and weatherization resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Must be a Rocky Mountain Power customer for account-specific arrangements or provider protections. Grants or discounts such as HEAT, HELP, and Lend A Hand have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Rocky Mountain Power electric customers in Utah, including Salt Lake County customers served by Rocky Mountain Power.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Rocky Mountain Power at 1-888-221-7070 or use the customer assistance links on the bill payment assistance page. Customers with a shutoff notice, medical need, or inability to pay should contact the provider as early as possible.

**Important Information to Know**
Payment arrangements and Equal Pay do not erase the bill. Medical certificate protections require follow-up and documentation and do not provide a grant by themselves.
resources.name: Rocky Mountain Power Bill Payment Assistance and Payment Arrangements

resources.description: Rocky Mountain Power's Home Electric Lifeline Program provides a monthly electric-bill discount for HEAT-eligible Rocky Mountain Power customers in Utah.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Monthly electric-bill discount for HEAT-eligible Rocky Mountain Power customers through the Home Electric Lifeline Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be a Rocky Mountain Power customer and meet HELP/HEAT income and program rules. Customers who receive a HEAT benefit on a Rocky Mountain Power account may be automatically enrolled for a limited period, while other customers may need to apply or recertify through the listed HELP/HEAT route.

**Population Served**
Low-income Rocky Mountain Power customers in Utah, including eligible customers in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask a HEAT intake worker about HELP enrollment when applying for HEAT, or call the listed HELP contacts at 801-961-7286 or 1-800-948-7540. People facing imminent shutoff should also contact Rocky Mountain Power and 211 right away.

**Important Information to Know**
HELP is a bill discount, not an emergency cash payment. Current discount amount, automatic enrollment status, and account-specific eligibility should be confirmed with HEAT or Rocky Mountain Power.
resources.name: Rocky Mountain Power Home Electric Lifeline Program

resources.address: 438 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Rocky Mountain Power's Lend A Hand is donated-fund energy assistance administered by The Salvation Army for Utah Rocky Mountain Power customers, with priority noted for households with senior or disabled family members.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Energy bill assistance from donated funds for Rocky Mountain Power customers through Lend A Hand, administered by The Salvation Army.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be a Rocky Mountain Power customer in an eligible Utah service area. Rocky Mountain Power says households with senior and disabled family members are prioritized. Salvation Army screening may require proof of account, income, hardship, HEAT notice, past-due balance, or disconnection risk.

**Population Served**
Rocky Mountain Power customers facing financial hardship, including customers in Salt Lake County where Rocky Mountain Power serves the electric account.

**How to Best Connect**
Call The Salvation Army at 801-969-0526 or toll free at 1-855-969-0526 to apply for Lend A Hand. Customers should also contact Rocky Mountain Power if they need a payment arrangement or have a shutoff notice.

**Important Information to Know**
Lend A Hand is donation-funded and not guaranteed. It is different from HEAT and HELP; customers may need to apply for those benefits separately or first.
resources.name: Rocky Mountain Power Lend A Hand

resources.address: 970 Emery St W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; 122 E 1700 S, Bldg. 3, Provo, UT 84606
resources.description: Rocky Mountain University Eye Institute provides comprehensive eye exams and basic prescription glasses at no cost for qualifying uninsured people who meet poverty-level guidelines, with Salt Lake City and Provo locations.
resources.hours: Provo page lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; call to confirm Salt Lake location hours and pro-bono appointment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive eye health and vision exams at no cost for qualified individuals, basic prescription glasses when eligible and available, and additional evaluations when medically necessary.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Individuals must be uninsured and meet federal poverty-level household income guidelines. Verification is required and may come through a school, clinic, food bank, charitable organization, or direct clinic vetting.

**Population Served**
Uninsured people who meet poverty-level guidelines and can use the Salt Lake City or Provo RMU Eye Institute location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-248-5550, email eyeinstitute@rmuhc.org, complete the referral form, book online, or ask in person. Bring proof of income if applying directly.

**Important Information to Know**
Free glasses depend on eligibility, need, and inventory. The page lists direct access but eligibility verification is required before services are covered at no cost.
resources.name: Rocky Mountain University Eye Institute Vision Care Without Coverage

resources.address: 1105 W 1000 N, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Rose Park Community Learning Center hosts community education opportunities and weekly adult ESL, with ongoing on-site registration for adult learners.
resources.hours: Adult ESL schedule is subject to change; submitted city guide listed Monday 5:30-7:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community education opportunities including adult ESL, job training, digital literacy workshops, and other community enrichment. Current city class guide evidence lists weekly evening adult ESL at Rose Park CLC.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For community members seeking adult English learning. The city class guide says ongoing on-site registration requires photo ID and proof of address.

**Population Served**
Rose Park and northwest Salt Lake City community members, including Salt Lake City School District families/community members.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-578-8554 or contact coordinator Angelica Ramos at Angelica.Ramos@slcschools.org. Register on site at 1105 W 1000 N and bring photo ID and proof of address.

**Important Information to Know**
The CLC page confirms community education but not every current ESL session. Confirm current class dates and whether the class is open before attending.
resources.name: Rose Park Community Learning Center Adult ESL

resources.address: 754 North 800 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Rose Park Neighborhood Center's Financial Aid for Passports program helps undocumented parents cover the cost of obtaining a passport book for a U.S. citizen child.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-5:00 PM; confirm application availability before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial help toward the cost of obtaining a passport book for a U.S. citizen child of undocumented parents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official overview says the program is designed for undocumented parents seeking a passport book for their U.S. citizen child. Current application window, grant amount, required documents, and payment method should be confirmed with Rose Park Neighborhood Center.

**Population Served**
Undocumented parents and their U.S. citizen children in the Salt Lake area who need help with passport-book costs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-301-8257, email info@gsfutah.org, or contact Rose Park Neighborhood Center at 754 North 800 West during Monday-Thursday office hours.

**Important Information to Know**
The detailed program page was protected from access during research, but the official community-services overview confirms the program's purpose. Confirm current funding and documents before referral.
resources.name: Rose Park Neighborhood Center Financial Aid for Passports

resources.address: 754 North 800 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Rose Park Neighborhood Center offers a seasonal free tax clinic for federal and state tax preparation, but the program is closed for the season as of the official 2026 page and expected to reopen with updated scheduling in January 2027.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-5:00 PM. Tax clinic is closed for the season and expected to post updated scheduling in January 2027.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Seasonal free tax-preparation clinic for community members needing help filing federal and state taxes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official overview does not list detailed eligibility rules. Seasonal tax clinics commonly limit return complexity and appointment availability; confirm current requirements when the clinic reopens.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake community members, including immigrant and refugee families near Rose Park, who need free tax-preparation help.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-301-8257, email info@gsfutah.org, or monitor the Rose Park Neighborhood Center tax clinic page. The official community page says the tax program is closed for the season and will reopen with updated scheduling in January 2027.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an immediate intake route as of September 29, 2026. It is retained as a seasonal tax resource because the official page states it will reopen with updated information and scheduling in January 2027.
resources.name: Rose Park Neighborhood Center Free Tax Clinic

resources.address: 754 N 800 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Good Samaritan Foundation's Rose Park Neighborhood Center offers immigrant and refugee services, resource referrals, grants for government filing fees when available, citizenship pathway support, and free immigration legal clinics in partnership with No More a Stranger Foundation.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-5:00 PM; free immigration legal clinics listed Tuesday and Thursday evenings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immigrant services for families, including assistance with resources and referrals, grants to help with government filing fees when available, citizenship pathway support, and free immigration legal clinics in partnership with No More a Stranger Foundation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For immigrants and refugees seeking support through the Rose Park Neighborhood Center. Filing-fee grants depend on availability and program fit.

**Population Served**
Immigrant and refugee families in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County, especially those who can access the Rose Park Neighborhood Center.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-301-8257, email info@gsfutah.org, or use the website's Apply Now links. The center is at 754 N 800 W, Salt Lake City, and lists office hours Monday through Thursday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Legal clinics are in partnership with No More a Stranger Foundation, so confirm clinic dates, appointment requirements, and whether the client's issue can be handled before attending.
resources.name: Rose Park Neighborhood Center Immigrant Services for Families

resources.address: 754 North 800 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Rose Park parent-and-toddler program for children under 3 with songs, story time, play, parent connection, and limited diaper assistance through participation or one-time help.
resources.hours: Office hours: Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM-5:00 PM. Play & Learn meets once a month; contact the program for current schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Play & Learn Program brings parents and toddlers together for songs, story time, play, and parent connection. The program also offers limited diaper assistance through its Utah Food Bank/Utah Diaper Bank partnership.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for parents and toddlers under age 3. Parent and child must attend together. Regular participation is required for ongoing assistance such as diapers, though one-time assistance may be available without enrollment.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City/Rose Park families with toddlers under age 3.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the interest form linked on the program page or call 385-301-8257. The program coordinator reaches out to schedule an in-person appointment to complete registration.

**Important Information to Know**
Diaper quantities are limited and not guaranteed. Families should call before relying on diaper availability.
resources.name: Rose Park Neighborhood Center Play & Learn Program

resources.address: 10894 S River Front Pkwy, South Jordan, UT 84095
resources.description: Roseman Dental, the clinical practice of Roseman University College of Dental Medicine, provides comprehensive reduced-cost dental care in South Jordan through student dentists, residents, and faculty providers, and accepts Medicaid and uninsured patients.
resources.hours: Call or use the website contact/schedule option for current appointment and urgent-care availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive dental care at reduced cost, including preventive care and more advanced dental procedures through a team-based dental school clinic model. The site also has an urgent-care pathway for dental emergencies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to patients who can use the South Jordan clinic. Roseman accepts most dental insurance plans, Medicaid, and patients without insurance. Call to confirm fit, costs, and whether the needed procedure is available.

**Population Served**
Dental patients in South Jordan, Salt Lake County, and the surrounding Salt Lake Valley, including uninsured and Medicaid patients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-878-1200 or use the website contact/schedule appointment option. The clinic is at 10894 S River Front Pkwy, South Jordan, UT 84095.

**Important Information to Know**
Care is reduced-cost, not free. The site states costs are typically up to 50% less than private practices. Urgent dental care should be scheduled when possible; walk-in availability is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Roseman Dental and Urgent Care Dental Clinic

resources.address: 5929 South 900 East, Salt Lake City, UT 84121
resources.description: Ruth's Kitchen is a food pantry operated by Discovery Christian Community that offers free fresh and non-perishable food to anyone in need. The provider states there is no registration or requirements.
resources.hours: Every Thursday at 6:30 PM; distribution usually takes 30-60 minutes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free food pantry with fresh and non-perishable food items at no cost.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider says there is no registration or requirements and that people should come as they are.

**Population Served**
Anyone in need who can reach Discovery Christian Community in the Murray/Salt Lake City area.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to Discovery Christian Community at 5929 S 900 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84121 on Thursdays at 6:30 PM. Enter through the north-facing side entrance because the main doors are locked during the week. Call 801-266-3600 or email office@DiscoveryChristian.org with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The page says Ruth's Kitchen is open twice a week but only shows Thursday at 6:30 PM in the visible schedule. Confirm any additional day before relying on it.
resources.name: Ruth's Kitchen Food Pantry

resources.address: 3171 Riverport Tech Center Dr, Maryland Heights, MO 63043
resources.description: Rx Outreach is a nonprofit mail-order pharmacy offering low-cost prescription medications with free delivery in all 50 states, no insurance requirement, no membership, and online or phone ordering.
resources.hours: Patient Contact Center: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM Central; Friday 7:00 AM-5:30 PM Central. Pharmacists: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM Central; Friday 7:00 AM-5:30 PM Central; Saturday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM Central.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost mail-order prescription medications, upfront medication pricing, free delivery in all 50 states, online account management, and phone support for ordering.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A valid prescription is required. Rx Outreach states no insurance is needed, with no hidden fees and no membership requirement. Some free-medication support programs have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Patients nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents, who need affordable prescription medications by mail.

**How to Best Connect**
Search medication prices and order online, or call 888-796-1234 or 314-222-0472 for patient support. Prescribers can submit prescriptions through the provider route.

**Important Information to Know**
Medications are low-cost rather than automatically free. Availability, price, shipping, and whether a specific medication is included must be checked before relying on the program.
resources.name: Rx Outreach Nonprofit Mail-Order Pharmacy

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC's Lineworker Pre-Apprenticeship is a workforce microcredential preparing students for entry-level electric power industry work with lineworker skills, safety training, pole climbing, rescue certifications, and OSHA 10-related training.
resources.hours: Course schedules vary by cohort; contact SLCC Workforce Training.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lineworker Pre-Apprenticeship workforce training for entry-level electric power industry work. Training covers electrical theory, safety, wooden pole climbing, ropes and rigging, transformers, grounding, switchgear and metering, bucket truck rescue, pole top rescue, First Aid/CPR/AED, OSHA 10 Construction, and career preparation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Course prerequisites and session availability vary. Utah residents may qualify for Short Term Intensive Training funding that can cover up to 50% of tuition. This is training, not a guaranteed apprenticeship or job offer.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake County and Utah seeking pre-apprenticeship training for lineworker or electric power industry entry-level positions.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the SLCC Lineworker Pre-Apprenticeship page or SLCC Enrole course pages to request information, register, or ask to be notified about the next scheduled program. Call SLCC Workforce Training at 801-957-7522 or email wte@slcc.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
Published program information has included a 16-week full-time option and a part-time option. Tuition was listed around $7,885 in SLCC materials and is subject to change; confirm current sessions, total cost, tools, transportation, and funding before referral.
resources.name: SLCC Lineworker Pre-Apprenticeship

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC's State Scholarships, Tuition Waivers, and Salt Lake Tech Scholarships page explains education funding pathways for eligible Utah residents and SLCC/Salt Lake Technical College students, including Adult Learner Grant, Technical Education Scholarship, SLTech Scholarship, and state tuition waivers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Information and application routes for SLCC-administered state grants, scholarships, technical education scholarships, SLTech scholarships, and state tuition waivers. Many applications run through Scholarship Universe or specific linked portals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Rules vary by award. Most state scholarship opportunities require FAFSA. Technical Education Scholarship and SLTech Scholarship are for eligible students in Salt Lake Technical College high-demand technical certificate programs; Utah residency, SAP, program type, and annual reapplication rules may apply.

**Population Served**
Utah residents and SLCC/Salt Lake Technical College students seeking education funding.

**How to Best Connect**
Review the SLCC scholarships page and submit questions to scholarships@slcc.edu. Apply through Scholarship Universe or the linked application portals when the relevant application is open.

**Important Information to Know**
Several listed 2026-2027 grant applications were closed on the official page. Awards are not guaranteed and are not universal free tuition.
resources.name: SLCC State Scholarships, Tuition Waivers, and SLTech Scholarship

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC Workforce Training funding applications let eligible Utah residents apply for Short Term Intensive Training, Strategic Workforce Initiative, and Utah Works funding for approved high-demand workforce training programs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Funding applications for eligible SLCC Workforce Training programs: Short Term Intensive Training funding, Strategic Workforce Initiative funding, and Utah Works funding.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility is determined through the funding application and is based on Utah residency and the selected eligible program. STIT pays a percentage of training costs for multiple high-demand programs; SWI pays 50% for IT pathway training; Utah Works pays the full cost for advanced manufacturing training.

**Population Served**
Utah residents, including Salt Lake County residents, applying for eligible SLCC Workforce Training programs.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the SLCC Enrole funding applications page, choose the relevant funding application, create or sign in to a profile, and submit the application. Call SLCC Workforce Training at 801-957-5367 for help.

**Important Information to Know**
The current funding applications are listed for July 1, 2026 through June 1, 2027. Approval is not guaranteed, and covered percentages differ by funding stream.
resources.name: SLCC Workforce Training Funding Applications: STIT, SWI, and Utah Works

resources.address: Online at jobs.utah.gov/mycase; paperwork mail: P.O. Box 143245, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3245
resources.description: Utah Department of Workforce Services is the statewide application front door for SNAP/Food Stamps. Salt Lake County residents can apply online, in person, or by mailed application; if approved, benefits start from the application date and expedited SNAP may be available within seven days when criteria and identity verification are met.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SNAP/Food Stamps application and eligibility processing for monthly food benefits on an EBT card. Expedited SNAP may be available within seven days for households that meet expedited criteria and verify identity.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on household income, expenses, household composition, immigration/citizenship rules, interview requirements, and verification. No documents are required just to submit an application, but DWS may require documents to decide the case.

**Population Served**
Utah households, including Salt Lake County residents, who need help buying food and may meet SNAP rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through myCase at jobs.utah.gov/mycase, apply in person at a DWS office, or mail a paper application to P.O. Box 143245, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3245. Call the Salt Lake area line 801-526-0950 or statewide toll-free 866-435-7414 for help.

**Important Information to Know**
Applying does not guarantee approval. Benefits generally start from the application date if approved, so submitting an application promptly matters.
resources.name: SNAP / Food Stamps

resources.address: 168 N. 1950 W., Suite 104, Salt Lake City, UT 84116; 50 N. Medical Drive, Clinic E22, Salt Lake City, UT 84132; 5126 W. Daybreak Parkway, South Jordan, UT 84009
resources.description: University of Utah Health's SUPeRAD Clinic provides integrated pregnancy and substance-use-disorder care for people who are pregnant, planning pregnancy, or within one year postpartum, with no referral required.
resources.hours: Call or text Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; not an emergency line.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pregnancy and postpartum care integrated with substance-use-disorder treatment, treatment-option counseling, harm-reduction support, medication for opioid use disorder when appropriate, care coordination, peer recovery support, behavioral-health support, and community-resource connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with a substance-use disorder who are planning to get pregnant, are pregnant, or had a pregnancy within the past year. The clinic states that anyone can contact the clinic regardless of insurance status and no referral is needed.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum people in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents, who need care related to substance use and pregnancy recovery.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 385-881-3035 Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM to learn more or make an appointment. Locations include Population Health Center, University of Utah Hospital Ambulatory Care Clinic, and South Jordan Health Center.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency line; call 911 for emergencies. Methadone may be coordinated with opioid treatment programs rather than prescribed directly by SUPeRAD. Insurance, financial assistance, appointment location, and medication pathway should be confirmed at intake.
resources.name: SUPeRAD Clinic - Substance Use and Pregnancy Care

resources.address: 660 South 200 East Suite 250, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Home-visiting program for parents and expecting parents with children prenatal to age 5 in Salt Lake and Ibapah/Wendover areas, offering culturally focused lessons, child-development support, and possible baby supplies/books.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family Spirit home visiting with approximately 55 lessons on child development, health, parenting, nutrition, life skills, infant care, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, crib safety, car seat safety, routines, and home safety. Families may receive baby supplies, books, and parent items.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For parents or expecting parents with children from prenatal to age 5 in the Salt Lake and Ibapah/Wendover areas. The provider states it is a zero-cost service for those who qualify.

**Population Served**
Families with young children and expecting parents in the Salt Lake area; the model was developed with Indigenous communities and the provider states it offers culturally focused care for all families.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Family Spirit Program Interest Form on Sacred Circle's website or call Sacred Circle's main number at 801-359-2256. The Salt Lake City clinic is at 660 South 200 East Suite 250.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility and visit capacity should be confirmed. Services may occur at home or clinic, with 1-4 visits per month depending on the family.
resources.name: Sacred Circle Healthcare Family Spirit Home Visiting Program

resources.address: 660 South 200 East Suite 250, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Sacred Circle Healthcare's SUD Recovery Clinic provides culturally sensitive outpatient substance-use treatment, dual-diagnosis care, behavioral-health interventions, therapy, and medication for addiction treatment in Salt Lake County.
resources.hours: Call for current appointment availability and location-specific scheduling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient SUD recovery services, individualized treatment planning, dual-diagnosis care, behavioral-health interventions, medication management, therapy, and medications to reduce withdrawal symptoms and cravings when appropriate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call to confirm appointment availability, payer requirements, and whether services are limited by tribal/IHS eligibility or open more broadly. The provider says it works flexibly with Medicaid and aims to make services Medicaid-eligible.

**Population Served**
Adults with substance-use disorders and co-occurring mental-health needs, with culturally sensitive services for the American Indian and Alaska Native community.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Sacred Circle Healthcare at 801-359-2256. Salt Lake City clinic address is 660 South 200 East, Suite 250, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; other Salt Lake County locations are also listed.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm current intake, coverage, and whether the client should attend the Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Pamela's Place, Fairbourne Station, or Gail Miller Wellness Center location.
resources.name: Sacred Circle Healthcare SUD Recovery Clinic

resources.address: 660 S 200 E Suite 250, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Sacred Circle Healthcare's Salt Lake City clinic provides primary care, dentistry, optometry, behavioral health, psychiatry, urology, physical therapy, podiatry, pain management, dietary services, recovery programming, and wellness services.
resources.hours: Call or use online booking for current appointment availability and location-specific schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Primary care, dentistry, optometry, behavioral health, wellness services, urology, Family Spirit, physical therapy, podiatry, pain management, recovery programming, psychiatry, and dietary services at the Salt Lake City clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Patients should call or book online to confirm new-patient availability, service location, payer requirements, and whether they need to establish care before dental, optometry, or specialty services.

**Population Served**

Patients in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County seeking integrated medical, dental, vision, behavioral-health, and specialty services. Sacred Circle has a tribal healthcare identity and also operates multiple Salt Lake County locations.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-359-2256 or use the online booking/patient portal links. The Salt Lake City clinic is at 660 S 200 E Suite 250, Salt Lake City, UT 84111.

**Important Information to Know**

Confirm the service location, payer rules, new-patient availability and whether established primary care is required. Behavioral-health therapy scope and psychiatry appointments are not fully detailed on the location page; confirm before referral.
resources.name: Sacred Circle Healthcare Salt Lake City Clinic

resources.address: 807 E South Temple St #200, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: Safe Space SLC provides inclusive, trauma-informed therapy in Salt Lake City and via telehealth across Utah, including LGBTQIA+ affirming care, BIPOC-affirming care, individual, family, teen/youth, young-adult, group, EMDR, ADHD/neurodivergent, anxiety, depression, and chronic-illness support.
resources.hours: Now accepting new clients in person and via telehealth across Utah; call or email for appointment times.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Inclusive trauma-informed therapy, including LGBTQIA+ affirming care, BIPOC-affirming care, individual therapy, family therapy, teen and youth therapy, young-adult therapy, group therapy, trauma therapy, EMDR, ADHD and neurodivergent support, anxiety and depression treatment, chronic illness/chronic pain support, and support for kids, teens, and parents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to clients who fit therapist availability, payment, insurance, and clinical scope. The contact page states it is accepting new clients in person and by telehealth across Utah.

**Population Served**
Utah clients seeking affirming therapy, including LGBTQIA+ clients, BIPOC clients, children, teens, young adults, families, neurodivergent clients, and people living with chronic illness or pain.

**How to Best Connect**
Email intake@safespaceslc.net or call 385-200-0535. In-person office: 807 E South Temple St #200, Salt Lake City; telehealth is advertised across Utah.

**Important Information to Know**
The candidate evidence says the practice does not take Medicaid or Medicare and may use private insurance, sliding scale, or superbills; confirm payment and provider fit before scheduling.
resources.name: Safe Space SLC Inclusive Trauma-Informed Therapy

resources.description: SafeLink Wireless offers Lifeline-supported mobile service for eligible low-income households, with eligibility based on qualifying benefits or income and application through SafeLink/National Verifier pathways.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lifeline mobile phone service for eligible households. SafeLink materials describe government-supported wireless service for qualified Lifeline subscribers; exact plan, device, data, and coverage should be confirmed for the applicant's ZIP code.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must qualify for Lifeline through a qualifying benefit program such as Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans and Survivors Pension Benefit, eligible Tribal programs, or household income at or below Lifeline limits. Annual recertification and documentation may be required.

**Population Served**
Low-income residents in areas where SafeLink offers Lifeline service, including Utah residents where address and ZIP-code availability are confirmed.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online at SafeLink Wireless or call 800-723-3546. Applicants may be routed through the Lifeline National Verifier and should have identity, address, and eligibility documents ready.

**Important Information to Know**
Only one Lifeline benefit is generally allowed per household. Approval and plan details do not guarantee that a specific phone, network, or data allowance will work well at a particular Salt Lake County address.
resources.name: SafeLink Wireless Lifeline Mobile Service

resources.description: SafeUT provides free, confidential 24/7 access to licensed counselors by app, web chat, phone, and tip submission for Utah students and school communities facing emotional crisis, safety concerns, bullying, self-harm concerns, or other problems.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free 24/7 chat or call with licensed counselors, confidential support for problems of any size, and safety-tip submission when someone is worried about harm, school threats, bullying, self-harm, or other safety concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for Utah students and school communities. Confidentiality is limited when someone is in danger or there is a safety concern.

**Population Served**
Utah students, parents/guardians, educators, and school communities needing crisis support or a way to report safety concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the SafeUT app or website buttons to start a chat, submit a tip, or start a call. Candidate phone is 833-372-3388.

**Important Information to Know**
SafeUT is not ongoing therapy. Counselors may contact authorities, schools, or emergency services when safety requires it.
resources.name: SafeUT Crisis Chat and Tip Line

resources.description: Free, confidential 24/7 SafeUT National Guard app and phone support connecting Utah Guard soldiers, veterans, civilian personnel, and families to licensed mental-health counselors trained in military culture.
resources.hours: 24/7, 365 days a year by app chat or call.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SafeUT National Guard provides free, confidential 24/7 chat and call support with licensed mental-health counselors. Counselors can listen, help with crisis intervention and safety planning, and connect users to other resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for Utah National Guard soldiers, veterans, civilian personnel, and their families. It requires app access for chat/call features; the public page also identifies a toll-free phone number in the submitted evidence.

**Population Served**
Utah Guard soldiers, veterans, civilian personnel, and their families statewide, including Salt Lake County residents in that population.

**How to Best Connect**
Download the free SafeUT National Guard app for Apple or Android and use Start a Chat or Start a Call. The submitted direct phone number is 833-372-3364.

**Important Information to Know**
This SafeUT version is designed around the National Guard community and does not include the school tip feature available in the general SafeUT app. Veterans without any Guard connection should confirm fit or use another veteran crisis/support route.
resources.name: SafeUT National Guard 24/7 Confidential Crisis Chat and Call Support

resources.address: 1745 W 7800 S, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: Salson Clinics is a West Jordan lead for medication-related substance-use treatment; submitted evidence and treatment directories describe outpatient medication treatment for opioid use disorder at the listed clinic, but current official service details could not be confirmed.
resources.hours: Hours not confirmed from a primary source; call before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Submitted evidence described outpatient medication treatment for opioid use disorder and medication-assisted therapy counseling. Public treatment directories also associate Salson Clinics with addiction treatment, but current official service details were not confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call to confirm the clinic is currently offering addiction treatment, medication for opioid-use disorder, counseling, accepted insurance, and whether new patients can self-refer.

**Population Served**
Potentially adults and young adults in West Jordan and Salt Lake County seeking outpatient medication-supported substance-use care; population details need confirmation.

Call 801-666-8640 for Salson Clinics at 1745 W 7800 S, West Jordan, UT 84088. Do not send a client without confirming current service scope.

This listing needs administrator resolution because the official addiction-recovery page could not be opened and the current primary-source evidence for SUD/MOUD scope is insufficient for routine referral. The lead appears geographically reachable and potentially relevant if confirmed.
resources.name: Salson Clinics Outpatient Medication Treatment Lead

resources.address: 3365 South 900 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84119
resources.description: The Salt Lake Area Gang Project coordinates a tattoo removal program with University of Utah plastic and reconstructive surgery to provide free gang-related tattoo removal for eligible former gang members in Utah.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free removal of gang-related tattoos for eligible former gang members, coordinated by the Salt Lake Area Gang Project with University of Utah plastic and reconstructive surgery. Larger tattoos may require multiple visits spaced at least six weeks apart.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have lived in Utah for at least one year; have no arrests or gang involvement within one year of applying; have no criminal activity for one year after incarceration, parole, or probation; have no unresolved court issues; submit a letter about future goals; and submit photos showing the gang-related tattoos. Exceptions may be reviewed case by case.

**Population Served**
Former gang members in Utah seeking to remove gang-related tattoos as part of leaving gang involvement and stabilizing work, safety, or community life.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-9770 to obtain an application. Return the completed application to Salt Lake Area Gang Project, 3365 South 900 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84119, ATTN: Tattoo Removal Program. Accepted applicants may need a prescreening interview.

**Important Information to Know**
Applications must be complete or they may be denied. Applicants are notified by mail or email, and accepted clients are responsible for keeping appointments. The program is narrow and only covers gang-related tattoos.
resources.name: Salt Lake Area Gang Project Tattoo Removal Program

resources.address: 3802 S 700 E, South Salt Lake, UT 84106
resources.description: Salt Lake Behavioral Health's Courage to Change/medical detox services provide drug and alcohol detox, addiction treatment, inpatient/residential addiction medicine, IOP substance-abuse track, case management, and 24/7 nursing support.
resources.hours: 24/7 service is advertised for the facility; call for admissions and bed availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Drug and alcohol detox, Courage to Change addiction treatment, individual and group therapy, inpatient/residential addiction medicine treatment, substance-abuse IOP track, case management, medical detox, and 24/7 registered nursing for detox patients.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Call for assessment, medical necessity, insurance/payment, bed availability, and whether detox or IOP is appropriate. The facility says most insurance is accepted and DHHS material lists financial assistance for those who need it.

**Population Served**

Adults in South Salt Lake and Salt Lake County needing detox, addiction treatment, or substance-abuse IOP assessment.

**How to Best Connect**

Use 801-264-6000 as the official home-page phone. Mention 801-455-3431 only as a program-specific/search-supported contact pending confirmation.

**Important Information to Know**

This is private-hospital care. Admission depends on clinical assessment, payment or insurance arrangements and bed availability. Confirm the current intake contact and address before travelling.
resources.name: Salt Lake Behavioral Health Courage to Change Program

resources.address: 3802 S 700 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84015
resources.description: Salt Lake Behavioral Health is an inpatient behavioral-health center offering adult mental health, adolescent mental health, crisis stabilization, medical detox, drug rehabilitation, and a military trauma unit, with same-day appointments and walk-ins accepted.
resources.hours: 24/7 service; same-day appointments and walk-ins advertised.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Acute psychiatric care for adults with suicidal thoughts, self-harm, depression, anxiety, and related needs; adolescent mental-health care for youth ages 12-18; crisis stabilization for acute psychiatric problems such as psychosis, delusions, and hallucinations; plus medical detox, drug rehabilitation, and military trauma services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call for assessment, payer verification, and level-of-care fit. Adolescents are listed as ages 12-18. Walk-ins are accepted, but admission depends on clinical appropriateness and capacity.

**Population Served**
Adults and adolescents in the Salt Lake City area needing inpatient, acute, or crisis behavioral-health treatment; active-duty and veteran clients may fit the military trauma unit.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-264-6000, use the online contact form, or walk in. The facility is at 3802 S 700 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84015 as listed on the official page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a low-cost outpatient counseling provider by default. Confirm insurance, financial responsibility, age fit, and whether inpatient or outpatient care is clinically appropriate.
resources.name: Salt Lake Behavioral Health Inpatient Behavioral Health Center

resources.address: 449 E 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Salt Lake City Comprehensive Treatment Center provides outpatient medication-assisted treatment and counseling for adults 18 and older with opioid-use disorder, including methadone, buprenorphine, Suboxone, and counseling.
resources.hours: 24/7 appointment scheduling by phone; online page showed same-day walk-in language but also said direct online scheduling may be unavailable, so call first.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient opioid addiction treatment with medication-assisted treatment and counseling. Medication options listed include methadone, buprenorphine, and Suboxone; services also include individual and group counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults age 18 and older of all genders who are struggling with opioid-use disorder. Intake includes evaluation and consultation with medical staff. Payments accepted include commercial insurance, self-pay, Medicaid, Medicare, and Veterans Affairs.

**Population Served**
Adults in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County seeking outpatient opioid-use treatment and medication support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 844-714-0335 for 24/7 appointment scheduling and intake help. The clinic is at 449 E 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84115.

**Important Information to Know**
The page says this location may be unable to schedule direct appointments through the online form and instructs people to use phone or chat for assistance. Verify same-day admission, dosing hours, pregnancy needs, and accepted insurance before referral.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Comprehensive Treatment Center

resources.address: Richmond Park, 444 E 600 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City Food Not Bombs is a mutual-aid food recovery distribution at Richmond Park on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday mornings until supplies run out.
resources.hours: Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday at 11:00 AM until supplies run out, per Salt Lake City Sustainability's 2023 article.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free recovered food distribution at Richmond Park. Volunteers set out food items and community members line up to choose items while supplies last.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Salt Lake City Sustainability quotes the group as serving the public with no required citizenship, ID, income proof, or documentation threshold.

**Population Served**
Members of the public in Salt Lake City, especially people experiencing poverty, limited food access, unsheltered homelessness, or informal shelter.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to Richmond Park, 444 E 600 S, Salt Lake City, on Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday at 11:00 AM. No program phone was found in the opened source.

**Important Information to Know**
Food is available until supplies run out, so arriving on time matters. Delivery support was mentioned in submitted city microgrant evidence but was not confirmed on the opened 2023 article; use the park distribution as the supported route.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Food Not Bombs Free Food Distribution

resources.address: Sorenson Computer Center, 1383 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Salt Lake City Information Management Services lists free public Wi-Fi locations and free computer access sites, including Sorenson Computer Center and Salt Lake City Public Library branches/computer labs.
resources.hours: Sorenson Computer Center open access hours listed Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-9:00 PM, Friday 9:00 AM-8:00 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; other site hours vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free public Wi-Fi and free computer access at listed Salt Lake City locations. The city lists Wi-Fi access at sites such as Sorenson Unity Center, YouthCity Liberty Park, SLCPD Pioneer Patrol Division, and Regional Athletic Complex, plus computer access at Sorenson Computer Center and Salt Lake City Public Library branches.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No income eligibility is listed for public Wi-Fi or open computer access. Users must follow site rules and availability limits.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake City who need temporary internet or computer access, including visitors and residents who cannot use home internet.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit one of the listed public Wi-Fi or computer sites during open hours. For Sorenson Computer Center questions, call 801-535-6529.

**Important Information to Know**
This is public access, not home internet service. Hours, computer availability, library branch schedules, printing, and account requirements may vary by site.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Free Public Wi-Fi and Computer Access

resources.address: 451 S State St, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City's Future Citizens PATH Program is a free citizenship pathway for eligible green-card holders living within Salt Lake City, including citizenship classes, interview and test preparation, legal help with naturalization and fee-waiver applications, and possible application-fee support.
resources.hours: Current class locations and times are provided after contacting program staff.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free citizenship support including a legal team to complete and submit citizenship and fee-waiver applications, assistance with application fees, 12 weeks of citizenship classes, civic education, and interview and test preparation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must live within Salt Lake City boundaries, be eligible green-card holders seeking U.S. citizenship, have basic English skills around ESL level 2 or higher, meet USCIS naturalization requirements, attend at least 75% of classes, complete 20 hours of civic community service, and attend legal-team appointments.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City residents who are lawful permanent residents and are preparing for U.S. citizenship.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the official interest form. Questions can go to the program email on the page or 801-535-6381; language access services are available. The page says a new class session has started and to email for current locations and times.

**Important Information to Know**
This program is limited to Salt Lake City residents, so it is not a countywide citizenship route. It is a pilot program, and class timing and grant availability may change.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Future Citizens PATH Program

resources.address: 2975 South Decker Lake Drive, Suite 200, West Valley City, UT 84119-6094
resources.description: The Salt Lake City Immigration Court is the EOIR court serving Salt Lake City-area immigration proceedings, with public hours, window filing hours, court contact information, operational-status information, and EOIR resources for people in immigration-court proceedings.
resources.hours: Public hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; window filing hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM, except federal holidays or emergency closures.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official immigration-court procedural access for people in removal or immigration-court proceedings, including filing window access, hearing information, court contact information, and links to EOIR resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with matters before the Salt Lake City Immigration Court or people needing official procedural information about that court. The court does not provide private legal advice or representation.

**Population Served**
People with immigration-court proceedings assigned to the Salt Lake City Immigration Court, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the EOIR Salt Lake City Immigration Court page for current court information and operational-status updates. The court is at 2975 South Decker Lake Drive, Suite 200, West Valley City, and the listed court phone in EOIR materials is 801-524-3000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a court, not a legal-services provider. People in proceedings should also seek qualified legal help as early as possible because court deadlines can be strict.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Immigration Court and EOIR Online Resource

resources.address: John L. Baxter Courthouse, 333 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; events rotate at Salt Lake City community locations
resources.description: Salt Lake City Justice Court Homeless Outreach Court helps people experiencing homelessness or similar housing instability resolve eligible Salt Lake City Justice Court cases and connect with legal help and community resources.
resources.hours: Outreach events rotate; resource fairs are listed for the second Friday of each month January-November. Call the court or check the current schedule before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outreach court events for eligible Salt Lake City Justice Court cases, access to legal help, UTA civil Transit Police ticket help at events, and connection to community resources such as jobs, benefits, health care, and housing-related help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people who are homeless or living in supportive housing, sober living, treatment centers, or other community places and who have eligible Salt Lake City Justice Court cases. The court generally cannot handle cases from other courts except some 3rd District Court cases when allowed and a judge is available.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or similar housing instability with Salt Lake City Justice Court cases.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake City Justice Court at 801-535-6300 or check the Homeless Outreach Court schedule before attending. Events rotate among Salt Lake City locations such as Workforce Services, Pioneer Park, Weigand Resource Center, and Library Square.

**Important Information to Know**
The outreach court excludes DUI-related charges, battery or assault, and domestic violence cases, except possible warrant recall when allowed. Spanish interpreter service is listed for first-Friday Homeless Outreach Court; call ahead for interpreter needs or a regular court date.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Justice Court Homeless Outreach Court

resources.description: Salt Lake City Public Utilities' Lead and Copper Program lets customers report service-line material and may provide free water sampling and lead service line replacement when SLCDPU confirms and prioritizes an eligible line.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lead service line identification, water-service-line survey, possible free water sample testing, and lead service line replacement through Salt Lake City Department of Public Utilities' Lead and Copper Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Property must be in the Salt Lake City Department of Public Utilities service area and have a service line that SLCDPU identifies or prioritizes for replacement. Eligibility depends on service-line material, property details, and the program schedule.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City Department of Public Utilities customers and property owners in the SLCDPU service area, including Salt Lake City and nearby areas served by SLCDPU.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online service-line material survey on the Lead and Copper Program website. For questions, contact Salt Lake City Public Utilities at 801-483-6900.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not bill-payment help. Replacement timing depends on confirmed service-line material, program prioritization, and city scheduling.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Lead and Copper Program / Lead Service Line Replacement

resources.address: Meeting location listed: Questar Gas Company, 1140 West 200 South, Salt Lake City, UT
resources.description: Salt Lake City Lions Club's Gift of Sight program provides eye examinations and eyeglasses for people in need in the Salt Lake City area, with an email contact for eyeglass assistance.
resources.hours: Club meetings listed as 1st and 3rd Thursday at 12:00 noon; email first for eyeglass assistance rather than going to the meeting location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Eye examinations and eyeglasses for people in need in the Salt Lake City area through the club's Gift of Sight eyeglass program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page states the program serves people in need in the Salt Lake City area. Detailed income, documentation, and funding rules are not posted publicly.

**Population Served**
People in the Salt Lake City area who need help obtaining an eye exam or eyeglasses.

**How to Best Connect**
Email slclions@gmail.com for assistance with eyeglasses. The e-Clubhouse page lists meetings at Questar Gas Company, 1140 West 200 South, Salt Lake City, but the meeting address should not be treated as a clinic or guaranteed intake site.

**Important Information to Know**
The page is current but some program text references older service counts. Confirm current funding, application steps, and appointment process by email before making a referral.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Lions Club Gift of Sight Eyeglass Program

resources.address: 451 S. State Street, #445, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City Housing Stability Division's Minor Repairs Program provides free funding up to $1,500 for small home repairs for low-income Salt Lake City homeowners whose household includes a senior age 62+ or a person with a disability.
resources.hours: Applications are open year-round online through Neighborly; call if help applying by phone is needed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free funding for small home repairs and maintenance through the Minor Repairs Program, up to $1,500 per household. The broader Fix Your Home page also describes Home Repairs loans for larger health, safety and structural repairs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be a Salt Lake City resident/homeowner, occupy the home needing repairs, have household income at or below 80% AMI, and have someone in the home who is a senior or has a disability. For this program, senior means at least age 62.

**Population Served**
Low-income Salt Lake City homeowners, including households with older adults age 62+ or a person with a disability.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Neighborly portal from the Minor Repairs page. For questions or help applying by phone, call 801-535-7233 or email housingstability@slc.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
The city states the application process takes about three months and repairs are free if approved. Required documents include photo ID, proof of disability if applicable, homeowner insurance and household income documents.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Minor Repairs Program

resources.address: 1151 S Redwood Road Suite #106, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Salt Lake City Mission operates a Food Pantry and Clothing Room that provides food boxes, clothing, school supplies, and other necessities to struggling neighbors and low-income families in Salt Lake City.
resources.hours: Mission general hours 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; food pantry hours Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 11:00 AM-2:00 PM on the current page, with another line mentioning the food pantry and clothing room Monday-Friday 11:00 AM-2:00 PM. Call or use the appointment scheduler before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Food boxes through Salt Lake City Mission's Food Pantry and Clothing Room. The same program also provides clothing, school supplies, and other necessities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
