The page describes help for struggling neighbors, low-income families, and people experiencing homelessness. It does not list income documents or visit limits on the opened page.

**Population Served**

People in Salt Lake City and surrounding communities who need food boxes or related basic necessities.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-355-6310, use the Food Pantry Appointment Scheduler linked from the provider page, or stop by 1151 S Redwood Road Suite #106. The page lists general Mission hours as 8:00 AM-3:00 PM and food pantry hours as 11:00 AM-2:00 PM on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

**Important Information to Know**

Published schedules differ. Call to confirm current food-pantry and clothing-room hours before travelling; supplies depend on availability.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Mission Food Pantry & Clothing Room

resources.address: 475 South 300 East, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City Police Department's Community Connection Center includes social workers/case workers and the Homeless Outreach Service Team, connecting people in Salt Lake City to individualized support, care coordination, case management, housing-application and navigation assistance, basic needs, behavioral-health navigation, and social-service resources. It is appointment-based, not walk-in.
resources.hours: Outreach response is weekdays during business hours through dispatch. Appointments by phone or email; the center is no longer walk-in.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Social-worker and case-worker support, care coordination, short-term therapeutic intervention, case management, housing application and navigation assistance, basic-needs connection, behavioral-health navigation, and Homeless Outreach Service Team connection to homeless social services and resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people in Salt Lake City who need individualized care, support, or community resources, including people experiencing homelessness or families/individuals in crisis. Outreach response is city-based and depends on dispatch and staffing.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake City, including individuals and families experiencing homelessness, crisis, behavioral-health needs, or basic-needs barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
To schedule an appointment, call 801-799-3533 or email communityconnectionteam@slc.gov. For outreach response on weekdays during business hours, call dispatch at 801-799-3000. Do not walk in; the center states it is no longer a walk-in facility.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency shelter and not a substitute for 911. Because it is police-department connected, consider client safety, warrants, immigration concerns, and comfort before using this route.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Police Department Community Connection Center / Homeless Outreach Service Team

resources.address: 475 South 300 East, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City Police Department Victim Advocate Program accepts U-visa certification and T-visa declaration requests connected to SLCPD matters from victims, nonprofit agencies, and law firms. Advocates help prepare supplemental forms and process requests for the certifying official.
resources.hours: Walk-in hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; advocate hotline 24/7; text line Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-10:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
U-visa certification and T-visa declaration request processing for qualifying crime or trafficking victims connected to Salt Lake City Police Department matters. Victim advocates help prepare Form I-918 Supplement B or Form I-914 Supplement B requests and process them for the certifying official.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For victims, nonprofit agencies, or law firms requesting U-visa or T-visa certification related to SLCPD. The certification is only one piece of an immigration case; USCIS decides the immigration benefit.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City crime victims, including victims who may qualify for U-visa or T-visa certification through SLCPD.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text the victim advocate hotline at 801-580-7969, meet with an advocate in person at the Public Safety Building, email through the victim-services page, or mail a written request to the Victim Advocate Program at Salt Lake City Police Department, PO Box 145497, SLC UT 84114-5497.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not immigration legal representation and does not submit the visa petition for the client. It is the local law-enforcement certification/declaration route when SLCPD is the appropriate certifying agency.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Police U-Visa and T-Visa Certification Requests

resources.description: Salt Lake City Prosecutor's Office handles Salt Lake City misdemeanor domestic-violence prosecutions and has a victim assistant contact for victims involved in those cases, with related support and coordination listed through the SLCPD victim-services resource page.
resources.hours: Call during business hours; co-location or advocate availability should be confirmed before sending a client in person.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victim-services contact for Salt Lake City misdemeanor prosecution matters, including domestic-violence cases handled by the City Prosecutor's Office. Public victim-services information links this route to case questions, court-process support, referrals, and coordination with other victim-service systems.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for victims in misdemeanor cases occurring in Salt Lake City that are handled by the Salt Lake City Prosecutor's Office. People represented by an attorney in a current prosecution case must work through their attorney for case questions.

**Population Served**
Victims connected to Salt Lake City misdemeanor criminal cases, including domestic violence cases occurring in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
For the victim assistant, call 385-468-7513 or text/call 385-321-6318. The City Prosecutor's Office main number is 385-468-7900. Confirm which advocate handles the case before relying on a specific staff contact.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a confidential shelter or community advocacy program. The City Prosecutor's Office is managed by the Salt Lake County District Attorney's Office under an interlocal agreement, so case routing can depend on whether the matter is city misdemeanor, county felony, or another jurisdiction.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Prosecutor's Office Victim Advocate / Victim Services for Domestic Violence Misdemeanor Cases

resources.description: Salt Lake City Public Library lists T-Mobile Wi-Fi hotspot kits for checkout by eligible adult cardholders, subject to very limited inventory, holds, and replacement-cost rules.
resources.hours: Available through Salt Lake City Public Library checkout when inventory is available; branch hours vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
T-Mobile Wi-Fi hotspot kits for temporary checkout through Salt Lake City Public Library. The kit is intended to provide mobile internet access while borrowed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Borrower must be age 18 or older, use their own valid Basic or Expanded Salt Lake City Public Library card, present photo ID, have an account in good standing, have held the card for at least 90 days, and sign or acknowledge the hotspot checkout agreement.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City Public Library cardholders who need short-term mobile internet access and meet adult checkout requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Search or place a hold through the library catalog, or contact a Salt Lake City Public Library branch for help. Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County residents can apply for a City Library card free of charge.

**Important Information to Know**
Inventory is very limited and holds may be high. Borrowers are responsible for loss or damage; listed replacement costs include the hotspot, charger/adapter, and case.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Public Library Hotspot Checkout

resources.address: 210 E 400 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City Public Library's Main Library offers staff-taught computer classes and Creative Lab classes, plus access to digital media equipment for eligible library cardholders.
resources.hours: Main Library hours vary by day; check the current branch or event page before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Computer Lab classes taught by library staff, ranging from beginner computer skills such as mouse use to Microsoft PowerPoint and other topics. The Creative Lab offers classes and access to equipment and software for video, audio, photography, and 3D media projects.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Computer and Creative Lab classes are public classes. The Creative Lab requires a current Basic or Expanded Salt Lake City Public Library card in good standing to use lab equipment, but a library card is not required to attend Creative Lab classes.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County residents who can attend classes at the Main Library; library-card rules apply for equipment use.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the Salt Lake City Public Library event calendar for current computer or Creative Lab classes, or call the Main Library at 801-524-8200. Some classes require registration.

**Important Information to Know**
Class topics, registration windows, and availability change by event calendar. This is class and lab access, not one-on-one case management or formal credential training.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Public Library Main Library Computer and Creative Lab Classes

resources.address: 210 East 400 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Official passport application acceptance facility at the Salt Lake City Main Library for first-time, child, older, name-change, and lost or stolen prior passport applications, with walk-in service and passport photos for a fee.
resources.hours: Mon-Thu 3:00 PM-7:00 PM; Fri 1:00 PM-5:00 PM; Sat 10:00 AM-5:00 PM; Sun noon-4:00 PM, subject to holiday closures.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Salt Lake City Public Library Passport Services is an official passport application acceptance facility. It accepts in-person passport applications and passport card applications, including cases where the most recent passport was lost or stolen, was issued more than 15 years ago, was issued before age 16, or a name change cannot be legally documented for renewal.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must bring a completed unsigned DS-11, proof of identity, proof of U.S. citizenship, a photo, and required payments. Minors may require additional documentation and parent presence.

**Population Served**
People applying for a U.S. passport or passport card who can use the Main Library acceptance facility.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk in during passport office hours at the Main Library, Level 3, 210 East 400 South, Salt Lake City. Call the library at 801-524-8200 for general questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a passport acceptance facility, not a same-day passport agency. Two separate payments are required. The library can take passport photos for a fee. Processing times depend on the U.S. Department of State.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Public Library Passport Services at Main Library

resources.address: Main Library, 210 East 400 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Main Library Resource Corner and Library Social Worker access point for practical Utah ID, Social Security card, and birth certificate navigation, including ID and birth-certificate voucher routes identified by the library's social-services page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Salt Lake City Public Library's Social Services Resources page provides step-by-step guidance for Utah ID cards, Social Security cards, and birth certificates. It identifies the Library Social Worker as a source for ID vouchers and birth certificate vouchers, and the Resource Corner as a Main Library access point for resource navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The ID and birth certificate guidance is aimed at people needing replacement documents, especially people without stable documents. Voucher availability and eligibility should be confirmed with the Library Social Worker or Resource Corner.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County library patrons and community members needing help navigating ID, Social Security card, or birth certificate replacement steps.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Resource Corner on Level 1 of the Main Library near the fireplaces, or call the City Library at 801-524-8200 and ask how to connect with the Library Social Worker or Resource Corner.

**Important Information to Know**
The library page is a practical access point and navigation resource, not a guarantee that a voucher or fee payment will be available on demand. Hours and partner schedules may change.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Public Library Resource Corner and Library Social Worker

resources.description: Salt Lake City Public Utilities states that customers who qualify for the Salt Lake County Tax Abatement Program are eligible for reductions in water, garbage, and stormwater charges.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Reduced Salt Lake City Public Utilities charges for eligible customers, specifically reductions in water, garbage, and stormwater charges tied to Salt Lake County Tax Abatement Program qualification.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Customer must qualify for the Salt Lake County Tax Abatement Program. The public utility page does not fully explain applicability for renters or non-owner utility account holders.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City Public Utilities customers who qualify for Salt Lake County tax abatement/property tax relief.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County at 385-468-8300 option 2 for abatement information. Customers should also contact Salt Lake City Public Utilities at 801-483-6900 to confirm how the reduction is applied to their utility account.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a bill reduction route, not emergency assistance or a grant. Confirm eligibility with Salt Lake County and Salt Lake City Public Utilities before relying on the reduction.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Public Utilities Bill Reductions / Abatements

resources.address: Glendale-Mountain View CLC: 1388 S Navajo St, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; Rose Park CLC: 1105 W 1000 N, Salt Lake City, UT 84116; Liberty CLC: 1078 S 300 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City School District Community Learning Centers operate mobile/community food pantries at Glendale-Mountain View, Rose Park, and Liberty CLCs.
resources.hours: Glendale-Mountain View CLC: 2nd Thursday 1:30-2:30 PM or while supplies last; Rose Park CLC: 1st and 3rd Monday 2:15-3:00 PM or while supplies last; Liberty CLC: 3rd Wednesday after the first Monday of each month 2:00-3:00 PM or while supplies last.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Learning Center food assistance through mobile/community food pantries at three Salt Lake City School District CLC sites.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The district food-resources page says any member of the community can come to one of the CLCs to receive food assistance during the listed days and times.

**Population Served**
Community members and families who can reach the Glendale-Mountain View, Rose Park, or Liberty CLC pantry sites in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Go during the posted pantry window: Glendale-Mountain View CLC, 2nd Thursday 1:30-2:30 PM; Rose Park CLC, 1st and 3rd Monday 2:15-3:00 PM; Liberty CLC, 3rd Wednesday after the first Monday of each month 2:00-3:00 PM. All are while supplies last.

**Important Information to Know**
These are scheduled distributions and may run out. They are distinct from school lunch benefits and are open to community members under the district's current food-resources page.
resources.name: Salt Lake City School District CLC Food Support and Pantries

resources.address: 440 E 100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City School District McKinney-Vento liaisons help students and families who lack fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime housing access school enrollment, stability, and supports. The district publishes direct liaison contacts and multilingual McKinney-Vento questionnaires.
resources.hours: Contact liaisons during school business hours; families can also work through the student's school office.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
McKinney-Vento student homelessness support, including help with school access, enrollment, stability, and support coordination for students lacking fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime housing. The district provides multilingual questionnaires and direct liaison contacts.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For students and families connected to Salt Lake City School District who lack fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime housing, including situations such as staying in shelters, motels, cars, parks, abandoned buildings, substandard housing, or doubled-up due to hardship.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City School District students and families experiencing homelessness or housing instability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call McKinney-Vento liaison Becky Baskett at 385-518-4818 or Mike Harman at 801-243-8351, email the liaison, or ask the student's school office for McKinney-Vento support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is district-specific. Families whose children attend or should attend Granite, Murray, Canyons, Jordan, or another district need that district's homeless liaison instead.
resources.name: Salt Lake City School District McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Liaisons

resources.address: 406 East 100 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City School District preschool evaluation access for children ages 3-5 with concerns across communication, motor, cognition, social/emotional, or adaptive development.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Preschool special education evaluations for children ages 3-5 across communication, motor, cognition, social/emotional, and adaptive skill domains. Parent intake forms are available in English and Spanish.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children ages 3-5 living in Salt Lake City School District boundaries with developmental concerns. Other Salt Lake County families should contact their resident school district.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City School District families with preschool-age children who may need special education evaluation or services.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the parent intake form on the Pre-K Services page. Call the district at 801-578-8599 for general help; the district index lists the Pre-school Special Education Evaluation Team at 801-578-8134.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not the front door for all Salt Lake County districts. Children younger than 3 are typically served through early intervention rather than district preschool special education.
resources.name: Salt Lake City School District Pre-K Services: Preschool Special Education Evaluations

resources.address: 501 E 1700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
resources.description: CDCU's Tenant Resource Center provides one-on-one rental counseling and housing navigation, with RAFT relocation assistance for qualifying low-income Salt Lake City renter households displaced by specific landlord-caused reasons.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free one-on-one rental counseling and community navigation for renters needing help finding affordable housing, accessing rental-assistance referrals, handling landlord issues, preventing eviction, reporting unsafe housing, or understanding day-to-day rental concerns. RAFT may provide relocation funds for eligible Salt Lake City renters displaced by demolition, major renovation, change of use, or expiration of income/rent restrictions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CDCU says the program started with Salt Lake City renters but aims to support anyone who reaches out. RAFT is limited to low-income Salt Lake City renter households at or below 80% AMI and only for the listed displacement reasons.

**Population Served**
Renters seeking housing navigation or tenant support, with RAFT specifically for Salt Lake City renter households facing qualifying landlord-caused displacement.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete CDCU's Community Resource Support Request or Tenant Resource Center intake form, call 801-893-3779, or visit a Navigator at 501 E 1700 S, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
CDCU states it does not currently have general rental-assistance funds except RAFT. RAFT is not a general rent-shortfall or ordinary eviction fund.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Tenant Resource Center and RAFT Relocation Assistance

resources.address: 550 Foothill Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84158
resources.description: The Salt Lake City VA Regional Benefit Office helps veterans, service members, and families access VA benefits, schedule VERA appointments, and get guidance on claims, pensions, VR&E, representatives, and decision reviews.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday. Service hours may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Benefit counseling and access help for VA disability compensation, education benefits, life insurance, pension, home loans, claim status, direct deposit, accredited representatives, homelessness-related VA connections, VR&E information, and decision review or appeal options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans, service members, family members, survivors, and caregivers seeking VA benefits or review of a VA decision. Specific benefits have separate VA eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Utah-area veterans, service members, survivors, caregivers, and family members who need VA benefits help.

**How to Best Connect**
Schedule a virtual or in-person VERA appointment online, visit the office, or call the VA benefits hotline at 800-827-1000. Bring current photo ID and relevant documents such as DD214, medical records, Social Security number, direct deposit information, and dependent information.

**Important Information to Know**
Walk-in and appointment availability can vary by service. Decision reviews have different tracks and deadlines, and accredited representatives can help choose the right option.
resources.name: Salt Lake City VA Regional Benefit Office and VERA Appointments

resources.address: 84 West 4800 South, Suite 100, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: No-cost confidential non-medical counseling for eligible veterans, service members, and family members, including PTSD, depression, grief, readjustment, military sexual trauma support, telehealth, and same-day crisis response.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; non-traditional hours may change. 24/7 Vet Center call center: 877-927-8387.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost confidential counseling in a non-medical setting, including individual, group, couples, and family counseling; support for PTSD, depression, grief, anger, trauma, readjustment, and military sexual trauma; telehealth and virtual visits; and referrals to VA or community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Vet Center eligibility is broader than ordinary VA health-care enrollment. Clients do not need to be enrolled in VA care, rated service-connected, or receiving VA benefits, but they must have qualifying service or meet Vet Center eligibility such as combat/hostility service, eligible reserve status, military sexual trauma, covered VA education-benefit use, or eligible family/bereavement criteria.

**Population Served**
Veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, eligible family members, and eligible bereaved family members in the Salt Lake area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-266-1499 to schedule or call the 24/7 Vet Center call center at 877-927-8387 after hours. Walk-ins are welcome, appointments are preferred, and anyone in crisis will be seen the same day. The center is at 84 West 4800 South, Suite 100, Murray.

**Important Information to Know**
Vet Centers are community-based counseling centers, not VA medical clinics. Bring service documents if available, but the center says staff can work with clients who do not have documents on hand.
resources.name: Salt Lake City Vet Center

resources.address: 451 S State St, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake City YouthCity Employment is a free career-readiness, workforce-readiness, and internship pathway for Salt Lake City high school students and youth, including afterschool programming and paid city department internships for eligible teens.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free career exploration, workforce readiness, professional skills, career pathway planning, resume development, workforce trainings, youth internships, and connections with Salt Lake City departments and community professionals. The 2026-2027 afterschool program runs September 28, 2026-April 14, 2027.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Afterschool programming is for Salt Lake City high school students with pathways for 9th-10th and 11th-12th graders. Summer youth internships are open to Salt Lake City youth in grades 7-12; paid city department internships require ages 16-18 and work eligibility.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City youth and high school students seeking career readiness, supervised work-based learning, and paid internship experience.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Register Now link on the YouthCity Employment page or call the Senior Community Programs Manager at 385-309-7439. City Hall is listed at 451 S State St, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Some summer internship levels are unpaid, while paid city department internships are an 8-week opportunity with schedules varying by department. Availability is limited by program year, age, grade, work eligibility, and cohort capacity.
resources.name: Salt Lake City YouthCity Employment

resources.address: 389 S 900 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: Intermountain Salt Lake Clinic LGBTQ+ Primary Care provides affirming primary care for LGBTQ+ patients and people with LGBTQ+ health-related concerns, including preventive care, STI/HIV prevention, PrEP/PEP, adult gender-affirming hormone therapy, behavioral health screening, labs/X-ray, and virtual follow-up options.
resources.hours: Hours were not displayed in the accessible page; call the clinic to schedule and confirm availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
LGBTQ+ affirming primary care, preventive care and wellness, chronic-condition management, screenings, immunizations, nutrition support, STI testing/prevention/treatment, HIV care, PrEP and PEP, mental and behavioral health screening and referrals, onsite labs and X-ray, adult gender-affirming hormone therapy, lab monitoring, and virtual follow-up options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic states it can only see patients who are members of the LGBTQ+ community or who have LGBTQ+ health-related concerns because of specialty focus and limited availability. Most patients do not need a referral for hormone therapy.

**Population Served**
LGBTQ+ adolescents and adults, and people with LGBTQ+ health-related concerns, in Salt Lake City and statewide Utah for eligible virtual services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-282-2600. The clinic is at 389 S 900 E, Salt Lake City. Ask about new-patient availability, insurance, financial assistance, and whether the visit can be virtual.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general low-income clinic; costs depend on insurance and financial-assistance eligibility. Gender-affirming care listed on the page is age 18+ for hormone therapy services.
resources.name: Salt Lake Clinic LGBTQ+ Primary Care

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: Salt Lake Community College Adult Learner Admissions Advisors help adults returning to school or changing careers understand admissions steps, submit applications, connect to departments, explore FAFSA and scholarships, and consider prior learning credit.
resources.hours: Student Services hours listed Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; enrollment info Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-8:00 PM, Friday 7:30 AM-4:30 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Admissions advising for adults returning to school, changing careers, finishing a degree, starting a new career, or exploring options. Advisors help with admissions steps, submitting applications, finding SLCC resources, program and campus questions, connecting to the right department, FAFSA assistance, scholarships, and prior learning credit information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For prospective or returning adult SLCC students. Program admission, tuition, financial aid, and placement requirements depend on the chosen SLCC program.

**Population Served**
Adult learners in the Salt Lake area considering SLCC programs, including people balancing work, family, or time away from school.

**How to Best Connect**
Schedule an adult learner admissions appointment online or call general enrollment help at 801-957-4073. The main campus address is 4600 S Redwood Road.

**Important Information to Know**
This is advising and admissions navigation, not direct tuition assistance or guaranteed admission to a program.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Adult Learner Admissions Advisors

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Student Center Room 002K, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC's Bruin Closet is a free clothing resource at the Taylorsville Redwood Campus with professional, casual, trade-specific, outerwear, footwear, and accessory items for students, staff, faculty, and community members as inventory allows.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free clean, gently used or new clothing for job interviews, internships, presentations, career fairs, work, school, and everyday life. Common inventory includes business/professional clothing, casual clothing, trade-specific wear, outerwear, footwear, accessories, and new socks when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students, staff, and faculty may take up to 10 items per semester. Community members may use the closet as inventory allows. If inventory is low, SLCC may prioritize students or temporarily limit community access.

**Population Served**
SLCC students, staff, faculty, and Salt Lake County community members needing clothing for school, work, interviews, or daily life.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Taylorsville Redwood Campus Student Center, Room 002K, during open hours. No appointment is needed and no sign-in is required; visitors tell staff how many items they are taking. Call Career Services at 801-957-4014 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Inventory is donation-based, first-come, first-served, and specific sizes or items are not guaranteed. Community access can be limited when inventory is low.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Bruin Closet

resources.address: SLCC campuses: Taylorsville Redwood, South City, and Jordan campuses
resources.description: Salt Lake Community College child care and family support for student parents, including campus child care sites, child care voucher assistance, family resources, and parent training/workshops.
resources.hours: South City child care listed Monday-Thursday 6:45 AM-10 PM and Friday 6:45 AM-5:30 PM; other site hours vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Campus child care, child care voucher assistance, parent resources, training and workshops, and family resources for SLCC student parents. Sites include Taylorsville Redwood, South City, and Jordan campuses.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed to assist Salt Lake Community College student parents. Some child care sites also serve staff, faculty, or community members depending on the site, but student-parent support is the main purpose. CCAMPIS discounted child care funds are income-based where available.

**Population Served**
SLCC student parents and their children; age ranges vary by child care site.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the relevant campus child care site. South City/Tim and Brenda Huval Child Care Center: 801-957-3070. Eccles Early Childhood Development Lab School: 801-957-4567. Jordan Campus Child Care Center: 801-957-6030 or email wendy.blanchard@slcc.edu and/or mhall18@slcc.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
Current openings, subsidy rules, child age eligibility, and rates vary by site. Most income-eligible students may pay no cost at the South City site when CCAMPIS grant funds are available.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Child Care and Family Services

resources.address: SLCC Jordan Campus, 3491 W Wights Fort Rd, High Tech Learning Center Room 173, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: Salt Lake Community College Dental Hygiene Clinic provides affordable preventive dental hygiene care in West Jordan, with services performed by students under licensed professional supervision.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:45 AM-11:45 AM and 12:45 PM-4:45 PM. Closed during summer semester, May-September. Scheduled appointments preferred; walk-ins only as available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Preventive dental hygiene care, including exam, cleaning, X-rays, fluoride, oral cancer screening, periodontal evaluation, sealants, home-care education, nutritional counseling, tobacco cessation, referral for restorative treatment, and optional additional services such as deep cleaning, prescription fluoride toothpaste, chlorhexidine rinse, and nitrous oxide for added fees.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to adults, seniors, children and teens ages 3-17, and SLCC students/faculty/staff. Dental insurance is not required or billed. Fees vary by population and service.

**Population Served**
Community members who can use the SLCC Jordan Campus clinic for preventive dental hygiene care, including children, teens, adults, seniors, and SLCC students/staff.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-957-6001 for clinic information and appointments. Scheduled appointments are preferred; walk-ins are taken only if availability allows.

**Important Information to Know**
This clinic does not provide emergency or general dentistry such as root canals, fillings, extractions, implants, or dentures. Treatment may take more than one visit and the clinic is closed during summer semester.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Dental Hygiene Clinic

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: The SLCC Dream Center provides individualized advising, mentorship, scholarship support, resource brokering, and policy navigation for students facing college barriers related to relocating to a new country, immigration status, or mixed-status family circumstances.
resources.hours: Summer 2026 Dream Center hours listed Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM; confirm current term hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individualized advising and mentorship, scholarship support, resource brokership, and policy navigation and advocacy for SLCC students and prospective students facing barriers related to relocation to a new country or immigration-status-related higher education issues.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for SLCC students and prospective students who need support navigating college access, in-state tuition, scholarships, and policies affected by immigration or relocation history. The public page does not list a separate income requirement.

**Population Served**
SLCC students and prospective students, including undocumented students, students from mixed-status families, immigrants, asylum seekers, and people with related relocation histories.

**How to Best Connect**
Start from the Dream Center page or SLCC application links, or call SLCC enrollment help at 801-957-4073 and ask for Dream Center connection.

**Important Information to Know**
This is education access and policy navigation within SLCC, not general immigration legal representation.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Dream Center

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Markosian Library Room 017, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC's GED Testing Center is an official local GED testing site where test-takers register through GED.com, schedule an appointment, pay GED testing fees, and bring required identification for the exam.
resources.hours: Testing is by scheduled appointment through GED.com and the testing center process.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GED testing access at SLCC's Testing Center. The SLCC page explains GED.com registration, appointment scheduling, payment, ID requirements, parking, and transcript requests.

**Eligibility Requirements**
GED test-takers must be at least 16. In Utah, test-takers age 16-18 whose high-school class has not graduated need permission from their school district's Adult Education Program before they can register online for the GED.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County and Utah GED test-takers who need an in-person testing location.

**How to Best Connect**
Register, schedule, and pay at GED.com first. For more information, call the GED Testing Center at 801-957-4627. Go to Markosian Library Room 017 at 4600 S Redwood Road for the scheduled test.

**Important Information to Know**
This is GED testing, not GED preparation or tutoring. Bring a valid government-issued photo ID on test day. Parking costs may apply.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College GED Testing Center

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC's PACE Scholarship Program is a college-readiness and scholarship pathway for eligible low-income and first-generation high-school students at participating Salt Lake County high schools, providing four years of mentorship and up to a six-semester SLCC scholarship after completion.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Four years of one-on-one mentorship, college-readiness skills, study and time-management support, career exploration, workshops, campus tours, and up to a six-semester scholarship to Salt Lake Community College after successful completion.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For eligible students at participating Salt Lake County high schools. Submitted program evidence identified incoming 9th-grade students at Cottonwood, East, Granger, Highland, Kearns, and West; confirm the current participating schools and application timing before applying.

**Population Served**
Low-income and first-generation Salt Lake County high-school students at participating schools.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply to PACE link on the SLCC PACE page or call SLCC enrollment information at 801-957-4073 for routing to the PACE office.

**Important Information to Know**
PACE is not a general adult scholarship. It is a multi-year high-school pathway, and application timing is narrow.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College PACE Scholarship Program

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: SLCC Utah Works offers tuition-free short-term workforce training through Talent Ready Utah in advanced manufacturing fields such as composites technician, injection molding technician, and aerospace assembly.
resources.hours: SLCC Student Services hours Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; Enrollment Info Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-8:00 PM, Friday 7:30 AM-4:30 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tuition-free short-term workforce training designed to move students quickly into work, including composites technician, injection molding technician, and aerospace assembly pathways.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants complete the Utah Works funding application. The page states approved students receive a code that makes the selected course charge $0; funding and course fit must be confirmed for the specific training.

**Population Served**
Utah and Salt Lake County residents seeking short-term advanced manufacturing training through SLCC.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the Utah Works application link on the SLCC Utah Works page. For program questions, contact Meagan Woodford at 801-957-2231 or mbaile54@slcc.edu. SLCC's main campus is 4600 S Redwood Road.

**Important Information to Know**
Tuition-free applies to approved Utah Works training, not every SLCC program. Dates, partner employers, and training availability can change by cohort.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Utah Works Tuition-Free Training

resources.address: 4600 South Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: Salt Lake Community College Veterans Services helps servicemembers, veterans, and dependents with VA education benefits, semester certification, campus Veterans Centers, transition to education/employment, and veteran student resources.
resources.hours: Student Services Hours listed by SLCC: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veterans Services provides assistance and support to SLCC servicemembers, veterans, and dependents completing educational goals. Services include VA education benefit information, semester certification forms after registration, Veterans Centers, residency and financial-aid resource links, VetSuccess resources, and student veteran community connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For SLCC students or prospective students who are servicemembers, veterans, or dependents. VA education-benefit certification requires registration and completion of the semester certification form.

**Population Served**
Servicemembers, veterans, and dependents attending or preparing to attend Salt Lake Community College.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at the SLCC Veterans Services website, use the listed Veterans Services contact/staff pages, or call SLCC general information at 801-957-4111 or enrollment help at 801-957-4073. The main Veterans Center is at Taylorsville Redwood Campus, Student Center room 059; another Veterans Center is at South City Campus.

**Important Information to Know**
This is for SLCC education-related support, not general VA claims or emergency aid. Direct Veterans Services phone details were not clearly exposed on the public page opened; use the website contact/staff links for current staff contact.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community College Veterans Services

resources.description: Salt Lake Community Mutual Aid describes a distro project that twice weekly distributes hot food and supplies to unhoused neighbors and replaces tents, gear, and propane in winter, but current public access details are not complete enough for routine referral.
resources.hours: Twice-weekly distro described; current locations and times not published on the opened About page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Mutual-aid distribution for unhoused neighbors, described as hot food and supplies, fresh socks, replacement tents and gear, winter propane refills, and community free-market events.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The About page frames distro for unhoused neighbors and community mutual aid. It does not list documents, fees, or formal eligibility screening.

**Population Served**

Unhoused neighbors and community members in Salt Lake City and the Salt Lake Valley.

**How to Best Connect**

The public About page lists contact@slcmutualaid.com. Administrators should confirm current distro schedule, locations, and whether someone can request survival gear directly before missionaries refer a client.

**Important Information to Know**

This is volunteer mutual aid with donation-dependent inventory and variable access. The remaining obstacle is current schedule/location and direct request process, not the identity of the organization.
resources.name: Salt Lake Community Mutual Aid Distro / Really Really Free Markets
resources.resolutionReason: Keep administrator-only; do not refer routinely until current schedule/direct access is confirmed.; Current schedule, locations and request process are not public enough for routine referral.

resources.address: 2001 S State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84190
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Caregiver Support Program offers caregiver information, support groups, education, consultation, short-term respite and limited supplemental supplies or equipment for eligible unpaid caregivers.
resources.hours: Call Caregiver Support during county business hours; training and support group sign-ups are available through the online calendar.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Caregiver support, including information and assistance, support groups, training, consultation, short-term respite and supplemental services such as supplies or equipment when eligible.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Respite and supplemental services require intake and eligibility. Eligible caregiver groups include adults 18+ caring for someone age 60+, adults 18+ caring for someone of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, older relatives age 55+ caring for children under 18, and older relatives including parents age 55+ caring for adults 18-59 with disabilities. The county states there is no financial eligibility or fee to participate.

**Population Served**
Unpaid family and informal caregivers in Salt Lake County, including caregivers of older adults, people with dementia, children being raised by older relatives and adults with disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Caregiver Support at 385-468-3280. Training and support group registration is available through the county online calendar.

**Important Information to Know**
All caregivers are eligible for information, support groups, training and consultation. Respite and supplemental services are more limited and require intake, eligibility and available resources.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Caregiver Support Program

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, PO Box 144575, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Home & Community Based Care / Supported Aging is the local front door for Medicaid Aging Waiver screening and related in-home support programs for older adults and medically frail adults who want to remain in an independent setting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Phone intake, case management, consultations, and coordination of in-home services. Programs listed by the county include Medicaid Aging Waiver, The Alternatives Program, and Veterans-Directed Home & Community Based Services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by program. Medicaid Aging Waiver applicants must be age 65 or older, have or be eligible for Medicaid, and be willing to have an in-home assessment with an Aging Waiver RN to determine medical need. Other programs may consider medical condition, income, assets, homebound or frailty considerations, and functional needs.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County older adults and medically frail adults who need help with activities of daily living or other supports to continue living independently; caregivers nearing burnout; and some disabled veterans through the veterans-directed option.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services at 385-468-3200 and ask for Home & Community Based Care, Supported Aging, or Medicaid Aging Waiver screening. The office is listed at 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
The state Medicaid page says the Aging Waiver referral process begins with the Area Agency on Aging. A phone intake starts screening but does not guarantee waiver approval, services, or immediate availability.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Home & Community Based Care / Supported Aging

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Housing Liaison helps older adults apply for affordable senior housing, understand housing options, address eviction-related problems, navigate housing barriers, and connect to aging-in-place resources.
resources.hours: Call during county business hours for current intake and appointment options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing navigation and advocacy for older adults, including help applying for housing, counseling on housing options and eviction consequences, help navigating barriers to securing housing, connection to Aging & Adult Services and community resources, and case-by-case assistance for seniors seeking housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Salt Lake County seniors or older adults who are unhoused, rent-burdened, at risk of homelessness, need affordable low-income senior housing, or have difficulty navigating housing applications.

**Population Served**
Older adults and seniors in Salt Lake County who need affordable senior-housing navigation, housing-barrier support, homelessness-prevention advocacy, or connection to aging-in-place resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services at 385-468-3200 and ask for the Housing Liaison Program. The listed office is 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
The county states Aging & Adult Services does not own or operate senior housing and does not provide rental assistance or housing funding. This is navigation, counseling, advocacy, and connection to resources; it does not guarantee placement or payment.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Housing Liaison Program

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Long-Term Care Ombudsman advocates for residents' rights in Salt Lake County nursing homes and assisted living facilities, investigates complaints, helps resolve care and quality-of-life problems, and provides long-term care information.
resources.hours: Information line Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Advocacy for residents in facility-based long-term care, including complaint investigation, problem-solving with facilities and other agencies, resident-rights information, and information about selecting nursing homes or assisted living facilities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Advocacy services are for people receiving facility-based care in Salt Lake County. There are no eligibility criteria to receive general long-term care information.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents in nursing homes, assisted living, and other facility-based long-term care; family members, facility staff, and community members seeking information about long-term care issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-3255 for information Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. The office is listed at 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an ombudsman and resident-rights advocacy program, not private attorney representation. Advocacy eligibility is tied to facility-based care in Salt Lake County.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Long-Term Care Ombudsman

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, PO Box 144575, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Meals on Wheels delivers nutritious midday meals Monday through Friday to eligible homebound older adults age 60+ in Salt Lake County, with phone enrollment and eligibility screening.
resources.hours: New client enrollment Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Meals on Wheels delivers nutritious midday meals to eligible frail and isolated older adults age 60+. Eligible participants may also receive weekend meals delivered on Thursday and Friday. Special diet options listed by the county include cut meat, pureed, no nut, no pork, and no seafood meals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be age 60 or older, homebound, a Salt Lake County resident, unable to prepare their own meals, and without family or other resources to help with meal preparation. Eligibility must be verified directly with the applicant by phone before meal delivery can start.

**Population Served**
Homebound, frail, or isolated Salt Lake County residents age 60+ who cannot prepare meals and lack other meal-preparation support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-3200 for new client enrollment Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM. Existing clients can call 385-468-3220. Loved ones and caregivers may call for information, but the county must verify eligibility directly with the applicant.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not universal meal assistance; eligibility screening is required. Meal delivery is generally weekday midday delivery, with weekend meals only for eligible individuals. Donations support the program, but the county presents them as donations rather than required fees.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Meals on Wheels

resources.address: 2001 S State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Refugee Program for Older Adults connects older refugees age 60+ in Salt Lake County to benefits, community resources, social engagement, ESL and citizenship education support, nutrition, meal delivery, medical transportation, and other aging-service options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Resource navigation and social-engagement support for older adult refugees. For refugees in the United States 1-5 years, the program can help with SNAP, SSI, Medicaid, ESL and citizenship education resources, nutrition, meal delivery, medical transportation, and other community service options. For refugees in the United States more than 5 years, it provides service and socialization referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The county page states the program serves older adult refugees age 60+ who live in Salt Lake County. Specific documentation, language access, and appointment process should be confirmed through Aging & Adult Services.

**Population Served**
Older adult refugees age 60 and older living in Salt Lake County, including newer arrivals and longer-term residents who need aging-service connections or socialization referrals.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services at 385-468-3200 and ask for the Refugee Program for Older Adults. The listed program office is 2001 S State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
The page names the program manager but does not list a separate public program phone; the main Aging & Adult Services number is the practical public route. Services differ depending on how long the person has been in the United States.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Refugee Program for Older Adults

resources.address: 2001 S State St, Ste S3-300, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Rides for Wellness provides door-to-door rides for Salt Lake County residents age 60 or older who lack transportation to vital medical appointments within Salt Lake County.
resources.hours: Rides Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM. New client enrollment Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:00 PM; 2nd Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Door-to-door transportation to vital medical appointments such as dialysis, chemotherapy and physical therapy. The program uses cars and wheelchair-accessible vans to accommodate mobility needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be age 60 or older, live in Salt Lake County, lack other means of transportation, and have appointments within Salt Lake County. Residents of nursing homes, rehabilitation centers or hospice facilities are not eligible. Eligibility screening is done by phone.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County older adults age 60 or older who need transportation to critical medical appointments and have no other ride option.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-3200 for new client enrollment. Call 385-468-3400 for transportation dispatch, cancellations or more program information. The county recommends calling two weeks in advance when possible.

**Important Information to Know**
A $3.00 donation per trip is suggested. Priority is given to people who schedule in advance and to low-income individuals. Loved ones or caregivers may call for information, but eligibility must be verified for the applicant.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Rides for Wellness

resources.address: 2001 S State St, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services senior centers list transportation availability for adults age 60 or older attending senior center meals, services and activities; callers should contact the relevant senior center for boundaries, scheduling and availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transportation connected to Salt Lake County senior centers for older adults attending senior center meals, services, classes or activities. Availability and rules are center-specific.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Generally for adults age 60 or older using Salt Lake County senior centers. The sealed evidence does not provide a single countywide ride boundary, fare or reservation rule.

**Population Served**
Older adults in Salt Lake County who need help getting to senior center programming, meals or activities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Aging & Adult Services at 385-468-3200 or contact the specific senior center the person wants to attend. Ask about transportation availability, pickup boundaries, reservation notice, costs and accessibility.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not promise a ride without checking with the relevant center. This is separate from Rides for Wellness medical transportation and may have different boundaries, schedules and capacity.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Senior Center Transportation

resources.address: 2001 S State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84190
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Senior Companion Program works with volunteers to help frail and isolated older adults age at home rather than move into long-term care.
resources.hours: Call Aging & Adult Services for current intake and availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The county overview describes Senior Companion as a program that works with volunteers to help frail and isolated older adults age at home rather than in long-term care. Companion support may be relevant for isolation, light support, caregiver relief, and aging-in-place needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public details are limited in current county materials. The program is described for frail and isolated older adults; call Aging & Adult Services to confirm client eligibility, availability, matching process, and whether the caller is seeking help for themselves, a loved one, or volunteering.

**Population Served**
Frail and isolated older adults in Salt Lake County who need support to remain at home, plus volunteers who may be matched with older adults through the county program.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services at 385-468-3200 and ask about Senior Companion. The main Aging & Adult Services office is listed at 2001 S State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
The official overview confirms the program but does not provide detailed client eligibility, current openings, or a separate public phone. Treat this as a county Aging & Adult Services intake question rather than a guaranteed match or immediate service.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Senior Companion Program

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Suite S2-300, Salt Lake City, UT 84190
resources.description: Salt Lake County access point for publicly funded mental health and substance use assessment/referral, including pathways relevant to pregnant and parenting women needing behavioral health treatment.
resources.hours: Access and Information: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed for lunch 12:00-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Access and information for mental health and substance use disorder assessment and referral through Salt Lake County's publicly funded behavioral health system. The county oversees contracted providers and assessment/referral services rather than providing all treatment directly.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Salt Lake County residents seeking publicly funded behavioral health services, including people with Medicaid/Optum Salt Lake County, no insurance, or limited ability to pay. Placement depends on assessment, funding, provider eligibility, and openings.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents with mental health or substance use treatment needs, including pregnant and parenting women needing behavioral health treatment access.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Behavioral Health Services Access and Information at 385-468-4707 during weekday business hours. For immediate behavioral health crisis, call or text 988.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not prenatal care and the county division does not itself provide all treatment. It is the county front door for assessment and referral into contracted behavioral health care.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Behavioral Health Services Pregnant and Parenting Women Treatment Access

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Suite S2-200, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Clerk services relevant to ID recovery, including certified copies of Salt Lake County marriage licenses for name-change proof and appointment-based passport acceptance for first-time, child, older, and lost or stolen passport applications.
resources.hours: Marriage Division: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Passport applications are accepted by appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Salt Lake County Clerk provides certified copies of Salt Lake County marriage licenses and operates a passport acceptance office. Marriage-license copies can support name-change proof for ID, Social Security, passport, benefits, and other paperwork. Passport acceptance includes cases where a passport was lost or stolen or cannot be renewed by mail or online.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Marriage copy service applies to Salt Lake County marriage licenses. A person requesting their own certified copy must provide identification; requests for someone else's record require a GRAMA request. Passport applicants must meet State Department requirements and bring required documents and payments.

**Population Served**
People needing Salt Lake County marriage records or local passport application acceptance in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
For marriage copies, walk in Monday through Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM at 2001 South State Street, Suite S2-200, call 385-468-7300, or email a GRAMA request to mpclerk@saltlakecounty.gov. For passports, schedule an appointment through the Clerk's passport page before going in.

**Important Information to Know**
Certified marriage copies cost $5 per copy plus $3 shipping if mailed. Passport applications require two separate payments, one to the U.S. Department of State and one to the Clerk's Office. The Clerk is an acceptance facility, not a same-day passport agency.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Clerk Marriage Records and Passport Acceptance Services

resources.address: 35 East 500 South, 5th Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake County District Attorney Survivor & Victim Support Services explains and links the county U-visa certification application route for qualifying crime victims who were helpful, are helpful, or are likely to be helpful in investigation or prosecution.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
County U-visa certification access through the Survivor & Victim Support Services Division. The county page explains USCIS Form I-918 Supplement B and links an application route for certification connected to qualifying criminal activity and cooperation with investigation or prosecution.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For direct or indirect victims of qualifying criminal activity where Salt Lake County District Attorney or a related county prosecution/law-enforcement pathway is the appropriate certifying entity. Certification does not itself grant immigration status.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County crime victims and their families who may need U-visa certification connected to county investigation or prosecution.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the county page's U-VISA Certification application link or call Survivor & Victim Support Services at 385-468-7570. Office address is 35 East 500 South, 5th Floor, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a certification pathway, not immigration legal representation. Clients should also work with a qualified immigration legal provider for the full U-visa petition and case strategy.
resources.name: Salt Lake County DA U-Visa Certification

resources.address: 35 East 500 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake County District Attorney's Conviction Integrity Unit reviews and investigates post-conviction claims of innocence and handles applications for conviction review from members of the public.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
County prosecutor review of post-conviction innocence claims, including review and investigation by the Conviction Review Unit and recommendations to the District Attorney. The official page links a conviction integrity application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For post-conviction claims of innocence connected to convictions handled by the Salt Lake County District Attorney's Office. The application must qualify under the unit's review process.

**Population Served**
People with Salt Lake County convictions who are asserting post-conviction innocence, and members of the public submitting conviction-review applications.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Conviction Integrity Unit page and its Conviction Integrity Application link. The District Attorney address listed for the office is 35 East 500 South, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a prosecutor review process, not independent legal advice, defense representation, or a substitute for court deadlines. People with appeal or post-conviction deadlines should also seek independent legal advice.
resources.name: Salt Lake County District Attorney Conviction Integrity Unit

resources.address: 35 East 500 South, 5th Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Camp HOPE America - Utah is a Salt Lake County District Attorney youth program with a week of camp plus year-round Pathways activities and mentoring for children and teens exposed to domestic violence.
resources.hours: Camp Hope office Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Evidence-based camping and mentoring program for children and teens exposed to domestic violence. The program includes a weeklong camp experience and Pathways, a year-round program with monthly activities and mentorship intended to support hope, healing, and trauma recovery.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For youth exposed to domestic violence. The public page does not spell out the full application window, age range, or referral details, so families or helpers should contact the Camp Hope manager to confirm current enrollment and fit.

**Population Served**
Children and teens in Utah/Salt Lake County who have been exposed to domestic violence.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Camp Hope Manager Byron Paulsen at 385-468-7802 or the Camp Hope office at 385-468-7700. Office address is 35 East 500 South, 5th Floor, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not crisis shelter, legal help, or an emergency hotline. It is a youth healing and mentoring program; enrollment timing and availability need confirmation before promising participation.
resources.name: Salt Lake County District Attorney's Office Camp HOPE America - Utah

resources.address: 2001 S State Street, Suite S2-100, Salt Lake City, UT 84190
resources.description: Salt Lake County's expungement toolkit and 402 reduction instructions provide self-service information, forms, and step-by-step guidance for Utah criminal record cleanup and conviction reductions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online self-help information and forms for Utah criminal record cleanup, including expungement toolkit guidance and 402 reduction instructions. The 402 reduction guide includes English and Spanish instructions and form steps.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with Utah criminal records who need expungement or a 402 reduction. Eligibility depends on the case type, conviction history, court, prosecutor response, waiting periods, and whether a reduction would help or hurt expungement eligibility.

**Population Served**
People with Utah criminal records, including Salt Lake County residents, who can use online self-service instructions and forms.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Salt Lake County's Legal & Justice expungement toolkit links and the 402 reduction instruction pages. The Mayor's Office of Homelessness & Criminal Justice Reform lists 385-468-7092 and 2001 S State Street, Suite S2-100, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is self-service guidance, not legal representation or fee assistance. The 402 reduction page warns that reductions can sometimes hurt expungement eligibility and suggests consulting an attorney if unsure.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Expungement Toolkit and 402 Reduction Instructions

resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department's Asthma Home Visiting Program provides free in-home asthma education for Salt Lake County residents of all ages with severe or uncontrolled asthma.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free asthma home visiting and asthma education focused on severe or uncontrolled asthma, triggers, medication use, and better asthma control.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people of all ages living in Salt Lake County with severe or uncontrolled asthma. The county lists qualifying factors such as asthma emergency-department visits or hospitalizations, oral steroid courses, unscheduled or urgent asthma visits in the past 12 months, or an Asthma Control Test score below 19.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents of any age with severe or uncontrolled asthma.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-5250, text 385-202-5178, or use the county email link on the asthma page. Ask about eligibility and whether a referral or Asthma Control Test is needed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is education and prevention support, not emergency care and not a replacement for a primary care clinician. For breathing emergencies, call 911 or use urgent/emergency medical care.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Asthma Home Visiting Program

resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department's BeWise program provides free heart-health risk screenings and health coaching for low-income uninsured or underinsured women ages 40-64.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free heart-health risk screenings and health coaching. Screenings include weight, height, BMI, blood pressure, cholesterol, glucose, and A1C for diabetics, plus lifestyle counseling around eating habits, physical activity, stress management, and other health concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For women ages 40-64 with low income who do not have health insurance or do not have enough health insurance.

**Population Served**
Eligible low-income uninsured or underinsured women ages 40-64 in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the BeWise / women's health contact listed for Salt Lake County Health Department; the submitted program numbers are 800-717-1811 and 385-468-4299. Ask about screening dates, enrollment, and documentation.

**Important Information to Know**
BeWise is preventive screening and coaching, not full primary care or urgent care. Eligibility is narrow and should be confirmed before referral.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department BeWise Women's Health Program

resources.address: South Redwood Public Health Center, 7971 S 1825 W, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: Salt Lake County child-safety program providing car-seat safety checks and low-cost car seats by appointment for families who need a seat and cannot afford one.
resources.hours: By appointment only, Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Car-seat safety checks for families who already have a car seat and low-cost car seats for families who need a car seat and cannot afford one. Safe Kids Salt Lake County also provides child injury-prevention education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Safety checks are appointment-based. Low-cost car seats are for families who need a car seat and cannot afford one; income/need guidelines apply.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County parents and caregivers transporting children in car seats.

**How to Best Connect**
Schedule an appointment online from the county child-safety page or call the Car Seat Program at 385-468-5284. Appointments are at South Redwood Public Health Center, 7971 South 1825 West, West Jordan.

**Important Information to Know**
Service is by appointment only. Not every family will qualify for a low-cost seat, and availability should be confirmed when scheduling.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Car Seat Program / Safe Kids Salt Lake County

resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department home-visiting program with Parents as Teachers for eligible pregnant families or families with a child under 3, plus broader home-visiting help for healthier pregnancies and child development.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free home-visiting nurses and educators help low-income families with healthier pregnancies, child development, parenting education, resources, and links to services. Parents as Teachers is for families who are pregnant or have a child under 3 and meet income guidelines.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Salt Lake County families who are pregnant or have a child under 3 and meet income guidelines. The county also offers other home-visiting programs with different eligibility.

**Population Served**
Low-income Salt Lake County pregnant families and families with young children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Health Department Home Visiting at 385-468-4100 or submit the Home Visiting Interest Form for Nurse-Family Partnership and Parents as Teachers.

**Important Information to Know**
This entry is for the county Parents as Teachers/general home-visiting front door. Families who are first-time mothers before 28 weeks may fit Nurse-Family Partnership; families with Medicaid children under 8 may fit Targeted Case Management.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Home Visiting / Parents as Teachers

resources.address: Multiple Salt Lake County immunization clinic locations
resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department immunization clinics provide required and recommended vaccines for children, adolescents, and adults, with appointment scheduling by phone and low-cost Vaccines for Children doses for eligible children.
resources.hours: Appointment line: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Same-day appointments are often available. Clinic hours vary by location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Required and recommended immunizations for children, adolescents, and adults, including school-required vaccines, recommended vaccines, travel immunizations, and immunization records support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to people needing vaccines. Costs vary by vaccine. Vaccines for Children doses are available for children age 18 or younger who are uninsured, on Medicaid/CHIP, or American Indian/Alaska Native, with listed administration costs.

**Population Served**
Children, adolescents, and adults in Salt Lake County who need immunizations or vaccine records.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-7468, also listed as 385-468-SHOT, to make an immunization appointment. Use the county site to check clinic locations, outreach clinics, accepted health plans, and current costs.

**Important Information to Know**
Adult vaccine costs vary, and insurance coverage should be confirmed with the specific plan. Same-day appointments are often available but not guaranteed. Vaccine stock and clinic location should be checked before travel.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Immunization Clinics

resources.address: Salt Lake Public Health Center, 610 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department's Infectious Disease Clinic provides STI/HIV screening, testing, diagnosis, treatment, PrEP services, partner notification, and related sexual-health services at the Salt Lake Public Health Center.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed until 1:00 PM on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of each month.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
STI/HIV screening, testing, diagnosis, and in many cases same-day treatment; testing for chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, HIV, herpes, trichomoniasis, mycoplasma, hepatitis B/C; PrEP provider services; DoxyPEP for eligible patients; genital wart treatment; and anonymous partner notification for certain infections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Testing is available to anyone age 14 or older, anyone sexually active, anyone with STD symptoms, anyone who thinks they are at risk or exposed, and anyone wanting routine sexual-health screening. Fees apply and the clinic cannot bill health insurance.

**Population Served**
People age 14 and older in Salt Lake County needing STI/HIV testing, treatment, PrEP, or sexual-health services, including people of all genders, identities, and sexual orientations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-4242 to make an appointment. Walk-ins are accommodated when possible, but appointments reduce wait time and guarantee being seen. Enter the clinic from 200 East at 610 S 200 E.

**Important Information to Know**
The office visit fee is listed as $60 for Salt Lake County residents and $80 for out-of-county residents, with separate test fees except for some HIV-only testing. Children are not allowed in exam rooms and cannot be left unattended in the lobby.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Infectious Disease Clinic
