resources.description: Free nurse home-visiting program for eligible first-time pregnant mothers in Salt Lake County, beginning before 28 weeks of pregnancy and continuing until the child turns 2.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Registered nurse home visits during pregnancy and early childhood, with support, advice, information for a healthy pregnancy and baby, parenting support, and regular visit schedule through the child's second birthday.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Must meet WIC-level income guidelines, be a first-time mother, live in Salt Lake County, and enroll before week 28 of pregnancy. The nurse must be able to make a home visit before the 28th week.

**Population Served**
First-time pregnant mothers in Salt Lake County who meet income and pregnancy-timing rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Nurse-Family Partnership at 385-468-3955 or submit the county Home Visiting Interest Form from the Nurse-Family Partnership page.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility is narrower than general home visiting. The program is free for eligible participants, but early enrollment is important because late pregnancy may make the family ineligible.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Nurse-Family Partnership

resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department's Stepping On Senior Fall Prevention program is a seven-week class for older adults that builds confidence and teaches fall-risk reduction through exercise, vision, medication, and community-safety education.
resources.hours: Call for upcoming class dates, locations, and enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Stepping On is a senior fall-prevention class that meets once a week for seven weeks for two hours, with an eighth follow-up session three months later. Guest professionals address exercise, vision, medication interactions, and community safety.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The county describes it as a Senior Fall Prevention class for older adults. Current class dates, locations, and any registration requirements must be confirmed when enrolling.

**Population Served**
Older adults in Salt Lake County who want to reduce fall risk and build confidence in fall-prevention behaviors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-5317 for more information or to enroll in an upcoming class.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a class-based prevention program, not emergency medical care, home modification, or physical therapy. Availability depends on current class scheduling.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Stepping On Senior Fall Prevention

resources.description: Salt Lake County public health nurse consultation and visit for families with a baby or child under 8 on Medicaid, focused on baby-care questions and locating services the family qualifies for.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free consultation and visit with a public health nurse for baby-care questions and help locating services the family qualifies for. The page links resources on crying, tantrums, EPSDT benefits, feeding, growth and development, safe sleep, and tummy time.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families whose baby or child is under age 8 and on Medicaid.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County families with Medicaid-enrolled children under age 8.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Targeted Case Management at 385-468-4018 or email through the county page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is distinct from Nurse-Family Partnership and Parents as Teachers. Confirm whether the visit is in-home, clinic-based, or another format when contacting the program.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Targeted Case Management - Home Visiting

resources.address: Salt Lake City office: 610 South 200 East, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department Vital Records is the local county access point for certified Utah birth and death certificates and abstracts of Utah marriage and divorce records for eligible requesters.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Certified copies of Utah birth and death certificates and abstracts of Utah marriage and divorce records. These records can support state ID, Social Security, name proof, benefits, housing, and other document-recovery steps.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Vital records are limited to eligible requesters such as the person named on the record, qualifying relatives, legal representatives, or others who can show legal need. Identification and relationship or legal-need documentation may be required.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake County who need Utah vital records and meet Utah vital-record access rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-4230 or use the county Vital Records page before going in person. The Salt Lake City office address in the lead is 610 South 200 East, Salt Lake City; county materials also reference West Jordan and West Valley City office access.

**Important Information to Know**
Fees generally apply unless a specific waiver applies. The county office is for Utah records; out-of-state records must be requested through the issuing state or local office.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Health Department Vital Records

resources.description: Salt Lake County Housing Rehabilitation Programs provide free HUD-funded assistance for eligible residential repairs and lead-safe work addressing health, safety, lead hazards, and critical housing needs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free housing rehabilitation and lead-safe assistance for eligible properties, including inspection, risk assessment, hazard identification, contractor coordination, and approved repair projects for health, safety, lead-based paint, and critical housing needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available to eligible homeowners, renters, landlords, and property managers in Salt Lake County. Household income must generally be at or below 80% of Area Median Income. Lead-focused work may require a pre-1978 home with a child under age 6 or pregnant woman living in or frequently visiting the home.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County households, tenants, homeowners, and property owners needing eligible health, safety, critical repair, or lead-safe housing work.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the pre-application on the county page. If documents cannot be uploaded, email them to Ayda Posso at aposso@saltlakecounty.gov. Call or text 385-315-0049 for Ayda Posso or 385-549-6704 for Jayson Kenney.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are free when the program approves the work, but eligibility, property condition, funding, and approved repair type control what can be done. Applications require income documentation for household members age 18 and older and valid ID copies.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Housing Rehabilitation Programs / Lead Safe Housing

resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department provides payor-of-last-resort financial assistance for cremation of indigent decedents who died in Salt Lake County and meet program criteria, including cases with no next of kin or qualifying next of kin.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance for cremation of deceased people who meet Salt Lake County indigent-disposition rules. The county uses a contracted mortuary and may consider burial at county expense for homicide victims at county discretion.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The decedent must have died within Salt Lake County and meet indigency criteria. With next of kin, both the decedent and next of kin/household criteria are reviewed. Income, benefits, life insurance, burial insurance, prepaid funeral plans, and other resources are considered.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County decedents with insufficient resources for final disposition and next of kin or responsible parties who cannot afford or decline responsibility under program rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Vital Records at 385-468-4230. Vital Records hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM. Application links are available on the Indigent Deaths page in English and Spanish.

**Important Information to Know**
Salt Lake County is payor of last resort. The program does not pay for funeral or memorial services, an urn or container, interment or burial costs, or transportation of cremains to a final resting place.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Indigent Deaths / Disposition of Indigent Remains

resources.address: Jail-release service; call 385-414-2120 for the access location.
resources.description: Salt Lake County Criminal Justice Services' Jail Resource and Reentry Program is a voluntary reentry resource point for anyone leaving the Salt Lake County Jail, offering individualized resources and referrals for behavioral health, Medicaid, supervision/legal services, phone chargers, and community services.
resources.hours: Monday-Sunday 7:00 AM-11:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Individualized resource information and referrals for people leaving jail, including mental-health and substance-use referrals, Medicaid, supervision and legal services, cell phone chargers, and other community service referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Services are voluntary and available to anyone leaving the Salt Lake County Jail during operating hours.

**Population Served**

People being released from the Salt Lake County Jail who need immediate reentry navigation and community-resource connections.

**How to Best Connect**

When leaving Salt Lake County Jail, ask staff about JRRP or call 385-414-2120. The county page lists daily hours of 7:00 AM-11:00 PM and a county contact address at 2001 S State Street, Ste S3-650; confirm the service location by phone rather than treating that administrative address as the jail-exit site.

**Important Information to Know**

This is an exit-lobby jail release resource, not a general walk-in office for people released from other facilities. It provides referrals and basic reentry help, not guaranteed placement, benefits approval, treatment admission, or legal representation.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Jail Resource and Reentry Program (JRRP)

resources.description: Salt Lake County Library offers Adult Core Skills, GED and citizenship practice, basic computer skills, online courses, career learning resources, and in-person branch classes for County Library cardholders and branch users.
resources.hours: Branch and class hours vary by location and event calendar.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult Core Skills resources for reading, writing, math, GED preparation, and U.S. citizenship; Basic Computer Skills; LinkedIn Learning, Universal Class, Creativebug, Brainfuse JobNow, Learning Express, and other adult learning resources. Branch classes and digital foundations events vary by calendar.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Some resources require a Salt Lake County Library card, branch access, or in-library use. Specific events may require registration.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County Library cardholders and branch users, including adult learners, GED learners, citizenship learners, job seekers, and people building computer skills.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-943-4636, visit a County Library branch, or use the All Resources page to open the relevant learning tool. Check the events calendar for current in-person classes.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a library learning resource hub rather than individualized case management. Database access rules differ by resource.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Library Adult Core Skills and Digital Learning Resources

resources.address: Multiple Salt Lake County Library branches
resources.description: Salt Lake County Library lends Chromebooks through its Library of Things and provides public internet access at branches, giving county cardholders and branch visitors temporary device and online access.
resources.hours: Branch hours vary; Chromebooks check out for 21 days when available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Chromebook checkout through the County Library's Library of Things and public internet access at library branches. Chromebooks are listed at all branches subject to availability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Chromebook checkout requires a library card and is limited to one Chromebook per card. The checkout period is 21 days, and all equipment must be returned together and on time.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County Library cardholders and branch visitors who need temporary computer or internet access.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit or call a Salt Lake County Library branch, or call the County Library system at 801-943-4636. Check current Chromebook availability before sending a client for pickup.

**Important Information to Know**
Chromebooks do not include home internet service; the borrower needs Wi-Fi to use them away from the library. Devices are subject to availability and are disabled if more than one day overdue.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Library Chromebook Checkout and Public Internet Access

resources.address: 2001 S State Street, Ste N1-130, Salt Lake City, UT 84190
resources.description: Salt Lake County Mayor's Office for New Americans serves county immigrant and refugee residents through resource connection, refugee and immigrant information, United for Citizenship, citizenship education resources, and events or initiatives that connect residents to trusted immigration nonprofits.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Countywide New American navigation and citizenship support, including refugee and immigrant resource connection, United for Citizenship, citizenship information, links to trusted immigration nonprofits, and New American community events.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open as a county government resource for New American, immigrant, and refugee residents of Salt Lake County. Specific citizenship workshops or partner services may have their own eligibility and scheduling rules.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County immigrants, refugees, lawful permanent residents preparing for citizenship, and other New American residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-4861 or use the email link on the county page. The office is at 2001 S State Street, Ste N1-130, Salt Lake City. Office hours are listed as Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a navigation and government resource office, not a law firm. For legal advice or representation, the office points residents toward trusted immigration nonprofits and legal-help resources.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Office for New Americans / United for Citizenship

resources.address: 8446 S Harrison St (340 W), Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: Salt Lake County adaptive recreation program offering sports, fitness, aquatics, socials, camps, inclusion support, and disability/plus-one fitness passes.
resources.hours: Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adaptive sports, physical activities, social events, adaptive fitness, adaptive aquatics, camps, Miracle League baseball, inclusion requests, disability/plus-one fitness pass, and adaptive personal training consultation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs are for people with physical, developmental, or intellectual disabilities or impairments. Participation is determined by individual abilities. Fees and registration rules vary by activity.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities or impairments who want inclusive and adaptive recreation in Salt Lake County. The county states nonresidents may participate.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-1515 or register online/in person for activities. For inclusion help, contact the Inclusion Manager at 385-468-1520. Office hours are Monday-Friday, 8 AM-5 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Schedules, fees, and capacity vary. Contact the program before attending a specific activity or asking for inclusion support.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Parks and Recreation Adaptive Recreation

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services provides free SHIP Medicare counseling to help Medicare beneficiaries and families compare coverage, reduce out-of-pocket costs, resolve billing errors, and apply for Medicaid or Extra Help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free, unbiased Medicare and health-benefits counseling. SHIP helps with Medicare questions, Medicare Part D and Medicare Advantage screenings, Medigap counseling, billing errors, fraud and abuse issues, Medicaid and Extra Help applications, and minimizing out-of-pocket health costs. Senior Medicare Patrol helps detect and report Medicare fraud and abuse.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Medicare beneficiaries and their families or caregivers in Salt Lake County. People outside Salt Lake County should contact their own local Area Agency on Aging.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County Medicare beneficiaries, older adults navigating Medicare, people eligible for Medicare because of disability, and family members or caregivers helping with Medicare decisions.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County SHIP at 385-468-3200. The SHIP office is listed at 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
SHIP is counseling and application help, not direct cash assistance and not an insurance sales office. Savings depend on plan choices, enrollment timing, and eligibility for Medicare Savings Programs, Medicaid, Extra Help, or other benefits.
resources.name: Salt Lake County SHIP Medicare Counseling

resources.address: Senior centers throughout Salt Lake County; Virtual Senior Center by phone, online, video conference, and self-guided activities
resources.description: Salt Lake County Senior Centers offer free membership for adults age 60+ and provide dining, health and wellness programs, exercise facilities, educational classes, social activities, and virtual or telephone-accessible programming.
resources.hours: Individual senior center schedules vary. Virtual Senior Center registration is by phone at 385-468-3299.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
County senior centers offer health and wellness programs, educational classes, exercise facilities, dining, and social activities for adults over age 60. The Virtual Senior Center offers online, video conference, telephone, and self-guided activities, including support groups, exercise classes, education, arts and crafts, and local-area tours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Membership is free and open to adults age 60 and over. Individual activities, meals, transportation, or center-specific programs may have separate registration, schedule, or eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County adults age 60+ who want meals, wellness activities, learning, exercise, social connection, or remote senior-center programming.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Virtual Senior Center at 385-468-3299 to register for virtual courses. For in-person programming, contact the nearest Salt Lake County senior center and confirm its schedule, meals, and registration steps.

**Important Information to Know**
Schedules, lunch availability, activities, and transportation options vary by site. The Virtual Senior Center can be useful for homebound or isolated older adults because some options are available by phone or without a computer.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Senior Centers and Virtual Senior Center

resources.address: 2001 South State Street, Ste S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: County phone-intake program for Salt Lake County adults 18+ who need help remaining independent and may qualify for The Alternatives Program home- and community-based services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Phone intake, case management, care coordination, and home- and community-based supports for adults who need help with daily living tasks when no other funding source is available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For The Alternatives Program, applicants must be age 18 or older, complete a phone intake reviewing ability to perform activities of daily living, and meet income and asset limits. Listed limits are $1,995 monthly income/$6,000 assets for a single person and $2,705 monthly income/$12,000 assets for a married couple.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County adults who need assistance to continue living independently because of functional limitations, frailty, or medical condition.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-3200 and ask for Home & Community Based Care or The Alternatives Program intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility and services are determined through intake and assessment. The program is not universally free or automatic; income, assets, and functional need matter.
resources.name: Salt Lake County The Alternatives Program / Home & Community Based Care

resources.address: 2001 S State St, Ste N1-200, PO Box 144575, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Treasurer Tax Relief Division oversees property-tax relief and related programs for qualified homeowners and some renters, including Circuit Breaker, Senior Deferral, Indigent Relief, Mobile Home Rent Relief, and Rent Relief for older residents who meet program rules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Salt Lake County tax-relief front door for Circuit Breaker Relief, Veteran Relief, Hardship Relief, Indigent Relief, Blind Relief, Senior Deferral, Mobile Home Rent Relief, and Rent Relief resources. Several listed programs are age-related, including Circuit Breaker, Indigent Relief, Senior Deferral, Mobile Home Rent Relief, and Rent Relief.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the relief type. The county page lists examples such as age 67+ or surviving spouse with household income up to $44,221 for Circuit Breaker, age 65+ or receiving disability benefits for Indigent Relief, age 75+ for Senior Deferral, and residents age 66+ with income below the listed threshold for Rent Relief. Ownership, residency, income, asset, disability, veteran, blindness, and deadline rules vary by program.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County homeowners and qualifying renters or mobile-home renters who meet tax-relief, age, disability, veteran, blindness, hardship, income, or asset requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Salt Lake County Treasurer Tax Relief Division at 385-468-8300, option 2, or visit 2001 S State St, Ste N1-200, Salt Lake City. Review the current tax relief page and 2026 program overview before applying.

**Important Information to Know**
Annual deadlines and required documents differ by program. A wheelchair is available on request for office visits. Some rent-relief links route to state tax systems rather than the county office. Relief is not automatic and may not cover the full bill.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Treasurer Tax Relief Programs for Older Adults

resources.address: 2001 South State St., Suite N1-200, PO Box 144575, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Treasurer property tax relief for eligible veterans with a service-connected disability, qualifying active-duty service members serving outside Utah, and some surviving spouses or minor children.
resources.hours: Application PDF lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; deadline listed as September 1, 2026 for the 2026 disabled veteran exemption application.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Property tax relief for eligible Salt Lake County veterans with a service-connected disability and active-duty service members serving outside Utah. In some cases, a spouse or minor child of a veteran who died because of service may also apply.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants generally must be veterans with a service-connected disability, active-duty service members who served more than 200 consecutive days of federal active duty outside Utah, or eligible surviving spouses/minor children. The property must be owned by the applicant; rental properties do not qualify. New applicants must provide a current VA or service-branch letter showing service-related disability percentage.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County homeowners who are eligible disabled veterans, qualifying active-duty service members, or eligible surviving spouses/minor children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Salt Lake County Treasurer Tax Relief Division at 385-468-8300 option 2, email taxrelief@saltlakecounty.gov, or use the Veteran Relief page to access current applications. The office is at 2001 South State St., Suite N1-200.

**Important Information to Know**
This is property tax relief, not emergency cash assistance. Applications have deadlines; the official page lists September 1 unless extended, and the 2026 application lists a September 1, 2026 deadline. Exemption amounts depend on disability percentage and current tax-year rules.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Treasurer Veteran Relief Property Tax Program

resources.address: 788 E Woodoak Ln, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Salt Lake County Health Department vehicle replacement assistance is an unresolved transportation lead: prior materials describe help replacing a failed-emissions vehicle, while current EVRAP information appears to use different rules and may not be accepting applications.
resources.hours: Air Quality Bureau: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Possible vehicle replacement financial assistance for owners of vehicles that fail emissions testing or meet clean-air replacement rules. Prior VRAP materials described assistance toward a newer, cleaner vehicle; current EVRAP materials appear to describe electric-vehicle replacement assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Unresolved. Prior VRAP materials described income limits, a recent failed emissions test, photo ID, income proof and vehicle registration. Current EVRAP materials appear to use different income and electric-vehicle rules and may not be accepting applications.

**Population Served**
Potentially Salt Lake County or Utah vehicle owners with older, failed-emissions or higher-polluting vehicles who meet income and program requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators should confirm current program status with the Salt Lake County Health Department Air Quality Bureau at 385-468-3837 or AirQuality@SaltLakeCounty.gov before client referral.

**Important Information to Know**
This should not be referred to clients until the current program name, open application status, eligible vehicle types and replacement-versus-repair rules are confirmed. The unresolved status is about program identity and access, not about ordinary capacity uncertainty.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Vehicle Replacement Assistance Program

resources.address: Multiple Salt Lake County WIC clinics, including Ellis Shipp, Salt Lake Downtown, Southeast Sandy, South Main, and South Redwood
resources.description: Salt Lake County WIC provides nutrition services and breastfeeding support, including direct call/text access to clinic-specific breastfeeding peer counselors for WIC participants and WIC-eligible families.
resources.hours: Clinic schedules vary; breastfeeding peer counselor numbers are listed for call or text.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
WIC nutrition counseling, nutrition education, growth checks for infants and children, breastfeeding counseling and education, breastfeeding classes, breast pumps, working-mother resources, and direct peer-counselor breastfeeding support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
WIC generally serves eligible pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5. Breastfeeding peer counselor support should be treated as WIC-linked support for WIC participants or WIC-eligible families, not a separate universal lactation clinic.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County WIC participants and WIC-eligible pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding families, infants, and young children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text the clinic-specific breastfeeding peer counselor number: Ellis Shipp 385-468-3761; Salt Lake Downtown 385-468-3669; Southeast Sandy 385-468-4344; South Main 385-468-3973; South Redwood 385-468-4368. For broader WIC appointments, contact Salt Lake County WIC.

**Important Information to Know**
Counselor availability may vary by clinic. Families needing full WIC benefits may still need a WIC appointment and eligibility documentation.
resources.name: Salt Lake County WIC Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Contacts
resources.phone: Ellis Shipp 385-468-3761; Salt Lake Downtown 385-468-3669; Southeast Sandy 385-468-4344; South Main 385-468-3973; South Redwood 385-468-4368

resources.address: Salt Lake clinic: 610 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; additional clinics in West Valley City, Sandy, South Salt Lake, and West Jordan
resources.description: Salt Lake County WIC provides nutrition education, nutritious foods through an eWIC card, breastfeeding support, health checks, and referrals for eligible pregnant/postpartum people, infants, and children under 5.
resources.hours: County WIC line Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Clinic hours vary; Salt Lake clinic Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM and Wednesday 9:30 AM-6:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
WIC nutrition program with nutritious food benefits through an eWIC card, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, immunization-record review, growth and health checks, and referrals to helpful agencies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For pregnant or breastfeeding women, people who have recently had a baby, infants, and children under 5 who meet income guidelines. Applicants are automatically income-eligible if they participate in Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF/FEP, but must bring proof to the appointment. Every person applying for WIC must be present.

**Population Served**
Eligible pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding people, infants, and children under age 5 in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County WIC at 385-468-4100 or contact a specific clinic to make an application appointment. The Salt Lake clinic is 385-468-3660 at 610 S 200 E.

**Important Information to Know**
Bring proof of income, identification, residency, and immunization records for each child or infant. Missing documents may delay qualification. WIC is supplemental nutrition support, not a full household grocery program.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Women, Infants & Children (WIC)

resources.address: 177 West Price Avenue (3610 South), South Salt Lake, UT 84115; 8781 South Redwood Rd, Suite 100, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: Salt Lake County Youth Services offers no-cost youth and family therapy, walk-in crisis counseling, short-term therapy, longer-term therapy for qualifying youth and young adults, and youth substance-use counseling at South Salt Lake, West Jordan, and virtual locations.
resources.hours: Walk-in therapy typically available 10 AM-8 PM Monday-Friday at either location, with limited weekend availability in South Salt Lake; case management available 24 hours at South Salt Lake and Monday-Friday 8 AM-8 PM at West Jordan.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost therapy programs, including walk-in crisis counseling for youth ages 5-17, 8 weeks of free mental-health therapy for Salt Lake County youth ages 5-17, longer-term therapy for financially qualifying youth and young adults ages 5-20, and substance-use counseling for youth up to age 20.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Short-term free mental-health therapy is for youth ages 5-17 who reside in Salt Lake County, with no income requirements. Longer-term therapy targets Medicaid, underinsured, and uninsured clients ages 5-20 who qualify financially. Substance-use counseling serves Salt Lake County youth up to age 20 with no income or insurance restrictions.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County youth and families, especially youth ages 5-17 and qualifying youth/young adults up to age 20.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online referral form or call South Salt Lake at 385-468-4500 or 385-468-4470, or West Jordan at 385-468-4610. South Salt Lake address: 177 West Price Avenue. West Jordan address: 8781 South Redwood Rd, Suite 100.

**Important Information to Know**
Crisis counseling is based on therapist availability and is not guaranteed. Youth with private insurance who likely need longer-term counseling may be referred to their insurance network.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Youth Services Counseling

resources.description: Salt Lake County Youth Services Family Peer Support Specialists provide no-cost peer support, resource connection, advocacy, and guidance for parents or primary caregivers whose children have mental-health or substance-use challenges affecting school, legal involvement, or risk of out-of-home placement.
resources.hours: Use the online contact form or referral form; no fixed office hours listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost family peer support, guidance, resource connection, local support-group information, advocacy at school, in court, and with mental-health providers, plus help identifying and prioritizing family goals and needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For parents or primary caregivers of children ages 5-18, or ages 18-26 if the youth still lives at home or has not graduated from high school. The child/youth must have mental-health or substance-use challenges causing trouble at school, with the law, or risk of out-of-home placement.

**Population Served**
Parents and primary caregivers in Salt Lake County whose child or youth has mental-health or substance-use challenges.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Salt Lake County Family Peer Support Specialists contact form, email link, or FPSS referral form on the county page. The general Youth Services phone from the candidate is 385-468-4500.

**Important Information to Know**
This is peer support and navigation, not clinical treatment. There is no cost and no set timeline for services.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Youth Services Family Peer Support Specialists

resources.address: 177 W Price Ave, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Salt Lake County Youth Services' Homeless Youth Walk-In Program provides 24-hour free services at the Youth Hub west entrance for homeless youth up to age 17, including overnight shelter, food, laundry, showers, and counseling. No ID is required.
resources.hours: Open 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
24-hour homeless youth walk-in services, including overnight shelter, food, laundry, showers, and counseling at the Youth Hub.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For homeless youth up to age 17. No ID is required to access the free services.

**Population Served**
Homeless youth up to age 17 in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the west entrance of the Youth Hub at 177 W Price Ave, South Salt Lake, or call 385-468-4470. The site is open 24/7.

**Important Information to Know**
This program is for minors up to age 17. Youth safety procedures, guardian contact, and next steps should be discussed with Youth Services staff onsite or by phone.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Youth Services Homeless Youth Walk-In Program

resources.description: Salt Lake County transitional living program providing safe housing, case management, life skills, employment stabilization, and transition support for young adults age 18-21 at risk of or experiencing homelessness.
resources.hours: Contact program staff by phone or the website form; application/referral form is online.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Milestone Transitional Living Program provides safe housing, housing-assistance referrals, community connections, life-skills workshops, job-training skills, higher-education connections, case management, mental-health support, and transition planning for young adults.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves young adults age 18-21 who are at risk of or experiencing homelessness. Participants must follow a substance-free environment, pay program fees that begin at $200/month and increase over time, meet monthly goals, and follow non-negotiable rules including no drugs or alcohol, violence, weapons, pets, overnight guests, criminal activity, or policy violations.

**Population Served**
Young adults ages 18-21 in Salt Lake County who are at risk of homelessness or experiencing homelessness and can participate in a structured transitional living program.

**How to Best Connect**
Download and submit the Milestone Referral Application from the county page or call the Milestone Program Manager at 801-518-0292. Questions can also be submitted through the website form.

**Important Information to Know**
Program fees are saved for the participant's transition to independence. The program has explicit substance-free and behavior rules; screen pets, guests, substance use, and ability to pay before referral.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Youth Services Milestone Transitional Living Program

resources.address: 177 W Price Ave, South Salt Lake, UT 84115; 8781 S Redwood Rd, Building #3, West Jordan, UT 84088; more than 80 Safe Place sites across Salt Lake County
resources.description: Salt Lake County Youth Services manages Safe Place in Utah, an immediate help and shelter access route for youth in trouble. Youth can go to a yellow Safe Place site, call Youth Services, text SAFE and their location to 4HELP or 44357, or go directly to Youth Services facilities.
resources.hours: Youth Hub in South Salt Lake is open 24/7. West Jordan Juvenile Receiving Center is Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-8:00 PM. Safe Place sites vary by location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immediate youth help and shelter access through Safe Place sites, Youth Services phone response, text access, and Youth Services facilities. Staff at Safe Place sites call Youth Services, and Youth Services can speak with the youth and arrange transport to facilities if the youth wants services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For youth in trouble who need a safe place to go for help or shelter. The national Safe Place description says it is for young people under 18, with some communities serving up to 21; Salt Lake County says any youth can access help through Safe Place or Youth Services.

**Population Served**
Youth in Salt Lake County who need immediate help, safety, or shelter access.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-4500, go to any location with a yellow Safe Place sign, text SAFE and your location to 4HELP or 44357, or go directly to the Youth Hub at 177 W Price Ave in South Salt Lake. The Youth Hub is open 24/7.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an immediate access route, not a long-term housing program. Age handling for older transition-age youth should be confirmed with Youth Services, especially for youth 18 or older.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Youth Services Safe Place Program

resources.address: 177 West Price Avenue (3610 South), South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Salt Lake County Youth Services Youth Hub is a free 24/7 South Salt Lake facility offering crisis counseling, referrals, and short-term placement for youth ages 8-17, with no appointment required.
resources.hours: Open 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free crisis counseling, referrals to community agencies, and short-term placement for youth. Youth may come on their own, parents may bring youth for individual or family crisis counseling, and law enforcement may bring youth for certain status or delinquency concerns that do not meet detention guidelines.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For youth ages 8-17. Youth under age 10 cannot stay overnight. No appointment is needed.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County youth ages 8-17 in crisis, in conflict at home, running away, truant, using substances, violating curfew, or acting beyond parental control.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-468-4470 or go to the Youth Hub at 177 West Price Avenue (3610 South), South Salt Lake. The facility is open 24/7.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a youth crisis and short-term placement access point, not ongoing outpatient therapy. Overnight limits apply for youth under age 10.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Youth Services Youth Hub

resources.address: 1383 S 900 W Suite 128, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Salt Lake Donated Dental Services provides comprehensive dental care for low-income and homeless individuals through donated and discounted programs at its Salt Lake County clinic.
resources.hours: Appointments are scheduled after income eligibility is confirmed. No walk-ins are accepted for Donated Dental Program appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive dental care, including oral surgery, preventive and periodontal maintenance, restorative care such as fillings, crowns, and bridges, dentures and partials, pediatric care including sedation, and priority for children in pain and noticeably swollen individuals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Donated Dental Program serves individuals at or below 100% of the Federal Poverty Level. Discounted Dental Program serves eligible individuals at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level who do not qualify for the donated program. Income verification must be emailed and printed proof of income is required at each visit.

**Population Served**
Low-income and homeless individuals in Salt Lake County who need dental care and meet program income rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-972-2747. Email income verification to treatment@donateddental.org before scheduling. Patients are scheduled in the order income eligibility is confirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
No walk-ins are accepted for Donated Dental Program appointments. Specialty treatments depend on specialist availability. Discounted program patients pay reduced prices at time of service after treatment prices are explained.
resources.name: Salt Lake Donated Dental and Discounted Dental Programs

resources.address: Parkview Elementary, Glendale Community Learning Center, and Liberty Community Learning Center, Salt Lake City, UT
resources.description: Salt Lake Education Foundation's Student and Family Support vision clinics connect Salt Lake City School District students and community members within district boundaries to free comprehensive eye exams and prescription glasses through Friends for Sight and volunteer optometry partners.
resources.hours: Appointments are scheduled through the Friends for Sight scheduling link; clinic schedules vary by site.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free comprehensive eye exams and prescription glasses through district vision clinics staffed by Friends for Sight, volunteer optometrists from the Utah Optometric Association, and Rocky Mountain University College of Optometry faculty and students.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Salt Lake City School District students and community members within district boundaries.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake City School District students and community members who live within district boundaries and need vision services.

**How to Best Connect**
Schedule an appointment using the Friends for Sight scheduling link on the Salt Lake Education Foundation page. Questions can be emailed to clinic@friendsforsight.org or directed by phone to 801-524-2020.

**Important Information to Know**
Clinic locations are listed at Parkview Elementary, Glendale Community Learning Center, and Liberty Community Learning Center. Confirm district-boundary eligibility, appointment availability, and which site is operating before sending a client.
resources.name: Salt Lake Education Foundation Student and Family Support Vision Clinics

resources.address: 4600 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84123
resources.description: Salt Lake Technical College at SLCC provides career-focused technical certificates, workforce training, and apprenticeship training in fields such as advanced manufacturing, construction trades, health care, IT, public safety, CDL, electrical, plumbing, lineworker, meter, and substation work.
resources.hours: SLCC Student Services hours Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; Enrollment Info Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-8:00 PM, Friday 7:30 AM-4:30 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career-focused certificates, degrees, not-for-credit workforce training, and apprenticeship training. Program areas include CNC/machining, engineering design, automotive, HVACR, welding, diesel, CDL, automation, electronics, medical assisting, CNA, pharmacy technician, EMT, law enforcement, electrical apprenticeship, low-voltage apprenticeship, plumbing apprenticeship, lineworker, meter, and substation programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements vary by technical certificate, degree, apprenticeship, workforce training, or ESL program. Some programs require placement testing, advising, program prerequisites, employer sponsorship, or specific registration steps.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County and area students seeking technical education, short-term workforce training, apprenticeships, or career-focused certificates through SLCC.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Salt Lake Tech Request Info or Apply Now links. For Salt Lake Technical College admissions, email sltech@slcc.edu or call 801-957-4073. For workforce training help, email wte@slcc.edu or call 801-957-5200.

**Important Information to Know**
Tuition, financial aid, admissions steps, and schedules vary by program. This is the practical SLCC technical-training front door, not a single free-training promise.
resources.name: Salt Lake Technical College at SLCC Technical Certificates and Apprenticeship Training

resources.address: 10000 Centennial Pkwy #111, Sandy, UT 84070
resources.description: Sandy Police Department lists a victim-assistance crisis line and is listed by Utah Safe at Home as a certified program assistant for domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, abuse, and related address-confidentiality enrollment.
resources.hours: Sandy police/public office hours should be confirmed; crisis line listed by the city is 801-568-6099.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victim-assistance contact through Sandy Police Department and Safe at Home certified program-assistant help for survivors who may need address confidentiality. This can include helping eligible survivors apply for Utah Safe at Home when domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, abuse, or trafficking makes their home address unsafe.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for victims connected to Sandy or people who need a Sandy Police victim advocate. Safe at Home eligibility requires being a Utah resident who is a victim of or threatened with qualifying abuse and meeting address-safety/move requirements; the application must be completed with a certified program assistant.

**Population Served**
Victims in Sandy, Utah, including domestic violence survivors and survivors seeking Safe at Home enrollment assistance through a certified program assistant.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Sandy victim crisis line at 801-568-6099. The police department address is 10000 Centennial Pkwy #111, Sandy. Call 911 for immediate danger.

**Important Information to Know**
The Sandy city page is sparse on detailed victim-advocacy services, so confirm advocate availability and fit before sending a client in person. Safe at Home does not accept direct applications without a certified program assistant.
resources.name: Sandy Police Department Victim Assistance

resources.description: Scenic Valley Employment LLC is listed in the official September 2026 USOR Approved Community Rehabilitation Program registry as an approved provider serving Salt Lake County, with a direct phone contact for employment-related rehabilitation services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
USOR-approved Community Rehabilitation Program services. The registry listing supports Scenic Valley Employment LLC's approved provider identity and Salt Lake County service area; the exact mix of job development, job coaching, supported employment, or other employment supports should be confirmed by phone.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Likely tied to Utah Vocational Rehabilitation or related funding, but the registry-only evidence does not publish complete eligibility or referral requirements. Call before relying on direct enrollment.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities or vocational rehabilitation needs in Salt Lake County who may need employment support from a USOR-approved provider.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Brandon Gerber at 385-245-9872 and ask whether Scenic Valley Employment LLC is accepting Salt Lake County clients, what services are currently available, and whether the person needs a USOR counselor or other funding authorization first.

**Important Information to Know**
This lead is supported by the official state CRP registry but no independent public website was verified. Do not send someone to an office without first confirming intake, capacity, and funding path by phone.
resources.name: Scenic Valley Employment LLC Supported Employment Services

resources.description: The Scott Lundell Military Survivors Tuition Waiver provides tuition waiver eligibility at Utah state schools for surviving dependents of service members killed in action on or after September 11, 2001.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tuition waiver at Utah state schools for eligible surviving dependents of qualifying service members.

**Eligibility Requirements**
UDVMA states surviving dependents of service members killed in action on or after September 11, 2001 are eligible. The student must work through the state school's process.

**Population Served**
Eligible surviving dependents attending Utah state schools.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the admissions office, financial-aid office, or veterans/military benefits office at the Utah state school the student attends or plans to attend.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a tuition waiver, not direct cash assistance. Schools handle the application process and may require documentation of survivor status and enrollment.
resources.name: Scott B. Lundell Military Survivors Tuition Waiver

resources.address: 5411 S. Vine St. Unit 4B, Salt Lake City, UT 84107
resources.description: Sego Lily Center for the Abused Deaf provides Utah domestic-violence and sexual-assault support for Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, and DeafDisabled people, with daytime local video-phone access in Salt Lake City and after-hours referral to the National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline.
resources.hours: Daytime local support during regular business hours; after-hours/weekend National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline listed for evenings, weekends, and holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Domestic violence and sexual-assault support for Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, and DeafDisabled people in Utah, including connection to services, resources, and abuse-healing support. The site provides local daytime video-phone contact and after-hours National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline access.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, and DeafDisabled people needing help with domestic violence, sexual assault, or abuse-related support. Contact the office or use the Get Help/Appointment route.

**Population Served**
Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, and DeafDisabled survivors in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
For Salt Lake City daytime support, use video phone 385-474-2083 or the Get Help/Appointment route. Address: 5411 S. Vine St. Unit 4B, Salt Lake City. After hours, weekends, and holidays, call the National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline at 855-812-1001. For immediate danger call or text 911 where available.

**Important Information to Know**
Local support appears office-hours based; after-hours crisis support routes to the national Deaf hotline. Confirm safe communication preferences before outreach.
resources.name: Sego Lily Center for the Abused Deaf Advocacy Services

resources.description: National one-on-one case management and lifetime support for critically wounded, ill, and injured service members, veterans, and military families, including financial/family assistance, transition, wellness, adaptive equipment, and Vietnam veteran support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Semper Fi & America's Fund provides one-on-one case management and tailored support, including financial and family assistance, bedside and basic-needs support, specialized equipment, home and vehicle adaptive modifications, transition support, vocational training, education and career development, integrative wellness, and the LCpl Parsons Welcome Home Fund for Vietnam veterans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Focused on critically wounded, ill, and injured service members, veterans, and military families from all branches of the U.S. Armed Forces. The Vietnam veterans fund focuses on service-connected injuries, combat-related wounds, and illnesses associated with Agent Orange exposure. Each request is individually reviewed.

**Population Served**
Critically wounded, ill, and injured service members, veterans, military families, and eligible Vietnam veterans nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 760-725-3680 or use the website contact route from the Need Assistance section.

**Important Information to Know**
Support is individualized and not every applicant will receive every type of assistance. This is not a crisis line or guaranteed grant program; expect case review and documentation.
resources.name: Semper Fi & America's Fund Service Member and Family Support

resources.description: Utah's Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program provides eligible seniors with seasonal coupons for fresh fruits, vegetables, herbs, and honey at authorized farmers markets, farm stands, and community distribution centers. The 2026 distribution period is May 1-September 30 and redemption runs May 1-October 15.
resources.hours: Seasonal: 2026 distribution May 1-September 30; redemption May 1-October 15
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Seasonal produce coupons for fresh fruits, vegetables, herbs, and honey at authorized farmers markets, farm stands, and community distribution centers. The candidate evidence lists a $50 coupon benefit for 2026.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Utah residents age 60 or older who meet Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program rules. Program funding is seasonal and first-come, first-served; proxy pickup may be allowed with completed paperwork.

**Population Served**
Older Utah residents, including eligible Salt Lake County seniors, who can apply through a distribution site and use authorized market locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-453-3663 or use the Utah DHHS Community Food Security Program page to find current distribution and redemption information. For 2026, distribution is listed from May 1 through September 30 and redemption from May 1 through October 15.

**Important Information to Know**
This is seasonal and may run out. As of late September 2026, the distribution deadline is September 30, 2026, with redemption continuing through October 15, 2026 for issued coupons.
resources.name: Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program

resources.description: Senior Planet from AARP offers free online classes, technology help, wellness and social programs, and a tech hotline for adults age 50+ who want to learn and connect digitally.
resources.hours: Tech hotline hours reported by AARP as Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-8:00 PM Eastern and Saturday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM Eastern; online class schedule varies.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free older-adult technology learning and digital community programs, including online classes, tech-help resources, wellness, social connection, work and money, creativity and discussion programming, plus a free tech hotline.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Senior Planet programs are designed for older adults and commonly welcome people age 50+. Some classes may require registration; many online offerings are free and remote.

**Population Served**
Adults age 50 and older, including Salt Lake County residents who can use remote classes, community features and hotline support.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit SeniorPlanet.org for classes and programs. Call the Senior Planet tech hotline at 888-713-3495 for help with technology questions or getting connected to programs.

**Important Information to Know**
Senior Planet is not a local Salt Lake office. Participants generally need a phone, computer, tablet or internet access depending on the service they want to use.
resources.name: Senior Planet from AARP

resources.address: 1763 Columbia Road NW, Suite 175, PMB 839009, Washington, DC 20009
resources.description: Free online veteran-to-veteran college and graduate admissions counseling for veterans and service members, including school selection, application strategy, essays, mentorship, and VetLink resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Service to School provides free college and graduate-school application counseling, school-selection help, essay/application feedback, admissions mentorship, VetLink partner resources, and veteran-led peer support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for U.S. military veterans and service members applying to undergraduate, MBA/business, law, healthcare/medical, and other graduate programs. Applicants create a profile and request admissions support online.

**Population Served**
Veterans and service members nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents pursuing higher education.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Admissions Support link on the Service to School website to create a profile and request support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is admissions counseling and mentorship, not financial aid or guaranteed admission. Match timing may depend on volunteer mentor and advisor capacity.
resources.name: Service to School Free Admissions Counseling for Veterans

resources.address: 2480 S 3400 W, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Sheet Metal Workers Local 312 JATC offers a five-year earn-and-learn sheet metal apprenticeship in West Valley City with paid on-the-job training, classroom instruction, wage advancement, and a direct application link.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Five-year sheet metal apprenticeship combining paid on-the-job training, classroom instruction, trade skills, and wage advancement. The program includes 900 classroom-related training hours and 8,000 on-the-job hours and is registered with the U.S. Department of Labor Office of Apprenticeship.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Apprentices are sponsored by the contractor they work for and Sheet Metal Workers Local Union 312. The page states the program pays for supplies and curriculum/books, while apprentices pay for personal tools and school tuition. Call or use the application link for current application requirements and opening status.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake County and the West Valley City area seeking sheet metal trade apprenticeship and paid career training.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Click Here for Application link on the apprenticeship page, call 801-972-2480, or contact the JATC at 2480 S 3400 W, West Valley City.

**Important Information to Know**
Applicants should confirm current openings, tuition, tool costs, sponsorship steps, and school registration details before applying. The page identifies Ogden-Weber Applied Technology College classroom registration, so class location/details should be confirmed.
resources.name: Sheet Metal Workers Local 312 JATC Sheet Metal Apprenticeship

resources.address: Liberty Park, Salt Lake City, UT; organization address 824 S 700 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
resources.description: Showers of Hope Utah provides free mobile showers and related dignity-centered support for people experiencing homelessness, with the official site listing Liberty Park on Wednesdays from noon to 4:00 PM and contact by email.
resources.hours: Wednesdays, noon to 4:00 PM at Liberty Park according to the official site; confirm by email before relying on the schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free mobile showers for people experiencing homelessness, plus related support that may include haircuts, meals, addiction recovery mentoring, mental-health support, and connection to resources when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**

People experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity in Salt Lake City.

This is a mobile hygiene service, not a daily shower site or shelter. Availability may depend on staffing, weather, funding, and supplies.

resources.description: SimpleCitizen is a paid online immigration application-preparation platform that helps with supported application types such as marriage and family green cards, citizenship, green-card renewal, DACA renewal, employment authorization, K-1 visa petitions, removal of conditions, and employment-based green cards, with optional legal review through an attorney network.

resources.informationText:

Paid online immigration application preparation for supported forms, including marriage-based green card, parent- or child-petitioned green cards, citizenship, green-card renewal, DACA renewal, employment authorization, K-1 fiance visa petitions, removal of conditions, and employment-based green cards. The process includes a questionnaire, form assembly, optional legal review, case-manager guidance, printing/shipping, filing instructions, and case tracking.

Best fit for people with application types supported by SimpleCitizen and enough stability to use an online paid service. The free eligibility quiz may help identify the application type, but complex cases may require independent legal advice.

**Population Served**
Immigration applicants who can use an online application-preparation service, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Started link or chat/support options on the SimpleCitizen website. Clients submit information and documents online and receive a prepared packet and filing instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a paid commercial service, not free legal aid. USCIS government fees are separate, and SimpleCitizen cannot guarantee approval. It is not a replacement for full legal representation in complicated or high-risk cases.

Children and families in the UT-Salt Lake chapter coverage area, including Salt Lake County households where children lack adequate beds.

Residents must live in a drug- and alcohol-free environment and follow house rules, including sobriety meetings, sponsorship, random drug testing, mandatory house meetings, and zero tolerance for drug or alcohol use, possession, or distribution. Adults seeking sober living or transitional housing in recovery from substance use who can live in a structured sober community.

Call 801-386-9889 or use the website contact form. Ask about current openings, house location, gender fit, fees, deposit, sobriety requirements, and whether scholarships or payment help exist.

This is not emergency shelter and is not free unless the provider confirms assistance. Openings and fees are not clearly posted; confirm before sending a client.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official replacement Social Security card requests. Some people can complete the request online; others may need to provide documents or use a local Social Security office.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The requester must meet SSA identity and citizenship or immigration-status proof rules. SSA generally requires original or certified documents and applies annual and lifetime replacement-card limits, with exceptions.

**Population Served**
People who need a replacement Social Security card, including Salt Lake County residents who can use national online/phone service or the Salt Lake City field office.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at SSA's replacement-card page or call 800-772-1213. The Salt Lake City field office listed in the lead is 175 East 400 South, Suite 500, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
A local office does not print the card the same day; cards are mailed after verification. People missing standard documents may need supporting original or certified records before SSA can issue a replacement.
resources.name: Social Security Administration Replacement Social Security Card

resources.hours: Phone representatives Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM local time; automated phone services 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Federal cash-benefit application access for Supplemental Security Income and Social Security Disability Insurance, including online applications, phone help, claim status, office locator support, and benefit information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SSDI generally requires disability or blindness and enough work history. SSI may be available to adults or children with little income/resources who have a disability or blindness, or to adults age 65+. SSA makes the official eligibility decision.

**Population Served**
People nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents, who may qualify for federal disability benefits or Supplemental Security Income.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through SSA, call 1-800-772-1213, or use TTY 1-800-325-0778. Phone representatives are available Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM local time; automated phone services are available 24/7. Use the SSA Office Locator before visiting in person.

**Important Information to Know**
SSA currently states disability applications average about 200 to 230 days for review. Benefits are not guaranteed, and applicants may need medical, income, resource, and work-history documentation.
resources.name: Social Security SSI and SSDI Benefits Application

User must have hearing loss that makes captions necessary to use the phone. Signup may require certification or eligibility information under FCC-regulated captioned telephone service rules.

People with hearing loss, including Salt Lake County residents, who need real-time captions for telephone conversations.

Deaf, hard-of-hearing, and speech-disabled people, including Salt Lake County residents, who use ASL or video relay to make and receive phone calls.

resources.description: South Salt Lake Justice Court Community Court helps unsheltered people with South Salt Lake Justice Court cases connect to treatment, medical care, housing, court staff, and community supports intended to reduce recidivism and stabilize court obligations.
resources.hours: Open court dates typically take place in the mornings on the second and fourth Wednesday of each month; exact dates and times change, so call before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Court connects eligible defendants with court staff and community partners for treatment, medical care, stable housing, long-term supports, and planning around sentencing obligations. Open court dates let people with open South Salt Lake Justice Court cases appear before a judge and meet resource providers even if they are not enrolled in the full program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Full program participants must have at least one open South Salt Lake Justice Court case, be currently experiencing homelessness, have no violent felony or sex offense charges or convictions, have a substance-use and/or mental-health disorder, voluntarily complete the CCAT assessment, and agree to work with the team on sentencing requirements. Open court dates are for individuals with open South Salt Lake Justice Court cases.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness who have South Salt Lake Justice Court cases, including people navigating court involvement and housing instability in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Justice Court at 801-483-6072 or use the Community Court contact form to ask about eligibility and confirm the next open court date. The court address is 220 E Morris Avenue, South Salt Lake City, UT 84115. Some defendants may attend from Road Home shelter locations by Webex.

**Important Information to Know**
This is court-based support, not general legal representation or a housing placement guarantee. Case eligibility, open court dates, and program acceptance should be confirmed before sending someone to court.
resources.name: South Salt Lake Justice Court Community Court

Best fit for victims and family members connected to South Salt Lake Police matters or South Salt Lake incidents. Call the advocate team to confirm fit and current availability.

Victims in South Salt Lake, including domestic violence and dating violence survivors. The city notes awareness of LGBTQIAP+, refugee, and non-English-speaking community needs and has a full-time Spanish-speaking advocate.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-412-3660 or the Spanish-speaking line at 801-412-3661. Victim advocate hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM. For non-emergency situations call 801-840-4000; call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: South Salt Lake Police Department Victim Services

resources.description: The South Salt Lake Utility Assistance Program helps eligible City of South Salt Lake residents with water, sewer, stormwater, and garbage utility charges, with approved payments made directly to the utility provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Utility-bill assistance for eligible South Salt Lake residents. Funding may help pay water, sewer, stormwater, and garbage utility expenses billed directly by the provider, up to the lesser of $150 or the outstanding account balance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The applicant must live in the City of South Salt Lake and have eligible water and/or sewer utility billing. Household gross income must be at or below 150% of the federal poverty line, with a life-changing event or significant income reduction. Assistance is limited to once per fiscal year and does not cover reconnection fees or returned-check fees.

**Population Served**
Low-income City of South Salt Lake residents with eligible utility accounts, including some tenants who pay the water or sewer provider directly and can document responsibility for the bill.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Promise South Salt Lake at 801-483-6057 or promise@sslc.gov, or go to 220 E Morris Ave. St. 350, South Salt Lake. The public page states the application period is October 1 through September 30.

**Important Information to Know**
Funds are limited and processed first come, first served after a complete application. Approved payments go directly to the utility provider, not to the resident.
resources.name: South Salt Lake Utility Assistance Program

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
South Valley Services provides safe shelter and ongoing supportive services for people impacted by domestic and sexual violence. Services include shelter, counseling, case management, advocacy, support groups, prevention, and a 24-hour helpline.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for people impacted by domestic violence or sexual assault. Shelter access and safety planning are handled through the helpline; the shelter location is confidential.

Women, men, and children impacted by domestic and sexual violence in Salt Lake County, Tooele County, Carbon County, and Emery County.

**How to Best Connect**
For Salt Lake County, call the 24-hour helpline at 801-255-1095 or text/TTY 801-870-5018. Do not go to the mailing address for shelter; use the helpline for safe access.

**Important Information to Know**
Emergency shelter location is confidential for safety. Translation services are available as needed, and services are provided in English and Spanish.
resources.name: South Valley Services Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Shelter Services

resources.address: 8000 S Redwood Rd, West Jordan, UT
resources.description: South Valley Services provides Salt Lake County domestic-violence shelter and advocacy services through a 24-hour helpline, emergency shelter, case management, clinical therapy, children’s services, classes, prevention/outreach, and walk-in advocacy-center access.
resources.hours: 24-hour helpline; West Jordan advocacy center Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM, Friday by appointment only, closed daily 12:00 PM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Domestic-violence helpline, emergency shelter, advocacy, case management, community resource center support, clinical therapy, children’s learning center, classes, prevention and outreach. Services are available in English and Spanish, with translation for any language available 24/7.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people needing help for domestic violence in Salt Lake County. Shelter and service access depend on safety assessment, current availability, and service fit through the helpline or advocacy center.

**Population Served**
Domestic violence survivors in Salt Lake County, including individuals and families seeking confidential support, shelter, safety planning, or advocacy.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Salt Lake 24-hour helpline at 801-255-1095 or TTY/Text 801-870-5018. People may also walk into the West Jordan Advocacy Center at 8000 S Redwood Rd, Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM, Friday by appointment only; office is closed 12:00 PM-1:00 PM daily.

**Important Information to Know**
The public address is the advocacy center, not necessarily shelter placement information. Call the helpline for shelter availability and safe planning before going anywhere if safety is a concern.
resources.name: South Valley Services South Valley Sanctuary and Advocacy Center

resources.address: 8000 S Redwood Rd, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: South Valley Services is listed in Utah DWS TANF Family Housing materials as a Salt Lake County pathway for eligible survivor families needing housing-related assistance such as deposits, short-term rent or mortgage help, utilities, application fees, back payments, and case management.
resources.hours: 24-hour helpline; West Jordan advocacy center Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM, Friday by appointment only, closed daily 12:00 PM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing-related financial assistance pathway for eligible domestic-violence survivor families through TANF Family Housing, including possible deposit assistance, short-term rent or mortgage assistance, utility assistance, housing application fees, back payments, and case management. South Valley Services also provides 24-hour domestic-violence helpline, shelter access, advocacy, clinical therapy, and community resource center support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
TANF Family Housing serves eligible families in short-term crisis and requires TANF needy-family eligibility and provider assessment. South Valley Services access is for people needing domestic-violence help in Salt Lake County; assistance depends on safety needs, eligibility, documentation, funding, and current fit.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County domestic-violence survivors and eligible families needing safe housing support after violence or housing crisis.

**How to Best Connect**
For the TANF Family Housing pathway, DWS materials list 435-228-6967 and in-person requests at 8000 S Redwood Rd, West Jordan. For domestic-violence help, call the Salt Lake 24-hour helpline at 801-255-1095 or TTY/Text 801-870-5018. Advocacy center walk-in hours are Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM and Friday by appointment, closed 12:00 PM-1:00 PM daily.

**Important Information to Know**
Financial assistance is not guaranteed and is likely paid to third parties rather than directly to the client. If safety is a concern, call the helpline before visiting. The public South Valley Services page confirms survivor services; the detailed financial-assistance scope comes from Utah DWS TANF Family Housing materials.
resources.name: South Valley Services TANF Family Housing / Survivor Housing Support Pathway

resources.address: 455 W Universal Circle, Sandy, UT 84070
resources.description: South Valley Training Company provides employment services for individuals with disabilities, including Voc Rehab-contracted assessments, job development, and job coaching for competitive integrated employment.
