This is a government appeal process, not legal advice or attorney representation. Hearings are generally by telephone, and parties must confirm the phone number they will use. Interpreters and disability accommodations can be requested through the Appeals Unit.
resources.name: Unemployment Insurance Appeals Unit

resources.description: Unified Police Department's Domestic Violence Advocate Program serves UPD communities in Salt Lake County with domestic-violence advocacy, jurisdiction-specific advocate contacts, safety planning information, court support, document support, and referrals to shelter, counseling, translation, support groups, and financial support.
resources.hours: Advocate availability varies by UPD community; call the listed jurisdiction advocate or non-emergency dispatch for routing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Domestic-violence advocate support for UPD-served communities, including help averting potential or continued violence, public education, document support, investigator follow-up advocacy, court support, and referrals for victim rights, support groups, translation, counseling, financial support, shelter, legal resources, and protective orders.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for survivors or incidents in UPD-served Salt Lake County communities such as Midvale/White City, Millcreek/Emigration Canyon, Holladay/Brighton, Magna/Copperton, and Kearns. Call the advocate for the relevant community.

**Population Served**
Domestic violence survivors in Unified Police Department jurisdictions in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the relevant advocate: Midvale/White City 385-468-9365; Millcreek/Emigration Canyon 385-468-9627; Holladay/Brighton 385-468-9446; Magna/Copperton 385-468-9602; Kearns 385-468-9520. For non-emergency dispatch call 801-840-4000; for emergency call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
Use the jurisdiction-specific advocate rather than the generic police number when possible. This is law-enforcement/system-based advocacy, not confidential shelter advocacy.
resources.name: Unified Police Department Domestic Violence Advocate Program
resources.phone: Midvale/White City 385-468-9365; Millcreek/Emigration Canyon 385-468-9627; Holladay/Brighton 385-468-9446; Magna/Copperton 385-468-9602; Kearns 385-468-9520; non-emergency 801-840-4000

resources.description: Free parent-to-parent support network for Utah families of children with special needs, including new-diagnosis visits, membership, education, meetups, and transition-related support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Parent-to-parent support, free membership, new diagnosis visits, family programs by age group, parental support, education, meetups, and connection to other families.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Membership is for parents and families of children with special needs. Membership is listed as free.

**Population Served**
Parents and families of children with special needs in Utah and the Wasatch Front.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Join United Angels link for membership or the Request a Visit link to connect with another parent. Current events and programs are listed through the website and event calendar.

**Important Information to Know**
In-person events and consultation capacity can vary. This is family peer support and education, not a substitute for clinical care, legal advice, or DSPD eligibility determination.
resources.name: United Angels Foundation Parent-to-Parent Special Needs Support

resources.address: 350 S Main Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Utah has a limited Pro Bono Assistance Program for qualified individual debtors defending certain adversary proceedings or responding to Chapter 5 bankruptcy demands.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Limited pro bono assistance program for qualified individual debtors defending an adversary proceeding affecting discharge and for individuals responding to Chapter 5 bankruptcy demands under Bankruptcy Code sections 544, 547, 548, 549, and 550.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to qualifying individuals in the specified bankruptcy litigation situations. It is not general bankruptcy filing help and does not cover every bankruptcy case.

**Population Served**
People with qualifying District of Utah bankruptcy matters, including Salt Lake County residents with relevant federal bankruptcy proceedings.

**How to Best Connect**
Review the Bankruptcy Court's Filing Without an Attorney page and General Order 22-001. For process questions, contact the Bankruptcy Court clerk at 801-524-6687 before relying on the program.

**Important Information to Know**
Court clerk staff cannot provide legal advice. The public page confirms the program but does not present a simple public application form, so clients should call the clerk or seek bankruptcy legal advice quickly if deadlines are pending.
resources.name: United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Utah Pro Bono Assistance Program

resources.address: Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse, 351 S West Temple, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Utah provides official pro se guides, forms, filing information, fee-waiver forms, and email filing/electronic notice forms for people filing federal civil cases without an attorney.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official federal court self-help forms and guides for unrepresented litigants, including civil rights complaints, employment discrimination complaints, motions to proceed without prepaying fees, service forms, sample filings, and email filing/electronic notice forms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people filing or responding in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah without an attorney. Forms must fit the federal case type and procedural requirements.

**Population Served**
Unrepresented federal civil litigants in the District of Utah, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the court's Pro Se Filing Information page for forms and guides. The courthouse is at 351 S West Temple, Salt Lake City, and the court phone listed in the lead is 801-524-6100.

**Important Information to Know**
This is procedural self-help information, not legal advice or representation. Federal deadlines and service rules can be strict, so clients may still need legal advice.
resources.name: United States District Court for the District of Utah Pro Se Filing Information

resources.address: 257 E 200 S, Suite 300, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: United Way of Salt Lake/Utah's Promise is listed by Utah DWS as a TANF Family Housing access point for Salt Lake County and Utah County families, with possible deposit, short-term rent or mortgage, utility, application-fee, back-payment, and case-management help for TANF-eligible families with a minor child.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
TANF Family Housing homeless-prevention support for eligible families, including possible deposit assistance, short-term rent or mortgage assistance, utility assistance, housing application fees, back payments, and case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Households must meet TANF Family Housing eligibility criteria, including having a minor child in the household. The provider must confirm eligibility, documentation, funding, and whether the family's situation fits program rules.

**Population Served**
TANF-eligible families with minor children in Salt Lake County and Utah County who need housing-stability or homeless-prevention assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 2-1-1 for access and community-resource routing. DWS also lists in-person access through Utah's Promise at 257 E 200 S, Suite 300, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is limited housing support, not guaranteed rent payment or immediate shelter. Funding, documentation, eligibility, and coverage limits must be confirmed at intake.
resources.name: United Way of Salt Lake TANF Family Housing at Utah's Promise

resources.address: Student Union, Room 70, 200 S Central Campus Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: The University of Utah Dream Center supports current and future University of Utah students, including undocumented students and students impacted by immigration, with college-access advising, resource connection, and direct appointments.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Education access and student-success support, including appointments with Dream Center staff, advising, connection to campus resources, and support for students affected by immigration-related barriers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for current or prospective University of Utah students who need support connected to undocumented status, immigration impact, or related higher-education access barriers. It is not a general immigration legal service.

**Population Served**
University of Utah current and future students, including undocumented students and students impacted by immigration.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-581-3470, email dream@utah.edu, use the contact form, or book an in-person or virtual Microsoft Teams appointment from the Dream Center website. The office is in the Student Union, Room 70, 200 S Central Campus Drive.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are specific to University of Utah access and student success. For legal immigration advice, connect with a qualified immigration legal provider rather than relying on this center.
resources.name: University of Utah Dream Center

resources.address: INSCC Building, 155 S 1452 E, Suite 350, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: The University of Utah English Language Institute offers fee-based English instruction through intensive, evening general English, and online programs for local and international students.
resources.hours: Program and office hours vary by session; contact ELI for current start dates, deadlines, and appointment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Academic English instruction through the Intensive English Program, General English evening classes, and online English programs. General English evening classes are for tourists on B1/B2 visas and local residents, not F-1 students.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on program type. Intensive English may fit international students seeking student visa study, tourists seeking part-time courses, and local students wanting a more challenging option; evening and online programs have separate visa and enrollment limits.

**Population Served**
Adults and students in the Salt Lake Valley and online learners who want structured English instruction through the University of Utah.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-581-4600 or use the ELI website program pages and contact link. The office is in the INSCC Building, 155 S 1452 E, Suite 350, Salt Lake City, UT 84112.

**Important Information to Know**
This is fee-based English instruction, not a free ESL program. Costs, session deadlines, visa rules, and whether the course meets the client's goal should be confirmed before applying.
resources.name: University of Utah English Language Institute

resources.address: 200 S Central Campus Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: University of Utah Financial Wellness Center hosts IRS VITA free tax-preparation services for University of Utah students and directs Utah community members to its Rose Park Community Center VITA site when appointments are open.
resources.hours: Tax appointments are seasonal; the page stated appointments were closed for the season and gave email contact for extensions, abatements, amended returns, and prior-year returns.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free tax preparation by IRS-certified VITA volunteers. The program has a University of Utah student site and a Rose Park Community Center site for Utah community members.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must meet IRS VITA qualifications. Separate links are provided for U.S. resident students, international students, faculty/staff, and community members.

**Population Served**
University of Utah students, international students, faculty/staff, and Utah community members who qualify for VITA tax help.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the tax clinic page to book when appointments are open. For filing extensions, abatements, amended returns, or prior-year filing, email vitataxes@utah.edu. The Financial Wellness Center can also be reached at 801-585-7379.

**Important Information to Know**
Regular appointments were listed as closed for the season when checked. This is tax filing help, not emergency cash assistance.
resources.name: University of Utah Financial Wellness Center VITA Tax Filing

resources.description: University of Utah Health Aging Brain Care Program provides evaluation, diagnosis, management, geriatric psychiatry support, caregiver education, and resources for memory and thinking disorders, with virtual care offered.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Evaluation, diagnosis, and management for dementia and other cognitive disorders; advanced neuroimaging; geriatric psychiatry support; anti-amyloid therapy for mild Alzheimer's disease when appropriate; disease education; caregiver support and resources; ongoing symptom management; clinical-trial and genetic-testing access; and virtual care options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for people with memory or thinking disorders who need clinical evaluation or management. Appointment availability, referral preferences, insurance coverage, and out-of-pocket costs depend on University of Utah Health intake and the person's plan.

**Population Served**
Older adults and others with cognitive symptoms such as memory loss, confusion, language changes, mood or personality changes, or suspected dementia, plus caregivers seeking education and resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an appointment through the University of Utah Health page or call 801-581-2628. Virtual appointments may be available through the health system's virtual care process.

**Important Information to Know**
This is medical specialty care, not emergency crisis care or a free social-service program. Insurance, referral needs, appointment availability, clinical appropriateness, and costs should be confirmed when scheduling.
resources.name: University of Utah Health Aging Brain Care Program

resources.description: University of Utah Health offers financial assistance, payment plans, cost-estimate help, and medication support resources for eligible U of U Health patients who cannot afford medical bills or prescriptions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance applications, payment plans, Medicaid eligibility links, price-estimate help, and pharmacy medication-support resources for University of Utah Health bills and prescriptions. Pharmacy pages list manufacturer assistance, co-pay support groups, grants, foundations, patient assistance offices, and Medication Support Service for uninsured U of U Health patients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Financial assistance depends on income guidelines, hardship review, approval, and documentation such as an application, hardship letter, bank statements, tax return, and recent income proof. Medication Support Service is for uninsured University of Utah Health patients who need help paying for medications and qualify through the program.

**Population Served**
University of Utah Health patients and guarantors with financial hardship, including uninsured or underinsured Salt Lake County residents receiving U of U Health care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call patient billing at 801-587-6303 or use MyChart/the online financial assistance application. For financial advocate questions, call 801-581-2957. Uninsured U of U Health patients needing medication payment help may call 801-581-2957 option 4 to ask about Medication Support Service.

**Important Information to Know**
This applies to University of Utah Health bills or U of U Health patients; it is not a universal charity-care or prescription-payment program. Approval, discount level, and medication assistance are not guaranteed.
resources.name: University of Utah Health Financial Assistance and Medication Support Service

resources.description: University of Utah Health GUIDE is a dementia care-navigation program for eligible Salt Lake County residents with dementia and Medicare Parts A and B, offering assessments, care plans, monthly check-ins, caregiver support, resource coordination, safety assessments, and possible respite.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GUIDE provides dementia-focused support such as annual comprehensive dementia assessment with a specialized provider, monthly phone check-ins, person-centered care plans, medication reviews, 24/7 caregiver support, caregiver education, community-resource coordination, transitional care support, in-home safety assessments for eligible participants, and respite services for eligible participants.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must have dementia, live in Salt Lake County, be enrolled in Medicare Parts A and B, and live at home or in an assisted living facility. The page states that Medicare Advantage, Special Needs Plans, and PACE are not eligible. A caregiver is not required to participate.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents living with dementia, with or without an unpaid caregiver, and their families or caregivers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the GUIDE team at 801-581-2628 or email guide@hsc.utah.edu. The team will review eligibility, start enrollment, and may arrange a comprehensive assessment visit at Madsen Geriatrics Clinic depending on the person's circumstances.

**Important Information to Know**
The page states there are no additional fees or copays to participate in GUIDE and Medicare benefits do not change. Eligibility is narrow; Medicare Advantage, Special Needs Plans, and PACE are excluded by the program page.
resources.name: University of Utah Health GUIDE (Guiding an Improved Dementia Experience)

resources.description: University of Utah Health Geriatric Care provides comprehensive, coordinated primary care for older adults, especially adults age 75+ with functional or cognitive limitations or multiple chronic conditions.
resources.hours: Clinic hours listed as 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Geriatric primary care through a patient-centered medical home, including medical exams, review of complex health and medication concerns, individualized treatment options, long-term provider relationships, shared decision-making, team-based care, and care management services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
University of Utah Health states geriatric care serves adults age 75+ and is best suited for people age 85+, people with functional or cognitive limitations, or people with multiple chronic medical conditions. Insurance, appointment availability, and costs depend on clinic intake and coverage.

**Population Served**
Older adults needing age-focused primary care, especially people age 75+ or medically complex older adults with balance problems, frequent falls, memory changes, multiple medications, depression, mobility problems, or three or more chronic conditions.

**How to Best Connect**
Call University of Utah Health Geriatric Care at 801-581-2628 to ask about appointments and whether geriatric primary care is a good fit.

**Important Information to Know**
This is medical primary care, not a free assistance program. Costs, insurance participation, referral needs, and appointment availability should be confirmed before scheduling.
resources.name: University of Utah Health Geriatric Patient-Centered Medical Home / Geriatric Care

resources.address: University of Utah Hospital, 50 N Medical Drive, Clinic 1A / Clinic E10, Salt Lake City, UT 84132
resources.description: University of Utah Health Infectious Diseases Clinic provides outpatient infectious disease care, HIV/AIDS care through Ryan White, and HIV PrEP services, including free PrEP for uninsured people who qualify.
resources.hours: PrEP appointments are offered Monday-Friday; call to schedule. Infectious Diseases appointment hours should be confirmed by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient infectious disease diagnosis and treatment, including HIV/AIDS and hepatitis care. Clinic 1A provides HIV/AIDS primary care, antiretroviral medications, case management, mental-health counseling, nutritional services, substance-use treatment linkage, health-insurance continuation support, and Ryan White care. The HIV PrEP clinic offers in-person and virtual PrEP appointments.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Infectious disease appointments are scheduled by phone and may involve referral or insurance review depending on the service. Ryan White services are for people living with HIV who meet program eligibility. Free PrEP is listed for people without health insurance who have a high chance of getting HIV; insured patients may use accepted insurance or be connected to another PrEP provider.

**Population Served**
People in Utah and the Mountain West needing infectious disease specialty care, people living with HIV/AIDS, and people at higher risk of HIV who need PrEP, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-585-2031 to schedule infectious disease, HIV/AIDS, or PrEP care. The clinic is at University of Utah Hospital, 50 N Medical Drive, Salt Lake City. Case management for Clinic 1A patients is listed at 801-585-2670.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a drop-in emergency service. PrEP scheduling pages also list 801-585-2512 for PrEP-specific appointment routing. Ryan White case management is for Clinic 1A patients enrolled in Ryan White programs.
resources.name: University of Utah Health Infectious Diseases Clinic / Clinic 1A HIV Care and PrEP Clinic

resources.address: 240 E Morris Ave, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: The Neurobehavior HOME Program provides coordinated primary medical care and mental-health care for children and adults with developmental disabilities who meet Utah Medicaid-related eligibility.
resources.hours: Call for current appointment availability. Telehealth appointments, including sick appointments, are listed for enrolled patients.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated primary care, preventive care, annual physicals and well-child checks, psychiatry, medication management, behavior management, counseling, psychology testing, case management, crisis management, dietitian/nutrition counseling, specialty-care referral, and billing/insurance support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must receive Utah Medicaid, have a developmental disability, have mental-health or behavioral challenges, and want both primary medical care and mental-health care from HOME. Medicaid determines whether a person qualifies for enrollment.

**Population Served**
Children and adults with developmental disabilities and behavioral or mental-health needs who have Utah Medicaid, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the HOME Program at 801-581-5515 with program questions. To ask whether someone qualifies for enrollment, call Medicaid at 1-866-608-9422. The clinic is at 240 E Morris Ave, South Salt Lake.

**Important Information to Know**
Enrollment is first come, first served as openings occur. People at the top of the list receive an intake packet before appointment scheduling. Current patients should use their assigned case manager as the main contact.
resources.name: University of Utah Health Neurobehavior HOME Program

resources.address: Redwood Health Center, 1525 W 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84119
resources.description: New American Services at Redwood Health Center helps New American, refugee, and immigrant patients access health care, interpretation, care navigation, Medicaid/CHIP help, financial aid, billing education, and community resources.
resources.hours: Redwood Health Center main hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-8:30 PM; Saturday-Sunday 9:00 AM-8:30 PM. Call to confirm New American Services availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Health-care navigation, culturally responsive primary care connection, interpreter support, Medicaid/CHIP application help, health-insurance education, medical billing education, financial-aid application help, medical-debt resource connection, pregnancy class, MyChart/digital access support, and community referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is designed for New American patients using Redwood Health Center. The official page says patients do not need a referral to see a New American team member. Bring ID, insurance card, Social Security card if available, medical records, and important paperwork to appointments.

**Population Served**
New Americans, former refugees, immigrants, and newcomers receiving or seeking care through Redwood Health Center in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Redwood Health Center at 801-213-9900. The center is at 1525 W 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84119. If medical records are needed, the fax number listed for Redwood scheduling is 801-213-9919.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a universal free-care program. Costs depend on U of U Health billing, insurance, Medicaid/CHIP eligibility, and any approved financial assistance. Redwood also has separate walk-in enrollment support times for Medicaid, CHIP, and Marketplace help.
resources.name: University of Utah Health New American Services at Redwood Health Center

resources.address: 168 N 1950 W, Suite 201, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Rose Park Primary Care Clinic is a University of Utah Health student-led, supervised primary care clinic offering exams, screenings, symptom care, chronic-condition care, post-hospital care, referrals, and community health worker support.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care delivered by medical school faculty and students, including regular health exams and screenings, care for symptoms such as stomach pain, muscle or joint pain, breathing issues, care after hospital stays, chronic-condition care such as diabetes care, referrals for other University of Utah Health care, community health worker support, and onsite food and clothing pantry connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page does not list a narrow eligibility rule. Patients should call to ask about new-patient availability, insurance, uninsured discounts, and whether the clinic fits their medical need.

**Population Served**
West Salt Lake and West Valley community members and other Salt Lake County residents seeking primary care through the Population Health Center.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-646-6399. The clinic is at 168 N 1950 W, Suite 201, Salt Lake City, UT 84116. Listed hours are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a supervised student-led primary care clinic. The official page does not promise free care; billing, insurance, and financial assistance should be confirmed before nonurgent services.
resources.name: University of Utah Health Rose Park Primary Care Clinic at Population Health Center

resources.address: 3690 S Main St, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: South Main Clinic offers University of Utah Health primary care for all stages of life, including family medicine, pediatrics, OB/GYN, midwife services, WIC, Medicaid eligibility workers, translation, and financial counselors.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care for all stages of life, including family medicine, pediatrics, OB/GYN, pregnancy care, midwife services, foster health care program, student-led care, Spanish language support, Medicaid eligibility workers, WIC, Holy Cross Ministries connection, and financial counselors.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic accepts most insurance, including Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare. The official page says uninsured patients may receive discounts based on income. Patients should call to confirm new-patient availability and service fit.

**Population Served**
South Salt Lake and Salt Lake County residents seeking primary care, pediatric care, pregnancy care, and related clinic supports.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-587-2525 or use the U of U Health appointment link. The clinic is at 3690 S Main St, Salt Lake City, UT 84115. Listed hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Discounts are based on income and are not the same as guaranteed free care. Confirm whether the requested service is through the medical clinic, dental clinic, WIC, or another onsite partner.
resources.name: University of Utah Health South Main Clinic

resources.address: Mobile program; recurring Salt Lake County stops include West Valley, Glendale, Kearns, South Salt Lake, and Midvale
resources.description: The Wellness Bus is a free mobile prevention program offering chronic-disease screenings, nutrition counseling, lifestyle coaching, interpretation, and referrals to medical, dental, and social-service resources.
resources.hours: Schedules change. September 2026 schedule lists recurring Salt Lake County stops in Glendale, Kearns, South Salt Lake, Midvale, and West Valley, generally in morning or afternoon blocks.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free chronic-disease screenings for blood glucose, blood pressure, cholesterol, and BMI; nutrition counseling; lifestyle coaching and education; chronic-disease education; interpretation; and referrals to health and social-service providers, including medical and dental resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No insurance or ID is required. Everyone is welcome, though most patients are adults age 18 and older; children who are overweight or obese and have diabetes risk factors may qualify.

**Population Served**
Residents of medically underserved communities reached by the mobile bus, including Salt Lake County stops in West Valley, Glendale, Kearns, South Salt Lake, and Midvale.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-587-5257 and check the current schedule before going. Screenings are first-come, first-served; first-time visitors should arrive at least 30 minutes before closing.

**Important Information to Know**
The Wellness Bus is a screening, coaching, education, and referral program, not a primary care or urgent treatment clinic. Schedules change frequently and some patients may not be seen before closing if demand is high.
resources.name: University of Utah Health The Wellness Bus

resources.address: 540 Arapeen Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
resources.description: University of Utah Lifelong Learning offers fee-based noncredit personal-enrichment and continuing education classes for adults 18+ across the Salt Lake Valley and online.
resources.hours: Classes start weekly; registration dates and class schedules vary by course.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Noncredit classes and workshops for adults, including art, craft, culinary, language, photography, technology, recreation, wellness, writing, literature, and other personal-enrichment topics.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Registration is open to adults 18 and older. No degree enrollment or matriculation is required. Individual courses may have fees, capacity limits, materials requirements, or prerequisites.

**Population Served**
Adults in Salt Lake County and nearby areas who want noncredit continuing education or personal-enrichment classes, including online learners where available.

**How to Best Connect**
Search and register through the University of Utah Lifelong Learning website, or contact University of Utah Continuing Education. The listed address is 540 Arapeen Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84108.

**Important Information to Know**
This is usually fee-based enrichment, not a degree, credential, GED, or basic-needs program. Confirm course cost, refund/drop policy, location, accessibility, and whether a class supports the client's practical goal.
resources.name: University of Utah Lifelong Learning Classes

resources.address: 201 S 1460 E, Student Services Building Room 105, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: The University of Utah Native Student Scholarship is a last-dollar tuition and mandatory-fee scholarship for eligible undergraduate degree-seeking students who are enrolled members of listed federally recognized tribes and meet University residency, FAFSA, and enrollment requirements.
resources.hours: Financial aid office hours were not confirmed in this preparation; contact the office before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Last-dollar scholarship support that covers remaining University of Utah undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees after other grants and scholarships are applied. The application page includes a Fall 2026 application link.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Must be an admitted University of Utah undergraduate degree-seeking student, qualify for resident tuition, enroll full-time, be an enrolled member of one of the listed federally recognized tribes, have proof of tribal enrollment, have a processed FAFSA on file by the first day of classes each semester receiving the scholarship, and maintain satisfactory academic progress for renewal.

**Population Served**
University of Utah undergraduate students who are enrolled members of eligible federally recognized tribes, including Native students from Salt Lake County who meet admission and residency/tuition criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Native Student Scholarship page to apply for the current term or contact the University Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid at financialaid@utah.edu or 801-581-6211. Office address: 201 S 1460 E, Student Services Building Room 105, Salt Lake City, UT 84112.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general scholarship for all Native students at any college. It is a last-dollar University of Utah scholarship and may be $0 for a semester if other grants/scholarships already cover tuition and mandatory fees; that semester still counts toward eligibility.
resources.name: University of Utah Native Student Scholarship

resources.address: 540 Arapeen Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
resources.description: The University of Utah Osher Lifelong Learning Institute offers noncredit courses, lectures, and activities for adults age 50 and better, with Salt Lake City, Sandy, and Zoom options and scholarship support for some participants.
resources.hours: Four terms per year; registration windows vary by term.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Noncredit lifelong-learning courses, lectures, special activities, free special events, and term-based learning opportunities. Prior official records and current program materials describe in-person and Zoom options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adults age 50 or better who become Osher members. Membership, class registration, course fees, and scholarship availability should be confirmed for the current term.

**Population Served**
Adults 50+ in Salt Lake County and nearby areas who want continuing education, enrichment, social connection, and lifelong learning through the University of Utah.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Osher at 801-581-6461, use the Osher contact form, review course listings at continue.utah.edu/osher, or contact the office at 540 Arapeen Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84108.

**Important Information to Know**
Osher courses are noncredit enrichment rather than degrees or workforce credentials. Fees, scholarships, course locations, and registration windows vary by term.
resources.name: University of Utah Osher Lifelong Learning Institute

resources.address: Salt Lake Legal Defenders Association, 275 E 200 S, Salt Lake City, UT
resources.description: University of Utah S.J. Quinney College of Law Pro Bono Initiative's Expungement Legal Site offers brief legal clinic help for barriers to employment such as expungements and outstanding warrants at a Salt Lake City clinic location.
resources.hours: 1st Thursday of every month, 5:00-7:00 PM; clients must arrive between 5:00 and 6:00 PM. Appointment or walk-in, subject to current clinic availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Brief legal clinic help for barriers to employment, including expungements and issues with outstanding warrants. Legal clinics generally provide short advice and recommendations rather than full representation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clinic availability is appointment or walk-in during listed clinic windows. Utah Courts advises calling Utah Legal Services ahead of time to see whether the person qualifies for an expungement.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County seeking help with record-related employment barriers, especially expungement questions and outstanding warrant issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an appointment online from the Utah Courts clinic listing, email probono@law.utah.edu, or call 801-581-5418. Walk-ins are encouraged during the listed clinic window at Salt Lake Legal Defenders Association, 275 E 200 S, Salt Lake City; arrive between 5:00 and 6:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a clinic for advice and screening, not guaranteed representation. Clinic dates can change; check the Utah Courts legal-clinics page or Pro Bono Initiative page before attending.
resources.name: University of Utah Pro Bono Initiative Expungement Legal Site

resources.address: SLLC Dream Center, West Valley Center Room 130, 3460 S 5600 W, West Valley City, UT 84128
resources.description: The University of Utah Pro Bono Initiative Immigration Legal Site is the current Salt Lake County free immigration clinic route listed by Utah Courts, offering walk-in immigration legal help on the fourth Wednesday of each month at the SLCC Dream Center, with additional statewide online and in-person community legal site options listed by Utah Courts.
resources.hours: Salt Lake County immigration legal site: 4th Wednesday of every month, walk-in only, 5:30 PM-7:30 PM. Other community legal site sessions vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free immigration legal clinic help for questions about citizenship, immigration status, deportation, visas, and general legal issues. Clinics provide advice and referrals; they are not the same as hiring a lawyer for ongoing representation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people seeking free legal clinic help with immigration issues. Utah Courts lists the Salt Lake County PBI immigration site as walk-in only, and statewide community legal site options may be by appointment or walk-in depending on date and location.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents and Utah residents needing free immigration legal clinic advice.

**How to Best Connect**
For the Salt Lake County PBI Immigration Legal Site, go to the SLCC Dream Center, West Valley Center Room 130, 3460 S 5600 W, on the fourth Wednesday from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM. For questions, email probono@law.utah.edu or call 801-581-5418.

**Important Information to Know**
Clinic routes can change. Use the Utah Courts legal clinics page or contact Pro Bono Initiative to confirm dates before attending. This is brief advice and referral help, not guaranteed ongoing representation.
resources.name: University of Utah Pro Bono Initiative Immigration Legal Site

resources.address: 383 South University Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: University of Utah S.J. Quinney College of Law Pro Bono Initiative Rainbow Law Legal Site offers free brief legal advice for LGBTQIA+ legal issues, including employment, name and gender marker changes, estate planning, and family law.
resources.hours: Clinic schedule and location vary; check the Pro Bono Initiative calendar before attending. Online appointments are limited and requested by email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free 30-minute brief legal advice through the Rainbow Law Legal Site for LGBTQIA+ legal issues, including employment, name and gender marker changes, estate planning, and family law. Volunteers provide advice and referrals but not court representation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Utah community members seeking brief advice on LGBTQIA+ legal issues. PBI does not provide direct representation, cannot appear in court, and cannot file paperwork for clients.

**Population Served**
LGBTQIA+ people and others with LGBTQIA+ legal issues in Utah, including Salt Lake County clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the PBI calendar for current Rainbow Law sessions and locations. For service questions, email probono@law.utah.edu or call 801-581-5418; phones are not monitored live and messages are returned in 2-3 business days. Online appointments are very limited and requested by email.

**Important Information to Know**
In-person clinics are walk-in only and not guaranteed. PBI consultations are brief advice sessions; people needing full representation or urgent filing help should also contact a legal-aid provider or attorney.
resources.name: University of Utah Pro Bono Initiative Rainbow Law Legal Site

resources.address: 383 South University Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: University of Utah S.J. Quinney College of Law Pro Bono Initiative Street Law Legal Site offers free brief legal advice on housing, employment, debt, bankruptcy, collections, credit, and small claims issues.
resources.hours: Clinic schedule and location vary; check the Pro Bono Initiative calendar before attending. Online appointments are limited and requested by email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free 30-minute brief legal advice through the Street Law Legal Site for housing issues, landlord/tenant disputes, eviction, employment discrimination or termination, harassment, debt, bankruptcy, collections, credit issues, and small claims.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Utah community members seeking brief advice on Street Law topics. PBI does not provide direct representation, cannot appear in court, and cannot file paperwork for clients.

**Population Served**
Utah residents, including Salt Lake County clients, with housing, employment, debt, or small-claims legal questions.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the PBI calendar for current Street Law sessions and locations. For service questions, email probono@law.utah.edu or call 801-581-5418; phones are not monitored live and messages are returned in 2-3 business days. Online appointments are very limited and requested by email.

**Important Information to Know**
In-person clinics are walk-in only and not guaranteed. This is brief legal advice and referrals, not ongoing representation, court appearance, or paperwork filing.
resources.name: University of Utah Pro Bono Initiative Street Law Legal Site

resources.address: Ray & Tye Noorda Oral Health Sciences Building, 530 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108; South Main Dental Clinic, 3690 S Main St, Salt Lake City, UT 84115; Greenwood Health Center, 7495 S State St, Midvale, UT 84047; additional Salt Lake City dental locations listed by U of U Health
resources.description: University of Utah School of Dentistry and University of Utah Health dental clinics provide comprehensive dental care from faculty, residents, and supervised student dentists, with reduced self-pay prices for student and resident care.
resources.hours: Hours vary by dental location; call for scheduling and site-specific availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Dental exams, cleanings, x-rays, fluoride, sealants, fillings, crowns, bridges, dentures, root canals, emergency dental services, extractions, oral surgery, dental implants, orthodontics/braces, pediatric dentistry, geriatric dentistry, and dental care for patients with special needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to patients of all ages. U of U Health accepts many insurance plans and Medicaid at all dental locations. People without dental insurance or paying out of pocket can request care from dental residents or supervised student dentists at reduced prices.

**Population Served**
Children, adults, older adults, uninsured or self-pay dental patients, Medicaid dental patients, and patients with special needs who can reach University of Utah Health dental sites in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-587-6453 or 801-58-SMILE. Ask which site and provider type fits the needed procedure, cost, insurance, and appointment timeline.

**Important Information to Know**
Faculty dentists charge full market rates. Residents are listed at 25-30% off most self-pay services, and student dentists are listed at 30-50% off most self-pay services. Oral Health Assistance Program financial assistance may be available but is not guaranteed.
resources.name: University of Utah School of Dentistry / University of Utah Health Student Dental Clinics

resources.address: 49 Center St, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: University of Utah student-run pro bono physical therapy clinics provide free PT for underserved and underinsured people in the Greater Salt Lake area who meet income guidelines.
resources.hours: Clinic times vary by site; call and leave a message for scheduling, cancellations, and current availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free physical therapy evaluation and treatment for movement, pain, balance, spine, joint, and neurologic functional impairments. Student physical therapists provide care under licensed physical therapist supervision at Midvale CBC Clinic, Maliheh Free Clinic, and a neuro pro bono clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for underserved and underinsured individuals in the Greater Salt Lake area who are at or below 150% of the federal poverty line.

**Population Served**
Greater Salt Lake area residents with physical impairments or injuries affecting work, recreation, or activities of daily living, including people with joint or spine pain, arthritis, weakness, movement or balance problems, stroke, multiple sclerosis, cerebral palsy, traumatic brain injury, Parkinson's disease, and related functional deficits.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 385-887-9002 and leave a message for scheduling, more information, or cancellations. The listed contact address is 49 Center St, Midvale, UT 84047.

**Important Information to Know**
This is physical therapy, not medical diagnosis or treatment of the underlying medical condition. Spanish interpreters are available at Midvale CBC and Maliheh Free Clinic when needed; other interpreters may be requested.
resources.name: University of Utah Student-Run Pro Bono Physical Therapy Clinics

resources.address: 200 S. Central Campus Drive, Union Building Room 418, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: The University of Utah Veterans Support Center serves military-connected students with education-benefit certification support, advocacy, mentoring, career guidance, campus connection, and VetSuccess/VR&E access.
resources.hours: Summer hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; VetSuccess/VocRehab Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Campus support for military-connected students, including advocacy, mentoring, career guidance, VA education-benefit request/certification support, military education benefits questions, VetSuccess/VocRehab on-campus counseling, and connection to campus veteran resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Primarily for University of Utah veterans, service members, spouses, dependents, and other military-connected students or prospective students.

**Population Served**
University of Utah military-connected students and prospective students.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit Union Building Room 418, call 801-587-7722, or email vetcenter@sa.utah.edu. For VA education-benefit certification questions, call 801-581-6945 or email MilEdBenefits@utah.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a university campus resource, not a countywide VA benefits office. People not connected to the University of Utah should use VA, UDVMA, DWS, or their own campus veteran office.
resources.name: University of Utah Veterans Support Center

resources.description: University of the People is an accredited, fully online nonprofit university offering tuition-free associate, bachelor's, master's, and certificate programs, with application and assessment fees rather than traditional tuition.
resources.hours: Online asynchronous programs; application deadlines and term calendars are posted by UoPeople.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online degree and certificate programs, including associate and bachelor's programs in business administration, computer science, and health science, bachelor's in general studies, selected master's programs, and certificate programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to qualified applicants who meet UoPeople admissions rules for the chosen program. Undergraduate admissions, graduate admissions, transfer, and English proficiency requirements vary by program.

**Population Served**
Students able to study online, including Salt Lake County residents who need flexible postsecondary education and can meet application and program requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the UoPeople application portal or request information through the UoPeople website. No public phone number was identified on the opened homepage.

**Important Information to Know**
UoPeople says it does not charge tuition for online college courses, course materials, or annual enrollment, but students pay a $60 application fee and per-course assessment fees. The site compares a full bachelor's degree cost at about $7,260. Students should confirm accreditation, licensing value, transferability, and field requirements before enrolling.
resources.name: University of the People Online Degree and Certificate Programs

resources.description: Unsheltered Utah is a grassroots Salt Lake City/Salt Lake County outreach organization that provides hot meals, supplies, cold-weather support, Code Blue Movie Nights, mobile case management, and coordination with partner providers for people living unsheltered.
resources.hours: No fixed public intake schedule was posted; contact the organization or use current Code Blue/shelter announcements for winter shelter nights.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Street outreach and unsheltered support, including hot meals, survival supplies, hygiene items, clothing and winter items when available, Code Blue Movie Nights, mobile case management, and coordination with existing social-service providers and partner churches for emergency winter shelter.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program focuses on people living unsheltered, often on the streets or outside public shelter. Public intake requirements and schedules were not clearly posted.

**Population Served**
Unsheltered people in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County; official materials also mention outreach to encampments in Ogden.

**How to Best Connect**
Use info@unshelteredutah.org or admin@unshelteredutah.org for contact. A community guide phone number, 408-464-1351, was submitted but was not confirmed on the official site; verify before relying on it.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a fixed daily drop-in center. Winter shelter availability depends on Code Blue conditions, partner sites, and current operations; use the Homeless Services Line or current shelter announcements for immediate overnight shelter decisions.
resources.name: Unsheltered Utah Outreach, Supplies, and Winter Shelter Support

resources.address: 120 West 1300 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84115; Murray Clinic 5450 South Green Street, Murray, UT 84123
resources.description: Urban Indian Center of Salt Lake provides state-licensed, culturally integrated behavioral-health services for urban Native relatives, including mental-health counseling, crisis and youth support, substance-use recovery, domestic-violence advocacy, and case management.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; closed for lunch 12:00 PM-1:00 PM; closed weekends and major tribal/federal holidays. Walk-in behavioral-health screenings listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-11:30 AM and 1:00 PM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

State-licensed, culturally integrated behavioral-health care, including individual counseling, family counseling, group counseling, crisis and Native youth support, suicide-prevention treatment, substance-use evaluation and recovery, domestic-violence survivor support, case management, Medicaid/CHIP enrollment help, and transportation support tied to care. Substance-use work includes court-approved assessments and aftercare/relapse prevention. Domestic-violence support includes survivor counseling, safety planning, crisis advocacy and shelter/protective-system navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The program is designed for urban Native relatives. If court, probation/parole, or DCFS involved, clients are asked to bring court orders, probation/parole agreements, and agent or case-manager contact information. Call or complete new patient intake to confirm fit and documentation.

**Population Served**

Urban Native and American Indian/Alaska Native community members in the Greater Salt Lake and Wasatch Front service area, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 801-486-4877 or complete the secure new patient packet online. Behavioral-health walk-in screenings are listed Monday-Friday from 9:00 AM-11:30 AM and 1:00 PM-4:30 PM. Community Center address is 120 W 1300 S, Salt Lake City; Murray Clinic is 5450 South Green Street, Murray.

**Important Information to Know**

Confirm service site, payer rules, patient eligibility and current assessment/treatment availability. This is not a 24/7 domestic-violence shelter or crisis line. For immediate crisis the center directs people to 988, NATIVE by text to 741741, or 911 for life-threatening emergencies.
resources.name: Urban Indian Center of Salt Lake Behavioral Health Services

resources.address: 120 W 1300 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84115; Murray Clinic 5450 S Green Street, Murray, UT 84123; administrative office 3489 W 2100 S Ste 100, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: Urban Indian Center of Salt Lake provides culturally integrated case management and life-resource support for urban Native community members, including help navigating local housing options, emergency shelter connections, stability programs, transportation support, Medicaid/CHIP enrollment, behavioral health, and primary care access.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; closed for lunch 12:00 PM-1:00 PM; closed weekends and major tribal/federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Culturally integrated community case management and life-resource support, including housing assistance navigation, emergency shelter connections, stability programs, low-income transportation support, Medicaid and CHIP enrollment help, behavioral health, substance-use recovery services, domestic violence advocacy, and primary care connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The new client registration page says applicants for programs and services must bring Certificate of Indian Blood or Tribal ID, Social Security card, photo ID, proof of residency, and income verification if applicable. Call if documents are missing or if help is needed before registering.

**Population Served**
Urban American Indian and Alaska Native community members in the Greater Salt Lake and Wasatch Front area, including renters, chronically homeless individuals, and LGBTQIA/Two Spirit community members.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-486-4877, email info@uicsl.org, send the online contact form, or complete the online new client registration packet. Regular office hours are Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM with lunch closure 12:00 PM-1:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
The contact page says there is no public restroom, public phone, solicitation, or loitering. This is not a 24/7 crisis or shelter site; immediate crisis needs should use 988 or 911 as appropriate.
resources.name: Urban Indian Center of Salt Lake Community Case Management and Housing Navigation

resources.address: Murray Clinic, 5450 S Green St, Murray, UT 84123
resources.description: Urban Indian Center of Salt Lake's Murray Clinic offers culturally grounded primary care, pediatrics, women's health, geriatrics, diabetes care, imaging, teleretinal screening, lab testing, pharmacy, psychiatry, and telehealth.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; closed for lunch 12:00 PM-1:00 PM; closed weekends and major tribal/federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care and general family medicine, pediatrics, women's health, geriatric care, diabetes management and education, diagnostic imaging, teleretinal screenings, lab testing, onsite pharmacy, psychiatric care, telehealth appointments, Medicaid assistance, and eyeglass voucher support described in clinic materials.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The center describes its mission as serving the American Indian and Alaska Native community in Salt Lake City and surrounding areas and centers urban Indigenous relatives. People should call before referral to confirm eligibility, fees, and whether services are available to non-Native community members.

**Population Served**
Urban Indigenous and American Indian/Alaska Native community members in Salt Lake County and surrounding areas, with clinic care available at the Murray location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-486-4877 or complete the online new patient packet. The Murray Clinic is at 5450 S Green St, Murray, UT 84123.

**Important Information to Know**
Official pages focus on culturally safe care for urban Native relatives. Medical emergencies should use 911 and psychiatric crisis should use 988. Eligibility and costs should be confirmed before presenting it as open to all clients.
resources.name: Urban Indian Center of Salt Lake Primary Care Clinic

resources.description: Utah Adult Protective Services is the official statewide reporting route for suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults, with weekday phone reporting and 24/7 online reporting.
resources.hours: Phone reporting Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; online reporting available 24/7. Call 911 for emergencies.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Receives reports of suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults. APS reporting can cover physical or sexual abuse, emotional or verbal abuse, caretaker neglect, self-neglect, and financial exploitation concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Reports are for suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation involving a vulnerable adult in Utah. Utah law requires people who have reason to believe a vulnerable adult is being abused, neglected, or exploited to notify APS or law enforcement. Call 911 if there is an emergency.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable adults in Utah, including older adults in Salt Lake County who may be experiencing abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation.

**How to Best Connect**
Report by telephone Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM at 1-800-371-7897, or report online 24/7 through the APS online reporting form linked on the Utah DHHS page. Call 911 for immediate emergencies.

**Important Information to Know**
APS is a protective reporting and investigation route, not guaranteed emergency response, financial assistance, or replacement for 911. APS generally investigates and connects to protective supports; emergency danger should go to 911.
resources.name: Utah Adult Protective Services

resources.address: 450 South State Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: The Utah Appellate Courts' Pro Bono Program helps self-represented parties with cases in the Utah Court of Appeals or Utah Supreme Court seek volunteer attorney assistance when they qualify and counsel is available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Specialized appellate pro bono program for self-represented parties with cases in the Utah Court of Appeals or Utah Supreme Court. Interested parties can contact the Deputy Clerk for qualification information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For self-represented parties with Utah appellate cases. Qualification is required, and there is no guarantee the program can provide a volunteer attorney for every eligible person.

**Population Served**
Self-represented people in Utah Court of Appeals or Utah Supreme Court cases, including Salt Lake County residents with appellate matters.

**How to Best Connect**
Email Deputy Clerk Hannah Hunter at hannahh@utcourts.gov for information on qualifying for the program. The appellate courts are at 450 South State Street, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general trial-court help desk and not guaranteed representation. Appeal deadlines are strict; clients should act quickly and preserve filing deadlines while seeking help.
resources.name: Utah Appellate Courts and Utah State Bar Pro Bono Commission Appellate Courts' Pro Bono Program

resources.address: 346 S Rio Grande St, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Utah Division of Archives and Records Service provides reference help and access to older public Utah government records, including historic vital, court, naturalization, name-change, probate, and other records.
resources.hours: In-person research is by appointment; remote reference is available by phone or email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Research access and reference help for older public Utah government records that may support identity recovery, including historic birth, death, marriage, divorce, naturalization, name-change, probate, and court records.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best for older public records held by Utah Archives. Recent non-public certificates or court records may need to be requested from Utah Vital Records, county clerks, or the court that handled the case.

**Population Served**
People needing older Utah public records or help locating the correct Utah record series, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-531-3847, use the Utah Archives research guides, or schedule an appointment for the Reference Room at 346 S Rio Grande St, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Archives is not the usual route for recent certified birth certificates, current divorce decrees, or non-public records. It is most useful when the person needs older records or help identifying where a Utah record is held.
resources.name: Utah Archives Reference Room and Historic Government Records

resources.address: Judy Ann Buffmire Building, 1595 W 500 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; main office 6855 Old Main Hill, Logan, UT 84322
resources.description: Utah Assistive Technology Program helps Utahns with disabilities access assistive technology through demonstrations, short-term loans, refurbished equipment, customizations, financing, small grants, and device resources.
resources.hours: Salt Lake City lab hours from prior official record: Tuesday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, Wednesday by appointment, Thursday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; call to confirm before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assistive technology lending library, device demonstrations, refurbished assistive technology resources, equipment available for demonstration/loan through AT4All, device customizations, assistive-technology financing, small grants, and small business loans. Devices may include mobility, vision, hearing/communication, daily-living, education, employment, and community-independence tools.

**Eligibility Requirements**
UATP accepts consumers within Utah and serves individuals with disabilities of all ages. Financing, grants, refurbished devices, and loans each have their own rules, availability, and approval process.

**Population Served**
Utahns with disabilities of all ages, including Salt Lake County residents, plus families and service providers who need assistive technology devices or services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-524-5152 for the statewide program. The Salt Lake City location is in the Judy Ann Buffmire Building at 1595 W 500 S. For the Salt Lake City lab, prior official record lists 801-887-9390 and robert.remund@usu.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
Inventory, loan availability, customization capacity, grant funding, and financing approval vary. Loans and financing are not guaranteed, and some options may involve cost or repayment.
resources.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program / Utah Assistive Technology Foundation

resources.address: 6835 Old Main Hill, Logan, UT 84322-6835
resources.description: Utah Assistive Technology Program and Utah Assistive Technology Foundation offer statewide assistive-technology financing, including reduced-interest loans and small grants that can help Utahns with disabilities obtain needed communication, computer, or other assistive devices.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
UATP and UATF offer assistive-technology loans, small grants, small business loans, information and assistance, reuse, customization, and lending library services. For this category, the relevant help is financing or grants for assistive technology such as communication devices, adaptive computer access, tablets used primarily for communication, or other disability-related technology.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Financing is for Utahns with disabilities. Small grants are for Utahns with disabilities who have low income at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines and no other funding source; grants must be approved before purchase or work begins. Loans depend on the financing program and review process.

**Population Served**
Utahns with disabilities of all ages who need assistive technology to be more independent at home, school, work, or in the community.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-524-5152 for information and assistance. For small grants, submit the application online, by email to tiffany.penrose@usu.edu, or by mail to Tiffany Penrose, 6835 Old Main Hill, Logan, UT 84322-6835. Alternative formats are available on request.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not general phone, internet, or computer bill assistance. Grants are limited, case-by-case, not retroactive, and may require documentation about the device and other funding attempts. Some fees may apply for reuse services.
resources.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program / Utah Assistive Technology Foundation Financing and Small Grants

resources.address: 6855 Old Main Hill, Logan, UT 84322
resources.description: Utah Assistive Technology Program financing options, in partnership with Utah Assistive Technology Foundation, provide assistive-technology loans, small grants, and small business loans to Utahns with disabilities.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assistive-technology loans, small grants, and small business loans to help purchase equipment that supports independence at home, school, work, and in the community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves Utahns with disabilities. Specific loan or grant eligibility, credit review, income limits, grant caps, and available funds depend on the financing option.

**Population Served**
Utah residents with disabilities of all ages who need assistive technology.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-524-5152 or use the financing links on the UATP website for loans, small grants, and small business loans. Services are statewide even though the listed program contact is in Logan.

**Important Information to Know**
Loans are not free assistance and may not be appropriate for clients who cannot safely take on debt. Small-grant availability and limits should be checked before relying on this as a payment source.
resources.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program Assistive Technology Financing

resources.address: 350 N State Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Utah Attorney General ID Theft Central is a lead for Utah identity-theft reporting and recovery instructions, but the current Utah reporting workflow needs confirmation because newer guidance may route victims to FTC IdentityTheft.gov.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The lead describes Utah ID Theft Central as a free web-based identity-theft reporting service that may provide an incident report, affidavit, law-enforcement case number, and customized recovery instructions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intended for Utah residents reporting identity theft or misuse of personal information. Current state workflow, whether idtheft.utah.gov remains active, and whether users are routed to the FTC system are unresolved.

**Population Served**
Utah residents, including Salt Lake County clients, dealing with identity theft or misuse of identity documents or personal information.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Utah Attorney General identity-theft information page and confirm the current reporting route before referral. The lead lists 801-366-0260 for the Utah Attorney General's Office.

**Important Information to Know**
This does not replace a stolen driver license, passport, Social Security card, or vital record by itself. The unresolved issue is whether the Utah ID Theft Central reporting workflow remains active or whether the practical front door is now FTC IdentityTheft.gov.
resources.name: Utah Attorney General ID Theft Central Lead
resources.resolutionReason: Retain as needs-resolution with correction flag. Before content freeze, decide whether to keep a Utah AG needs-resolution lead or restore/rename the direct FTC IdentityTheft.gov front door from candidate 1079 evidence.; The current state reporting workflow is consequential and unresolved; if active, it would pass reach and direct online access for Utah residents.

resources.address: 350 N State Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Utah@EASE connects qualifying Utah service members, veterans, retirees, Guard members, and Reserve members with volunteer attorneys for covered Utah civil legal matters.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal referral and possible volunteer attorney guidance or representation for covered Utah civil legal matters, including SCRA, USERRA, tenant issues, debt, consumer fraud, predatory lending, immigration, and wills.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Utah active-duty servicemembers, veterans and retirees with Honorable or General discharges, and Guard or Reserve members who are currently serving or separated. Covered matters are limited and generally exclude matters where the opposing party is a federal, state, county, or city entity.

**Population Served**
Eligible military service members, veterans, retirees, National Guard members, and Reserve members with covered Utah civil legal issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Utah@EASE page for the current contact route or call the Utah Attorney General's Office at 801-366-0260. Requests are screened for referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Criminal, family law, personal injury, VA claims, and legal matters against a public entity are not covered according to prior supported evidence. Matching with a volunteer attorney is not guaranteed until eligibility and case fit are reviewed.
resources.name: Utah Attorney General's Office Utah@EASE

resources.address: 4315 S 2700 W, Taylorsville, UT 84129
resources.description: Utah Department of Public Safety Bureau of Criminal Identification is the official statewide source for petition-based expungement certificates of eligibility, expungement application forms, and application status lookup.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official expungement certificate-of-eligibility process for petition-based Utah criminal-record expungement, application forms, eligibility information, status lookup, and Expungement Section assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the person's full criminal history, waiting periods, pending cases, probation/parole/incarceration status, protective orders, fines, restitution, offense limits, and other statutory criteria. Traffic and cannabis expungements may go directly through the court and may not require a BCI certificate.

**Population Served**
People with Utah criminal records who need to determine eligibility for petition-based expungement or check an expungement application status.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the BCI expungements page for forms and status tools. For expungement questions, contact the Expungement Section at 801-281-5198 or bciexpungements@utah.gov. The BCI office is at 4315 S 2700 W, Taylorsville.

**Important Information to Know**
BCI is not legal representation. Fees may apply, processing can take months, and a certificate is only one step; many cases still require filing papers with the correct court within the certificate deadline.
resources.name: Utah BCI Expungement Certificate of Eligibility

resources.address: 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-2001
resources.description: Utah Breast & Cervical Cancer Screening Program helps eligible low-income, uninsured, and underinsured Utah women access breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnostic services, treatment linkage, and patient navigation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Breast and cervical cancer screenings, diagnostic services, patient navigation, education, and connection to treatment resources through local health departments, federally qualified health centers, and community clinics.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves Utah women ages 21-64 who are low income and uninsured or underinsured. Call the program to determine whether a person qualifies for a free screening or appointment.

**Population Served**
Low-income, uninsured, or underinsured Utah women ages 21-64, including Salt Lake County residents, who need breast or cervical cancer screening or diagnostic follow-up.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-717-1811 to see if you qualify or to schedule an appointment. The program office address is 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-2001.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is focused on screening, diagnostic services, navigation, and linkage. Treatment coverage depends on program rules, Medicaid or other treatment pathways, and clinical findings.
resources.name: Utah Breast & Cervical Cancer Screening Program

resources.address: 302 W 5400 S Ste 100, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Utah CNA Training Centers provides UNAR-approved hybrid CNA training with online coursework, in-person labs and clinicals, state-exam preparation, and direct online enrollment at Murray and other Utah training locations.
resources.hours: Schedules depend on online coursework, lab, and clinical availability; call or enroll online for current schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
State-approved CNA training with hybrid online coursework, hands-on labs, clinical training, and Utah CNA certification exam preparation. The program includes 100 total hours: 49 online, 27 lab, and 24 clinical hours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students enroll online, complete registration/onboarding, and pay tuition. Program details include completion within 60 days. Clinical and certification requirements may include additional documentation, supplies, testing, and health/background requirements; confirm before enrolling.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County and Utah residents seeking Certified Nursing Assistant training for entry-level health care employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Enroll Now link on the Utah CNA Training Centers website or call 801-990-9333. The Murray location is the administrative office, classroom, and skills lab; clinical training may occur at approved health care facilities rather than the selected training location.

**Important Information to Know**
Published tuition is $575. Required supplies and state-testing fees are separate. Financial help may be available through workforce development, adult education, employers, or community partners, but the program is not universally free.
resources.name: Utah CNA Training Centers CNA Training Program

resources.description: Utah Career Center offers paid earn-while-you-learn apprenticeship pathways in Plumbing/Pipefitting/Welding and HVAC&R, combining classroom instruction with full-time on-the-job training through its Utah Mechanical Contractors Association and UA Local 140 partnership.
resources.hours: Application steps are online; class and on-the-job schedules vary. Daytime courses are listed as Monday-Friday approximately 8:00 AM-5:00 PM during course periods.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Five-year apprenticeship programs in Plumbing, Pipefitting and Welding (PPW) and HVAC&R. Apprentices earn while they learn through classroom instruction and full-time on-the-job training under experienced journeymen.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be at least 18, have a high school diploma or GED, upload required documents including proof of age, submit a complete online application, and pass a 10-panel drug test through Concentra. Additional assessment, orientation, and interview steps follow.

**Population Served**
People in Utah, including Salt Lake County residents, seeking paid trade apprenticeship training in plumbing, pipefitting, welding, or HVAC&R.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online application link on the Utah Career Center FAQ/apply page. For application status or reactivation questions, contact Kyra Hester at kyra@ucctrades.com or call 801-295-6198.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not immediate day labor. Applicants should be ready for drug testing, documentation, interviews, training schedules, possible fees, and employer/union requirements. Confirm current openings and classroom/worksite expectations before applying.
resources.name: Utah Career Center Plumbing, Pipefitting, Welding and HVAC&R Apprenticeships

resources.description: Utah Case Management provides Housing Related Services and Supports case management for eligible Targeted Adult Medicaid members, including weekly case manager visits, personal development planning, housing stabilization supports, coordination with health providers, and possible help with housing-related financial barriers such as deposits, utilities, moving expenses, furnishings, and licenses.
resources.hours: Online enrollment/contact; allow up to 10 business days after enrollment before following up if not contacted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing Related Services and Supports case management, including weekly case manager visits, personal development planning, educational classes, coordination with mental health, substance use, peer support, crisis intervention, transportation, medical and dental providers, community transition services, housing stabilization, and possible funds for security deposits, essential furnishings, utility setup or deposits, moving expenses, work licensure, DMV licensure, and related barriers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
