Vets4Warriors offers confidential peer support by phone, chat, email form, and request-a-call form. Peers listen, provide support, and help callers work through challenges or connect with resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The line serves the U.S. military community, including active duty, Guard, Reserve, veterans, loved ones, family members, and caregivers. It is not a substitute for emergency medical or crisis response.

**Population Served**
Military service members, veterans, military families, loved ones, and caregivers nationwide, including people in Salt Lake County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 855-838-8255 any time. People may also use chat, send a private message through the website, or request a call back.

**Important Information to Know**
The service is available 24/7/365 and is peer support rather than therapy, medical treatment, or emergency response. In an immediate emergency, use 911 or a crisis service.
resources.name: Vets4Warriors 24/7 Military Peer Support Line

resources.address: 1990 W North Temple, Salt Lake City, UT
resources.description: Ville 1990 is identified in current government materials as an emergency shelter site on North Temple with about 200 people staying there during a transition toward deeply affordable housing units; clients should use the homeless-services shelter line to confirm placement and current access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter beds at the Ville 1990 site while the former hotel transitions toward deeply affordable housing. Government materials describe the site as sheltering approximately 200 individuals, with a planned conversion to 105 deeply affordable housing units.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people experiencing homelessness who are directed through the Salt Lake County homeless-services system. Current placement rules, walk-up availability, documentation, and whether the site is accepting new guests must be confirmed through the shelter access line.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County who may be placed through the emergency shelter system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999 before going to the site. Do not assume walk-up access or availability at 1990 W North Temple without current confirmation.

**Important Information to Know**
Official materials describe Ville 1990 as operating while in a housing-transition period, and funding/transition details have changed over time. Confirm current operating status, bed access, safety rules, and whether clients are being directed there before referral.
resources.name: Ville 1990 Emergency Shelter / Housing Transition

resources.address: 1589 W Broadway, Ste 200-324, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Vista Care Utah provides home- and community-based disability supports, including day, residential, supported apartment, supported employment, supportive home care, shared living/host home, and related DSPD-contracted services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vista Care Utah lists day services, residential services, supported apartment program, supported employment, supportive home care, shared living/host homes, representative payee, technology supports, and other supportive services. Utah DHHS 211 lists DSPD-contracted services such as companion services, host home support, personal assistance, respite, and supported living.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Vista Care's Utah page directs people to contact Utah leadership for eligibility requirements. Utah DHHS 211 lists Vista Care as a DSPD contract provider, so many services may require DSPD, waiver, or other funding authorization.

**Population Served**
People in Utah with disabilities who need supported living, residential, day, employment, host home, personal assistance, respite, or related home- and community-based supports.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the contact form on Vista Care's Utah page or call the Utah listing at 720-688-1387. The Utah DHHS 211 provider record lists the application/referral process as call.

**Important Information to Know**
This appears to be a provider of funded disability services, not the state front door for DSPD eligibility. Missionaries should ask about funding status and whether the person already has DSPD/waiver authorization or private-pay options before treating Vista Care as an available placement.
resources.name: Vista Care Utah Disability Support Services

resources.address: 697 W 4170 S, Murray, UT 84123
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah operates the Center for Women and Children as a 24/7 social-model detox program for adult women in Salt Lake County, with case management, recovery groups, peer support, MAT access, and linkage to longer-term treatment; parenting women may be able to bring young children.
resources.hours: 24/7 detox program per assigned Salt Lake County evidence; call first to confirm capacity and fit.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Social-model, non-medical detoxification for women, with meals, case management, recovery groups, peer support, access to medication-assisted treatment, and help linking to assessment, referral, and longer-term substance-use treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adult women in Salt Lake County who meet detox criteria. Parenting women may be able to admit with children age 10 and under. Clients with medically complex withdrawal needs should be screened carefully because this is non-medical detox.

**Population Served**
Adult women in Salt Lake County who need withdrawal support; parenting women with young children may be served when program criteria and capacity allow.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-261-9177 before arrival. The listed location is 697 W 4170 S, Murray, UT 84123.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a 24/7 social-model detox program, not hospital-level medical detox. Cost is described as sliding-scale, and staff may help uninsured clients apply for Medicaid; verify current bed availability, fees, and medical appropriateness before referral.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Center for Women and Children Detoxification Program

resources.address: 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah Cornerstone Counseling is a Salt Lake County community behavioral-health clinic for adults age 18 and older with mental-health concerns such as depression, trauma, and anxiety, offering outpatient counseling with a direct phone/email route and walk-in new-client intake hours.
resources.hours: Program page lists Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-5:30 PM and Friday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; new-client walk-in intake Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM. Another VOA treatment-services page lists slightly later closing times, so call before arriving late in the day.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient behavioral-health counseling for adults with mental-health concerns such as depression, trauma, anxiety, and related needs. VOA states Cornerstone specializes in addiction, mental health, trauma, and intimate partner violence treatment, with individual, group, and family counseling and community-resource connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adult Salt Lake County residents age 18 and older who are struggling with mental-health concerns can access treatment. Sliding-fee availability is based on Salt Lake County residence, family size, and income; clients should confirm payer fit and any documentation needed at intake.

**Population Served**
Adults age 18 and older in Salt Lake County needing outpatient community mental-health care, especially people who face cost or access barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-355-2846 or email admissions@voaut.org to access mental-health services. New-client intake is listed as walk-in Monday through Thursday from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM at 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City. Intake forms are available online but are not required before the first appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Cornerstone is outpatient counseling, not a 24/7 crisis center. VOA pages list slightly different regular closing times; call first if planning to go near closing. Cornerstone offers a sliding fee schedule for Salt Lake County residents, but final cost depends on income, family size, and payer details.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Cornerstone Counseling

resources.address: Cornerstone Counseling: 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; Family Counseling Center: Murray, UT
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah provides trauma-informed domestic-violence counseling for Salt Lake County survivors, offenders, and child witnesses of intimate partner violence through Cornerstone Counseling and the Family Counseling Center.
resources.hours: Family Counseling Center: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-7:00 PM. Cornerstone Counseling: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Trauma-informed counseling addressing intimate partner violence, anger management, interpersonal communication, healing from traumatic experiences, and other domestic-violence-related issues. Services are offered through two VOA Utah counseling centers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone residing in Salt Lake County who is a survivor or offender of intimate partner violence, and child witnesses of domestic violence, are listed as eligible. Call to confirm intake, fees, insurance or Medicaid fit, safety fit, and current openings.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County residents affected by intimate partner violence, including survivors, people who have used violence, and children who witnessed domestic violence.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Family Counseling Center at 801-261-3500 or Cornerstone Counseling at 801-355-2846. Cornerstone also lists admissions@voaut.org and walk-in/location information at 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is counseling, not emergency shelter or a 24/7 crisis response. Fees were not fully established from the public page; confirm payment, Medicaid, and safety fit before referral.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Domestic Violence Counseling

resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah Family Counseling Center provides outpatient counseling for individuals and families in the Salt Lake Valley, including mental-health services, LGBTQ+ affirmative therapy, child and adolescent counseling, couples/family counseling, trauma, grief, domestic-violence-related counseling, and addiction/co-occurring support.
resources.hours: Program page lists Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-6:30 PM and Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; VOA treatment/contact sections also list Monday-Thursday until 7:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient counseling for individuals and families. Services listed by VOA include mental-health treatment, LGBTQ+ affirmative therapy, addiction and co-occurring support, couples and family counseling, domestic-violence-related counseling, grief and loss counseling, trauma counseling, services for children and adolescents, and treatment for disorders including anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, and personality disorders.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VOA welcomes people of all backgrounds needing mental-health, LGBTQ+ counseling, and addiction services. The public page does not list a strict residence or income rule; clients should call or email to confirm clinical fit, age fit, openings, payment, and insurance.

**Population Served**
Individuals, couples, children, adolescents, and families in the Salt Lake Valley who need outpatient counseling. VOA states the center has Spanish-speaking therapists and welcomes LGBTQ+ clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-261-3500 or email fccinfo@voaut.org to ask for an appointment or more information. The office is at 650 E 4500 S, Suite 300, Murray.

**Important Information to Know**
Insurance and payment options listed by VOA include Aetna, BCBS, Medicaid, Optum Medicaid, UHC, SelectHealth, Humana, Molina, and PEHP; clients should confirm current plan participation and out-of-pocket cost. VOA pages differ slightly on Thursday closing time, listing 6:30 PM in one place and 7:00 PM in another.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Family Counseling Center

resources.address: 131 E 700 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah's Geraldine E. King Women's Resource Center is a 24-hour emergency shelter and homeless resource center for women age 18 and older experiencing homelessness in and around Salt Lake City, with meals, clothing, hygiene items, laundry, showers, and companion-animal accommodation.
resources.hours: Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter and resource-center services for women experiencing homelessness. Basic needs include meals, clothing, hygiene items, laundry access, showers, and a companion-animal-friendly environment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Women age 18 or older who are experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake City may access emergency shelter at the Geraldine E. King Women's Resource Center. Bed availability and intake fit must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Women age 18 and older experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake City and the surrounding area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999 for bed availability, or inquire in person at 131 E 700 S, Salt Lake City, or at the Weigand Center at 437 W 200 S. VOA's contact page lists the Women's Resource Center phone as 801-893-6678.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a women-specific emergency shelter/resource center. Bed availability and access to supplies can change. VOA states the center is welcoming for companion animals.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Geraldine E. King Women's Resource Center
resources.phone: Homeless Connections Hotline 801-990-9999; Women's Resource Center 801-893-6678

resources.address: 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah's Homeless Outreach Team provides mobile outreach and basic-needs support for individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake County, while its City Outreach subteam focuses on unsheltered people in Salt Lake City proper and around resource centers.
resources.hours: Homeless Outreach Team: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. City Outreach Team: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM. VOA administration office: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mobile homeless outreach and basic-needs help. Available items may include food, water, hygiene supplies, clothes, shoes, sunscreen, bug spray, hand warmers, sleeping bags, and other supplies. The team also connects people experiencing homelessness to housing, legal, medical, shelter, and other crucial services. The City Outreach Team is the Salt Lake City-focused outreach subteam.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Homeless Outreach Team serves individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake County. The City Outreach Team serves people who are unsheltered in Salt Lake City proper, including around resource centers. Supplies depend on availability.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Salt Lake County, with a Salt Lake City-specific pathway for unsheltered people in the city proper.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Victoria Daul, Homeless Outreach Program Director, at 801-503-4116 or victoria.daul@voaut.org. VOA's contact page also lists 801-631-7584 for the Homeless Outreach Team. People seeking City Outreach services can use the same 801-503-4116 contact.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outreach and basic-needs support, not a guaranteed shelter bed or guaranteed inventory of supplies. Try both outreach numbers if needed because VOA publishes 801-503-4116 on the adult homeless services page and 801-631-7584 on the contact page.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Homeless Outreach Team

resources.address: 888 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah's Homeless Youth Legal Clinic provides free consultation, representation, and legal education for homeless youth under age 23 and current Youth Resource Center clients in Salt Lake City.
resources.hours: Legal case manager drop-in Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; attorney drop-in Wednesday evenings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal consultation, representation, and legal education for eligible homeless youth. The clinic helps youth with legal issues that affect independence, employment, housing, and stability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current clients of the Youth Resource Center and youth experiencing homelessness under age 23 are eligible. Attorney availability and representation depend on clinic assessment and capacity.

**Population Served**
Homeless or imminently homeless youth under age 23, including Youth Resource Center clients, in Salt Lake City.

**How to Best Connect**
Email uinise.tu'avao@voaut.org to request an appointment, or drop in to meet with a legal case manager Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. Attorney drop-in services are available Wednesday evenings. The Youth Resource Center is at 888 S 400 W, Salt Lake City; general YRC phone: 801-364-0744.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a population-specific legal clinic for youth experiencing homelessness. A drop-in meeting does not guarantee full representation in every matter.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Homeless Youth Legal Clinic

resources.address: Main Library primary desk: 210 E 400 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; also Salt Lake City Public Library branch locations
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah's Library Engagement Team provides library-based homeless outreach, basic-needs help, and case management for homeless, at-risk, chronically unsheltered, and low-income patrons at Salt Lake City Public Library locations.
resources.hours: Main Library desk: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 10:00 AM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Library-based outreach and case management. Help may include basic needs such as food, clothing, and hygiene; resource information; enrollment in benefits and housing programs; medical-care coordination; employment assistance; transportation coordination to hospitals, detoxification, and domestic-violence shelters; and coordination with community partners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VOA states that any age group visiting Salt Lake City Libraries' eight branch locations is eligible for Library Engagement Team services. Supplies and team availability depend on current staffing and inventory.

**Population Served**
Homeless, at-risk, chronically unsheltered, and low-income individuals and families who visit Salt Lake City Public Library locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit a Salt Lake City Public Library location and ask library staff about the VOA Library Engagement Team. The primary desk is on the first floor of the Main Library at 210 E 400 S, Salt Lake City. Contact Victoria Daul at 801-503-4116 or victoria.daul@voaut.org for program questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The Main Library desk is listed for Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM. This is an outreach and case-management access point, not a guaranteed clothing closet or supply room.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Library Engagement Team

resources.address: 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah operates Men's Detoxification at Recovery on Redwood as a 24/7 social-model detox option for Salt Lake County adults, with meals, case management, peer support, recovery groups, MAT access, and links to assessment and referral.
resources.hours: 24/7 detox program per assigned Salt Lake County evidence; call first to confirm capacity and fit.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Social-model, non-medical detoxification for men, with meals, case management, peer support, recovery groups, access to medication-assisted treatment, and help connecting to assessment, referral, and longer-term substance-use treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Salt Lake County adults age 18 and older who meet criteria for men's social detox and can manage activities of daily living. People with medically complex withdrawal needs may require a higher medical level of care.

**Population Served**
Adult men in Salt Lake County who need withdrawal support in a social-model detox setting.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-363-9400 before arrival. The listed location is 1875 S Redwood Road, Salt Lake City, UT 84104.

**Important Information to Know**
This is non-medical detox and uses a sliding fee scale. Verify current bed availability, fees, clinical appropriateness, and whether the client needs medically managed withdrawal care before referral.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Men's Detoxification at Recovery on Redwood

resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah PREP provides no-cost coordinated specialty care for Salt Lake County youth and young adults ages 14-26 experiencing first-episode psychosis or clinical high risk for psychosis, including referral screening, case management, medication management, therapy, family education, occupational therapy, peer support, and employment or education support.
resources.hours: Call or email for referral and screening; no public walk-in hours are listed for PREP.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Early psychosis intervention and coordinated outpatient care for up to two years. Services listed by VOA include case management, psychiatric medication management, psychotherapy, occupational therapy, peer support, family education and support, and employment or education support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth and young adults ages 14-26 who live in Salt Lake County and are experiencing a first episode of psychosis or are at clinical high risk for psychosis. The referral process asks for the client's name, date of birth, a completed PRIME screener, and mental-health history information.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County youth and young adults ages 14-26 with early psychosis symptoms or clinical high risk for psychosis, and their families or support systems when the client wants family involvement.

**How to Best Connect**
Clients, family members, friends, or medical/behavioral-health professionals can start the referral. Call 385-500-3692 or email prep@voaut.org and ask about PREP screening.

**Important Information to Know**
VOA states there is no cost to clients regardless of insurance or income and that PREP works with all insurance providers, including Medicaid, and accepts clients without insurance. This is an early psychosis specialty program, not a general crisis line or walk-in clinic.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah PREP - Prevention and Recovery from Early Psychosis

resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah's THRIVE Supported Employment Program uses the IPS model to help participants obtain and maintain competitive community jobs while receiving treatment and vocational counseling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
THRIVE helps participants find and keep meaningful competitive jobs in the community. Employment Specialists support job search, qualifications, job placement based on strengths and preferences, partnerships with local employers, continuing employment support, and vocational counseling for job difficulties, job loss, or conflict.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page says anyone wanting to work is welcome regardless of mental illness or barriers such as criminal record and substance use, as long as the person is willing to get treatment. Insurance and program admission details should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
People in Salt Lake County with mental-health, criminal-record, substance-use, or other barriers who want employment and are willing to participate in treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
Clients can ask their therapist for a referral or contact Cornerstone Counseling Center at admissions@voaut.org. Community partners can email thrive@voaut.org. For private insurance questions, call 801-355-2846 ext. 0.

**Important Information to Know**
THRIVE is connected to treatment participation and may involve insurance or VOA behavioral-health admission steps. The program does not guarantee a job or immediate opening.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah THRIVE Supported Employment Program

resources.address: 888 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah Youth Empowered Solutions to Succeed (YESS) supports Salt Lake County youth and young adults ages 16-25 who are homeless or housing insecure and/or have mental illness or substance-use needs, with mental-health therapy/support, case management, supported employment and education, peer support, and referrals.
resources.hours: DWS provider manual lists the site daily 8:30 AM-6:00 PM and consultation/enrollment contact Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transition-age youth support that includes case management, mental-health therapy and support, supported employment, supported education, peer support services, and referrals to community supports and agencies. Utah DHHS describes YESS as helping young people enter adulthood in areas such as housing, employment, education, and community living.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Serves Salt Lake County youth and young adults ages 16-25, until the 26th birthday, who are homeless or housing insecure and/or have a mental illness or substance use disorder.

**Population Served**
Salt Lake County youth and young adults ages 16-25 who are experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity and may also have mental-health or substance-use needs.

**How to Best Connect**
For consultation or enrollment, email yessreferrals@voaut.org or call 385-799-5976 ext. 171 Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. The program site is listed at 888 S 400 W, Salt Lake City; the Youth Resource Center site phone is listed as 801-364-0744 ext. 707.

**Important Information to Know**
The VOA YESS page could not be fetched in this check, but current Utah DHHS and Utah DWS materials list the program and direct enrollment route. Confirm current openings and whether the client should start through YESS enrollment or the Youth Resource Center drop-in pathway before sending someone in person.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Youth Empowered Solutions to Succeed (YESS)

resources.address: 888 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Volunteers of America, Utah's Youth Resource Center is a drop-in resource center and emergency shelter for youth ages 15-22 who are homeless or imminently at risk of homelessness, offering meals, showers, laundry, housing and employment case management, medical and dental care assistance, and on-site mental-health access.
resources.hours: Drop-in center hours 8:30 AM-7:30 PM. Daily intake hours 8:30 AM-6:00 PM. Services for enrolled clients are available 24/7; the center transitions to a 50-bed emergency shelter from 7:30 PM-8:30 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Drop-in youth resource center and emergency shelter. Services include essential basic-needs items, three hot meals a day, pantry food, showers, laundry, life-skills groups, housing and employment case management, dental and medical care assistance, on-site mental-health access, and a legal clinic for youth using the center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth must be homeless or imminently at risk of homelessness and age 15-22 to use the program and its resources.

**Population Served**
Youth ages 15-22 in Salt Lake City and the surrounding area who are experiencing homelessness or imminent risk of homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Arrive during drop-in center hours, 8:30 AM-7:30 PM, at 888 S 400 W, Salt Lake City. Daily intake hours are 8:30 AM-6:00 PM. For more information, call 801-364-0744 ext. 707; VOA's contact page also lists the Youth Resource Center main phone as 801-364-0744.

**Important Information to Know**
From 7:30 PM to 8:30 AM, the center operates as a 50-bed emergency shelter. Services for enrolled clients are listed as 24/7, but new intake is restricted to the listed intake hours. Confirm bed availability, minor consent questions, and specific supplies directly.
resources.name: Volunteers of America, Utah Youth Resource Center

resources.description: WAYtoGO Transportation provides private non-emergency transportation for ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher trips to medical and care-related appointments in Salt Lake, Wasatch, and Utah counties.
resources.hours: Service hours are published by the provider but should be confirmed when scheduling; exact current hours were not confirmed in this preparation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Non-emergency transportation for ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher riders, including trips to doctor, dental, clinic, physical therapy, stroke rehabilitation, hospital discharge, rehabilitation, skilled nursing, outpatient, and long-distance appointments.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No public low-income eligibility or universal free-service rule was confirmed. Riders should expect private-pay rates unless insurance, facility payment, or another payer is confirmed directly with the provider.

**Population Served**
People needing non-emergency medical or care-related transportation in the provider's stated service area of Salt Lake, Wasatch, and Utah counties, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-500-0359 to ask about availability, vehicle type, pickup and drop-off addresses, wait time, mobility equipment, total price, and payment method before scheduling.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency ambulance service and is not listed as a free program. A targeted fetch of the provider website timed out during preparation, so current rates, service hours, and Salt Lake County availability should be confirmed by phone before a client depends on the ride.
resources.name: WAYtoGO Transportation Ambulatory, Wheelchair, and Stretcher Transportation

resources.address: Woods Cross, UT
resources.description: Western Electrical Contractors Association offers a Utah Commercial Electrical Registered Apprenticeship at its Salt Lake City region training facility in Woods Cross, with paid on-the-job training and tuition paid by employing WECA member contractors.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A four-year Commercial Electrical Registered Apprenticeship for inside wireman work, combining paid on-the-job training with accelerated classroom and hands-on lab sessions at the Woods Cross training facility.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be at least 18, have a high school diploma or GED, and pass required entrance steps including color identification, basic skills testing, multi-craft aptitude testing, and oral interview. Apprentices may have to travel to job sites.

**Population Served**
People in the Salt Lake City region seeking commercial electrical apprenticeship training and employment through WECA member contractors.

**How to Best Connect**
Use WECA's Apply for Apprenticeship Online link from the Utah apprenticeship page. Review the minimum requirements and job-preview information before applying.

**Important Information to Know**
WECA states apprentice school tuition costs are paid by the WECA member contractors who employ apprentices. Applicants should confirm current Utah openings, exact training address, contractor employment requirements, and whether they can meet travel and schedule demands.
resources.name: WECA Utah Commercial Electrical Registered Apprenticeship

resources.address: 9385 S Snowbird Center Dr, Snowbird, UT 84092-9000
resources.description: Wasatch Adaptive Sports provides adaptive recreation lessons, group activities, equipment rentals, veterans programming, and scholarships for children, adults, and veterans with disabilities in Snowbird and Salt Lake Valley-area locations.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adaptive recreation instruction, group sessions, and equipment rentals in activities such as cycling, mountain biking, paddle sports, yoga, skiing, and snowboarding. Lessons are participant-centered and often include one-on-one adaptive instruction and needed equipment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs are for participants with disabilities or adaptive needs. Registration is required, and some programs have limited spots, seasonal schedules, lesson limits, waitlists, or separate scholarship rules.

**Population Served**
Children, adults, and veterans with disabilities who want adaptive sports, recreation, or active-living opportunities in the Snowbird and Salt Lake Valley area.

**How to Best Connect**
Start through the Participate page for registration, lesson inquiry, current-program questions, and seasonal sign-up links. The general phone submitted for the organization is 801-834-0476; some activity pages list program-specific contacts.

**Important Information to Know**
Costs vary by activity. Examples on the official page include $20 adaptive cycling lessons, free virtual yoga in 2026, and winter lesson pricing that may be higher. Up to 100% scholarship assistance is available for some lessons, but not all lesson types or multi-day options.
resources.name: Wasatch Adaptive Sports Adaptive Recreation, Equipment Rentals, and Scholarships

resources.address: Snowbird Resort, 9385 S. Snowbird Center Dr., Snowbird, UT 84092-9000
resources.description: Veterans-specific adaptive recreation and social activity program offering outdoor activities, adaptive instruction, equipment, and 100% scholarship support for eligible veterans.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Wasatch Adaptive Sports provides veterans programming with outdoor recreational and social activities such as skiing, snowboarding, cycling, mountain biking, and snowshoeing. Programs use adaptive equipment and instruction to support skill-building, camaraderie, self-esteem, and connection to the outdoors.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The veterans program is for veterans coping with military-related physical, cognitive, or emotional difficulties. New participants should complete the getting-started process before scheduling lessons or activities.

**Population Served**
Veterans with military-related physical, cognitive, or emotional difficulties who can participate in Snowbird and Wasatch Front-area activities.

**How to Best Connect**
New participants should start through the veterans program page's "Get Started" route. Returning participants can call 801-834-0476 or use the contact form to sign up for the next lesson. The main listed location is Snowbird Resort, 9385 S. Snowbird Center Dr., Snowbird, UT 84092-9000.

**Important Information to Know**
The veterans program page says all WAS Veterans Programs are available 100% on scholarship through donor support. Activity locations vary by season and program; some ski/snowboard locations are at Snowbird, Sundance, Alta, and other resorts by request, while cycling can occur on paved trails in Salt Lake City, Murray, American Fork, and Provo.
resources.name: Wasatch Adaptive Sports Programs for Veterans

resources.address: City Farm, 743 W 1300 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Wasatch Community Gardens' Green Team provides farm-based transitional employment, work-readiness training, job-skills workshops, job placement assistance, mentoring, and ongoing support for women facing or experiencing homelessness.
resources.hours: Program workdays are described as Tuesday-Friday for 16 weeks, with about 6.5 hours per workday; cohort timing varies.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Farm-based transitional employment, on-the-job training, weekly life and job skills workshops, job placement assistance, mentoring, action planning, partner-employer connections, and ongoing support after graduation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is intended for women facing homelessness. Participants do not have to be unemployed, but should be able to commit to a Tuesday-Friday schedule for 16 weeks on the farm. People unsure whether they qualify should contact the program team.

**Population Served**
Women in Salt Lake City facing or experiencing homelessness who are working toward stable housing and reliable employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Job Training Program Director Jackie Rodabaugh at 801-948-0431 or jackie@wasatchgardens.org. The farm is at 743 W 1300 S; make an appointment before stopping by to see the farm.

**Important Information to Know**
The program serves up to about 16 women annually. Housing is not automatically provided, though case management helps participants navigate community housing resources.
resources.name: Wasatch Community Gardens Green Team Job Training Program

resources.address: 8420 South Wasatch Boulevard, Cottonwood Heights, UT 84121
resources.description: Wasatch Recovery Treatment Center is a south Salt Lake Valley addiction treatment provider listing social detox, residential treatment, day treatment, intensive outpatient treatment, medication management, and sober living, with direct phone contact and online scheduling.
resources.hours: 24-hour phone contact was described in the assigned evidence; program schedule and intake hours should be confirmed directly.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Addiction treatment across multiple levels of care, including social detox, residential treatment, day treatment, intensive outpatient programming, medication management, and sober living. Directory-derived information also described buprenorphine/naloxone treatment and transportation assistance, but those details should be confirmed directly.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Clinical level of care, detox fit, medication services, residential admission, insurance, Medicaid participation, self-pay costs, and any foundation discount access must be confirmed during intake.

**Population Served**

People in Cottonwood Heights, Salt Lake County, and the Wasatch Front seeking substance-use treatment at outpatient, residential, or sober-living levels.

**How to Best Connect**

Use Cottonwood Heights wording for the address and preserve the online scheduling/phone route.

**Important Information to Know**

Avoid stating a precise detox medical level; official sources conflict between social detox and medically supervised detox wording.
resources.name: Wasatch Recovery Treatment Center

resources.address: Utah Community Action intake: 1307 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: West Jordan City's Utility Hardship Program provides limited bill assistance for low-income West Jordan residents with short-term need, with applications handled through Utah Community Action and payments sent directly to West Jordan City.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Utility Hardship Program helps low-income West Jordan residents with West Jordan utility bills. Assistance is paid directly to West Jordan City and priority is given to households with a disconnect notice or disconnected service.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Funds are only available to West Jordan City residents. The household must have gross income under 150% of federal poverty guidelines, have suffered a life-changing event, or have experienced a significant income reduction. Assistance is limited to $300 and once per year.

**Population Served**
West Jordan residents with West Jordan utility bills who have short-term payment assistance needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Utah Community Action at 801-359-2444 to apply. West Jordan lists Utah Community Action at 1307 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104 as the application contact.

**Important Information to Know**
This program is city-specific and does not help residents outside West Jordan or bills from other utility providers. If a household does not qualify, Utah Community Action may direct them to other Salt Lake County assistance programs.
resources.name: West Jordan City Utility Hardship Program

resources.address: 8000 S Redwood Road, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: West Jordan City Victim Assistance provides immediate crisis response, safe shelter coordination, court advocacy, emotional support, resources, and referrals for victims of domestic violence, other violent crimes, and critical incidents connected to West Jordan.
resources.hours: City Hall hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, excluding state and federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immediate crisis response, safe shelter coordination, court advocacy, emotional support, resources, and referrals for victims of domestic violence and other violent crimes or critical incidents. The division also supports victim safety and offender accountability through prosecution of domestic-violence-related crimes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for victims connected to West Jordan incidents or West Jordan criminal-justice processes. Contact the program to confirm whether it is the right advocate for the case.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors and other violent-crime victims connected to West Jordan, Utah.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-566-6511 or email wjvap@westjordan.utah.gov. The listed office is at West Jordan City Hall, 8000 S Redwood Road, with public hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Call 911 for immediate danger.

**Important Information to Know**
This is city/system-based advocacy, not a confidential community shelter program. Confidentiality and records may differ from a community domestic-violence agency.
resources.name: West Jordan City Victim Assistance

resources.address: 3636 South Constitution Boulevard, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: West Valley City Victim Services Office provides advocacy for crime victims, including domestic-violence victims, with walk-in or appointment access, mobile crisis advocates, shelter/safe-haven transportation, court support, protective-order help, and language-accessible victim information.
resources.hours: Office advocates are available Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM. After-hours advocate crisis line is listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Advocacy for victims of crime, including domestic violence. Services include education, information, resources, encouragement, immediate crisis intervention through mobile team advocates, transportation to shelters and safe havens when needed, court-process education, advocate support at hearings, assistance with no-contact orders and protective orders, and a private waiting area for victims and witnesses.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for victims connected to West Valley City incidents or West Valley City prosecution/police processes. Contact the office to confirm case fit.

**Population Served**
Crime victims in West Valley City, including domestic-violence survivors. A full-time Spanish-speaking advocate is listed, and resource information is available in several other languages.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk in or schedule an appointment by calling 801-963-3223. For after-hours crisis advocate help, call 801-231-8185. The office is in the Public Safety Building at 3636 South Constitution Boulevard.

**Important Information to Know**
This is prosecution/system-based advocacy, not a confidential shelter agency. Advocates are always available after hours by crisis line, but immediate danger should go to 911.
resources.name: West Valley City Victim Services Office

resources.address: Utah Training Center, 8149 S Welby Park Drive, West Jordan, UT 84088
resources.description: Western States Carpenters Training Fund offers carpenter and allied-trades apprenticeship access through training centers, including a Utah training center in West Jordan, with classroom instruction and on-the-job training.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Carpenter and allied-trades apprenticeship access. Applicants can apply through training centers, join the eligible applicant list, and, if selected, sign an apprenticeship agreement and apply for union local membership. Apprentices receive on-the-job training and classroom instruction.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Minimum entry requirements include being at least 18, or 17 with parent or guardian approval; for certain trades and states, having a high school diploma or GED; ability to perform the work of the trade; and transportation or a reliable way to get to job sites and apprenticeship classes. Prior job-site or tool experience is not required.

**Population Served**
People seeking carpentry or allied-trade apprenticeship training in the Western States Carpenters region, including Salt Lake County residents able to access the West Jordan training center.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an application for the craft apprenticeship program at a training center. The fund office phone is 855-533-5282 and email is fundoffice@wsctf.org. Confirm Utah center application procedures and current craft openings before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
Selection from an eligible applicant list is not immediate enrollment. Applicants should confirm required documents, current openings, union steps, and job-site transportation expectations.
resources.name: Western States Carpenters Training Fund Carpenter and Allied Trades Apprenticeship - Utah Training Center

resources.address: Westminster University Site: 1840 S 1300 E, Room 118, Salt Lake City, UT 84105; Salt Lake County Government Center tax-season site: 2001 S State St, North Building, Salt Lake City, UT 84190
resources.description: Westminster Low Income Taxpayer Clinic helps eligible taxpayers resolve federal IRS disputes through representation, consultation, education, and advocacy, with services free of charge or for a nominal fee.
resources.hours: LITC appointment requests go to the Tax Clinic Director. Westminster University site is by appointment only outside tax season, April-December; VITA/TCE tax-season site hours differ from LITC services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low Income Taxpayer Clinic help with IRS disputes, including audits and examinations, IRS notices and tax-account problems, unpaid balances and collection disputes, installment agreements and collection alternatives, federal tax liens and levies, IRS appeals, tax-credit disputes, innocent spouse relief, identity-theft-related tax-account issues, and representation before the IRS or United States Tax Court.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For eligible low-income taxpayers and taxpayers who speak English as a second language. All requests are reviewed for eligibility, urgency, the nature and merits of the tax issue, and clinic resources.

**Population Served**
Taxpayers with IRS disputes, including Salt Lake County residents, who meet LITC eligibility and case-fit requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an appointment or initial consultation by contacting Tax Clinic Director Jovana Sisovic at jsisovic@westminsteru.edu or 801-832-2635. Briefly describe the IRS issue and any response deadline, but do not email Social Security numbers, full tax returns, or other sensitive documents.

**Important Information to Know**
The LITC generally does not provide routine tax-return preparation; Westminster's VITA/TCE services are separate. Contacting the clinic does not guarantee acceptance or representation. Services are free or nominal fee, and language assistance and reasonable accommodations are available on request.
resources.name: Westminster Low Income Taxpayer Clinic

resources.address: Salt Lake County Government Center, 2001 S State St, North Building, Salt Lake City, UT 84190; Westminster University site: 1840 S 1300 E, Room 118, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
resources.description: Westminster Tax Clinic provides free IRS-certified VITA tax preparation, electronic filing, TCE services for older adults, financial education/asset-building support and related tax clinic services at Salt Lake County seasonal sites and appointment-only off-season contact routes.
resources.hours: Salt Lake County Government Center tax-season hours listed for 2026: Monday-Thursday 4:30-9:30 PM, Friday 10:00 AM-2:00 PM, Saturday 10:00 AM-6:00 PM. Outside tax season, Westminster University site is by appointment only through the Tax Clinic Director.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free VITA tax preparation, electronic filing, financial education and asset-building services for eligible taxpayers. Westminster also lists TCE appointments for taxpayers age 60 and older and Low Income Taxpayer Clinic help for IRS disputes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VITA is for low- to moderate-income individuals and families and IRS VITA priority groups, including people with disabilities, older adults, military members, veterans, Native American tribal members and limited-English-proficiency taxpayers. TCE appointments are for taxpayers age 60 or older. All returns must be within IRS VITA/TCE scope.

**Population Served**
Eligible community taxpayers in Salt Lake County and seasonal partner sites, including low- to moderate-income households and other IRS VITA/TCE priority groups.

**How to Best Connect**
During tax season, schedule an appointment through the Westminster Tax Clinic page for the Salt Lake County Government Center or listed partner site. Outside tax season, contact Tax Clinic Director Jovana Sisovic at jsisovic@westminsteru.edu or 801-832-2635 to request an appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Appointments are required; walk-ins are not guaranteed and may be declined. The Westminster campus does not accept drop-off packets. Nonresident, international and active-duty military returns are prepared only by specialized certified volunteers at designated times and sites.
resources.name: Westminster Tax Clinic VITA and TCE Tax Preparation

resources.address: 1840 S 1300 E, Gore School of Business Room B14, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
resources.description: Westminster University's Community Clinic and Training Center provides free mental-health counseling and treatment for community members through supervised graduate counseling students, with individual, family, couples, and group counseling when the clinic is in session.
resources.hours: Open between September and May: Monday 12:30-7:00 PM, Tuesday 12:30-5:00 PM, Wednesday 12:30-5:00 PM, Thursday 12:30-7:00 PM, Friday-Sunday closed. The page also notes summer closure and fall scheduling beginning in mid-August.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free counseling and mental-health treatment through Westminster's Community Clinic and Training Center. Services include individual, family, couples, and group counseling for concerns such as trauma, depression, anxiety, grief, attachment issues, bipolar disorder, and addictions, delivered by graduate counseling students under licensed supervision.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to community members when the clinic is in session and able to schedule. The clinic is not for current Westminster students, who are directed to Integrated Wellness Mental Health Services. It cannot provide psychiatric prescribing, crisis services, treatment for severe alcohol or substance-use problems, chronic or acute suicidality, unmedicated psychosis, or needs requiring more intensive care.

**Population Served**
Community members in the Salt Lake area seeking no-cost counseling, including children, adolescents, adults, couples, families, and groups when the clinic can accept the case.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-832-2626 or email cctc@westminsteru.edu to ask about an intake appointment. The clinic does not provide walk-in services. The location is Gore School of Business, Room B14, 1840 S 1300 E, Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a university training clinic with seasonal academic-year operations, not crisis care or psychiatry. The clinic is free, but availability depends on the academic calendar, staffing, and whether the client's needs fit the clinic's scope.
resources.name: Westminster University Community Clinic and Training Center for Mental Health

resources.address: 10437 S Jordan Gateway, South Jordan, UT 84095
resources.description: White Tree Medical provides South Jordan-area ambulatory detox and addiction medical care, including a 24-hour intake line, same-day appointments, buprenorphine-based outpatient medical detox when appropriate, case management, and addiction health care.
resources.hours: 24-hour intake line advertised in assigned evidence; appointment hours not otherwise confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ambulatory detox and addiction medical care, including same-day appointment options, buprenorphine-based outpatient medical detox when clinically appropriate, case management, and ongoing addiction health care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Outpatient detox requires clinical assessment and may require a treatment companion during the acute phase. It is not appropriate for every withdrawal situation, especially when medical risk is high.

**Population Served**
People in South Jordan and the Salt Lake County area who may be clinically appropriate for outpatient detox or addiction medical care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-503-9211. The listed location is 10437 S Jordan Gateway, South Jordan, UT 84095.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm insurance, cash costs, same-day availability, medication plan, companion requirement, and whether a higher level of withdrawal care is needed before referral. Optum's Salt Lake County guide lists the provider as an ambulatory detox option, but final placement depends on assessment.
resources.name: White Tree Medical Ambulatory Detox and Addiction Care

resources.address: 700 Foothill Blvd., Salt Lake City, UT 84113
resources.description: Utah state veterans home in Salt Lake City offering skilled nursing, rehabilitation, memory care, long-term care, and respite care for eligible veterans and certain family members.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
William E. Christoffersen Salt Lake Veterans Home provides post-acute rehabilitation, extended skilled nursing care, memory care, long-term nursing-home care, daily activities, and residential care focused on veterans and eligible family members.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah states that, in general, a veteran is eligible for admission to Utah veterans homes if they served on active duty or deployed while serving in the reserves. Spouses of veterans and Gold Star parents are also eligible for admission. Admission also depends on clinical need, payer source, available beds, and the home's assessment process.

**Population Served**
Veterans needing nursing-home level care, eligible spouses of veterans, and Gold Star parents who can be served at the Salt Lake City veterans home.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-584-1900 to ask about admissions, current availability, documents, payer options, and assessment steps. The home is located at 700 Foothill Blvd. in Salt Lake City.

**Important Information to Know**
Utah states there is no cost for veterans with a 70% or higher service-connected disability; for veterans below that threshold, VA per diem may subsidize part of the cost. Spouses and Gold Star parents may be eligible for admission, but Utah states their care is not covered or subsidized by VA.
resources.name: William E. Christoffersen Salt Lake Veterans Home Skilled Nursing and Memory Care

resources.description: The Women Veterans Call Center is a free, confidential VA call, text, and chat guide to VA services, benefits, eligibility, enrollment, and local women veterans contacts.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-10:00 PM ET; Saturday 8:00 AM-6:30 PM ET; closed federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free confidential navigation for VA health care, benefits, eligibility, enrollment, appointments, prescriptions, maternity care contacts, Women Veterans Program Managers, MST, homelessness, environmental exposures, and related VA questions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Women veterans may call for themselves, and a friend, relative, or caregiver may call for them. VA says people can use the service even if they are not registered with VA or enrolled in VA health care; all veterans may use it for infertility treatment options, MST, or harassment at VA.

**Population Served**
Women veterans and people helping women veterans; some services also apply to other veterans seeking specified women-health, infertility, MST, or harassment information.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 855-829-6636, or use the online chat feature on the Women Veterans Health Care site during posted hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a navigation and direct-referral call center, not crisis response. For crisis, use 988 then press 1, text 838255, or start Veterans Crisis Line chat.
resources.name: Women Veterans Call Center

resources.address: PO Box 618, Quakertown, PA 18951
resources.description: Women for Sobriety offers the New Life Program, free women-centered peer recovery support meetings online and in person, and CARE support for friends and family; Salt Lake County residents can use the online meeting route even when no local in-person meeting is confirmed.
resources.hours: Meeting times vary; use the official meeting information and registration route for the current schedule and time zones.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Women-centered, abstinence-based peer recovery support through the New Life Program, online and in-person peer-facilitated meetings, and CARE support for friends and family. This is peer support, not detox or clinical treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to women age 18 and older seeking sobriety. Meeting registration, current meeting times, and any format-specific requirements should be checked on the official website.

**Population Served**
Adult women seeking sobriety from substance use, plus friends and family through the CARE support option.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Women for Sobriety website to find and register for current online or in-person meetings, or call 215-536-8026 for organizational contact. Salt Lake County residents should expect to use online meetings unless a current local meeting is confirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
Access is described as free, but donations or optional costs may apply depending on activity or materials. No current Salt Lake County in-person meeting was established in the sealed evidence; confirm meeting times, time zones, and registration before referral.
resources.name: Women for Sobriety New Life Program

resources.address: 201 S Main Street #2300, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Women's Business Center of Utah offers free business advising, trainings, tools, templates, online courses, funding resources, and networking support for Utah women starting or growing businesses.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; advising, including evenings and weekends, is available upon request.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free one-on-one business advising, live and virtual training workshops, online academy courses, business templates, funding resources, networking opportunities, and statewide support for starting, running, growing, and funding a business.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The FAQ says any adult in Utah interested in starting or growing a business, regardless of industry, is welcome to use services. Advising sessions are free; trainings are often free or low-cost.

**Population Served**
Utah women entrepreneurs and aspiring business owners, including Salt Lake County residents; public FAQ language says any adult in Utah interested in starting or growing a business can access services.

**How to Best Connect**
Sign up for WBCUtah services online, then schedule an advising session or register for trainings. Contact info@wbcutah.org or call 801-328-5066 or 801-364-3631. The Salt Lake office is at 201 S Main Street #2300.

**Important Information to Know**
This is entrepreneurship and self-employment support, not wage job placement. Ask about any training fees, scholarships, and whether advising will be virtual or in person.
resources.name: Women's Business Center of Utah Business Advising and Entrepreneurial Training

resources.description: WomensLaw.org Email Hotline provides U.S.-based legal information related to domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking by secure email, with emails answered or reviewed by an attorney.
resources.hours: Online email hotline; response time listed as 1-5 business days when open to new users.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Secure email hotline for U.S.-based legal information related to domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking. Emails are answered or reviewed by an attorney.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For U.S.-based survivors, loved ones, and advocates seeking legal information related to domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking. It does not provide legal advice, representation, or phone calls.

**Population Served**
Survivors and supporters in the United States, including Utah residents who need legal information and cannot safely or easily call.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the WomensLaw.org Email Hotline website to create or sign into an account and submit a question when the hotline is open to new users.

**Important Information to Know**
Expected response time is 1-5 business days when open. The page recently displayed a temporary closure notice for new users until September 22, 2026, while returning users could still log in; check the current page before relying on immediate access.
resources.name: WomensLaw.org Email Hotline

resources.description: National Wounded Warrior Project registration and resource center for no-cost programs serving eligible post-9/11 veterans, active-duty service members, family members, caregivers, and support systems.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Wounded Warrior Project registration is the entry point for no-cost WWP programs, services, and resources, including connection, mental wellness, physical wellness, financial wellness, benefits help, family support, peer support, and employment programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
WWP registration generally serves post-9/11 veterans and active-duty service members who served on or after September 11, 2001. The official criteria include service period and discharge or good-standing requirements; family members, caregivers, and support people may register, with the warrior's eligibility verified.

**Population Served**
Post-9/11 veterans, active-duty and transitioning service members, National Guard and Reserve members, family members, caregivers, and key support people nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Register online through the WWP registration page or call 888-997-2586 for registration and eligibility questions. The page also links separate warrior and family registration routes.

**Important Information to Know**
WWP states programs are no-cost and that living near a WWP office is not required because support can be in-person or virtual. Eligibility verification may be instant through ID.me or Login.gov, or may take 5 to 7 business days when instant verification is not available.
resources.name: Wounded Warrior Project Registration and Resource Center

resources.address: 1010 South 120th St Ste 130, Omaha, NE 68154
resources.description: National nonprofit offering direct support programs for combat-wounded veterans and their families, including caregiver respite assistance, adaptive vehicle grants, family retreats, and welding training.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Wounded Warriors Family Support offers programs for combat-wounded veteran households, including caregiver respite and supplemental services, Mobility is Freedom adaptive vehicle grants, family retreats, and no-cost welding training. Caregiver respite assistance can include meals, housekeeping, medical travel grants, and in-home care services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs focus on combat-wounded veterans and their families or caregivers. Each program has its own requirements; for example, Mobility is Freedom lists combat-related loss of limb, spinal cord injury, or salvage limb injury as eligibility examples.

**Population Served**
Combat-wounded veterans, their families, and caregivers. The caregiver respite program describes nationwide service to caregivers and families of wounded war veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the main office at 402-502-7557. For caregiver respite questions, call 402-932-7036 or use the online application link on the caregiver respite page. For Mobility is Freedom questions, the program page lists Martin Duarte at 760-405-7777 and Martin.Duarte@wwfs.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Wounded Warriors Family Support states it is not affiliated with Wounded Warrior Project. Mobility is Freedom says new vehicle-grant applications are suspended for the remainder of 2026 and directs people to check for updates in January 2027. Dunham House is described as a Nebraska residential community and should not be treated as a Salt Lake County housing option.
resources.name: Wounded Warriors Family Support Programs

resources.description: Xfinity Internet Essentials provides low-cost home internet for qualifying households in Xfinity service areas, with Internet Essentials and Internet Essentials Plus tiers and a discounted computer purchase option.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable home internet for qualifying households. Xfinity lists Internet Essentials at $14.95/month for up to 75 Mbps and Internet Essentials Plus at $29.95/month for up to 100 Mbps, plus access to low-cost computers, Wi-Fi hotspots, and internet training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must live where Xfinity Internet service is available, participate in qualifying assistance programs or meet income eligibility, not be an existing Xfinity Internet customer or have had Xfinity Internet within the past 90 days, and have no Comcast debt less than one year old.

**Population Served**
Qualifying low-income households in Xfinity service areas, including parts of Salt Lake County where Xfinity serves the address.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online at the Internet Essentials application link or call 1-844-389-4681 for help.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a discounted paid plan, not free internet. Taxes, professional installation, restrictions, advertised-speed limits, and address availability may apply.
resources.name: Xfinity Internet Essentials

resources.address: YWCA Utah public campus: 322 East 300 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; Family Justice Center: 310 East 300 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: YWCA Utah provides a 24/7 domestic-violence crisis line and confidential survivor services for people needing safety and family-violence support, including emergency shelter access, safety planning, child advocacy, case management, referrals, food services, drop-in child care, and housing support through the Salt Lake Area Family Justice Center.
resources.hours: 24/7 crisis line for safety and emergency shelter. Family Justice Center hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM and Friday 9:00 AM-1:00 PM; appointments recommended.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
24/7 crisis-line access for safety and family-violence services, emergency shelter access for domestic-violence situations, confidential survivor services, safety planning, child advocacy, case management, drop-in child care, community-resource referrals, food services, and Family Justice Center help with advocacy, protective-order connection, emergency shelter navigation, housing support, and economic empowerment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people needing safety and family-violence services, including domestic-violence survivors and children. Shelter access depends on safety assessment, current availability, and fit through the crisis line. Family Justice Center partner schedules and services vary.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors and families in the Salt Lake area, including women, men, and children seeking confidential safety support or emergency shelter.

**How to Best Connect**
For emergency shelter due to domestic violence, call the 24/7 crisis line at 801-537-8600 or call 911 for immediate danger. For Family Justice Center appointments, call 801-236-3370 or TTY 711. Outside agencies making housing referrals may call 801-537-8600 or email advocates@ywcautah.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not assume shelter beds are available or that the public campus address is the shelter placement location. Call the crisis line first for safe planning and current shelter access. Walk-in Family Justice Center services are limited, so appointments are recommended.
resources.name: YWCA Utah Domestic Violence Emergency Shelter and Salt Lake Area Family Justice Center
resources.phone: 24/7 crisis line 801-537-8600; Family Justice Center 801-236-3370; TTY 711

resources.address: 310 East 300 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: YWCA Utah's Salt Lake Area Family Justice Center provides free, confidential, co-located, victim-centered services for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, elder abuse, and stalking, including crisis intervention, safety planning, advocacy, protective-order connection, immigration assistance, employment support, emergency shelter navigation, housing support, and economic empowerment.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM; Friday 9:00 AM-1:00 PM. Walk-in services are limited and appointments are recommended.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Confidential co-located services for survivors, including crisis intervention, safety planning, danger assessment, advocacy and case management, police-report support, protective-order information and Legal Aid connection, immigration assistance through partners, job and education assistance, support groups, emergency shelter navigation, housing support, and economic empowerment services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For victims and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, elder abuse, and stalking. Partner schedules and service fit may vary; call ahead for appointments and partner availability.

**Population Served**
Survivors in the Salt Lake area, including adults and families affected by domestic violence, sexual assault, elder abuse, or stalking. Translation services and safe spaces for children to play are listed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Family Justice Center at 801-236-3370 or TTY 711 to schedule an appointment. The location is the Center for Families at YWCA Utah, 310 East 300 South, Salt Lake City. For after-hours crisis or emergency shelter, call 801-537-8600.

**Important Information to Know**
Walk-in services are currently limited, so scheduling in advance is recommended. Emergency shelter access goes through the 24/7 crisis line, not ordinary Family Justice Center business-hours intake.
resources.name: YWCA Utah Salt Lake Area Family Justice Center

resources.address: 322 East 300 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: YWCA Utah's Kathleen Robison Huntsman Apartments are an affordable/supportive housing program for families, with expanded eligibility for single parents with children who meet selection criteria, want supportive services, meet community living standards, and meet financial requirements; priority remains for households with domestic-violence or trauma history.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable housing at YWCA Utah's Kathleen Robison Huntsman Apartments, with supportive services focused on safety, stability, goals, and self-sufficiency. Public YWCA materials describe flexibility between transitional 24-month leases and permanent shorter or longer rental leases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Single parents with children may apply if they meet KRH Apartments selection criteria, want to engage in YWCA supportive services, follow community living standards, and meet financial requirements. YWCA says priority remains for families with any history of domestic violence or trauma, and applications may use Section 8 vouchers or other funding sources.

**Population Served**
Families with children, especially domestic-violence or trauma-affected families, and qualifying single-parent households with children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call YWCA Utah's main line at 801-537-8604 or, for survivor-service and housing-support connection, call 801-236-3370. Ask specifically whether Kathleen Robison Huntsman Apartments applications or waitlist access are currently open and what financial documentation is required.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page verifying the KRH Apartments eligibility expansion is dated 2020 and does not publish a current application packet, vacancy status, waitlist status, rent amount, or full selection criteria. Confirm current application steps before treating this as an immediate housing option.
resources.name: YWCA Utah The Kathleen Robison Huntsman Apartments

resources.address: 210 East 400 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Year Up United's Salt Lake City Career Pathways program offers tuition-free job training for young adults ages 18-29 through flexible virtual and in-person engagement, with local tracks in banking, business operations, customer success, and data analytics, followed by job support through YUPRO Placement.
resources.hours: Apply online; Fall 2026 Salt Lake City start dates listed as September 2026 and October 2026.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tuition-free job training for young adults, with flexible virtual and in-person engagement. Fall 2026 Salt Lake City tracks listed on the official page include banking, business operations, customer success, and data analytics. The pathway includes hands-on experience, professional development, possible internships, and job support through YUPRO Placement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Salt Lake City page states the Fall 2026 programs are designed for young adults ages 18-29. Application status, start-date availability, and full eligibility should be confirmed through the online application.

**Population Served**
Young adults ages 18-29 in the Salt Lake City area who are seeking career training and full-time employment pathways.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the Apply or Become a Student link on the Salt Lake City location page or call the national Year Up United line at 855-YEARUP1. The Salt Lake City location address is 210 East 400 South.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is tuition-free, but cohort timing matters. The opened official page listed Fall 2026 starts in September and October 2026, so applicants should confirm which tracks are still accepting applications.
resources.name: Year Up United Career Pathways in Salt Lake City

resources.address: P.O. Box 388, Fortine, MT 59918
resources.description: Remote nonprofit that helps people legally change their name and gender marker and update identity documents such as birth certificates, driver licenses, Social Security records, U.S. passports, and other records.
resources.hours: Free consultations and meetings are offered remotely during work and evening hours; exact appointment times are set through booking or contact.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Your Identity Transitions helps with legal name and gender-marker changes, including preparing petition documents, assisting with court filing, monitoring the filing, preparing for a hearing if one is required, ordering certified copies after a court order, preparing birth-certificate amendment paperwork, and giving instructions and documents for updating a driver license, Social Security record, and passport.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is for people seeking legal name and/or gender-marker changes and related identity-document updates. The nonprofit states that it works with clients from every U.S. state and provides services remotely. Financial assistance or a reduced service fee may be available based on income.

**Population Served**
The organization is trans-operated and states that its mission is to serve the transgender and queer community and other parties who need name and gender-marker change help.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the website to book a free consultation, request a quote, or use the contact form. Clients may also call 817-366-8694 or email michele@youridentitytransitions.org. Meetings can be held remotely by phone, Discord, or Zoom.

**Important Information to Know**
The consultation is free. Published sliding-scale service fees are $450 for income at or above 200% of the federal poverty level, $350 for 100%-200%, and $225 for 100% or lower; court, certificate, passport, and agency fees may still vary. The organization is a Montana-registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Its staff and volunteers disclose that they are nonlawyers and cannot give legal advice or represent clients as attorneys.
resources.name: Your Identity Transitions Legal Name & Gender Marker Change Assistance

resources.description: Zion Healing Academy, doing business as Zion Vocational Rehabilitation Center, is listed by USOR as an approved Community Rehabilitation Program provider serving Salt Lake, Tooele, and Davis counties for supported employment-related services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
USOR lists Zion Healing Academy DBA Zion Vocational Rehabilitation Center as an approved Community Rehabilitation Program provider. The CRP list covers supported job-based training, supported employment, customized employment, IPS supported employment, Pre-ETS, supported education, financial literacy, and other service columns; clients should ask which approved services are available for their situation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The USOR listing identifies service to Salt Lake, Tooele, and Davis counties. Services may require Vocational Rehabilitation, DSPD, or another disability-service funding or authorization route.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities or vocational rehabilitation needs in Salt Lake, Tooele, and Davis counties who may need supported employment or related CRP services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the listed CRP contact, Francis Weah, at 801-657-6671. If funding or referral path is unclear, contact USOR Vocational Rehabilitation and ask about Zion Vocational Rehabilitation Center as a CRP option.

**Important Information to Know**
Public information located for this pass was the official USOR CRP list rather than a standalone provider website or street address. Confirm current intake, capacity, services offered, and funding requirements before referral.
resources.name: Zion Vocational Rehabilitation Center Supported Employment

resources.address: 2711 Lyndon B. Johnson Freeway, Suite 1065, Dallas, TX 75234
